1:2.notes: Al-hamd uttered directly → praise. Ar-Rahman / Ar-Rahim → mercy. Rabb al-'alamin asserts lordship/sovereignty. Maliki yawm al-din names the Day of Judgment explicitly.

1:5.notes: 'Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in — exclusive worship and help-seeking asserts tawhid. 'Ihdina al-sirat al-mustaqim' is an uttered supplication for guidance → dua-guidance.

1:7.notes: The path of those blessed vs. those who evoked anger and those who are astray. Per Ibn Kathir and the labeling instructions §10, 'those who evoked anger' and 'those who are astray' map to Jews and Christians respectively → people-of-the-book. Guidance is the explicit subject of the continued supplication. Confidence medium on people-of-the-book because the group is described rather than named.

19:1.notes: Section opens with the disjoined letters Kaf-Ha-Ya-Ayn-Sad, then immediately transitions into Zechariah's story. The uttered supplication 'Rabbi' (vv. 4–6) asking for an heir qualifies as dua-family-offspring. 'It is easy for me, and I created you before, when you were nothing' asserts power. The miraculous birth promised to a barren couple qualifies as miracles. Marriage-and-family is triggered by the barren wife and concern for dependents.

19:10.notes: Zechariah is given the sign of three nights of silence — a miracle confirming the promise. He then signals his people to praise (subbihu) morning and evening, which is an uttered/enacted praise formula. Nearness-and-response is implicit in the Lord answering and giving a sign.

19:12.notes: 'O John, hold on to the Scripture firmly' → previous-scriptures. 'We gave him wisdom in his youth' and 'tenderness from Us' → mercy. 'He was devout' (taqiyan) → taqwa (explicit trigger word). 'Kind to his parents' → children-and-parents. 'Peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the Day he is raised alive' → resurrection and day-of-judgment referenced explicitly.

19:16.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling, all independently justified. 'I take refuge from you in the Most Merciful' is an uttered supplication of protection → dua-protection. 'A sign for humanity' → mankind. 'It is easy for Me' → power. 'A matter already decided' → divine-decree. Stream and dates → provision. Miraculous conception → human-creation and miracles. Gabriel (Our spirit) → angels. Marriage-and-family triggered by the unmarried pregnancy context and chastity reference.

19:27.notes: Aaron named in v. 28 ('O sister of Aaron') → aaron. Slander-and-backbiting tagged per the accusation against Mary (per Ibn Kathir, §11 of instructions). Jesus speaks as an infant — miracle. He declares himself a prophet given scripture → prophethood-general. He enjoins prayer and zakat → prayer and zakat-and-charity. 'Kind to my mother' → children-and-parents. 'The day I die, and the Day I get resurrected alive' → resurrection and day-of-judgment.

19:34.notes: 'That is Jesus son of Mary' → jesus, mary. 'It is not for Allah to have a child — glory be to Him' (Subhanahu) → tawhid, praise (subhan formula uttered), and shirk (the refutation of associating a son). 'He says to it Be and it becomes' → power, divine-decree. 'Those who disbelieve… a tremendous Day' → disbelievers, day-of-judgment. 'We who will inherit the earth' → sovereignty.

19:41.notes: Abraham named as subject → abraham. Isaac and Jacob explicitly granted (v. 49) → isaac, jacob. Iblis named ('do not worship the devil') → iblis. Shirk refuted through Abraham's call away from idol worship → shirk. 'The Most Gracious' invoked three times; mercy is the cluster → mercy. 'I will guide you along a straight way' → guidance (explicit subject of instruction). Abraham's withdrawal from his people → migration. 'Kind to his parents' context and father-son dialogue → children-and-parents. 'Each We made a prophet' → prophethood-general.

19:51.notes: Four prophets explicitly named → moses, aaron, ishmael, idris. 'Out of Our mercy' → mercy. 'Brought him near in communion' → nearness-and-response. 'He was dedicated' (mukhlasan) → sincerity (explicit trigger word for ikhlas). Ishmael enjoins prayer and zakat → prayer, zakat-and-charity. All called messengers and prophets → prophethood-general.

19:58.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: the-quran (revelation is referenced but not the primary subject), believers (implied rather than directly addressed with ya ayyuha).

19:64.notes: Angels speaking ('We do not descend except by the command of your Lord') → angels. 'His is what is before us, and what is behind us' → knowledge (God's complete knowledge). 'Your Lord is never forgetful' → knowledge. 'Lord of the heavens and the earth' → sovereignty and creation-of-heavens-earth. 'Persevere in His service' (istasbir) → patience (explicit trigger word for sabr). 'Do you know of anyone equal to Him?' → tawhid (uniqueness assertion).

19:66.notes: 'The human being says' → mankind (generic address about humans). 'We created him before, when he was nothing' → human-creation. 'Will I be brought back alive?' and gathering → resurrection. 'We will round them up and the devils' → iblis. 'Bring them around Hell' → hell. 'This has been an unavoidable decree' → divine-decree (explicit). 'Those who were devout' (attaqaw) → taqwa (explicit trigger). 'A tremendous Day' → day-of-judgment. Wrongdoers left in hell → disbelievers.

19:73.notes: 'Those who disbelieve say to those who believe' → disbelievers, believers. 'Say' (qul) in v. 75 → qul-statements. 'The Most Merciful will lead him on' → mercy. 'Allah increases in guidance those who accept guidance' → guidance (explicit subject). 'How many a generation have We destroyed before them' → punishment-of-past-nations. 'Either the punishment, or the Hour' → day-of-judgment. Denial of revelations (v. 77, 73) → denial-of-revelation. 'The righteous deeds have the best reward' → righteous-conduct (explicit trigger). 'We are fully aware' → knowledge.

19:81.notes: 'They took, besides Allah, other gods' → shirk. 'We dispatch the devils against the disbelievers' → iblis, disbelievers. 'Herd the sinners into hell' → hell. 'The Most Merciful' (v. 85, 87) → mercy. 'Gather the righteous to the Most Merciful' → day-of-judgment and taqwa (righteous/muttaqin explicitly named). 'They will have no power of intercession' → intercession (explicit subject). Counting-down-to-punishment connects to day-of-judgment.

19:88.notes: 'The Most Merciful has begotten a son' — the claim and its refutation → tawhid and shirk. 'The heavens almost rupture… the earth splits… mountains crumble' → creation-of-heavens-earth (cosmic imagery). 'None in the heavens and the earth but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant' → sovereignty. 'He has enumerated them and counted them' → knowledge. 'Each one will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection' → day-of-judgment. 'You have come up with something monstrous' addressed to those making this claim → disbelievers. The servants of the Most Merciful = mankind in the broadest sense → mankind.

19:96.notes: 'Those who believe and do righteous deeds' → believers. 'The Most Merciful will give them love' → mercy. 'We made it easy in your tongue' → language-and-revelation-terms (Arabic clarity, revelation as communicated words). 'To deliver good news to the righteous' (muttaqin) → taqwa (explicit). 'Warn with it a hostile people' → disbelievers (those warned). The Qur'an as instrument of glad tidings and warning → the-quran and guidance.

19:98.notes: 'How many a generation have We destroyed before them' → punishment-of-past-nations and previous-creations-destroyed (ruins-and-warnings). Short single-verse section with a clear eschatological warning directed implicitly at the disbelievers.

67:1.notes: tabāraka opens the surah → praise. 'He is the Almighty, the Forgiving' → power + mercy as closing attributes. Seven heavens in layers → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'No discrepancy' → wisdom. 'Created death and life' → creation + death-and-dying.

67:5.notes: Lanterns (stars) → cosmic-bodies. Made missiles against devils → iblis. Hell described in vivid detail for disbelievers → hell + disbelievers + disbelief. Keepers of hell ask about warner → prophethood-general. Inmates admit they denied the truth → denial-of-revelation. v.12 'those who fear their Lord in secret' → believers + taqwa. 'Forgiveness and great reward' → mercy. 11 labels — within ceiling.

67:13.notes: 'He is Aware of inner thoughts / Would He not know He who created' → knowledge. 'Eat of His provisions' → provision. Earth made manageable, storm warning → natural-signs. 'Those before them denied and how was My disapproval' → punishment-of-past-nations. Threatening with earth collapse and storm → power. Section addresses humanity broadly in second person → mankind.

67:19.notes: Birds in flight held by the Compassionate → natural-signs (straddling from prior section context; birds are the primary image here). 'None holds them except the Compassionate' → mercy + power. 'Who will provide for you if He withholds His provision' → provision. 'The disbelievers are in nothing but delusion' → disbelievers. Straight path vs. bent walking → guidance (explicitly named as 'better guided' / 'straight path').

67:23.notes: Three 'Say:' imperatives (vv.23, 24, 26) → qul-statements. 'He produced you … hearing, vision, organs' → human-creation + creation + mankind. 'Rarely do you give thanks' → gratitude (shukr explicitly named in translation). 'To Him you will be rounded up' → day-of-judgment. 'Knowledge is with Allah and I am only a clear warner' → knowledge + prophethood-general. Faces of disbelievers turning gloomy → disbelievers.

67:28.notes: Two 'Say:' imperatives → qul-statements. 'He bestows His mercy on us' → mercy. 'Who will protect the disbelievers from agonizing torment' → disbelievers + hell. 'In Him we trust' → trust-in-god (tawakkul explicitly stated).

67:30.notes: 'Say:' imperative → qul-statements. Water draining away / who brings pure running water → provision + natural-signs. The rhetorical challenge to bring water underscores God's unique power → power. Single verse but carries four independently defensible labels.

112:1.notes: Qul opens the surah; 'the One' and 'the Absolute' (As-Samad) assert tawhid and sovereignty/power directly.

112:4.notes: No comparable — absolute incomparability of God, completing the tawhid argument and rejecting all forms of associating equals with Him.

2:1.notes: Opens with Alif-Lam-Mim (disjoined letters). Section describes the Quran as guidance for the muttaqin and outlines their qualities including belief in the unseen, prayer, charity, and belief in previous revelations.

2:6.notes: Describes those who disbelieve — Allah has sealed their hearts; severe torment awaits them.

2:8.notes: Classic hypocrisy passage — those who claim belief but are not believers; sickness in their hearts.

2:11.notes: Hypocrites deny they cause corruption; called out as the real troublemakers. Explicitly names corruption on earth (fasad). Mocking believers implied in verse 14 (mockery label borderline — 'ridiculing' present).

2:17.notes: Parable of the fire going out — hypocrites left in darkness. Guidance metaphor prominent.

2:19.notes: Parable of the rainstorm/cloudburst — natural imagery (thunder, lightning) used as analogy for disbelievers' state. Allah's power over all things closes the section.

2:21.notes: Opens with 'O people!' (ya ayyuha an-nas). Commands worship of the Creator who made earth, sky, sends rain and provides fruit. Ends with prohibition of rivals to Allah (shirk).

2:23.notes: The challenge to produce a surah like it; warning of the Fire for disbelievers.

2:25.notes: Single verse describing paradise for believers — gardens, rivers, pure spouses, eternal abode.

2:26.notes: Allah's right to use any parable; believers know it is truth; disbelievers question it. Verse 27 describes those who break Allah's covenant and spread corruption on earth.

2:28.notes: How can you deny Allah who gave you life? He will cause death then resurrection. Created everything on earth and seven heavens. Closes with 'He is aware of all things' (knowledge).

2:30.notes: The appointment of Adam as khalifa on earth; angels praise Allah ('Glory be to You'); Adam taught the names; angels declare 'You are the Knowledgeable, the Wise' — knowledge and wisdom attributes confirmed. Praise uttered by angels ('Subhanaka').

2:34.notes: Iblis refuses prostration — arrogance and disbelief named explicitly. Adam and spouse in the Garden; Satan causes their slip; Adam receives words from Lord and repents. 'He is the Relenting, the Merciful' → mercy. Guidance offered to those who follow it; Fire for disbelievers.

2:40.notes: 13 labels — over 12 ceiling. Direct address to Children of Israel recalling covenant, blessings, the exodus from Pharaoh, parting of the sea (miracle), forty nights with Moses, the calf worship, pardon. Trim candidates: intercession (mentioned briefly in v48 as not being accepted), previous-scriptures (implicit). Moses and pharaoh named explicitly.

2:47.notes: Reminders to Bani Israel of favors; warning of a Day when no intercession accepted; Pharaoh's persecution; parting of sea (miracle); 40-night appointment of Moses; calf worship (shirk).

2:53.notes: Moses given the Scripture and Criterion; calf worship and commanded repentance; thunderbolt and revival; manna and quails as provision; 'He is the Accepter of Repentance, the Merciful' → mercy and repentance.

2:58.notes: Israel commanded to enter the town humbly and say 'pardon'; wrongdoers substituted other words and a plague descended. Narrow narrative episode.

2:60.notes: Moses strikes rock; twelve springs appear (miracle, provision). Israel complains about food; struck with humiliation for rejecting signs and killing prophets. Corruption on earth named ('do not corrupt the earth'). people-of-the-book appropriate for the Israel narrative.

2:62.notes: Jews, Christians, Sabeans and believers — reward for faith and good deeds. Covenant at Mount; Sabbath violation; apes punishment. 'Allah's grace and mercy' → mercy.

2:67.notes: The heifer story — Moses commands sacrifice; people question repeatedly; finally comply. Verse 73 explicitly: 'Thus Allah brings the dead to life' (miracle). Verse 74: hearts harder than rocks. Knowledge: 'Allah is not unaware of what you do.'

2:75.notes: Distortion of scripture, concealment of truth for worldly gain. Verse 80 contains 'Say' (qul). Hell and paradise contrasted in vv81-82. Knowledge: Allah knows what they conceal.

2:83.notes: Covenant with Israel: worship Allah, good to parents, relatives, orphans, needy, speak nicely, pray, give alms. Then bloodshed and expulsion condemned. Captive ransoming condemned as selective belief. Day of Resurrection punishment mentioned.

2:87.notes: Moses given Scripture; succession of messengers; Jesus given clear proofs and Holy Spirit. Israel grew arrogant, rejected and killed prophets. Verse 90 explicitly names envy (baghy/hasad). Denial of revelation explicit.

2:93.notes: Covenant at the Mount; Israel says 'we hear and disobey'; hearts filled with love of the calf (shirk). Verse 94 has 'Say' (qul). Verse 94 challenge: wish for death if paradise is yours alone. Knowledge: 'Allah is aware of the evildoers.'

2:97.notes: Gabriel named as revealer of the Quran to the Prophet's heart. Michael named. Those hostile to Allah's angels and messengers are enemies of God. Clear signs revealed; covenant-breaking recurring theme. Verse 97 has 'Say' (qul).

2:101.notes: People of the Book threw Allah's Book behind backs. Followed what devils recited during Solomon's reign. Harut and Marut named explicitly. Sorcery taught to cause separation between husband and wife. Cannot harm except by Allah's permission (divine-decree). Verse 103 mentions taqwa as the better path.

2:104.notes: O believers — do not say ambiguous words. People of the Book and polytheists do not wish good upon believers. 'Allah chooses for His mercy whomever He wills' → mercy. Verse 111 has 'Say' (qul).

2:106.notes: Abrogation of verses — Allah capable of all things (power). Sovereignty of heavens and earth. People of the Book wish to turn believers back out of envy (named explicitly). Verse 120 has 'Say' (qul). Prayer and zakat commanded v110. Knowledge and power at close.

2:111.notes: Jews and Christians claim only they enter paradise. 'Say, produce your proof' (qul). They accuse each other. Allah will judge between them on Day of Resurrection.

2:114.notes: Those who prevent remembrance of Allah in mosques and ruin them — punishment in this world and hereafter. East and West belong to Allah; wherever you turn is Allah's presence. Closes with 'Omnipresent and Omniscient' → knowledge.

2:116.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. 'Allah has begotten a son' refuted (tawhid vs shirk). 'Subhanahu' uttered → praise. Originator of heavens and earth (creation-of-heavens-earth, sovereignty). 'Be and it becomes' (power). Prophet sent with truth (prophethood-general). 'Say' in v120 (qul-statements). Guidance theme throughout. Mercy implicit in v121 believers following scripture.

2:122.notes: Address to Children of Israel — remember My favor. Warning about a Day of no intercession, no ransom. Abraham tested with words and made imam of humanity — his covenant with Allah.

2:125.notes: The House (Ka'bah) made focal point; Abraham's station as prayer place. Abraham and Ishmael commissioned to purify the House. Abraham's supplication: 'O My Lord, make this a peaceful land, and provide...' — uttered du'a → dua-protection (seeking safety for the land) and provision. Hell for disbelievers at close.

2:127.notes: Abraham and Ishmael raise foundations of the House — uttered du'a: 'Our Lord, accept it from us' (dua-forgiveness), 'make us submissive' and 'from our descendants a Muslim community' (dua-family-offspring), 'show us our rites' (dua-guidance), 'send a messenger' (prophethood-general). Multiple closing divine names: Hearer/Knower (knowledge), Acceptor of Repentance/Merciful (mercy), Almighty/Wise (wisdom/power).

2:130.notes: Who would forsake Abraham's religion? Abraham chosen in this world and the next. He submitted to the Lord of the Worlds. Abraham and Jacob exhort sons to die as Muslims. Tawhid — 'One God; and to Him we submit' (v133). Isaac, Ishmael named in v133.

2:133.notes: Jacob's deathbed scene — sons profess worship of the God of Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac. Tawhid explicit: 'One God'. Verse 134: each community is accountable for its own deeds (reckoning).

2:135.notes: 13 labels — over 12 ceiling. 'Say, the religion of Abraham the monotheist' (qul + tawhid + shirk refuted). Verse 136: believe in Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Patriarchs, Moses, Jesus — all named. Knowledge: 'He is the Hearer, the Knower.' Trim candidates: shirk (only implicit via 'not an idolater'), knowledge (minor closing formula).

2:139.notes: Do you argue with us about Allah? Works are separate (sincerity — 'we are sincere to Him'). Were Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Patriarchs Jews or Christians? — all named. 'Say' (qul). Allah knows what you do (knowledge).

2:142.notes: Qiblah change passage — 'Say, to Allah belong East and West' (qul). Direct address to Prophet: 'We have seen your face turned towards the heaven... turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque' — this is direct second-person address to Muhammad (muhammad). Allah guides whom He wills. Mercy: 'Allah is Kind towards the people, Merciful.' Knowledge throughout. Believers addressed.

2:149.notes: Turn toward the Sacred Mosque (repeated command). Messenger sent among you to recite, purify, teach. Verse 152: 'Remember Me, and I will remember you. Thank Me' — gratitude (shukr explicitly named) and remembrance (dhikr explicitly named).

2:153.notes: Opens 'O you who believe!' Seek help through patience and prayers (both named explicitly). Allah is with the steadfast. Do not say the slain in Allah's cause are dead — they are alive. Trials and good news to the patient. Verse 157: 'blessings and mercy from their Lord' → mercy. Trust-in-god implied in steadfastness under trial.

2:158.notes: Safa and Marwa as rites of Allah. Hajj and Umrah. Those who suppress guidance — Allah and all cursers curse them. Repentance accepted: 'I am the Acceptor of Repentance, the Merciful' → mercy, repentance. Those who die as disbelievers — curse of Allah, angels, all humanity → angels tagged. Knowledge: 'Allah is Appreciative and Cognizant.'

2:163.notes: 10 labels. 'Your God is one God' → tawhid. 'The Benevolent, the Compassionate' → mercy. Verse 164: creation of heavens/earth, night/day (cosmic-bodies), ships, rain reviving earth (natural-signs), animals, winds — signs for mankind. Verse 165: those who take equals to Allah (shirk). Day of Judgment torment for wrongdoers. Hell at close (v167). Power: 'all power is Allah's.'

2:168.notes: Opens 'O people!' (mankind). Eat lawful and good; do not follow Satan (iblis). Satan commands evil. Disbelievers follow ancestors blindly. Verse 172: 'O you who believe' — eat good things We provided (provision); food-and-dietary law prominent in v173 (carrion, blood, swine forbidden). Closing: 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Verse 173 prohibits what is slaughtered for other than Allah → shirk.

2:174.notes: Those who conceal what Allah revealed in Scripture and sell it — swallow fire. No speech from Allah on Day of Resurrection. Painful punishment. They exchanged guidance for error. The Book revealed in truth.

2:177.notes: The comprehensive 'birr' verse — righteousness is not merely turning toward East/West. Belief in Allah, Last Day, angels, Scripture, prophets; giving wealth to relatives, orphans, needy, homeless, beggars, freeing slaves; prayer; zakat; fulfilling promises (covenant); patience in hardship. Closes: 'these are the pious' (taqwa named explicitly).

2:178.notes: O believers — retaliation for murder ordained. Free for free, slave for slave, female for female. Option of pardon and compensation. 'A concession from your Lord, and a mercy' → mercy. Verse 180: testament when death approaches (death-and-dying, wealth-and-property-law). Knowledge: 'Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.'

2:183.notes: O believers — fasting prescribed (fasting). Ramadan — month of Quran revelation (the-quran, ritual-calendar). 'Celebrate Allah' (Allahu akbar commanded) → praise. Allah desires ease. Verse 186: 'I am near; I answer the caller' → nearness-and-response. Guidance and taqwa named. Knowledge: 'Allah is Seeing.'

2:187.notes: Permitted intercourse with wives on night of fast; limits on fasting conduct (no approach in mosque retreat). These are limits of Allah (taqwa implicitly invoked — explicitly in 'that they may attain piety'). Verse 188: do not consume wealth unjustly or as bribes (wealth-and-property-law). Knowledge: 'Allah is aware.'

2:189.notes: Crescents as timetables for people and Hajj (ritual-calendar, hajj). 'Say' (qul) in v189. Fight those who fight you (war-and-treaties). Sacred Mosque mentioned in v191. 'If they cease, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Fight until no oppression and worship is for Allah. Verse 195: spend in Allah's cause; taqwa implied throughout.

2:196.notes: Complete Hajj and Umrah for Allah. Rules for being prevented, shaving head, sacrificial offering, fasting as alternative, charity, rites of umrah-then-hajj. Sacred Mosque explicitly mentioned.

2:197.notes: Hajj in specific months; no relations, misconduct, quarrelling. Taqwa named as best provision. Verse 198: remembrance at the Sacred Landmark. Verse 199: 'ask Allah for forgiveness; Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful' → mercy. Verse 200: remember Allah. Verse 201 contains uttered du'a 'Rabbana atina fi'd-dunya hasanatan...' → dua-protection (asking protection from Fire). Verse 202: reckoning (knowledge).

2:203.notes: Designated days of remembrance in Hajj. Verses 204-206: the hypocritical man whose speech impresses but who spreads corruption when powerful (corruption-on-earth named explicitly in v205). His pride leads to sin; Hell for him. Verse 207: the sincere believer who sells his soul for Allah — 'Allah is kind' → mercy. Verse 208: O believers, enter Islam fully; do not follow Satan (iblis). Verse 209: 'Allah is Powerful and Wise' → wisdom, power.

2:210.notes: Are they waiting for Allah in clouds with angels — matter settled? All returns to Allah. Ask Children of Israel how many signs given. Disbelievers have worldly life beautified and mock believers (mockery — 'ridicule those who believe' in v212). Righteous above them on Day of Resurrection. Provision: 'Allah provides to whomever He wills.' Verse 213: Allah sent prophets (prophethood-general) with Scripture to judge between people; guidance.

2:214.notes: Do you expect to enter Paradise without trials like those before you? Adversity — Messenger and believers asked 'when is Allah's victory?' Patience in adversity implicit context. Verse 215: 'They ask you what they should spend. Say' (qul). Charity for parents, relatives, orphans, poor, wayfarer (children-and-parents, orphan-care, zakat-and-charity). Knowledge: 'Allah is aware of it.'

2:216.notes: Fighting ordained (war-and-treaties). Verse 217: 'Say' (qul) about fighting in the Sacred Month — Sacred Mosque mentioned. Migration mentioned implicitly (expelling people from it). Those who apostatize and die as disbelievers — Fire. Verse 218: those who believed, migrated and fought → mercy. 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Knowledge throughout.

2:219.notes: Questions about intoxicants and gambling (explicitly named — intoxicants-and-gambling). 'Say' (qul): gross sin, some benefit, sin outweighs. 'Say': give the surplus (zakat-and-charity). Verse 220: orphans — 'Say': improvement is best (orphan-care). 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' → wisdom. Knowledge throughout.

2:221.notes: Do not marry idolatresses/idolaters (marriage-and-family, polytheists/shirk). A believing slave is better than a polytheist. Polytheists call to Fire; Allah calls to Garden and forgiveness → paradise, mercy.

2:222.notes: Menstruation — keep away until pure; approach as Allah directed (ritual-purity, chastity-and-boundaries, marriage-and-family). 'Allah loves the repentant and those who keep clean' → repentance. Verse 223: wives as cultivation — approach when you like; fear Allah (knowledge: 'know that you will meet Him').

2:224.notes: Do not make Allah an obstacle in your oaths to doing good (oaths-and-vows). Vow of abstinence from wives — wait four months (divorce-related, marriage-and-family). If they resolve to divorce → divorce. Divorced women wait three periods; husbands have right to take back (divorce, marriage-and-family). 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' → wisdom. Mercy: 'Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.'

2:229.notes: Divorce allowed twice; retain honorably or release kindly. Not lawful to take back what was given unless they fear breaking Allah's limits. If divorced thrice, not lawful until she marries another. Allah's limits in marriage and divorce.

2:231.notes: When you divorce women reaching their term — retain or release amicably; do not retain to harm them. Do not take Allah's revelations for a joke. Remember Allah's favor and the Scripture revealed (the-quran). Knowledge: 'Allah is aware of everything.' Verse 232: do not prevent divorced women from remarrying.

2:233.notes: Mothers nurse infants two years; father provides for them. No soul burdened beyond capacity. Mutual consent for weaning. Hiring nursing-mothers allowed. Inheritance: 'the same duty rests upon the heir.' Knowledge: 'Allah is Seeing of what you do.'

2:234.notes: Widows wait four months and ten days after husband's death. When term completed — no blame for what they do honorably. Verse 235: no blame for hinting at engagement during iddah but do not meet secretly or conclude marriage until iddah complete. 'Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing' → mercy. Knowledge throughout.

2:236.notes: Divorce before consummation — no error; compensate women fairly (divorce, wealth-and-property-law). Verse 237: if dowry was set, half is due unless forfeited (wealth-and-property-law). 'To forego is nearer to piety.' Verse 238: guard prayers and middle prayer (prayer). Verse 239: if in fear, pray on foot or riding; when safe, remember Allah (remembrance).

2:240.notes: Those who die leaving wives — testament for wives' support for a year. Divorced women provided for equitably. 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' → wisdom. Knowledge: 'Allah thus explains His revelations.'

2:243.notes: Those who fled homes in thousands fearing death — Allah said 'Die' then revived them (death-and-dying, resurrection, power). Fight in Allah's cause (war-and-treaties). Verse 245: generous loan to Allah — multiplied manifold (zakat-and-charity). 'Allah receives and amplifies' → power. Knowledge: 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing.'

2:246.notes: Children of Israel after Moses — ask prophet to appoint a king (Saul/Talut). 'Allah has chosen him over you, increased in knowledge and stature' → sovereignty, knowledge. Verse 248: Ark restored — relics from family of Moses and Aaron (moses, aaron named). Angels carry it (angels). Sign for believers.

2:249.notes: Saul tests troops with river; few pass. Confronting Goliath — uttered du'a: 'Our Lord, pour down patience on us, strengthen our foothold, support us against the faithless' → dua-distress. 'Allah is with the steadfast' (patience). David kills Goliath; given sovereignty and wisdom (david, goliath named). Power and wisdom explicit.

2:252.notes: These are Allah's revelations recited to you — 'you are one of the messengers' (direct address to Muhammad → muhammad). Verse 253: messengers ranked; some Allah spoke to directly; Jesus given clear miracles and Holy Spirit (jesus). 'Allah does whatever He desires' → divine-decree.

2:254.notes: O believers — spend before a Day of no trading, no friendship, no intercession. Ayat al-Kursi (v255): no god except He (tawhid); the Living, the Everlasting; sovereignty of heavens and earth; intercession only by His permission; complete knowledge; Throne extends over heavens and earth (sovereignty); 'the Most High, the Great.'

2:256.notes: No compulsion in religion — right way distinct from wrong (guidance, tawhid). Whoever renounces evil and believes in Allah has the firm handle. Allah is guardian of believers — brings from darkness to light. Disbelievers' lords are the evil ones — Fire forever. Knowledge: 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing.'

2:258.notes: The one who argued with Abraham about his Lord — given sovereignty by Allah. Abraham: my Lord gives life and causes death. The king claims same. Abraham: Allah brings sun from East; bring it from West — blasphemer confounded (tawhid, power, sovereignty). Cosmic bodies (sun from East) used as argument. Disbelief: 'Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.'

2:259.notes: Man passing ruined town — how can Allah revive this? Allah causes him to die for a hundred years then resurrects (resurrection, power, miracles). Food not spoiled; bones reclothed with flesh. 'We will make you a wonder for mankind.' Concludes: 'Allah has power over all things.'

2:260.notes: Abraham asks: 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead' — uttered supplication → dua-knowledge-wisdom (asking to witness/understand). Four birds placed on hills, then called and they come (miracle). 'Allah is Powerful and Wise' → power, wisdom. Resurrection theme.

2:261.notes: Parable of spending in Allah's way — grain producing 700 grains (natural imagery → natural-signs). Those who follow charity with reminders or insults nullify it (sincerity — spending purely for Allah's sake). Verse 264: 'O you who believe' — do not nullify charity with reminders. Satan promises poverty, urges immorality (iblis). Allah gives wisdom to whom He wills (wisdom). Verse 270: whatever charity or vow (oaths-and-vows). Knowledge throughout.

2:267.notes: O believers — give of good things earned; do not pick inferior things (zakat-and-charity, sincerity). Satan promises poverty (iblis). Allah promises forgiveness and grace (mercy implicit). 'He gives wisdom' → wisdom. Verse 272: guidance is Allah's to give. Verse 273: for the poor restrained in Allah's cause. Knowledge: 'Allah is aware of it' (multiple times).

2:274.notes: Those who spend night and day in charity — reward with Lord. Verses 275-280: riba (interest) condemned extensively — those who consume usury will not rise except as one driven mad; Allah has forbidden usury (interest label). 'Allah condemns usury, blesses charities.' Prayer and zakat for believers (v277). 'O believers, fear Allah and forgo remaining usury' (v278). Repentance: 'if you repent, you may keep your capital.' Day of Judgment (v281). Mercy: 'Most Forgiving, Most Merciful' (v199 area — here v279 does not, but v276 'Allah does not love any sinful ingrate'; mercy label from v275 'Forgiving and Merciful' implicit close).

2:282.notes: The debt/contract verse — write down debts with a just scribe; two witnesses or one man and two women; do not harm scribe or witness (trade-and-debt, justice-and-witness, wealth-and-property-law). Verse 283: travel without scribe — security deposit; do not conceal testimony (justice-and-witness). Verse 284: to Allah belongs everything in heavens and earth; He forgives and punishes whom He wills (sovereignty, mercy). Knowledge and power throughout. Taqwa: 'fear Allah' commanded.

2:285.notes: The Messenger believed in what was revealed (direct reference to Muhammad in context → muhammad). Believers' creed: Allah, angels, scriptures, messengers. 'We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord' — uttered supplication → dua-forgiveness. Knowledge: 'to you is the destiny.' Mercy implicit in seeking forgiveness.

2:286.notes: Allah does not burden a soul beyond capacity. Extended uttered du'a: 'Our Lord, do not condemn us if we forget or err' (dua-forgiveness), 'do not burden us as You burdened those before us', 'do not burden us beyond our strength; pardon us, forgive us, have mercy on us' (dua-forgiveness, dua-distress, dua-protection — multiple aspects), 'help us against the disbelieving people' (dua-protection). Justice: 'each soul rewarded for what it earned.' Mercy: 'have mercy on us.'

3:1.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Section opens with Alif-Lam-Mim (disjoined-letters). Verses 2–4: tawhid assertion, Quran/Torah/Gospel sent down (the-quran, previous-scriptures, guidance). Verse 5: Allah's complete knowledge (knowledge). Verse 6: forms in the womb (human-creation), closing 'Almighty, the Wise' (power, wisdom). Verse 7: the-quran (muhkam/mutashabih), disbelief implied in 'those with deviation'. Verse 8: uttered du'a 'Our Lord, do not cause our hearts to swerve… bestow mercy' → dua-guidance. Verse 9: Day of gathering, no doubt (day-of-judgment).

3:10.notes: Verse 10: disbelievers as fuel for the Fire (hell, disbelievers, disbelief). Verse 11: Pharaoh's people named (pharaoh, punishment-of-past-nations), Allah strict in retribution (justice). Verse 12: 'Say' command (qul-statements), rounded into Hell (hell). Verse 13: two armies, Allah supports whom He wills — miracle/sign at Badr context but no named battle here.

3:14.notes: Verse 14: worldly desires contrasted with what is with Allah. Verse 15: 'Say' (qul-statements), paradise for the muttaqun (paradise, taqwa). Verse 16: uttered du'a 'Our Lord, we have believed, forgive us our sins, save us from the Fire' — this is dua-forgiveness. Verse 17: patient (patience), charitable/spending (zakat-and-charity). Believers are the addressed/described group throughout.

3:18.notes: Verse 18: Allah, angels, and people of knowledge witness tawhid (tawhid, angels, justice, knowledge, wisdom). Verse 19: Islam as the religion, People of the Book disputed out of envy (people-of-the-book, disbelief). Verse 20: 'Say' command twice (qul-statements), guidance theme ('if they submit they are guided') (guidance).

3:21.notes: Verses 21–22: killing prophets, rejecting signs → painful punishment, deeds nullified (disbelief, denial-of-revelation, justice). Verse 23: People of the Book called to Scripture, some turn away (people-of-the-book). Verse 24: false claims about the Fire (disbelief). Verse 25: gathering on Day of no doubt, each soul paid in full (day-of-judgment, reckoning, justice).

3:26.notes: Verse 26: 'Say, O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty…' — this is an uttered praise-supplication directed to Allah (qul-statements, sovereignty, power). 'In Your hand is all goodness' (provision). Verse 27: merging night into day (cosmic-bodies), bringing living from dead and dead from living (this is a power/creation image), provision without measure (provision). The 'Say, O Allah…' formula is both qul-statements and an uttered address to God — closest to dua-gratitude given 'In Your hand is all goodness' framing, but primarily sovereignty/power assertion.

3:28.notes: Verse 28: believers not to take disbelievers as protectors (believers, disbelievers), taqwa-based exception ('unless to protect yourselves') (taqwa). Verse 29: 'Say' (qul-statements), Allah knows what is in hearts (knowledge, power). Verse 30: Day when each soul finds its deeds presented (day-of-judgment), Allah warns of Himself. Verse 31: 'Say' (qul-statements), Allah forgiving and merciful (mercy). Verse 32: 'Say' (qul-statements), obey Allah and the Messenger.

3:33.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Verse 33: Adam, Noah, family of Abraham, family of Imran chosen (adam, noah, abraham, family-of-imran, prophethood-general). Verse 35: wife of Imran's vow — uttered du'a 'My Lord, I have vowed…' (dua-family-offspring). Verse 36: Mary named (mary). Verse 37: Zechariah as guardian (zechariah), provision miraculously found with Mary (provision), 'Allah provides to whom He wills' (provision, knowledge). Verse 38: Zechariah's uttered du'a 'My Lord, bestow on me good offspring' (dua-family-offspring). Verse 39: Angels call to Zechariah (angels), John announced (john). Verse 40: Allah does what He wills (power implied, but closing 'Allah does what He wills' is power). Verse 41: sign of muteness, 'praise in the evening and morning' (remembrance).

3:42.notes: Verse 42: Angels address Mary, Allah chose and purified her (mary, angels). Verse 43: Mary commanded to bow and prostrate with those who bow (prayer). Verse 44: 'These are accounts from the Unseen, which We reveal to you' — revelation of unseen narrative (the-quran, prophethood-general).

3:45.notes: Verse 45: Angels give Mary glad tidings of Jesus/Messiah (mary, jesus, angels). Verse 47: 'Allah creates whatever He wills… Be and it is' (power, divine-decree). Verse 48: Jesus taught Torah and Gospel (previous-scriptures). Verse 49: Sent to Children of Israel (children-of-israel), miracles: clay bird, healing blind and leprous, reviving dead (miracles). Verse 50: confirms Torah (previous-scriptures). Verse 51: 'Allah is my Lord and your Lord, worship Him' (tawhid).

3:52.notes: Verse 52: Jesus senses disbelief, disciples declare faith (jesus, disciples, believers, disbelief). Verse 53: Disciples utter du'a 'Our Lord, we have believed…count us among the witnesses' — uttered supplication, closest to dua-forgiveness given 'forgive' not explicit but 'count us' is petition; however the du'a here is more of submission/witness. Re-evaluating: the supplication in v53 'Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed… count us among the witnesses' is an uttered du'a of submission/guidance — tagging dua-forgiveness is borderline; using it as the closest available category. Verse 54: they plotted and Allah planned (plotting).

3:55.notes: Verse 55: Allah addresses Jesus — terminating his life, raising him, clearing him of disbelievers, followers to be superior until Day of Resurrection (jesus, disbelievers, believers, day-of-judgment). Verse 56: severe punishment for disbelievers in this world and next (hell, disbelievers). Verse 57: believers who do good get full reward (paradise, believers, justice). 'Allah does not love the unjust' (justice).

3:58.notes: Verse 58: 'This is what We recite… the Wise Reminder' (the-quran, wisdom). Verse 59: likeness of Jesus like Adam, created from dust, 'Be and he was' (jesus, adam, human-creation, power). Verse 60: 'The truth is from your Lord'. Verse 61: dispute about Jesus, call to invoke Allah's curse on liars — mutual cursing challenge with People of the Book context (people-of-the-book). Verse 62: 'There is no god but Allah' (tawhid), 'Allah is the Mighty, the Wise' (wisdom). Verse 63: Allah knows the corrupt. Verse 64: 'Say, O People of the Book…' (qul-statements, people-of-the-book), call to worship Allah alone (tawhid).

3:65.notes: Verse 65: People of the Book argue about Abraham, Torah and Gospel came after him (people-of-the-book, abraham). Verse 66: Allah knows, they do not (knowledge). Verse 67: Abraham was a hanif Muslim, not a polytheist (abraham, tawhid). Verse 68: those most deserving of Abraham are those who followed him, the Prophet, and the believers (abraham, believers).

3:69.notes: Verse 69: a party of People of the Book wants to lead believers astray (people-of-the-book, disbelief). Verse 70: 'O People of the Book, why do you reject revelations?' (people-of-the-book, disbelief). Verse 71: concealing truth (people-of-the-book). Verse 72: plot to believe then disbelieve (people-of-the-book). Verse 73: 'Say' (qul-statements), guidance is Allah's guidance (guidance), 'Allah is Bounteous and Knowing' (knowledge). Verse 74: 'He specifies His mercy for whomever He wills' (mercy).

3:75.notes: Verse 75: People of the Book — some trustworthy, some not; lying about Allah (people-of-the-book, trade-and-debt). Verse 76: fulfilling commitments, taqwa (covenant, taqwa). Verse 77: exchanging covenant of Allah for small price, no share in Hereafter, Day of Resurrection (covenant, day-of-judgment, justice). Verse 78: twisting the Scripture with tongues, attributing lies to Allah (people-of-the-book, previous-scriptures).

3:79.notes: Verse 79: No prophet would say 'be my worshipers rather than Allah's' — refutation of prophet-worship (prophethood-general, tawhid, shirk). Verse 80: nor would he command worship of angels and prophets as lords (angels, prophethood-general, shirk). 'Would he command you to infidelity after you have submitted?' — anti-shirk argument.

3:81.notes: Verse 81: Allah took covenant of the prophets to believe in and support a messenger who confirms what they have (covenant, prophethood-general, muhammad — the covenant is widely understood to reference Muhammad's prophethood). Verse 82: whoever turns away is deceitful. Verse 83: everything in the heavens and earth submits to Allah (tawhid, sovereignty).

3:84.notes: 14 labels — over ceiling. Verse 84: 'Say, we believe in Allah, and what was revealed to us, and Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Patriarchs, Moses, Jesus…' (qul-statements, abraham, ishmael, isaac, jacob, patriarchs, moses, jesus, prophethood-general, previous-scriptures, tawhid). Verses 85–91: whoever seeks other than Islam loses (disbelief), those who disbelieve after believing — curse (disbelief), those who repent afterwards (repentance, mercy). Verse 92: spend of what you cherish — 'Allah is aware' implies knowledge but not enough for label. Trim candidates: previous-scriptures (secondary to tawhid here), mercy (only verse 89 close).

3:93.notes: Verse 93: food permissible to Children of Israel, what Jacob forbade before Torah (children-of-israel, food-and-dietary), 'Say, bring the Torah' (qul-statements, previous-scriptures). Verse 95: 'Say, follow the religion of Abraham the Monotheist' (qul-statements, abraham, tawhid). Verse 96: first house at Bekka, blessed guidance (mosques-and-sacred-places). Verse 97: Station of Abraham, pilgrimage duty (hajj-and-pilgrimage, mosques-and-sacred-places, abraham). Verses 98–99: 'Say, O People of the Book…' (qul-statements, people-of-the-book).

3:100.notes: 11 labels. Verse 100: 'O you who believe' (believers), warning against following People of the Book (people-of-the-book, disbelief). Verse 101: 'How could you disbelieve when Allah's revelations are recited to you' (the-quran, guidance). Verse 102: 'O you who believe, revere Allah with due reverence' (believers, taqwa). Verse 103: hold fast to the rope of Allah, remember Allah's blessings, saved from pit of fire (remembrance, mercy, practical-ethics). Verse 104: community calling to virtue (practical-ethics). Verse 105: do not divide like those who disputed. Verses 106–107: Day when faces whitened/blackened (day-of-judgment), Allah's mercy for the righteous (mercy). Verse 108: revelations recited in truth, Allah desires no injustice (the-quran). Verse 109: to Allah belongs everything in heavens and earth (sovereignty).

3:110.notes: Verse 110: 'You are the best community… advocate moral, forbid immoral' (believers, practical-ethics), People of the Book mentioned (people-of-the-book). Verse 111: they will not harm you beyond insult. Verse 112: humiliation upon them for rejecting signs and killing prophets (people-of-the-book, disbelief). Verses 113–115: among People of the Book an upright community reciting Allah's revelations, believing in Last Day (people-of-the-book, knowledge — 'Allah knows the righteous').

3:116.notes: Verse 116: disbelievers' wealth and children avail nothing, inhabitants of Fire (disbelievers, disbelief, hell). Verse 117: parable of frosty wind destroying harvest — natural imagery as metaphor (natural-signs). Short section, 4 labels appropriate.

3:118.notes: Verse 118: 'O you who believe, do not befriend outsiders who wish you harm' (believers, disbelievers), hatred from their mouths (plotting). Verse 119: they say 'we believe' when meeting but bite fingers in rage — hypocritical behavior (hypocrisy), 'Allah knows what is within the hearts' (knowledge). Verse 120: 'if you persevere and maintain righteousness' (patience, taqwa), their schemes will not harm you.

3:121.notes: Verse 121: direct address to the Prophet leaving home to assign battle positions (muhammad, islamic-history-and-community, war-and-treaties), 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' (knowledge). Verse 122: two groups almost faltered, Allah their protector (believers, trust-in-god). Verse 123: Allah gave victory at Badr (islamic-history-and-community, power). Verses 124–125: angels reinforcing believers — 3000 and 5000 (angels, power). Verse 126: victory only from Allah the Almighty, the Wise (power). Verses 127–128: cutting off disbelievers, Allah's decree. Verse 129: 'Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful' (mercy implied — but checking: 'Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful' → mercy).

3:130.notes: Verse 130: 'O you who believe, do not feed on usury' (believers, interest, taqwa). Verse 131: guard against Fire prepared for disbelievers (hell). Verse 132: obey Allah and Messenger for mercy (mercy). Verse 133: race toward forgiveness, garden as wide as heavens and earth (paradise, repentance). Verse 134: those who give in prosperity and adversity (zakat-and-charity), restrain anger, forgive people. Verse 135: when they commit wrong, remember Allah, ask forgiveness (repentance). Verse 136: reward is forgiveness and gardens (paradise, mercy). Verse 147 context not here — closing: patience referenced in 'endurance' in next section.

3:137.notes: Verse 137: past societies destroyed, travel the earth to see fate of deniers (punishment-of-past-nations, previous-creations-destroyed). Verse 138: proclamation to humanity, guidance and advice for the righteous (guidance). Verse 139: 'Do not waver… you are superior if you are believers' (believers). Verse 140: alternation of days between people (divine-decree, islamic-history-and-community, war-and-treaties). Verse 141: Allah proves believers, eliminates disbelievers (disbelievers). Verse 142: 'do you expect to enter Paradise before Allah distinguishes those who strive and the steadfast' (day-of-judgment, patience). Verse 143: you wished for death before facing it (war-and-treaties).

3:144.notes: Verse 144: 'Muhammad is no more than a messenger' (muhammad, prophethood-general), if he dies or is killed — death reality (death-and-dying), 'Allah will reward the appreciative' (gratitude). Verse 145: no soul dies except by Allah's leave at a predetermined time (divine-decree, death-and-dying). Verse 146: many prophets fought alongside godly people, did not waver (prophethood-general, patience, war-and-treaties). Verse 147: uttered du'a 'Our Lord, forgive us our offences… strengthen our foothold, help us against the disbelieving people' (dua-forgiveness). Verse 148: Allah gave them reward of this world and Hereafter (islamic-history-and-community).

3:149.notes: Verse 149: 'O you who believe, if you obey those who disbelieve they will turn you back' (believers, disbelievers). Verse 150: 'Allah is your Master and the Best of Helpers' (trust-in-god). Verse 151: terror into hearts of disbelievers because they associate partners (shirk, hell, disbelievers). Verse 152: Allah fulfilled His promise, they faltered, He pardoned (divine-decree, mercy, islamic-history-and-community, war-and-treaties). Verses 153–154: retreat from battle, slumber sent for security, hypocritical thoughts; 'Say, everything is up to Allah' (qul-statements implied but not explicitly labeled here — actually 'Say' appears in v154 → qul-statements). Verse 155: Satan caused them to backslide (iblis, mercy — 'Allah is Forgiving and Prudent').

3:156.notes: Verse 156: 'O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieved and said of their brethren…had they stayed they would not have died' (believers, disbelievers, death-and-dying, war-and-treaties), 'Allah gives life and causes death' (death-and-dying, divine-decree). Verse 157: if killed in cause of Allah, forgiveness and mercy from Allah (mercy, war-and-treaties). Verse 158: if you die or are killed, to Allah you are gathered (death-and-dying, divine-decree).

3:159.notes: Verse 159: direct address to the Prophet — 'it is by grace from Allah that you were gentle with them' (muhammad, mercy), instruction to pardon, seek forgiveness, consult (practical-ethics), 'put your trust in Allah' (trust-in-god), 'Allah loves the trusting' (trust-in-god). Verse 160: if Allah supports you none can overcome you (power), 'let the believers put their trust in Allah' (believers, trust-in-god).

3:161.notes: Verse 161: not for a prophet to act dishonestly; dishonesty brought on Day of Resurrection (prophethood-general, day-of-judgment, reckoning). Verse 162: one who pursues Allah's approval vs. one who incurs wrath — refuge is Hell (hell, justice, disbelievers). Verse 163: different ranks with Allah (justice, reckoning).

3:164.notes: Verse 164: 'Allah has blessed the believers, as He raised up among them a messenger' (believers, muhammad, prophethood-general), recites revelations, purifies, teaches Scripture and wisdom (the-quran, guidance). Verse 165: 'Say, it is from your own selves', Allah able to do all things (knowledge — 'Allah is Able'). Verse 166: what befell on the day two armies clashed was with Allah's permission (islamic-history-and-community, war-and-treaties). Verse 167: to know the hypocrites (hypocrisy), they said 'if we knew how to fight we would have followed you' (hypocrisy, war-and-treaties).

3:168.notes: Verse 168: hypocrites said 'had they obeyed us they would not have been killed' (hypocrites), 'then avert death from yourselves' (death-and-dying). Verse 169: those killed in Allah's cause are alive at their Lord, well provided for (death-and-dying, provision, paradise — 'alive, at their Lord'). Verse 170: delighting in Allah's grace, happy for those who have not joined them (paradise, provision). Verse 171: they rejoice in grace from Allah (paradise). Verse 172: those who responded to Allah and Messenger after suffering (believers, war-and-treaties). Verse 173: 'Allah is enough for us, He is the Excellent Protector' — declaration of trust (trust-in-god). Verse 174: came back with grace, pursued what pleases Allah. Verse 175: 'That is only Satan frightening his partisans' (iblis), 'fear Me if you are believers' (believers).

3:176.notes: Verse 176: do not be saddened by those rushing into disbelief, terrible torment (disbelievers, disbelief, hell). Verse 177: those exchanging blasphemy for faith, painful torment (disbelief). Verse 178: Allah only respites disbelievers to increase in sinfulness (disbelievers, knowledge). Verse 179: Allah will not leave believers without distinguishing wicked from sincere (knowledge, taqwa), Allah chooses from messengers whom He wills (prophethood-general). Verse 180: those who withhold what Allah gave — bad for them, encircled by hoardings on Day of Resurrection (greed-and-miserliness, day-of-judgment), 'To Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth' (sovereignty).

3:181.notes: Verse 181: 'Allah has heard those who said Allah is poor and we are rich' — blasphemy (people-of-the-book, disbelief), wrongful killing of prophets (prophethood-general), 'taste the torment of the burning' (hell). Verse 182: 'Allah is not unjust' (justice). Verse 183: 'Say' (qul-statements), messengers came before with proofs (prophethood-general). Verse 184: if they accuse of lying, messengers before were accused — Psalms, Illuminating Scripture (previous-scriptures, prophethood-general). Verse 185: 'Every soul will taste death' (death-and-dying), reward on Day of Resurrection (day-of-judgment), whoever enters Paradise has won (paradise). Verse 186: tested through possessions and persons, hear abuse from People of the Book and polytheists (people-of-the-book).

3:187.notes: V187 describes the covenant Allah took from those given Scripture to proclaim it — they disregarded it (people-of-the-book, previous-scriptures, covenant, disbelief). V188 warns those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done — punishment awaits them. This is a general warning applicable to the People of the Book in context.

3:189.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Verse 189: 'To Allah belongs sovereignty of heavens and earth, Allah has power over all things' (sovereignty, power). Verse 190: creation of heavens and earth, alternation of night and day (creation-of-heavens-earth, cosmic-bodies, natural-signs). Verse 191: those who remember Allah standing/sitting/lying (remembrance), reflecting on creation, uttered du'a: 'Our Lord, You did not create this in vain, glory to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire' (praise — 'subhanaka', dua-protection). Verse 192: uttered du'a 'Our Lord, whomever You commit to the Fire, You have disgraced…' (dua-protection). Verse 193: uttered du'a 'Our Lord, forgive us our sins… make us die with the virtuous' (dua-forgiveness). Verse 194: uttered du'a 'Our Lord, give us what You have promised… do not disgrace us on Day of Resurrection' (day-of-judgment). Verse 195: Allah answers — those who emigrated, fought, killed (migration, paradise).

3:196.notes: Verse 196: do not be impressed by disbelievers' movements (disbelievers, disbelief). Verse 197: brief enjoyment, then Hell (hell). Verse 198: for those who feared their Lord — gardens beneath which rivers flow (paradise, taqwa). Short section, 5 labels appropriate.

3:199.notes: Verse 199: among People of the Book are those who believe in Allah and what was revealed, humble before Allah (people-of-the-book, humility — 'khashi'in'), do not sell revelations for cheap price, their reward with their Lord, 'Allah is swift in reckoning' (knowledge — 'swift in reckoning' maps to knowledge/justice; using knowledge as the closer attribute for 'He observes/accounts'). Single verse, 3 labels appropriate.

3:200.notes: Verse 200: 'O you who believe, be patient, advocate patience, be united, revere Allah' (believers, patience, taqwa). Short closing verse; 3 labels fully justified.

4:1.notes: Opens with 'O people!' (yā ayyuhā an-nās) → mankind. Covers creation from single soul → human-creation. Orphan property and marriage permissions → orphan-care, marriage-and-family. 'Fear your Lord' is explicit taqwa instruction. 'Allah is Watchful' → knowledge (attribute of oversight/awareness).

4:5.notes: Instructions on managing property of the immature and orphans, handing over wealth at maturity, witnessing the handover. 'Allah suffices as a Reckoner' → knowledge/oversight attribute.

4:7.notes: Verses 7–9 set out inheritance shares and warn about orphan wealth. Verse 10 warns those who consume orphan wealth will roast in a Blaze → hell. Verse 9 explicitly says 'let them fear Allah' → taqwa trigger. Knowledge: closing attribute 'Allah is Watchful over all things' implied.

4:11.notes: Detailed inheritance shares for children, parents, spouses, siblings. Closing formula 'Allah is Knowing and Judicious' → knowledge + wisdom. Verses 13–14 give paradise/hell outcomes for obedience/disobedience.

4:15.notes: Rules on lewdness (four-witness requirement, confinement), punishment for two offenders, doctrine of repentance. Verse 17 explicitly names 'repentance' as its subject → repentance. 'Allah is Redeemer, Full of Mercy' → mercy. 'Knowing and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom. Verse 18: those who die as disbelievers → disbelief. Death-at-deathbed scenario → death-and-dying.

4:19.notes: Opens with 'O you who believe' → believers. Prohibits inheriting women against their will, rules on coercing wives, dowry retrieval upon divorce → marriage-and-family, divorce, wealth-and-property-law. Verse 21 references 'a solid commitment' (mithāqan ghalīẓan) → covenant. 'Allah has placed much good' and 'Allah is Merciful towards you' → mercy.

4:22.notes: Forbidden marriage categories — stepmother, mothers, daughters, sisters, foster-mothers, mothers-in-law, stepdaughters, wives of genetic sons, two sisters simultaneously. Closing 'Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful' → mercy. Verse 24 closing 'All-Knowing, Most Wise' → knowledge + wisdom.

4:25.notes: Rules on marrying believing slave women for those who cannot afford free women → marriage-and-family, manumission-and-captives. Verse 26 God intends to guide believers in ways of those before → guidance. Verse 27 repentance theme implicit but verse 26 mentions God wants 'to redeem you' (yatūba) → repentance. 'Allah is Knowing and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom. 'Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful' → mercy.

4:29.notes: Opens 'O you who believe' → believers. Prohibits consuming wealth illicitly, requires mutual consent in trade → trade-and-debt, wealth-and-property-law. Prohibits killing yourselves → anger-and-violence. Verse 30: wrongdoer cast into Fire → hell. Verse 31: avoidance of major sins leads to honorable admission → paradise. Verse 32: 'do not covet' explicitly → envy. Closing 'Allah has knowledge of everything' → knowledge. 'Allah is Merciful' → mercy.

4:34.notes: Men as protectors/maintainers of women, righteous wives, dealing with marital discord, arbitration. Verse 35 closing 'Allah is Knowledgeable, Expert' → knowledge + wisdom.

4:36.notes: 14 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: children-and-parents (subsumed under righteous-conduct in this section), disbelievers (brief closing mention).

4:43.notes: Opens 'O you who believe' → believers. Rules on approaching prayer while drunk → prayer, intoxicants-and-gambling. Rules on janaba, tayammum, wudu conditions → ritual-purity. Closing 'Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving' → mercy.

4:44.notes: Those given a share of the Book buying error → people-of-the-book. Verse 46: Jews specifically twisting words, saying 'We hear and disobey', slandering the religion → children-of-israel, slander-and-backbiting. 'Allah cursed them for their disbelief' → disbelief. 'Allah knows your enemies' → knowledge. 'Allah sufficient as Protector' → guidance (divine attribute of protection/guidance implied); confidence medium on guidance — using knowledge instead is cleaner. Keeping guidance for the 'Allah knows your enemies, sufficient Protector/Supporter' language.

4:47.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. Verse 47: address to People of the Book, mention of Sabbath-breakers → people-of-the-book, children-of-israel. Verse 48: Allah does not forgive shirk → shirk. Verse 51: belief in superstition and evil powers (jibt and taghut) → shirk (also). Verse 52: Allah cursed them → disbelief. Verse 53: stinginess / not giving a speck → (not greed per se, rhetorical). Verse 54: they envy people for what Allah gave → envy. 'We gave the family of Abraham the Book' → abraham. Verse 55: Hell as inferno → hell. Verse 56: skins replaced in fire → hell. 'Allah is Most Powerful, Most Wise' → power + wisdom. Angels as witnesses v.166 (not this section). Verse 49: 'Allah purifies whom He wills' → mercy. Note: angels not in this section; removing. Adding mercy for purification and forgiveness theme.

4:57.notes: Short single-verse section: those who believe and do good deeds admitted to gardens forever with purified spouses → paradise, believers.

4:58.notes: Verse 58: command to return trusts and judge with justice → justice-and-witness, practical-ethics. 'Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing' → knowledge. Verse 59: 'O you who believe, obey Allah and the Messenger' → believers. Verses 60–63: hypocrites seeking Satanic legislation, shunning the Messenger → hypocrites. 'Allah knows what is in their hearts' → knowledge. Prophethood-general: obedience to the Messenger as the subject of multiple verses → prophethood-general.

4:64.notes: Verse 64: messengers sent to be obeyed; if they had sought forgiveness, would have found Allah Relenting and Merciful → prophethood-general, repentance, mercy. Verse 65: true belief requires submitting to the Messenger's judgment → prophethood-general. Verse 68: 'guided on a straight path' → guidance. Verse 69: those who obey are with prophets, sincere, martyrs, upright → paradise. Verse 70: 'That is the grace from Allah. Allah suffices as Knower' → knowledge. Verse 66 mentions 'migrate' → not tagging migration as it's hypothetical.

4:71.notes: Verse 71: 'O you who believe, take precautions, mobilize' → believers, war-and-treaties. Verses 72–73: laggard hypocrite behavior → hypocrites. Verse 74: fight in cause of Allah → war-and-treaties. Verse 75: 'Rabbanā akhrijnā…' uttered supplication by oppressed → dua-distress. Verse 76: believers vs. disbelievers, allies of the Devil → disbelievers, iblis.

4:77.notes: Verse 77: 'Restrain your hands, perform prayers, spend in charity' → prayer, zakat-and-charity. They ask why fighting was ordained → war-and-treaties. 'Say: the enjoyments of this life are brief' → qul-statements. 'Wherever you are, death will catch up with you' → death-and-dying. 'All is from Allah' → divine-decree. Verse 81: 'put your trust in Allah' (tawakkal) used but not the explicit subject → not tagging trust-in-god. Hypocrites conspiring secretly → hypocrites. 'Allah writes down what they conspire; Allah is Guardian' → knowledge.

4:82.notes: Verse 82: 'Do they not ponder the Quran?' → the-quran. 'Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found much discrepancy' → the-quran (divine origin argument). Verse 83: broadcasting news without verifying, referring to Messenger and those in authority → practical-ethics, prophethood-general. 'Were it not for Allah's blessing and mercy' → mercy.

4:84.notes: Verse 84: fight in cause of Allah, rouse the believers → war-and-treaties, believers. 'Allah is Stronger in Might' → power. Verse 85: interceding for good/evil causes → intercession. Verse 86: returning greetings with better → practical-ethics. Verse 87: 'Allah—there is no god except He. He will gather you to the Day of Resurrection' → tawhid, day-of-judgment.

4:88.notes: Verses 88–91 entirely about the hypocrites — their nature, the command not to ally with them unless they emigrate → hypocrites, migration. Verse 90: treaty-bound people exempted → covenant, war-and-treaties. 'Allah led astray… you will never find for him a way' → guidance (divine withdrawal of guidance). 'Had Allah willed, He would have given them power over you' → power.

4:92.notes: Rules on accidental killing of a believer: blood money, freeing a slave, fasting two months as repentance → anger-and-violence, manumission-and-captives, fasting, repentance. Treaty contexts → covenant, war-and-treaties. 'Allah is All-Knowing, Most Wise' → knowledge + wisdom. Verse 93: deliberate killing → hell (not tagged as its own label here, the punishment is named — tagging mercy for the overall framing). Verse 94: 'O you who believe, investigate when journeying' → believers. 'Allah is Merciful' → mercy.

4:95.notes: Those who strive in Allah's cause versus the inactive among believers — strivers preferred by a degree. Both promised good, strivers greater reward. Closing 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy.

4:97.notes: Angels taking souls of those who wronged themselves, questioning why they didn't emigrate → angels, migration, death-and-dying. Their refuge is Hell → hell. Verse 99: 'Allah may pardon them; Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving' → mercy. Verse 100: emigrating for Allah's sake → migration.

4:101.notes: Shortening prayers while travelling in fear → prayer, ritual-calendar-and-sacred-time (prayer timing). Prayer in congregation during battle (fear prayer) → prayer, war-and-treaties. Verse 102: detailed fear-prayer instructions → prayer, war-and-treaties. 'Disbelievers are your manifest enemies' → disbelievers. Verse 104 closing 'Allah is Knowledgeable and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom.

4:105.notes: Verse 105: 'We revealed the Scripture to judge between people' → the-quran, prophethood-general, justice-and-witness. Verse 106: 'ask Allah for forgiveness; Allah is Forgiver and Merciful' → mercy. Verse 107: 'do not argue for those who deceive themselves' → plotting. Verse 108: they hide from people but not Allah → knowledge. Verse 109: 'who will argue with Allah on the Day of Resurrection?' → day-of-judgment. Verse 110: seeking forgiveness → mercy. Verse 111: 'Allah is Aware and Wise' → knowledge + wisdom. Verse 112: blaming innocent person = slander → slander-and-backbiting.

4:113.notes: Verse 113: direct address to the Prophet ('towards you', 'taught you what you did not know') → muhammad. 'Allah has revealed to you the Scripture and wisdom' → the-quran. 'Allah's goodness towards you is great' → mercy. Verse 114: no good in much private counsel except advocating charity (sadaqah), kindness, reconciliation → zakat-and-charity (sadaqah), practical-ethics. 'Seeking Allah's approval' → sincerity. Verse 115: following path other than believers' leads to Hell → disbelief (not tagged; the verse is a warning but disbelief not the subject per se). Knowledge + wisdom from verse 111 carry over but verse 113 section's own closing is 'Allah's goodness towards you is great' — knowledge from 'taught you what you did not know'.

4:116.notes: Verse 116: shirk not forgiven → shirk. Verse 117: invoking females (idols) and a rebellious devil → iblis, shirk. Verses 118–120: Iblis's vow to mislead, alter creation, make promises — Satan's scheme → iblis. Verse 121: Hell for followers of Satan → hell. Verse 122: believers doing righteous deeds enter paradise → paradise. Verse 123: people of the scripture mentioned → people-of-the-book. Verse 125: 'follows the faith of Abraham the Monotheist; Allah has chosen Abraham for a friend' → abraham. Verse 125: submitting wholly to Allah → tawhid (implicit but not labelled separately — sovereignty fits better for 'to Allah belongs what is in heavens and earth' v.126). 'Who is more truthful in speech than Allah?' → sovereignty. Mercy from broader forgiveness theme in 116: 'He forgives anything less' → mercy.

4:127.notes: Verse 127: 'Say, Allah gives you a ruling about them (women)' → qul-statements. Ruling about orphaned women whose inheritance is withheld, desire to marry them, helpless children → orphan-care, marriage-and-family, justice-and-witness. 'Whatever good you do, Allah knows it' → knowledge.

4:128.notes: Rules on wife fearing maltreatment or desertion, reconciliation → marriage-and-family, divorce. Verse 128: 'if you do what is good, and practice piety (taqwa)' — explicit → taqwa. Verse 129: 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Verse 130: 'Allah is Bounteous and Wise' → wisdom (and provision implicit but not labelled).

4:131.notes: Verse 131: 'To Allah belongs everything in the heavens and the earth' → sovereignty. 'We instructed those given the Book before you, and you, to be conscious of Allah (ittaqū)' → taqwa. People of the Book explicitly addressed → people-of-the-book. 'If you refuse — to Allah belongs…' → sovereignty, disbelief. 'Allah is in no need, Praiseworthy' (Hamid) → praise (uttered formula? No — it's an attribute claim, not an uttered formula of praise). Verse 133: 'O people, if He wills He can do away with you' → mankind, power. Verse 134: 'Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing' → knowledge.

4:135.notes: Verse 135: 'O you who believe, stand firmly for justice as witnesses to Allah' → believers, justice-and-witness. Verse 136: 'believe in Allah, the Messenger, the Book sent to him, the Book sent before' → the-quran, previous-scriptures. 'Whoever rejects Allah, His angels…' → angels. '…and the Last Day, has strayed' → disbelief. Verse 137: believe-disbelieve cycle → disbelief. Verse 138: 'inform the hypocrites of painful punishment' → hypocrites. 'Allah is Aware of what you do' → knowledge. Mercy from broader context of forgiveness, but closing formula here is punishment → not adding mercy.

4:139.notes: Verse 139: hypocrites allying with disbelievers instead of believers → hypocrites, disbelievers, believers. 'All glory belongs to Allah' → sovereignty. Verse 140: hearing Allah's revelations rejected and ridiculed → mockery, the-quran. 'Allah will gather hypocrites and disbelievers into Hell' → hell. Verse 141: 'Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection' → day-of-judgment.

4:142.notes: Verses 142–143: hypocrites pray lazily, showing off, remember Allah little → hypocrites, prayer, sincerity. Verse 144: 'O you who believe, do not befriend disbelievers' → believers, disbelievers. Verse 145: hypocrites in the lowest level of the Fire → hell. Verse 146: those who repent, reform, hold fast → repentance, sincerity. 'Allah will give the believers a great reward' → mercy. Verse 147: 'What would Allah accomplish by your punishment if you have given thanks and believed' → mercy. Verse 148: Allah does not like bad public speech except when wronged → practical-ethics. 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' → knowledge. Verse 149: pardoning offences → mercy.

4:150.notes: Verses 150–151: those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, separating between Allah and messengers → disbelievers, people-of-the-book (in context), prophethood-general. 'Prepared for disbelievers a shameful punishment' → hell. Verse 152: those who believe in Allah and His messengers without distinction → prophethood-general. 'Allah is Forgiver and Merciful' → mercy. Knowledge implied through 'Aware' but not explicit in this section.

4:153.notes: 15 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: knowledge (closing formula, lower priority), wisdom (closing formula), prayer and zakat-and-charity (only mentioned briefly in v.162 closing).

4:163.notes: 20 labels — well over the 12 ceiling. This section is the major prophets-list passage; every named figure must be tagged. Trim candidates: knowledge, wisdom, power (closing formulas), angels (brief v.166), previous-scriptures (Psalms mention only), patriarchs (list mention).

4:170.notes: 14 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: knowledge and wisdom (closing formula v.170 only), sovereignty (brief mention).

4:174.notes: Verse 174: 'O people, a proof has come from your Lord; We sent down a clear light' → mankind, the-quran. Verse 175: those who believe and hold fast → believers. 'He will admit them into mercy and grace' → mercy. 'Guide them to Himself in a straight path' → guidance.

4:176.notes: Verse 176: 'Say, Allah gives you a ruling concerning the person who has neither parents nor children (kalālah)' → qul-statements, inheritance. Rules on siblings' shares → inheritance, marriage-and-family (family estate). 'Allah is Aware of everything' → knowledge.

112:3.notes: Refutation of begetting and being begotten — a direct denial of the attributes ascribed to God by polytheists and Christians; tawhid plus implicit anti-shirk.

91:1.notes: Sun, moon, day, night → cosmic-bodies; sky and earth built/spread → creation-of-heavens-earth and creation; soul proportioned → human-creation. 'Inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness' names taqwa explicitly (the word taqwāhā appears in v.8), triggering the concept label. Successful/failing tied to purifying/corrupting the soul rounds out the moral frame.

91:11.notes: Thamud named explicitly → thamud. The messenger of Allah here is Salih per unanimous tafsir → salih. The she-camel is Salih's miraculous sign → miracles. 'Denied in its pride' → arrogance (istakbara/ṭaghwā used). 'Called him a liar' → denial-of-revelation and disbelief. 'Their Lord crushed them for their sin' → punishment-of-past-nations and justice (God's just retribution named explicitly).

91:15.notes: Single verse. 'He does not fear its sequel' asserts God's absolute sovereignty and fearless authority in executing judgment — sovereignty and justice. No named figures, no du'a, no cosmology beyond implicit divine power.

94:1.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet — 'Did We not soothe your heart… lift from you your burden… raise your reputation?' All four verses are addressed to him personally, not as a Qul-command. 'Soothe your heart' and 'lift your burden' invoke God's mercy and power on his behalf. 'Raised your reputation' reflects provision/favour.

94:5.notes: Still in direct address to the Prophet. 'With hardship comes ease' (repeated twice) is the explicit subject of patience and trust in God — the section names the dynamic of hardship/ease and commands turning to devotion after work, which is a concrete trigger for both patience and trust-in-god.

94:8.notes: 'And to your Lord turn for everything' — direct address to the Prophet commanding total reliance on God (trust-in-god) and orientation toward Him in worship (prayer/devotion).

97:1.notes: The Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) is the occasion of the Qur'an's revelation, making both the-quran and ritual-calendar-and-sacred-time applicable. divine-decree is triggered by the very name 'al-Qadr' (the Decree) and the act of sending down.

97:4.notes: Angels and the Spirit descend by their Lord's leave — angels as collective subject. 'By the leave of their Lord' invokes divine-decree. The night context carries over the ritual-calendar-and-sacred-time label per straddling-section convention.

97:5.notes: A one-verse section describing the Night of Decree as peace until dawn. No named figures, no uttered du'a, no divine attributes explicitly named beyond the peaceful character of the night itself. Single-label section is appropriate given the brevity.

99:1.notes: The earth's violent shaking and disgorging its loads are classic signs-of-the-hour imagery. 'Man says, What is the matter with it?' tags mankind. God inspiring the earth tags divine-decree.

99:6.notes: People emerging in droves to be shown their works is reckoning on the Day of Judgment. 'Whoever has done an atom's weight of good will see it' makes righteous-conduct the explicit subject of the verse, meeting rule 5's concrete trigger.

99:8.notes: The evil-deeds counterpart to 99:6-7. Reckoning and Day of Judgment apply clearly. Disbelief is a borderline tag — the verse refers generically to 'evil' (sharr) rather than naming disbelief specifically; however the eschatological showing of evil deeds is the primary warning context for disbelievers throughout the Qur'an. Confidence medium on disbelief; the other two are high.

102:1.notes: Abundance/rivalry (takathur) is the explicit subject — maps to greed-and-miserliness. 'Until you visit the graveyards' invokes death-and-dying. The stern rebuke ('you will know') implies addressees are heedless/disbelieving — tagging disbelief generously. Mankind is the universal addressee.

102:5.notes: Direct vision of Jahannam (al-Jahim) is the explicit content — hell is the primary label. The conditionality ('if you knew') implies their current ignorance/heedlessness. Mankind as universal addressee.

102:8.notes: Single verse: being questioned on the Day about bliss (ni'am) — reckoning and day-of-judgment both apply. Mankind as universal addressee.

105:1.notes: The People of the Elephant (Ashab al-Fil) are the Abrahah-led army that marched on Mecca. Quraysh is tagged because this event is historically tied to the protection of the Sacred Mosque and the Meccan context; per Ibn Kathir this surah was directly addressed to the Quraysh as a reminder of God's protection of their city. 'Their plan go wrong' triggers plotting.

105:3.notes: The swarms of birds (tayr ababil) are a miraculous natural instrument of divine punishment. Natural-signs tagged for birds-in-flight as divine agents; power tagged for God's omnipotence in deploying them.

105:5.notes: Short concluding verse describing the total destruction of the army. Power and punishment-of-past-nations are the core labels; no new thematic elements introduced beyond those established in the prior sections.

106:1.notes: Section describes the security (ilaf) of Quraysh's winter and summer trade journeys — a divine provision framing. No dua uttered, no closing attribute formula.

106:3.notes: Command to worship 'the Lord of this House' — the Ka'bah — directed at Quraysh. This is a command to worship/prayer rather than an uttered supplication.

106:4.notes: God feeding them against hunger = provision; securing them against fear = power/protection. Both are divine-attribute claims substantiated by the verse content. 'Mercy' applies as the benevolent care framing these gifts to Quraysh.

107:1.notes: Verse 1 denies the religion (dīn) — triggers disbelief and denial-of-revelation. Verses 2–3 depict mistreatment of the orphan and failure to feed the poor — orphan-care and corruption-on-earth are both concretely triggered.

107:4.notes: Woe to praying hypocrites who are heedless and performative — prayer and hypocrisy are explicit. Verse 6 'put on the appearance' is the concrete trigger for sincerity (its absence) per rule 5.

107:7.notes: Withholding basic assistance (al-māʿūn) is the explicit trigger for greed-and-miserliness and zakat-and-charity (refusal to give). Practical-ethics applies as the section depicts a failure of ordinary social assistance.

111:1.notes: Abu Lahab is a named Qurayshi opponent; the section condemns him and declares his fate in a Flaming Fire. 'His wealth did not avail him' triggers greed-and-miserliness. punishment-of-past-nations is borderline here since Abu Lahab is a contemporary, not a past nation — trim candidate if reviewer prefers.

111:4.notes: Abu Lahab's wife as firewood carrier heading to the same punishment; marriage-and-family is tagged because she is explicitly introduced as his wife and her fate is tied to that relationship.

111:5.notes: Single verse describing the rope of thorns around her neck as part of her punishment in the Fire. Minimal thematic content beyond the punishment image.

113:1.notes: Opens with 'Qul' → qul-statements. 'I take refuge' is an uttered supplication → dua-protection. 'Lord of Daybreak' asserts sovereignty and creation.

113:3.notes: Continuation of the uttered refuge supplication → dua-protection. 'Those who practice sorcery' (al-naffathat fil-uqad) → sorcery. 'The darkness as it gathers' references the night/dark sky → cosmic-bodies.
