113:5.notes: Still within the uttered supplication for refuge → dua-protection. 'Evil of an envious when he envies' explicitly names envy → envy.

114:1.notes: Opens with 'Say' (qul) → qul-statements. Addresses the Lord/King/God of mankind → mankind, sovereignty, tawhid. The entire surah is a uttered supplication for refuge → dua-protection.

114:4.notes: The sneaky whisperer is the Shaytan/Iblis figure. The supplication for refuge continues from 114:1 — straddling rule applies, dua-protection tagged on both. Whispers into hearts of people → mankind.

114:6.notes: Clarifies that the whisperer is from among jinn and people → jinn and mankind. Short closing verse; no new divine attributes or du'a uttered here beyond what was established in prior sections.

62:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with glorification (tasbih) of Allah with His names al-Malik, al-Quddus, al-Aziz, al-Hakim — sovereignty, power, wisdom all named explicitly, and the act of glorification triggers 'praise'. Verses 2–4 describe the sending of Muhammad to the unlettered, teaching Scripture and wisdom — prophethood-general and muhammad (substantively about him and his mission, not merely a qul). Verse 5 addresses those entrusted with the Torah who failed it — people-of-the-book, previous-scriptures, denial-of-revelation, disbelief. 'Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people' → guidance (by its denial). 12 labels — at the ceiling, all independently justified.

62:6.notes: Two explicit 'Say:' (qul) commands → qul-statements. Addressed to 'those who follow Judaism' → people-of-the-book. Death as the inescapable reality — verses 7–8 → death-and-dying. 'Knower of the Invisible and the Visible' → knowledge. 'He will inform you of what you used to do' → reckoning. Their failure and cowardice about death linked to their transgressions → disbelief.

62:9.notes: Opens with 'O you who believe' → believers. Command to hasten to Friday prayer → prayer, ritual-calendar-and-sacred-time (Jumu'ah as a sacred time marker). 'Hasten to the remembrance of Allah' and 'remember Allah much' → remembrance. 'Drop all business' and 'seek Allah's bounty' address commerce and livelihood → trade-and-debt, provision.

62:11.notes: Contains 'Say:' (qul) → qul-statements. Section describes the companions leaving the Prophet standing during the sermon — direct reference to Muhammad personally (not just a recitation command), so muhammad is also warranted. 'Business or entertainment' → trade-and-debt. 'Allah is the Best of providers' → provision. The implicit contrast between worldly distraction and remembrance of Allah supports remembrance, though it is not the explicit subject — included because 'remember Allah much' in the preceding section straddles here and the contrast is the section's entire point.

63:1.notes: Muhammad is tagged because the section is directly addressed to him ('When the hypocrites come to you') and is substantively about his encounter with the hypocrites. Knowledge tagged for 'Allah knows' and 'Allah bears witness'. Disbelief tagged for verse 3 ('they believed, then disbelieved; their hearts were sealed'). Oaths-and-vows tagged for 'they treat their oaths as a cover'.

63:5.notes: Arrogance explicitly named: 'turning away arrogantly' (mustakbirun). Guidance tagged for 'Allah does not guide the sinful people'. Sovereignty tagged for 'To Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth' and 'power belongs to Allah'. Zakat-and-charity tagged for the hypocrites' instruction not to spend on those with the Messenger. Plotting tagged for the hypocrites' coordinated scheme to withhold spending and their threat to expel believers from Medina. Believers tagged for verse 8 referencing 'the believers' directly.

63:9.notes: Believers addressed directly with 'O you who believe'. Remembrance (dhikr) is the explicit subject: 'do not let your possessions or children distract you from the remembrance of Allah'. Children-and-parents tagged for 'nor your children'. Death-and-dying tagged for the deathbed scenario in verse 10. Divine-decree tagged for the implied appointed time (ajal). Dua-distress tagged because verse 10 contains an uttered supplication: 'My Lord (Rabbi), if only You would delay me for a short while'—a spoken du'a in distress at the approach of death. Zakat-and-charity tagged for 'give from what We have provided for you' and 'so that I may be charitable'.

63:11.notes: Divine-decree is the explicit subject: 'Allah will not delay a soul when its time (ajalaha) has come'. Knowledge tagged for the closing formula 'Allah is Informed (Khabir) of what you do'. Death-and-dying tagged for the appointed term of the soul.

73:1.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('O you Enwrapped one', 'We are about to give you a heavy message', 'remember the Name of your Lord') justifies `muhammad`. Night vigil / qiyam al-layl instructions → `prayer`. Rhythmic recitation of the Quran → `the-quran`. 'Remember the Name of your Lord' → `remembrance`. 'There is no god but He' → `tawhid`. 'Take Him as a Trustee' → `trust-in-god`. 'Lord of the East and the West' invokes cosmic orientation; borderline for `cosmic-bodies` but East/West as celestial markers supports it.

73:10.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('endure patiently what they say, and withdraw from them') → `muhammad`. 'Endure patiently' explicitly names the concept → `patience`. 'Those who deny the truth' → `disbelievers`. 'Shackles, a Fierce Fire, food that chokes, painful punishment' → `hell`. 'On the Day when the earth and mountains tremble' → `day-of-judgment`. The warning about the deniers receiving punishment echoes the punished-nations motif; however the punishment here is eschatological rather than historical, so `punishment-of-past-nations` is borderline — omitted in favour of keeping the label clean.

73:15.notes: Pharaoh explicitly named → `pharaoh`. The sending of a messenger to both this community and Pharaoh → `prophethood-general` and `muhammad` (the Prophet addressed as the messenger sent). Pharaoh's defiance and seizure → `punishment-of-past-nations`. The Day turning children grey-haired, heaven shattering → `day-of-judgment`. 'Persist in unbelief' → `disbelief`. 'Whoever wills, let him take a path to his Lord' → `guidance`.

73:20.notes: Direct address to the Prophet and the believers ('you … along with a group of those with you') → `muhammad` and `believers`. 'Observe the prayers' → `prayer`. 'Give regular charity' / 'lend Allah a generous loan' → `zakat-and-charity`. 'Read of the Quran what is possible' → `the-quran`. 'Allah knows … He has pardoned you' → `knowledge` (divine knowledge of human capacity) and `mercy` (pardoning, 'Forgiving and Merciful'). 'He has pardoned you' / 'seek Allah's forgiveness' → `repentance` (turning back; acceptance of the repentant). 'Seek Allah's forgiveness … Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' is an uttered imperative to seek forgiveness, but 'istaghfiru' is a command rather than a quoted supplication — however it functions as an urging that borders on uttered du'a in community context; tagged `dua-forgiveness` at medium-confidence note. 'Others fighting in Allah's cause' → `war-and-treaties`. 10 labels — within ceiling.

81:1.notes: Verses 1–14 enumerate the cataclysmic signs of the Hour (sun rolled up, stars dimmed, mountains set in motion, oceans set aflame → signs-of-the-hour + cosmic-bodies + natural-signs), followed by the gathering and pairing of souls, the publicly opened records, and the bringing near of Fire and Paradise (reckoning, hell, paradise, resurrection). The interrogation of the girl buried alive implies divine justice (justice). Day-of-judgment captures the overall setting.

81:15.notes: Oath by the receding stars and night/dawn (cosmic-bodies) introduces the section. 'Noble messenger endowed with power, eminent with the Lord of the Throne, obeyed and honest' refers to Gabriel (angels), affirming the Qur'an's divine origin (the-quran, prophethood-general). 'Your friend is not possessed' directly addresses the audience about Muhammad (muhammad — substantive defence of his person). 'He saw him on the luminous horizon' describes the vision of Gabriel. Rebuttal of the accusation that it is a devil's word = denial-of-revelation. 'Lord of the Throne' = sovereignty.

81:27.notes: Two-verse section: the Qur'an is described as a Reminder to all mankind (the-quran, mankind) for whoever wills to go straight (guidance — God as source of guidance is the explicit subject of the verse).

81:29.notes: Single verse asserting that human will is subordinate to Allah's will, and attributing lordship to 'the Lord of the Worlds' — divine decree (divine-decree), absolute sovereignty (sovereignty), and the implicit oneness/supremacy of God (tawhid).

85:1.notes: The oath by the sky/constellations triggers cosmic-bodies. The Promised Day is the Day of Judgment. The People of the Trench narrative involves persecution of believers by disbelievers. 'Allah the Almighty, the Praiseworthy' and 'sovereignty of the heavens and earth' and 'Allah is witness over everything' invoke power, sovereignty, and knowledge. The trench episode is a punishment-of-past-nations type warning. The burning of believers in the trench is anger-and-violence.

85:10.notes: Verse 10 contrasts those who tempt believers and do not repent (hell) with those who believe and do righteous deeds (paradise). Repentance is named explicitly ('then do not repent'). Righteous deeds ('amilu al-salihat') is explicitly named as the trigger for the paradise reward.

85:12.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Verse 12 asserts God's severe power (power). Verse 13 'begins and repeats' touches creation/resurrection but most directly divine omnipotence (power, divine-decree). Verse 14 'Forgiving, the Loving' → mercy. Verse 15 'Possessor of the Glorious Throne' → sovereignty. Verse 16 'Doer of whatever He wills' → power, divine-decree. Verses 17-18 name Pharaoh and Thamud → pharaoh, thamud, punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 19 'those who disbelieve are in denial' → disbelievers, denial-of-revelation. Verse 20 'Allah encloses them' → knowledge/sovereignty. Verse 21 'Glorious Quran' → the-quran. Trim candidates if needed: creation (only implicit in 'begins and repeats'), knowledge (subsumed by sovereignty in v20 context).

85:22.notes: Single verse: 'In a Preserved Tablet' (lawh mahfuz). This directly references the preservation of the Quran in the Preserved Tablet (the-quran) and the concept of divine decree/predestination (divine-decree).

90:1.notes: Verse 1–2 swear by Mecca and address the Prophet directly ('you are a resident'), warranting `muhammad`. Verse 3 ('a father and what he fathered') alludes to Adam or Abraham per tafsir — not naming either explicitly, so no person label applied. Verse 4 'We created man in distress' → `human-creation` and `mankind`. Verse 5 'Does he think no one has power over him?' → `power` / `sovereignty`.

90:6.notes: Verse 6 boasts of spending wealth (arrogance/miserliness framing) → `greed-and-miserliness`. Verse 7 'Does he think no one sees him?' → `knowledge` (God's all-seeing). Verses 8–9 enumerate God's gifts of eyes, tongue, lips → `human-creation`. Verse 10 'We showed him the two ways' → `guidance`.

90:11.notes: Verse 13 'freeing of a slave' → `manumission-and-captives`. Verse 14–16 feeding orphan and destitute → `orphan-care` and `zakat-and-charity`. Verse 17 explicitly names patience (sabr) → `patience`; also names kindness/mercy as mutual counsel → `righteous-conduct`. Verse 17 'those who believe' → `believers`. Verse 18 'people of happiness' is the reward for the above, implying paradise but not describing it explicitly — not tagging `paradise`. Verse 19 'those who defy Our revelations' → `disbelievers` and `disbelief`. Verse 19 'people of misery' anticipates the fire closing in the next verse; `hell` carried here as straddling (rule 1) since verse 20 is the immediate consequence of verse 19's judgment.

90:20.notes: Single verse: 'Upon them is a padlocked Fire' → `hell`. The 'them' refers to the disbelievers from verse 19 → `disbelievers` carried over per straddling rule.

92:1.notes: Night and day are cosmic/natural oath-signs; 'He who created the male and the female' is an invocation of human creation and God as Creator. 'Your endeavors are diverse' is the transitional moral framing — no explicit concept label triggered.

92:5.notes: Giving + righteousness (taqwa named explicitly: 'is righteous / ittaqa') triggers both `zakat-and-charity` and `taqwa`. Stinginess ('bakhl') triggers `greed-and-miserliness`. Denying goodness triggers `disbelief`. God easing the path is `divine-decree`.

92:12.notes: 'It is upon Us to guide' → `guidance`. 'To Us belong the Last and the First' → `sovereignty`. 'Fierce Blaze' → `hell`. 'He who denies and turns away' → `disbelief`. 'The devout (al-atqa)' → `taqwa` explicitly named. 'Gives his money to become pure' → `zakat-and-charity`. 'Seeking no favor in return / only seeking the acceptance of his Lord' → `sincerity` explicitly modeled. 'None will burn in it except the very wicked' implies reckoning-based sorting → `reckoning`.

92:21.notes: Single verse: 'And he will be satisfied' — the reward of the devout, implying entry into divine pleasure/paradise. Short section; single label is appropriate per the rules.

93:1.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet throughout ('Your Lord did not abandon you', 'your Lord will give you'). Oath by morning light and settling night → cosmic-bodies. 'Guided you' and 'give you' invoke guidance and provision. 'The Hereafter is better for you' points to paradise/eschatological reward.

93:6.notes: Sustained direct address to the Prophet recounting three divine favors: sheltering him as an orphan (→ orphan-care, muhammad), guiding him when wandering (→ guidance), and enriching him when in need (→ provision).

93:9.notes: Direct second-person commands to the Prophet: do not oppress the orphan, do not rebuff the petitioner. Orphan-care is explicit. Practical-ethics covers the general moral instruction on social conduct. Muhammad tagged for direct second-person address.

93:11.notes: Direct address to the Prophet: 'proclaim the blessings of your Lord.' Gratitude tagged because the command is to publicly acknowledge/thank God for His blessings (shukr-flavored). The-quran considered: proclaiming God's blessings is often read as referring to the Qur'anic message itself (per Ibn Kathir), making it borderline; tagged medium confidence. Could also support praise but the command is to proclaim blessings, not to utter a praise formula.

95:1.notes: The fig and olive are sworn by as natural signs; Mount Sinai is associated with Moses and is a sacred place; 'this safe land' refers to Mecca (sacred mosque region). Moses tagged because Mount Sinai is his revelatory site per tafsir — borderline under rule 5 but defensible via rule 3 (named place strongly associated with a named figure). Confidence medium on moses tag specifically.

95:4.notes: Explicitly about the creation of man in the best form and his reduction — core human-creation content. 'Man' here is universal, warranting mankind tag.

95:6.notes: Verse 6 contrasts believers who do righteous deeds with their unbounded reward (paradise implied). Verse 7 directly names rejection of the religion (din), triggering disbelief and day-of-judgment labels. 'Righteous deeds' explicitly named as the subject, satisfying rule 5 trigger for righteous-conduct.

95:8.notes: 'Wisest of the wise' (ahkam al-hakimin) invokes wisdom and justice as divine attributes. In context of the surah's argument about judgment and accountability, reckoning is substantively implied by 'al-din' carried forward from verse 7.

100:1.notes: The opening oath-images (racing horses, sparks, dawn raid) are vivid oath-by-creation formulas. 'natural-signs' captures the created phenomena invoked; 'war-and-treaties' captures the raiding/warfare imagery. Some commentators read these as purely metaphorical oath-vehicles rather than literal battle descriptions, hence medium confidence on 'war-and-treaties'.

100:6.notes: 'Indeed, the human being is ungrateful to his Lord' — al-insan (mankind) is the explicit subject; ingratitude/kanud is the named fault. 'Fierce in his love of wealth' triggers 'greed-and-miserliness'. The ingratitude toward the Lord also touches 'disbelief' in the sense of kufr al-ni'mah (denial of blessing), though 'disbelief' in the full theological sense is borderline — tagging it because the Arabic 'kanud' carries the connotation of denial/rejection.

100:9.notes: 'When the contents of the graves are scattered around' = resurrection; 'contents of the hearts are obtained' = the reckoning of deeds and intentions. All three eschatology labels are concretely triggered.

100:11.notes: 'Their Lord, on that Day, is fully informed of them' — 'that Day' anchors 'day-of-judgment'; 'fully informed' (khabir) is a direct invocation of the divine attribute of complete knowledge.

101:1.notes: The surah opens with the rhetorical triple — 'The Shocker / What is the Shocker / What will explain to you what the Shocker is?' — which is a characteristic Qur'anic build-up naming the Day of Judgment without yet describing it. No named figures, no divine attributes, no du'a.

101:4.notes: 'The people will be like scattered moths' triggers mankind (universal humanity as subject on the Day). Mountains like tufted wool is a cosmic sign-of-the-Hour image; it also carries natural-signs (earthly matter transformed). Scales heavy/light is the reckoning. Pleasant life = paradise (implicit reward); the Abyss (Hawiyah) = hell.

101:10.notes: Single rhetorical question — 'Do you know what it is?' — referring back to the Abyss (Hawiyah). No new content beyond anticipation of the next verse's answer. Kept to two labels; the section has no independent thematic content beyond bridging toward the hell description.

101:11.notes: Single verse: 'A Raging Fire.' — the answer to the rhetorical question of 101:10. Minimal thematic content; hell is the only defensible label. Single-label section is appropriate for a one-verse section of this type per rule 2.

104:1.notes: Verse 1 names the humazah/lumazah (slanderer/backbiter) → slander-and-backbiting. Verses 2–3 describe hoarding wealth and false confidence in it → greed-and-miserliness. The subject is a specific type of wrongdoer/disbeliever addressed in third person.

104:4.notes: The Crusher (al-Hutamah) is introduced as the punishment awaiting the slanderer/hoarder. Clear eschatological warning about being thrown into hell.

104:6.notes: Allah's kindled Fire that reaches the hearts — a vivid description of Jahannam's punishment. 'Allah's Fire' invokes God's power/sovereignty over punishment.

104:9.notes: Brief closing verse describing the columns that enclose them in the Fire — continuation of the hell description. Single label is appropriate for this very short closing verse.

98:1.notes: The 'Clear Evidence' (al-bayyinah) is the messenger reciting purified scripts — this is prophethood and the Qur'an as subject. People of the Book and Polytheists are explicitly named. Muhammad is tagged because the section is substantively about his role as the messenger bearing the clear evidence, not merely a 'Say:' command.

98:5.notes: 'Devoting their faith to Him alone' (mukhlisina) is an explicit trigger for both tawhid and sincerity. Prayer and zakat are explicitly named. The verse addresses what the People of the Book and Polytheists were commanded, so both group labels apply as contextual referents carried over from the preceding section.

98:6.notes: 'Those who believe and lead a righteous life' is an explicit trigger for righteous-conduct. Hell and Paradise are both described. Believers are the contrasting group explicitly referenced in verse 7.

98:8.notes: 'Gardens of Eternity beneath which rivers flow' is paradise. 'Allah is pleased with them' invokes divine mercy/pleasure. 'Whoever fears His Lord' is an explicit trigger for taqwa. Note: the section list included a duplicate/malformed entry '98:8 (verses 8–7)' which appears to be a data error; labeled the valid 98:8 entry covering verse 8 only.

86:1.notes: The oath is by the sky and the piercing star — cosmic-bodies is primary. No divine attributes named explicitly; no people, no du'a.

86:4.notes: The guardian/protector over every soul alludes to the recording angels. Human creation from gushing liquid is an explicit human-creation trigger. 'Let man consider' is a universal address to mankind.

86:8.notes: God's ability to return man = power + resurrection. 'The Day when secrets are disclosed' = day-of-judgment + reckoning. Man having no strength or supporter on that Day reinforces reckoning.

86:11.notes: Oaths by the sky (cosmic-bodies) and the cracking earth (natural-signs). 'It is a Decisive Word / no joke' refers to the Qur'an as the subject — the-quran label applies.

86:15.notes: The section explicitly names scheming/plotting (makr) by them and God's counter-plan — plotting label is directly triggered. The subject is the disbelievers.

86:17.notes: Addressed to the Prophet with an imperative directive ('give the blasphemers respite'). This is a command form directed at the Prophet, functionally parallel to qul-statements; confidence medium because the imperative here is 'famahhil' rather than strictly 'qul'. Disbelievers are named explicitly (al-kafirin).

87:1.notes: Opening command 'Praise the Name of your Lord, the Most High' is an uttered/commanded praise formula — tagging `praise` per §5.6b since the section itself is a glorification utterance. Creation, guidance, and provision of pasture are explicit. Natural signs: the pasture produced and turned to debris.

87:6.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('We will make you read… We will ease you') warrants `muhammad`. Revelation/Qur'an preservation is the subject (`the-quran`). 'He knows what is declared and what is hidden' → `knowledge`. 'Ease you into the Easy Way' → `guidance`. 'Except what Allah wills' → `divine-decree`. 'So remind' → `remembrance`.

87:10.notes: 'The reverent will remember' — 'reverent/those who fear' implies taqwa explicitly named as the dividing criterion. 'The wretched will avoid it… enter the Gigantic Fire… neither die nor live' → `hell`. Disbelievers as the wretched who reject the reminder → `disbelievers`.

87:14.notes: 'Purifies himself' → `righteous-conduct` (explicit subject of the exhortation). 'Mentions the name of his Lord, and prays' → `prayer` and `remembrance`. 'The Hereafter is better' → `day-of-judgment`. 'This is in the former scriptures' → `previous-scriptures`.

87:19.notes: Single verse naming Abraham and Moses in the context of their scriptures. Both prophets tagged per rule 3. `previous-scriptures` applies directly.

88:1.notes: Section opens with 'the overwhelming' (al-ghashiyah) — a name for the Day of Judgment — then describes the fate of those roasting in fire with thorns for food. Disbelievers implied as the shamed faces.

88:8.notes: Contrasting section describing joyful faces in a lofty Garden — classic paradise description. Believers implied as those satisfied with their endeavor.

88:17.notes: Camels and earth are natural-signs; sky raised and mountains installed point to creation-of-heavens-earth and God's power as Creator.

88:21.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('You are only a reminder', 'You have no control over them') — qualifies as direct address to Muhammad. Prophethood-general covers the reminder-messenger role. Disbelief tagged for 'whoever turns away and disbelieves'. Remembrance (dhikr) triggered by 'so remind' (fadhakkir).

88:24.notes: 'The greatest punishment' for disbelievers; 'to Us is their return' and 'upon Us rests their reckoning' — reckoning and justice explicitly named. Disbelievers carried over from 88:23 context of those who turn away and disbelieve.

89:1.notes: Oath by the daybreak, ten nights, even and odd, and the receding night. 'Ten nights' is understood by most tafsir as the first ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah (or Muharram), linking to sacred time. No named figures, no du'a, no eschatology.

89:5.notes: 'Ad (Iram of the pillars), Thamud (carvers of rocks), and Pharaoh are all explicitly named. 'Spread much corruption therein' — concrete trigger for corruption-on-earth. 'Your Lord poured down upon them a scourge of punishment' — divine justice and power asserted. 'Your Lord is on the lookout' — divine knowledge/watchfulness.

89:15.notes: The section addresses 'man' broadly — mankind in universal terms. Explicit mention of not honoring the orphan (orphan-care trigger), not urging feeding of the poor (zakat-and-charity/practical-ethics trigger), devouring inheritance with greed (wealth-and-property-law), and loving wealth with immense love (greed-and-miserliness concrete trigger).

89:21.notes: Earth is leveled and crushed (resurrection/day-of-judgment imagery). The Lord comes with angels row after row (angels). Hell is brought forward (hell). Man remembers too late and regrets (reckoning). None will punish or shackle as He does on that Day (day-of-judgment, power implied but punishment framing fits reckoning/day-of-judgment).

89:27.notes: The tranquil soul is addressed and invited to return to the Lord pleased and accepted, then to enter among His servants — implicitly the righteous/believers. 'Enter among My servants' signals nearness and divine acceptance (nearness-and-response). Verse 30 is a separate section; paradise is only implicit here via 'enter among My servants,' but the address of the contented soul and its return to the Lord is the dominant theme.

89:30.notes: Single verse: 'Enter My Paradise.' Direct and explicit description of paradise. Short section with one clear label.

96:1.notes: The command 'Read' (iqra') is the first revelation event, marking prophethood; 'taught by the pen / taught man what he never knew' invokes divine knowledge and language/revelation. 'Created man from a clot' triggers human-creation and creation. God's generosity ('Most Generous') is a divine-attribute but maps most naturally to 'provision' or 'knowledge' — tagging 'knowledge' as the primary attribute since teaching is the substance. No uttered du'a, no named figures.

96:6.notes: 'Man oversteps all bounds when he considers himself exempt' is an explicit arrogance trigger (the concept of transgression/self-sufficiency is the section's subject). 'To your Lord is the return' invokes the Day of Judgment. The self-exempting posture is linked to disbelief/denial.

96:9.notes: 'A servant when he prays' is an explicit prayer trigger. 'Advocates righteousness' — the Arabic is taqwa (أَمَرَ بِٱلتَّقْوَىٰ), making taqwa an explicit trigger per rule 5. 'Upon guidance' explicitly names guidance. 'Disbelieved and turned away' = disbelief and denial-of-revelation. 'Allah sees' = divine knowledge. The antagonist preventing prayer is the subject of the wider Abu Jahl passage per tafsir, but no named figure appears in the translation.

96:15.notes: 'We will drag him by the forelock' and 'We will call the Guards (Zabāniyah)' — the Zabāniyah are the angels/keepers of hell, so 'angels' and 'hell' both apply. Arrogance and disbelief carry over from the prior section's subject (the one who did not desist). 'Punishment-of-past-nations' is borderline here — this is a direct threat rather than a historical warning; may trim. Confidence medium on 'punishment-of-past-nations' specifically.

96:19.notes: 'Do not obey him; but kneel down and come near' — direct second-person command to the Prophet (direct address), making 'muhammad' applicable per §5.2. 'Kneel down' (prostrate) is a prayer command. 'Come near' (nearness-and-response could apply but the command is directed at the worshipper approaching God, not asserting the divine attribute directly — tagging 'practical-ethics' for the ethical conduct instruction instead). The sajdah marker (۩) confirms the prostration theme.

103:1.notes: The oath 'By Time' and the declaration that the human being is in loss establish a universal address to humanity and an eschatological verdict. No named figure, no du'a, no divine attribute closing formula — kept minimal accordingly.

103:3.notes: The exception clause names believers explicitly ('those who believe'), names righteous deeds ('do good works' — a concrete trigger for righteous-conduct), and names patience ('recommend patience') — a concrete trigger for the patience label per rule 5. Truth-enjoining is covered under righteous-conduct.

108:1.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('We have given you…', 'pray to your Lord') justifies `muhammad`. 'Given you plenty' invokes `provision`. 'Pray to your Lord and sacrifice' is a command for prayer/ritual, justifying `prayer`. Al-Kawthar is understood as divine gift/abundance, reinforcing `provision`. `praise` is not strictly uttered here but `prayer` covers the worship command.

108:3.notes: Verse 3 refers to the one who hates the Prophet — per Ibn Kathir this is identified as a Qurayshi opponent (often 'As ibn Wa'il) who mocked the Prophet as 'cut off' (abtar) after the death of his sons. `mockery` applies as the enemy's action being referenced. `quraysh` tagged per the specific historical identity of the antagonist. `disbelievers` tagged as the opponent is a disbeliever. Confidence medium because the specific identity relies on tafsir rather than the surface text alone.

109:1.notes: Opens with qul and directly addresses the disbelievers. The declaration of not worshipping what they worship is a tawhid assertion and a rejection of shirk.

109:3.notes: Continuation of the mutual disavowal — no qul in this section. The repeated negation of shared worship continues the tawhid/shirk theme.

109:6.notes: Section 109:6 appears twice in the breaks list — treated as one section covering only verse 6. 'To you your religion and to me my religion' is the closing declaration of religious distinctness, anchored in tawhid. No qul in this verse.

110:1.notes: The 'conquest' refers to the Fath Makkah per Ibn Kathir; 'people entering the religion in multitudes' is a universal address (mankind) and a historical milestone (islamic-history-and-community). God's victory (nasr) implies sovereignty; mass entry into the faith implies guidance.

110:3.notes: Section 110:3 appears twice in the input (verses 3–2 and 3–3); the second entry carries the actual verse text and is the operative section. 'Celebrate the praise of your Lord' (fasabbih bihamdi rabbika) → praise. 'Seek His forgiveness' → repentance (tawbah explicitly named via istighfar). 'He is the Accepter of Repentance' (Tawwāb) → mercy (the Tawwāb name clusters under mercy). The command is directed to the Prophet in the second person ('your Lord') → muhammad. The empty 110:3 (verses 3–2) shares the same section ID and is subsumed here.

5:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with 'O you who believe' (yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū). Covers fulfilling commitments/covenants, lawful livestock, prohibition of hunting during pilgrim sanctity, sacrosanctity of the Sacred Month and Sacred House, and cooperation in righteousness. 'Allah decrees whatever He wills' → divine-decree. 'Allah is severe in punishment' → power (as justice/retributive power). taqwa is explicitly named ('fear Allah').

5:3.notes: Lists prohibited foods in detail. 'Today I have perfected your religion' → marks completion of the Qur'anic revelation/religion (the-quran). Prohibition of animals sacrificed on altars → shirk. 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. 'Today those who disbelieve have despaired' → disbelievers. The divine completion of favor and approval of Islam → divine-decree.

5:4.notes: Opens with 'They ask you… Say' → qul-statements. Covers lawfulness of game, food of People of the Book, and marriage to chaste women from the Book. 'Allah is Swift in reckoning' → reckoning (and implicitly knowledge). Verse 5 includes 'whoever rejects faith his work is in vain' → disbelief. Marriage rules with dowry and chastity conditions → marriage-and-family + chastity-and-boundaries.

5:6.notes: Verse 6 details wudu and tayammum → ritual-purity, clearly tied to prayer. 'Allah intends to complete His blessing upon you that you may be thankful' → gratitude (shukr explicitly invoked as purpose). Verse 7 calls on believers to remember Allah's covenant and that 'Allah knows what the hearts contain' → knowledge. Covenant ('He covenanted with you') → covenant.

5:8.notes: Opens with 'O you who believe!' Justice and fair testimony command. 'That is nearer to piety' → taqwa explicitly named. 'Allah is informed of what you do' → knowledge. Verse 9: believers who work righteousness have forgiveness and great reward → paradise (implied). Verse 10: disbelievers who reject revelations → hell + disbelief + denial-of-revelation.

5:11.notes: 'O you who believe! Remember Allah's blessings when He restrained their hands from you' → nearness-and-response (God responding to protect). 'In Allah let the believers put their trust' → trust-in-god explicitly named. God's restraining enemy hands → power.

5:12.notes: Covenant with Children of Israel, twelve chiefs, conditions of prayer and zakat and believing in messengers. 'I will remit your sins and admit you into Gardens' → paradise. 'Whoever disbelieves afterwards has strayed' → disbelief. Twisting words and breaking pledge → covered by covenant breach. Verse 13: hardened hearts, twisting scripture. Verse 14: Christians' broken pledge, enmity until Day of Resurrection → people-of-the-book. 'Allah loves the doers of good' → implies guidance.

5:15.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: mankind (not explicitly 'O mankind' but 'everyone on earth' in v17 is universal); tawhid could be merged under the refutation context. Verses 15–19: address to People of the Book, the Qur'an as light and clear Book (the-quran, previous-scriptures, guidance, prophethood-general). Verse 17: refutation of 'Allah is the Christ son of Mary' → jesus, mary, disbelief, tawhid, sovereignty ('To Allah belongs the sovereignty…'), power ('He creates whatever He wills'). Verse 18: Jews and Christians claiming to be children of Allah, 'Say' → qul-statements. Verse 19: 'O People of the Book' again, 'Allah is Capable of everything' → power. Direct qul in verse 17 and 18.

5:20.notes: Moses addressing his people, reminding them of Allah's blessings, prophets placed among them, commanding entry into the Holy Land. The people refuse and Moses prays: 'My Lord! I have control only over myself and my brother, so separate between us and between the wicked people' (verse 25) → uttered du'a → dua-distress (calling on God in face of the people's rebellion/confrontation). God's response — forbidden for forty years — → divine-decree. 'Put your trust in Allah if you are believers' (verse 23) → trust-in-god.

5:27.notes: Story of Adam's two sons (Cain and Abel) — the first murder. 'Allah accepts only from the righteous' → taqwa (explicitly named, 'muttaqin'). The killing → anger-and-violence. 'You will bear among the inmates of the Fire' → hell. Verse 31: regret and repentance imagery. Verse 32: ordained for Children of Israel — whoever kills a soul is as if he killed all mankind → children-of-israel, justice-and-witness. Verse 33: punishment for those who spread corruption on earth → corruption-on-earth, war-and-treaties (fighting Allah and His Messenger). Verse 34: 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy; repentance before apprehension → repentance.

5:35.notes: 'O you who believe! Be conscious of Allah' → taqwa explicitly named. 'Strive in His cause' (jihad). Verse 36: disbelievers cannot ransom themselves from 'the torment of the Day of Resurrection' → disbelievers, day-of-judgment. Verse 37: 'They want to leave the Fire but they will not' → hell.

5:38.notes: Theft punishment — cutting of hands → wealth-and-property-law, justice-and-witness (legal judgment). 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' → power (Mighty/Aziz). Verse 39: whoever repents and reforms → repentance; 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Verse 40: 'To Allah belongs the kingdom of the heavens and earth' → sovereignty; 'Allah is Capable of everything' → power.

5:41.notes: Direct address 'O Messenger!' → muhammad. Hypocrites who say 'We believe' with mouths but not hearts → hypocrites. Jews twisting words, listening to lies → people-of-the-book, disbelief. Torah as source of judgment (verse 43–44) → previous-scriptures, justice-and-witness. 'Disgrace in this world and great punishment in the Hereafter' → hell. 'Allah is the Knower of the unseen' → knowledge. Verse 45: lex talionis (eye for eye) → justice-and-witness.

5:46.notes: Jesus son of Mary sent confirming the Torah, given the Gospel containing guidance and light → jesus, mary, previous-scriptures, prophethood-general, guidance. 'Guidance and counsel for the righteous' → taqwa (muttaqin explicitly named as the audience for the Gospel's guidance).

5:48.notes: Direct address implied for the Prophet (judge between them) → muhammad. The Qur'an revealed confirming and superseding previous scriptures → the-quran, previous-scriptures. 'For each We have assigned a law and a method' → divine-decree. 'Had Allah willed He could have made you one nation' → divine-decree. 'To Allah is your return… He will inform you of what you disputed' → reckoning. Verse 50: 'Is it the laws of the time of ignorance they desire?' → people-of-the-book context. No explicit qul here; dropping qul-statements. guidance is the explicit subject of 'He guides to ways of peace'.

5:51.notes: 'O you who believe! Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies' → believers, people-of-the-book. Verse 52: those with sickness in their hearts racing to them → hypocrites. 'Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people' → guidance (negated, denial thereof). Verse 53: believers' reaction to hypocrites whose works have failed → disbelievers.

5:54.notes: 'O you who believe! Whoever goes back on his religion' — apostasy warning. Allah will bring people who love Him, humble toward believers, stern with disbelievers, striving in Allah's way → war-and-treaties (striving/jihad). Verse 55: 'Your allies are Allah, His Messenger, and the believers who pray and give zakat' → prayer, zakat-and-charity. 'Allah is Embracing and Knowing' → knowledge, mercy (Waasi' = Embracing/all-encompassing, which maps to mercy/provision cluster; 'Alim = knowledge).

5:57.notes: 'O you who believe! Do not befriend those who take your religion in mockery' → mockery explicitly named. People of the Book and disbelievers who mock → people-of-the-book, disbelievers, mockery. Verse 58: they take the call to prayer as a joke → prayer. Verse 59: 'Say, O People of the Scripture…' → qul-statements. Verse 60: 'Say, Shall I inform you…' → qul-statements. Turned into apes and swine for idol worship → disbelief. 'Fear Allah' → taqwa.

5:61.notes: Those who come saying 'We believe' while concealing disbelief → hypocrites, disbelief. 'Allah is well aware of what they hide' → knowledge. Verse 62: competing in sin and consuming illicit earnings → corruption-on-earth, greed-and-miserliness. Verse 63: rabbis not preventing sinful speech or consuming forbidden wealth → corruption-on-earth. Verse 64: Jews say 'Allah's hand is tied' → people-of-the-book; 'His hands are outstretched; He gives as He wills' → sovereignty, provision (mercy cluster); 'they strive to spread corruption on earth' → corruption-on-earth. Verse 65–66: if People of the Book believed → people-of-the-book, mercy (forgiveness of sins, Gardens of Bliss). 'Allah does not love the corrupters' confirms corruption-on-earth.

5:67.notes: Direct address 'O Messenger, convey…' → muhammad. 'Allah will protect you from the people' → nearness-and-response (but I will prioritize prophethood-general and muhammad for the messenger-protection theme). Verse 68: 'Say, O People of the Scripture…' → qul-statements, people-of-the-book, previous-scriptures. Verse 69: believers, Jews, Sabeans, Christians who believe and do right → sabeans, believers, disbelievers (implicitly). 'Allah does not guide the disbelieving people' → guidance (negated).

5:70.notes: Covenant with Children of Israel and rejection of messengers → children-of-israel, covenant, prophethood-general, disbelief. Verse 72: refutation 'Allah is the Messiah son of Mary' → jesus, mary, shirk, tawhid. 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord' → tawhid. 'Whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise and his dwelling is the Fire' → hell. Children of Israel addressed by Jesus → children-of-israel.

5:73.notes: Refutation of Trinity ('Allah is the third of three') → tawhid, disbelief, shirk. 'There is no deity except the One God' → tawhid. 'Will they not repent?' → repentance. 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Verse 75: 'The Messiah son of Mary was only a messenger… his mother was a woman of truth' → jesus, mary. Verse 76: 'Say, Do you worship besides Allah…' → qul-statements. 'Allah is the Hearer, the Knower' → knowledge (closing formula). Verse 77: 'Say, O People of the Scripture…' → qul-statements, people-of-the-book.

5:78.notes: Cursed were disbelievers among Children of Israel 'by the tongue of David and Jesus son of Mary' → david, jesus, mary, children-of-israel. 'Because they rebelled and transgressed' → corruption-on-earth. Verse 79: not preventing one another from wrongs → corruption-on-earth. Verse 80: befriending disbelievers, 'wrath of Allah fell upon them and in the torment they will remain' → hell. Verse 81: many of them are immoral → disbelief, denial-of-revelation.

5:82.notes: Jews and polytheists most hostile; Christians nearest in affection → people-of-the-book, polytheists, disbelievers. 'Among them are priests and monks and they are not arrogant'. Verse 83: Christians weeping on hearing the Qur'an, uttering: 'Our Lord, we have believed, so count us among the witnesses' → this is an uttered du'a; 'count us among the witnesses' is a request to be included with the truthful → dua-guidance (asking to be guided/included on the right path). Verse 84: 'hope that our Lord will include us among the righteous' → dua-guidance reinforced. Verse 85: Gardens beneath which rivers flow → paradise. Verse 86: disbelievers who deny signs → hell, disbelievers.

5:87.notes: 'O you who believe! Do not prohibit the good things Allah has permitted' → food-and-dietary (lawful things). Verse 88: eat lawful provision → food-and-dietary. Verse 89: rules on oaths and atonement — feeding ten needy people, clothing them, freeing a slave, or fasting three days → oaths-and-vows, manumission-and-captives, fasting. 'Thus Allah makes clear His Revelations that you may be grateful' → gratitude (shukr explicitly invoked). 'Allah is Forgiving and Clement' → mercy.

5:90.notes: 'O you who believe! Intoxicants, gambling, idolatry, and divination are abominations of Satan's doing' → intoxicants-and-gambling, shirk (idolatry), iblis (Satan explicitly named). Verse 91: Satan wants to provoke strife through intoxicants and gambling and 'prevent you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer' → remembrance, prayer. Verse 92: 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger'. Verse 93: believers who do righteous deeds and maintain piety — 'Allah loves the charitable'.

5:94.notes: 'O you who believe! Allah will test you with game… that Allah may know who fears Him at heart' → taqwa (fear of Allah). Test during pilgrim sanctity → hajj-and-pilgrimage. Killing game while in ihram forbidden → food-and-dietary. Verse 95: penalty for killing game during pilgrim sanctity, offering to Kaabah → hajj-and-pilgrimage, sacred-mosque-and-qiblah. 'Allah is Almighty, Avenger' → power. Verse 96: sea catch permitted, land game forbidden during pilgrim sanctity → food-and-dietary. 'Fear Allah to Whom you will be gathered' → day-of-judgment. 'Allah forgives what is past' implies knowledge.

5:97.notes: 'Allah has appointed the Kaabah, the Sacred House, a sanctuary for the people' — for the people (mankind broadly as beneficiaries) → mankind (sanctuary established for an-nās). Sacred Month and offerings → ritual-calendar-and-sacred-time. 'That you may know that Allah knows everything' → knowledge. Verse 98: 'Allah is severe in retribution and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy, power. Verse 99: 'The Messenger's sole duty is to convey' → prophethood-general. 'Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal' → knowledge.

5:100.notes: Verse 100: 'Say: the bad and the good are not equal' → qul-statements. 'Fear Allah' → taqwa. Verse 101: 'O you who believe! Do not ask about things…' — while the Quran is being revealed → the-quran (Qur'an as subject of revelation process). 'Allah is Forgiving and Clement' → mercy. Verse 103: 'Those who disbelieve fabricate lies about Allah' — Arab superstitions about animals → disbelievers, shirk (fabricating lies about Allah regarding idolatrous animal-dedication customs). Verse 104: following forefathers rather than coming to Allah's revelation → disbelief, denial-of-revelation. 'Allah knows' (implicit) → knowledge.

5:106.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: angels (they appear in the broader context as 'Holy Spirit' in v110 but are not the primary subject of verses 106–108); death-and-dying (verse 106 mentions death but it's the legal occasion not the theological subject). Verses 106–108: rules for testimony in the making of a bequest when death approaches → justice-and-witness, wealth-and-property-law, death-and-dying. Verse 109: Day when Allah gathers messengers → day-of-judgment, prophethood-general. 'You are the Knower of the unseen' → knowledge. Verse 110: direct address 'O Jesus son of Mary' → jesus, mary; Jesus speaking to the people, supported by Holy Spirit (Gabriel/angels), healed blind and leprous, revived dead, molded birds from clay → miracles, children-of-israel (protected from Children of Israel). Verse 111: 'When I inspired the disciples' → disciples.

5:112.notes: Disciples asking Jesus about a table from heaven → jesus, mary (referenced), disciples. Jesus's du'a: 'O Allah, our Lord, send down for us a table from heaven… provide for us; You are the Best of providers' (verse 114) → uttered supplication, dua-distress (asking for a miraculous provision in context of need for reassurance and sign). The table as a miraculous sign → miracles, provision ('You are the Best of providers' → provision). Verse 115: 'I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves thereafter I will punish...' → power, knowledge (God's awareness and response).

5:116.notes: Allah questioning Jesus: 'Did you say take me and my mother as gods?' → jesus, mary, shirk (the false claim), tawhid (Jesus's denial). Jesus says 'Glory be to You! (Subhānaka)' → praise (uttered glorification). 'You know what is in my soul' → knowledge. Verse 117: Jesus's testimony of his mission — 'worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord'. Verse 118: 'You are the Mighty and Wise' → wisdom (Hakim), power (Aziz). Verse 119: Day when truthful benefit from truthfulness → day-of-judgment. 'They will have Gardens… Allah is pleased with them' → paradise.

5:120.notes: 'To Allah belongs the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and what lies in them' → sovereignty. 'He has power over everything' → power. The heavens and earth as belonging to Allah → creation-of-heavens-earth.

6:1.notes: Opens with 'al-hamdu lillah' → praise. Creation of heavens/earth and human creation from clay are explicit. Knowledge of secrets/public → knowledge attribute. Appointed term → divine-decree. Disbelievers ascribe equals → shirk. They turn from signs and deny → denial-of-revelation.

6:6.notes: Destroyed generations → punishment-of-past-nations / previous-creations-destroyed. Rain/rivers imagery → natural-signs. Disbelievers call the book sorcery → denial-of-revelation. The angel demand → angels. God's ability to send a sign → power.

6:10.notes: Multiple 'Qul' commands → qul-statements. Messengers mocked before → mockery, prophethood-general. 'To whom belongs what is in heavens and earth? To Allah' → sovereignty, tawhid. 'He inscribed mercy' → mercy. Gathering on Day of Resurrection → day-of-judgment. Those who deny God own associates → shirk. 'He is the Hearing, the Knowing' → knowledge (but covered by sovereignty/mercy cluster here). Knowledge is explicitly named in v13 → adding knowledge.

6:17.notes: Multiple Qul commands → qul-statements. 'He is Capable of everything' → power. 'The Supreme over His servants' → sovereignty. 'The Wise, the Expert' → wisdom, knowledge. 'This Quran was revealed' → the-quran. 'He is but One God' → tawhid. Rejection of other gods → shirk. People of the Book recognize it → people-of-the-book. Gathering of polytheists on Judgment Day (vv.22-24) → day-of-judgment. Polytheists deny being idolaters on that Day → shirk reinforced.

6:25.notes: Covers sealed hearts, denial of revelation, standing before the Fire, denial of resurrection, the Hour coming. Hell (Fire) → hell. Day of standing before the Lord → day-of-judgment. 'We will not be resurrected' → resurrection (denial of it). Disbelievers as collective subject throughout.

6:33.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('what they say grieves you') → muhammad. Messengers rejected before and they 'endured' (sabaru) → patience (sabr is named explicitly in v34). Prophethood as category → prophethood-general. 'Allah willed could have gathered them to guidance' → guidance. Denial of revelations → denial-of-revelation.

6:37.notes: Multiple Qul commands → qul-statements. 'Allah is Able' → power. Animals and birds as communities → natural-signs. 'He wills, sets on a straight path' → guidance, divine-decree. Those who reject are deaf/dumb → denial-of-revelation.

6:42.notes: Messengers sent to past communities, affliction → punishment-of-past-nations, prophethood-general. Satan adorned their deeds → iblis. 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds' (v45) → praise. 'Cut off the last remnant' → punishment-of-past-nations reinforced.

6:46.notes: Multiple Qul commands → qul-statements. 'If Allah took away your hearing' → power. Messengers as bearers of good news and warners → prophethood-general. Those who reject → denial-of-revelation, disbelievers. 'I do not know the future / I only follow revelation' → knowledge (God's exclusive knowledge of the unseen).

6:51.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('warn with it') → muhammad. Believers who call upon their Lord morning and evening → believers, prayer. 'No protector or intercessor apart from Him' → intercession. 'Perhaps they will grow in piety' (yattaqun) → taqwa. Fear of gathering before Lord → day-of-judgment.

6:54.notes: Multiple Qul commands → qul-statements. 'Peace be upon you, your Lord has prescribed mercy' → mercy. 'Repents and reforms' → repentance. 'He is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy reinforced. 'I am forbidden from worshiping those you pray to besides Allah' → tawhid, shirk. 'I will not follow…I would be lost' → guidance.

6:63.notes: Multiple Qul commands → qul-statements. 'Who delivers you from the darkness?' → power. 'Yet you associate others' → shirk. God able to send punishment → power reinforced. 'Your people rejected it' → disbelievers. 'Gossip about Our revelations' → denial-of-revelation context; 'the-quran' fits as the revelations being discussed are the Qur'an. Taqwa mentioned (v69) → taqwa. Hell mentioned (v70: scalding water, painful punishment) → hell.

6:71.notes: Multiple Qul commands → qul-statements. 'Guidance of Allah is the guidance' → guidance. 'Shall we invoke besides Allah?' → shirk, tawhid. 'Perform the prayers' → prayer. 'Gathered to Him' → day-of-judgment. 'Created the heavens and earth in truth' → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'His is the sovereignty on the Day the trumpet is blown' → sovereignty. 'Knower of secrets and declarations' → knowledge. 'Wise, the Expert' → wisdom.

6:74.notes: Abraham's da'wah and rejection of idols → abraham, shirk. Vision of heavens and earth → creation-of-heavens-earth. Planet, moon, sun observed and rejected as lords → cosmic-bodies. Final declaration of monotheism → tawhid.

6:80.notes: Abraham argues with his people → abraham. 'Do you argue with me about Allah when He has guided me?' → guidance, tawhid. 'My Lord comprehends all things in knowledge' → knowledge. Closing: 'Your Lord is Wise and Informed' → wisdom, knowledge. Those who believe and don't mix with wrongdoing have security → believers.

6:84.notes: 14 labels — over the 12 ceiling. This section is the great prophet-list (vv.84-90). Every named prophet must be tagged per rule 3. Prophethood-general applies throughout. Guidance is explicitly named ('each We guided'). Previous scriptures named ('We gave them the Book'). Qul at v90 → qul-statements. Trim candidates if needed: elisha (brief mention), lot (brief mention), qul-statements (minor relative to the list).

6:91.notes: Multiple Qul commands → qul-statements. Moses and the Scripture revealed to him → moses, previous-scriptures. 'The Quran, blessed, verifying what preceded' → the-quran. People of the Book conceal the scripture → people-of-the-book. 'Dedicated to their prayers' (v92) → prayer. Falsehood against Allah, false revelation claims → denial-of-revelation. Angels taking souls of wrongdoers at death → angels; day-of-judgment themes → day-of-judgment.

6:95.notes: Splitting grain and seed, living from dead → natural-signs, creation. Dawn, night, sun, moon for calculation → cosmic-bodies. Stars for navigation → cosmic-bodies reinforced. 'Almighty, All-Knowing' → power, knowledge. Produced from a single person → human-creation.

6:99.notes: Rain, vegetation, grains, fruits → natural-signs, provision. 'They attributed to Allah partners—the sprites' → shirk, jinn. 'Glory be to Him' (Subhanahu) → praise. 'Originator of heavens and earth' → creation. 'There is no god except He' (v102) → tawhid. 'No vision can grasp Him' → knowledge implied but knowledge label not strictly named; 'He has knowledge of all things' (v101) → knowledge.

6:104.notes: Multiple Qul commands → qul-statements. 'Insights have come to you from your Lord' → the-quran, guidance. 'Follow what was revealed' → the-quran. 'There is no god but He' → tawhid. 'Turn away from the polytheists' → polytheists, shirk. 'Had Allah willed, they would not have practiced idolatry' → divine-decree.

6:108.notes: Do not insult their gods → practical-ethics. 'For every prophet an enemy—human and jinn devils' → prophethood-general, jinn, iblis. 'Had your Lord willed' → divine-decree. Disbelievers' refusal to believe even with miracles → denial-of-revelation. Angels mentioned (v111) → angels. Qul not prominent in this passage but not absent; swearing/miracle-demand context → denial-of-revelation confirmed.

6:114.notes: Multiple Qul commands → qul-statements. 'He is the One who revealed the Book' → the-quran. 'Those to whom We gave the Book know it is truth' → people-of-the-book. 'The Word of your Lord completed in truth and justice' → guidance. 'He is the Hearer, the Knower' → knowledge. 'There is no changing to His words' → divine-decree. 'Your Lord knows best who strays' → knowledge reinforced.

6:118.notes: Eating what Allah's name is pronounced over, dietary prohibitions → food-and-dietary. Address to believers implied ('if you indeed believe') → believers. 'Your Lord knows best the transgressors' → knowledge.

6:121.notes: Do not eat what Allah's name was not pronounced over → food-and-dietary. 'The devils inspire their followers to argue' → iblis. 'If you obey them, you would be polytheists' → shirk. Light vs. darkness metaphor for guidance/disbelief → guidance, disbelief. Plotting of criminal leaders (v123) → plotting. 'They conspire' (yamkurun) → plotting.

6:126.notes: Short section (2 verses). 'This is the straight path of your Lord' → guidance. 'For them is the Home of Peace with their Lord' → paradise. 'He is their Master' → sovereignty.

6:128.notes: Address to assembly of jinn and mankind → jinn, mankind. 'The Fire is your dwelling' → hell. Gathering on the Day → day-of-judgment. 'Did messengers not come to you?' → prophethood-general. 'We testify against ourselves that we were disbelievers' → disbelief. 'Your Lord is Wise and Informed' → wisdom, knowledge. 'Your Lord is the Rich Beyond Need, the Possessor of Mercy' → mercy. Qul in v135 → qul-statements.

6:136.notes: Pagan allocation of crops/livestock for idols → shirk, polytheists. Dietary restrictions imposed by polytheists → food-and-dietary. Killing children for idols (vv.137, 140) → anger-and-violence, children-and-parents. Forbidding what Allah has provided → provision.

6:141.notes: Gardens, crops, livestock → natural-signs, provision. 'Eat of its fruit, give its due' → food-and-dietary. 'Eat of what Allah provided, do not follow Satan' → food-and-dietary. Multiple Qul commands (vv.143-144) → qul-statements. Pagan taboos on animals challenged → shirk. 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' (v145) → mercy.

6:145.notes: Multiple Qul commands → qul-statements. Dietary prohibitions (carrion, blood, swine) → food-and-dietary. Jewish dietary laws (v146) → people-of-the-book. 'Your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. 'Had Allah willed, we would not have practiced idolatry' (v148) → divine-decree, shirk. Polytheists' argument → polytheists.

6:151.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. 'Come let me tell you what your Lord has forbidden' → qul-statements. 'Associate nothing with Him' → tawhid, shirk. 'Honor your parents' → children-and-parents. 'Do not kill your children—We provide for you' → provision, children-and-parents, anger-and-violence. 'Do not come near indecencies' → chastity-and-boundaries. 'Do not kill the soul' → anger-and-violence. 'Property of the orphan' → orphan-care. 'Full weight and measure equitably', 'when you speak be fair' → justice-and-witness. 'Fulfill your covenant with Allah' → covenant. 'That you may refrain from wrongdoing' (tattaqun) → taqwa. Broad ethical list → righteous-conduct.

6:154.notes: Moses given the Scripture → moses, previous-scriptures. 'This blessed Scripture We revealed' → the-quran. 'Guidance and mercy' → guidance, mercy. 'Two parties before us' → people-of-the-book. Those who deny → denial-of-revelation. Waiting for angels or signs of Lord → angels, signs-of-the-hour. Qul in v158 → qul-statements.

6:159.notes: Multiple Qul commands → qul-statements. 'Guided me to straight path, creed of Abraham the Monotheist' → abraham, tawhid. 'Who was not a polytheist' → shirk. 'My prayer and worship…devoted to Allah' → prayer. 'No soul bears the burdens of another' → justice. 'Then to your Lord is your return, He will inform you of your disputes' → reckoning. Those who divide religion into sects → prophethood-general context.

6:165.notes: Single verse. 'He made you successors on the earth' → mankind, sovereignty. 'Raised some in ranks over others to test you' → divine-decree. 'Quick in retribution' → justice. 'Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Human creation as vicegerents → creation.

7:1.notes: Section opens with Alif-Lam-Mim-Sad → disjoined-letters. The scripture is described as revealed for warning and reminder for believers. Verse 3 addresses those who should follow what is revealed, with implicit contrast to those who do not.

7:4.notes: Verses 4–5 describe past towns destroyed; verses 6–7 reference questioning of messengers and their peoples on the Day; verses 8–9 describe the scales of justice on that Day.

7:10.notes: Adam named explicitly (v19); Iblis named; angels commanded to prostrate. Section covers creation of humans, the provision of livelihood on earth, Iblis's arrogance and refusal to prostrate, his threat to waylay humanity, and God's warning about filling Hell with those who follow Iblis. Paradise is referenced (v19: Adam and wife told to inhabit the Garden).

7:20.notes: Satan whispers to Adam and Eve; they eat from the tree; they utter the du'a 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; unless You forgive us and have mercy on us…' (v23) → dua-forgiveness. v24–25 describe descent to earth to live and die → death-and-dying. The couple and their relationship grounds marriage-and-family.

7:26.notes: Address is 'O children of Adam'; clothing of piety (taqwa) is explicitly named as best → taqwa label triggered by explicit naming of the concept. Satan's role in driving parents out is referenced again. v27 notes devils are made friends of disbelievers.

7:28.notes: Multiple 'Say:' (qul) commands → qul-statements. v29: 'My Lord commands justice' → justice. v29: 'stand devoted at every place of worship' → mosques-and-sacred-places. v29: 'call upon Him dedicating your faith to Him alone' → sincerity (ikhlas explicitly invoked). v30: contrast between guided and misguided, those who take devils as patrons → disbelievers. Idolaters claiming God commands indecency → shirk-adjacent but more precisely disbelief/denial; shirk fits v30 (taking devils as patrons beside Allah).

7:33.notes: Single qul-statement section. God forbids shirk explicitly ('associate with Allah anything…') → shirk. Forbids immorality, sin, aggression. v34: every nation has an appointed time (ajal) → divine-decree.

7:35.notes: Address: 'O Children of Adam' (mankind). Messengers sent to warn → prophethood-general. v35: 'whoever practices piety' (taqwa explicitly named) → taqwa. v36: those who reject and are arrogant → hell. v37: soul-taking at death, testimony against selves. v38: jinn and humans entering Fire together → jinn. Hell described in detail → hell. Day of reckoning and judgment implied throughout.

7:40.notes: v40–41: arrogant rejecters cannot enter paradise → arrogance, paradise, hell, disbelievers. v42: believers and righteous deeds → believers, paradise. v43: inhabitants of paradise say 'Praise be to Allah who guided us' → praise (al-hamdu lillah uttered) and guidance. v43: messengers came with truth → prophethood-general. v44–45: exchange between paradise and hell dwellers; those who hindered from Allah's path and denied the Hereafter → denial-of-revelation.

7:46.notes: The A'raf (Elevations) narrative — people between paradise and hell. v47: uttered du'a-like: 'Our Lord, do not place us among the wrongdoing people' — this is a supplication addressed to God → dua-protection (borderline; classified as uttered plea). v48: arrogance of those in fire noted explicitly → arrogance. v49: mercy of God mentioned ('you swore Allah will not touch with mercy') → mercy.

7:50.notes: Fire inmates call to Garden inhabitants for water → hell, paradise. Allah has forbidden provisions for disbelievers → disbelievers. v51: those who took religion lightly, deceived by worldly life, Day of Judgment — denial of revelations.

7:52.notes: Scripture described as detailed with knowledge, guidance and mercy → the-quran, guidance, mercy. v53: on the Day, those who ignored it will ask for intercessors → intercession, day-of-judgment. Messengers referenced → prophethood-general. Those who disregarded it → disbelief.

7:54.notes: v54: creation of heavens and earth in six days, throne, night/day cycle, sun moon stars → creation-of-heavens-earth, cosmic-bodies, sovereignty, power. 'Tabaraka Allah' → praise. v55: prayer humbly and privately. v56: 'do not corrupt on earth' → corruption-on-earth; 'Allah's mercy is close' → mercy. v57–58: wind, clouds, rain, dead land revived, fruits → natural-signs, provision. Resurrection analogy.

7:59.notes: Noah sent to his people, calls to worship Allah alone → noah, tawhid, prophethood-general. People reject him → denial-of-revelation. Noah and believers saved in the Ark, rest drowned → punishment-of-past-nations. The Ark as miraculous salvation → miracles.

7:65.notes: Hud sent to 'Ad → hud, ad. Calls to tawhid → tawhid. People mock him → denial-of-revelation. References Noah's people (v69) → noah. 'Ad destroyed, Hud and believers saved by mercy → punishment-of-past-nations, mercy.

7:73.notes: Salih sent to Thamud → salih, thamud. She-camel as sign/miracle → miracles. Calls to tawhid → tawhid. Arrogant elite explicit ('those who were arrogant') → arrogance. v74: 'do not roam the earth corruptingly' → corruption-on-earth. Thamud hamstring camel, quake destroys them → punishment-of-past-nations. Denial → denial-of-revelation.

7:80.notes: Lot and his people; their lewdness explicitly named → lot, chastity-and-boundaries. Lot's wife referenced → marriage-and-family. His people expelled him; rain of punishment → punishment-of-past-nations. Denial of Lot's message → denial-of-revelation.

7:85.notes: Shuayb to Madyan → shuayb, madyan. Full measure and weight, do not cheat → trade-and-debt, justice. 'Do not corrupt the land' → corruption-on-earth. v87: 'be patient until Allah judges' — patience explicitly named → patience. Tawhid called to → tawhid. Prophethood framed → prophethood-general.

7:88.notes: Arrogant elite threaten expulsion of Shuayb → arrogance. v89: 'Our Lord embraces all things in knowledge' → knowledge. 'In Allah we place our trust' → trust-in-god. 'Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth' → dua-distress (uttered du'a in distress/conflict). Quake destroys rejectors → punishment-of-past-nations. Denial of Shuayb → denial-of-revelation.

7:94.notes: Every town sent a prophet, afflicted with misery so they may humble themselves → prophethood-general. Pattern of prosperity then seizure → punishment-of-past-nations. v96: 'had they believed and turned righteous (taqwa)' → taqwa explicitly named. Blessings of heaven and earth → provision.

7:97.notes: Warning to towns not to feel secure from God's might → punishment-of-past-nations. v99: 'Allah's plan' (makr) → divine-decree. v100: could strike for sins, seals hearts → knowledge (God's knowledge of their sins), disbelief. v101: messengers came with clear signs but they would not believe → prophethood-general, denial-of-revelation. v102: untrue to covenants.

7:103.notes: Moses sent to Pharaoh with miracles → moses, pharaoh, prophethood-general, miracles. Staff turned to serpent, white hand → miracles. Pharaoh's people accuse him of sorcery → sorcery. Aaron mentioned via 'his brother' in v122 — but v122 is in section 7:113. Children of Israel referenced (v105) → children-of-israel. Rejecters → denial-of-revelation, punishment-of-past-nations.

7:113.notes: Magicians contest Moses → sorcery. Moses's staff swallows illusions → miracles. Magicians believe; Aaron named in v122 → aaron. Pharaoh threatens crucifixion → pharaoh. v125–126: magicians utter 'Our Lord, pour out patience upon us and receive our souls in submission' → dua-distress (du'a uttered under threat of death). Pharaoh as tyrant → disbelief. Aaron explicitly named (v122) → aaron.

7:127.notes: Pharaoh plans to kill sons of Israelites → pharaoh, children-of-israel. Moses tells people: 'seek help in Allah and be patient' → patience (explicitly commanded). 'The earth belongs to Allah… the future belongs to the righteous' → sovereignty, taqwa (righteous/muttaqun referenced). Trust in God implicit in 'seek help in Allah' → trust-in-god.

7:130.notes: Plagues sent on Pharaoh's people — flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood as signs (miracles) → miracles, moses, pharaoh. They are arrogant → arrogance. Promise broken → denial-of-revelation. Pharaoh's people drowned; Children of Israel inherit the land → punishment-of-past-nations, children-of-israel.

7:138.notes: Children of Israel cross sea, ask Moses for a god like the idolaters → shirk. Moses corrects: no god but Allah who has favored you → tawhid. Reference to Pharaoh's oppression (v141) → pharaoh, children-of-israel.

7:142.notes: Moses's 40-night appointment, leaves Aaron in charge → moses, aaron. Moses asks to see God → nearness-and-response. Moses falls unconscious, recovers: 'Subhanaka, I repent to you' → praise (subhan uttered), repentance. God says He has chosen Moses for His messages and speech → prophethood-general. God tells Moses to take the tablets → previous-scriptures (the tablets are Torah precursor). v144: 'be one of the thankful' → gratitude? The command 'be thankful' is explicit enough to trigger the concept label.

7:145.notes: Tablets inscribed with guidance → previous-scriptures, guidance. v146: 'those who behave proudly without justification' → arrogance. They will not believe in signs → denial-of-revelation. v147: those who deny revelations and the Hereafter, deeds come to nothing → day-of-judgment.

7:148.notes: The golden calf → shirk (idolizing the calf), children-of-israel. v149: calf-worshippers regret and say 'Unless our Lord extends His mercy and forgives us…' — uttered near-du'a → dua-forgiveness (the phrase is uttered in indirect speech, borderline; classified as uttered on basis that the wording 'our Lord' introduces it). Moses returns angry, confronts Aaron → moses, aaron. v151: Moses utters 'My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy' → explicit dua-forgiveness. v153: repentance accepted, Lord is Forgiving and Merciful → mercy, repentance.

7:154.notes: Moses picks up tablets: guidance and mercy therein → guidance, mercy. v155: Moses chooses 70 men, tremor strikes, he utters du'a: 'My Lord, had You willed…forgive us and have mercy…You are the Best of Forgivers' → dua-forgiveness. 'This is but Your test — You misguide whom You will and guide whom You will' → divine-decree. 'Our Lord, embraces all things in knowledge' → knowledge (already in 7:89 context but here independently).

7:156.notes: 13 labels — over 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: sovereignty (only briefly in v158, subsumed by tawhid assertion), previous-scriptures (supporting detail rather than main subject). All independently justified.

7:159.notes: Community of Moses's people that guides by truth → moses, children-of-israel. Twelve tribes, twelve springs from rock → miracles. Clouds, manna and quails → provision, natural-signs. v161: enter gate in humility; sins forgiven → covenant (implicit promise tied to entering the town). v162: plague sent for substituting words → punishment of wrongdoing. Previous scripture context (tablets, divine instructions) → previous-scriptures.

7:163.notes: Sabbath violation by town near the sea → children-of-israel, people-of-the-book (Jews specifically), ritual-calendar-and-sacred-time (Sabbath). v165: those who prohibit evil saved; wrongdoers punished → punishment-of-past-nations. v166: transformed into apes. v167: God announces perpetual suffering until Day of Resurrection; 'swift in retribution yet Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy, justice.

7:168.notes: Scattered into communities, tested with good and bad → children-of-israel. v169: inherited the Scripture, chose worldly goods, 'we will be forgiven' — covenant to uphold Scripture → previous-scriptures, covenant. v170: those who adhere to Scripture and establish prayer → prayer. v170: 'We will not waste the reward of the reformers' → righteous-conduct? Only 'reformers' referenced, not the concept named. v169: 'the Home of the Hereafter is better for the cautious' → taqwa (cautious = muttaqun). v171: mountain suspended, told to take Scripture with strength and be taqwa → taqwa.

7:172.notes: The primordial covenant: God draws out descendants of Adam, makes them testify 'Am I not your Lord?' → mankind (descendants of Adam = humanity), tawhid (God's lordship affirmed). v173: ancestor's shirk cited as excuse refuted → shirk. Day of Resurrection cited → day-of-judgment. The act of witnessing written into destiny → divine-decree.

7:175.notes: Story of one given signs who detached from them; Satan followed him → iblis. He clung to desires, metaphor of panting dog → disbelief, denial-of-revelation. v178: whom Allah guides is guided; whom He misguides → guidance. v179: Hell created for many jinn and humans → hell, jinn. They have hearts/eyes/ears that do not perceive → denial-of-revelation.

7:180.notes: v180: Most Beautiful Names belong to Allah → tawhid. Call upon Him by them; those who blaspheme His names will be repaid → disbelief. v181: community that guides by truth → guidance. v182–183: Allah's plan (kayd) for rejecters → divine-decree. v184: 'He is but a plain warner' → prophethood-general. v185: 'Have they not observed the government of heavens and earth and what Allah created' → creation-of-heavens-earth. v186: Allah misguides the transgressor → divine-decree.

7:187.notes: Two qul commands about the Hour → qul-statements. 'Knowledge of it rests with my Lord; none can reveal it except He' → knowledge, signs-of-the-hour. v188: 'Say, I have no control over benefit or harm to myself except as Allah wills; I am only a warner and herald' — the Prophet's limited role described; this is direct address about the Prophet's nature and role → prophethood-general, muhammad (substantively about his role and limitations, qualifying as section about him personally).

7:189.notes: Created from single person, made spouse → human-creation, marriage-and-family, creation. Pregnancy; couple pray: 'if You give us a good child, we will be among the thankful' → dua-family-offspring (uttered supplication for offspring). v190: they attribute partners to Him → shirk. v191–192: idols create nothing, are themselves created → tawhid.

7:193.notes: v193–198: refutation of idols who cannot speak, see, or hear → shirk, tawhid. 'My Master is Allah… He takes care of the righteous' → tawhid, believers. v195: 'Say, call upon your partners…' → qul-statements. v199: 'Be tolerant, command decency, avoid the ignorant' → practical-ethics (explicit moral instruction for conduct). v200: 'take refuge with Allah' from Satan → iblis. 'He is Hearing and Knowing' → knowledge. v201: the righteous reminded themselves when Satan strikes → believers.

7:203.notes: v203: qul command — 'I only follow what is inspired to me' → qul-statements, prophethood-general. 'This is insights from your Lord and guidance and mercy for people who believe' → the-quran, guidance, mercy, believers. v204: 'when the Quran is recited, listen to it' → the-quran. v205: 'remember your Lord within yourself humbly and fearfully morning and evening' → remembrance (dhikr explicitly commanded as the subject of the instruction).

7:206.notes: Those in God's presence (angels) are not arrogant about worship → angels, arrogance (arrogance negated explicitly — 'not too proud'). They recite His praises → praise (tasbih uttered). The verse ends with prostration mark (sajda).

8:1.notes: Section opens with 'Say' (qul) regarding war spoils (anfal). Verses 2-4 describe the true believers' qualities: hearts trembling at Allah's mention, reliance on Him, prayer, spending. Closing promise of forgiveness and generous provision maps to mercy and provision. taqwa explicitly named ('be mindful of Allah'). trust-in-god explicit ('upon their Lord they rely'). paradise/high standing implied by 'high standing with their Lord'. prayer and zakat-and-charity explicitly named in v.3.

8:5.notes: Section covers the lead-up to and context of Battle of Badr: believers' reluctance, God's promise of one of two groups, Allah's plan to establish truth, angels sent as reinforcement (v.9), Allah inspiring angels to terrify and strike disbelievers (v.12), closing threat of the Fire (v.14). 'Mighty and Wise' in v.10 → power and wisdom. divine-decree implicit in 'Allah intends to prove the truth with His words'. Hell explicitly named in v.14.

8:15.notes: Opens with 'O you who believe' (yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū) → believers. Commands on battlefield conduct; fleeing triggers divine wrath and Hell (v.16). v.17: 'It was not you who killed them but Allah' and 'not you who launched but Allah' → divine-decree and power. 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' → knowledge. v.18 Allah undermining disbelievers' strategy → power.

8:20.notes: Opens with 'O you who believe' → believers. Commands obedience; warns against those who say 'we hear' but do not (v.21) — implicit hypocrisy reference, though the word is not used explicitly here; these are described as the worst animals (v.22). v.23 Allah's knowledge of what is in hearts → knowledge. v.24 'Allah stands between a man and his heart' → divine-decree/knowledge. v.25 warns against discord/fitna and notes 'Allah is severe in retribution'. taqwa not explicitly named but practical-ethics is triggered by the moral instruction on obedience and avoiding discord. Confidence medium on taqwa — the concept is present as instruction but not named; dropping it.

8:26.notes: v.26 reminds believers of when they were few and oppressed; God sheltered, supported, provided — 'so that you may be thankful' → gratitude explicitly named. v.27 'O you who believe, do not betray' → practical-ethics. v.28 wealth and children as a test → children-and-parents is borderline (it mentions children as fitna, not as a parenting/duty section). v.29 'If you remain conscious of Allah' → taqwa explicitly named. Dropped children-and-parents as the mention is incidental. trust-in-god not explicitly named; dropped. mercy from God's sheltering act implicit but not named; kept provision (rizq mentioned). Revised labels below.

8:30.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. v.30 'they plotted against you' directly addresses Muhammad and names the plot → muhammad + plotting. v.31 denying revelation as 'myths of the ancients' → denial-of-revelation. v.32 disbelievers' mocking challenge → mockery could apply but primary label is denial-of-revelation. v.33 Muhammad's presence among them. v.34 Sacred Mosque mentioned explicitly → sacred-mosque-and-qiblah. v.35 their false prayer at the House. v.36-37 disbelievers' spending and Hell. v.38 'Say to those who disbelieve' → qul-statements. v.39 fight until no persecution. v.40 'Allah is your Protector, Best Supporter' → power/sovereignty. 'Allah is Mighty and Wise' → wisdom. Trim candidates: migration (not explicitly named in text, implied by expulsion context — drop it), islamic-history-and-community (contextual but not named — keep as this is clearly Badr/Mecca context).

8:41.notes: v.41 legislates the khums (one-fifth) of war spoils for Allah, Messenger, relatives, orphans, poor, wayfarer → wealth-and-property-law, orphan-care, zakat-and-charity. 'Day of Distinction' = Battle of Badr → islamic-history-and-community. 'Allah is Capable of everything' → power. v.42 describes the arrangement of forces as Allah's predetermined decree → divine-decree. 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' → knowledge.

8:43.notes: v.43 Allah showed the enemy as few in the Prophet's dream ('in your dream' — direct address to Muhammad) → muhammad. 'He knows what the hearts contain' → knowledge. v.44 Allah made each army appear fewer in the other's eyes to fulfill His predetermined matter → divine-decree. 'To Allah all matters revert' → divine-decree/sovereignty. Islamic battle context → islamic-history-and-community.

8:45.notes: Opens with 'O you who believe' → believers. v.45 'remember Allah much' → remembrance explicitly named. v.46 'be steadfast, Allah is with the steadfast' → patience explicitly named (sabr). v.47 warns against those who left boastfully (batar) and barring from Allah's path — arrogance not using the word kibr, but 'boastfully' (batarana) is the explicit concept trigger. v.48 Iblis named → iblis. Iblis made their deeds appear good (plotting/deception) → plotting is borderline but not the section's primary focus; keep iblis.
