8:49.notes: v.49 hypocrites and those with sick hearts → hypocrites; 'whoever trusts in Allah' → trust-in-god explicitly. v.50 angels taking disbelievers at death → angels. v.51 'Allah is not unjust' → justice. v.52 'like the people of Pharaoh' → pharaoh, punishment-of-past-nations; 'Allah is Powerful, Severe in punishment' → power. v.53 Allah does not change a blessing until people change themselves → knowledge ('Allah is Hearing and Knowing'). v.54 people of Pharaoh drowned → pharaoh (again), punishment-of-past-nations, denial-of-revelation ('they denied the signs'). 11 labels — within ceiling.

8:55.notes: v.55-56 worst creatures are disbelievers who break treaties → disbelievers, covenant (treaty-breaking explicitly). v.57-58 battle instructions and breaking off with treacherous people → war-and-treaties. v.59-60 prepare military power; 'whatever you spend in Allah's way' → zakat-and-charity borderline, but context is military preparation not charity. v.61 'if they incline to peace… put your trust in Allah' → trust-in-god explicitly; 'He is the Hearer, the Knower' → knowledge. v.62-63 Allah supported with believers and united hearts; 'Mighty and Wise' → power, wisdom. v.64 'O prophet!' direct address → muhammad. v.65 'O prophet!' again → muhammad (already tagged). v.65-66 steadfast believers defeating larger armies; 'Allah is with the steadfast' → patience explicitly. 10 labels — within ceiling.

8:67.notes: v.67 'It is not for a prophet to take prisoners' — addresses the Prophet directly regarding prisoners of war → muhammad, manumission-and-captives, war-and-treaties. 'You desire materials of this world but Allah desires the Hereafter' → implied eschatology but not a primary label. 'Allah is Strong and Wise' → power, wisdom. v.68 'predetermined decree' → divine-decree. v.69 'consume what you have gained, legitimate and wholesome; remain conscious of Allah' → taqwa explicitly; 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. wealth-and-property-law for the ruling on legitimacy of war gains.

8:70.notes: v.70 'O prophet! Say to those you hold prisoners' → muhammad (direct address) + qul-statements (Say command). Promise of forgiveness and better than what was taken → mercy. 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. v.71 warning about intended betrayal; 'Allah is Knowing and Wise' → knowledge, wisdom.

8:72.notes: v.72 describes those who believed, emigrated, and struggled as allies of one another → believers, migration, islamic-history-and-community; 'except against a people with whom you have a treaty' → covenant, war-and-treaties. 'Allah is Seeing of what you do' → knowledge.

8:73.notes: v.73 disbelievers as allies of one another; unless believers maintain their alliances 'there will be turmoil in the land, and much corruption' → corruption-on-earth explicitly named (fasad kabir). v.74 true believers — those who emigrated and struggled — will have forgiveness and bountiful provision → mercy (forgiveness), provision. Kept mercy for the forgiveness promise.

8:75.notes: v.75 those who believed afterwards and emigrated belong with the community; 'family members are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah' → inheritance (this phrase is the basis for the inheritance/kinship rules; Ibn Kathir reads this as abrogating the mutual-inheritance of emigrant brotherhood in favor of blood ties). children-and-parents: family/kinship dimension is explicitly stated but it's more specifically about inheritance priority. Keeping inheritance as primary; children-and-parents borderline — keeping it as the family-priority rule applies to kin generally. 'Allah is Cognizant of everything' → knowledge.

9:1.notes: Direct address involving the Messenger and the polytheists; annulment of treaties proclaimed on Day of Greater Pilgrimage. 'Allah loves the righteous' (taqwa trigger).

9:5.notes: Sword verse context with conditional reprieve on repentance, prayer, zakat. Closing 'Forgiving, Merciful' invokes mercy.

9:8.notes: Describes faithlessness of polytheists toward treaties; contrasted with those who repent and perform prayer/zakat.

9:13.notes: Exhortation to fight those who broke oaths and plotted against the Messenger; closing 'Knowledgeable and Wise' invokes knowledge and wisdom. Direct reference to the Messenger being plotted against.

9:17.notes: Contrasts polytheists maintaining mosques vs. true believers; promises of paradise and mercy for the latter. 'Most likely to be guided' invokes guidance.

9:23.notes: Direct address 'O you who believe'; 'Say:' command present. Battle of Hunayn referenced (9:25) — Islamic history. Closing 'Forgiving and Merciful' invokes mercy.

9:28.notes: Direct address 'O you who believe'; polytheists barred from Sacred Mosque; fight commanded against People of the Book until jizya; 'Aware and Wise' invokes knowledge and wisdom; 'enrich you from His grace' invokes provision.

9:30.notes: Jews and Christians named; Jesus (the Messiah) named; rabbis and priests taking lords; 'no god except He, glory be to Him' — tawhid and praise. 'He sent His Messenger with guidance' invokes guidance and prophethood-general.

9:34.notes: Direct address 'O you who believe'; rabbis and priests consuming wealth illicitly; hoarding gold and silver; punishment in hellfire on the Day.

9:36.notes: Twelve months decreed since creation of heavens and earth; four sacred months; fight polytheists; 'Allah is with the righteous' — taqwa trigger. Postponement (nasi') denounced as disbelief.

9:38.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. Direct address 'O you who believe'; cave episode references Muhammad directly; 'Mighty and Wise' invokes power and wisdom; 'Say:' commands present (9:51, 52, 53); divine-decree ('what Allah has ordained'); trust-in-god explicitly named ('let the faithful put their trust'). Trim candidates if needed: islamic-history-and-community (subsumed by war context), migration (implied rather than explicit topic).

9:43.notes: Verses 43–55 — large section. Direct address to Muhammad ('May Allah pardon you'); hypocrites described at length; plotting (9:48); 'Say:' commands (9:51, 52, 53); divine-decree ('Nothing will happen except what Allah has ordained'); trust-in-god explicitly named; hell (9:49). 11 labels — within ceiling.

9:56.notes: Hypocrites swearing falsely, criticising distribution of charity; 9:60 defines zakat recipients including freeing slaves (manumission); closing 'All-Knowing, Most Wise' invokes knowledge and wisdom.

9:61.notes: Hypocrites insulting the Prophet (slander); 'Say:' command; 'mercy for those who believe' invokes mercy; hellfire for those who oppose Allah and Messenger.

9:64.notes: 14 labels — overflow. Hypocrites fearing Qur'anic revelation about them; mockery explicitly named; 'Say:' command (9:64, 65); hellfire for hypocrites/disbelievers; 9:69 references past nations; 9:70 names Noah, Aad, Thamood, Abraham, Madyan. Trim candidates: punishment-of-past-nations (subsumed by the named peoples), prophethood-general (only implicit).

9:71.notes: Believing men and women as allies; prayer and zakat explicitly named; 'Allah will have mercy on them'; 'Noble and Wise'; gardens with rivers promised.

9:73.notes: Direct address 'O Prophet'; fight disbelievers and hypocrites; their abode is Hell; hypocrites plotted (9:74); repentance offered as alternative.

9:75.notes: Hypocrites who broke promises to Allah; their stinginess after receiving bounty; 9:79 — mockery of charitable believers; 9:80 — forgiveness withheld; 'Knower of the unseen' invokes knowledge; 'Allah does not guide the immoral' invokes guidance.

9:81.notes: Those who stayed behind the Messenger; 'Say:' command (9:81); hellfire explicitly mentioned.

9:84.notes: Prophet forbidden from praying over dead hypocrites; sealed hearts; the Qur'anic surah as trigger for exemption requests (9:86); paradise promised to those who strive (9:89).

9:90.notes: Desert-Arabs seeking exemption; excuses; those who cannot go (weak, sick, poor) excused; 'Forgiving and Merciful' invokes mercy; 9:92 — Prophet's knowledge of their inability.

9:94.notes: Hypocrites making excuses on return; 'Say:' command; Allah informed the Prophet about them; 'Knower of the Invisible' invokes knowledge; hellfire for hypocrites (9:95).

9:97.notes: Desert-Arabs most steeped in disbelief and hypocrisy; 'Knowing and Wise'; 9:98 — those who treat charity as a fine; 9:99 — those who believe and give charity to draw near to Allah; 'Allah will admit them into His mercy'; 'Forgiving and Compassionate' invokes mercy.

9:100.notes: The Pioneers — first Emigrants and Supporters; Allah pleased with them; gardens promised. A historically specific verse about the early Muslim community.

9:101.notes: Hypocrites in Medina and around; some confess sins (repentance); zakat/charity collection ordered (9:103); 'Acceptor of Repentance, the Merciful' invokes mercy and repentance; 'Hearing and Knowing' invokes knowledge; 'Aware and Wise' invokes wisdom; 'Say:' command (9:105); divine-decree (awaiting Allah's decree, 9:106).

9:107.notes: Mosque of harm (Masjid al-Dirar) built by hypocrites; contrasted with mosque founded on taqwa; taqwa explicitly named (9:108, 109); 'Knowing and Wise' invokes knowledge and wisdom; hellfire (9:109); plotting implied in building the harm-mosque.

9:111.notes: Allah purchased believers' lives for paradise; promise in Torah, Gospel, Quran — previous-scriptures and the-quran both apply; covenant ('promise binding on Him'); 9:112 lists 'those who praise' (al-hamidun) — praise uttered/described; prayer (those who kneel and bow); repentance (al-ta'ibun).

9:113.notes: Prophet and believers forbidden from seeking forgiveness for polytheists; Abraham's story of disowning his father explicitly named; 'Allah would never lead astray after guiding' invokes guidance; 'knowledge of all things'; 'dominion of heavens and earth' invokes sovereignty.

9:117.notes: Allah redeemed the Prophet, Emigrants, and Supporters in the hour of difficulty; the three left behind redeemed; 'Kind and Compassionate' invokes mercy; 'Redeemer, the Merciful' invokes mercy and repentance.

9:119.notes: Direct address 'O you who believe'; 'Be conscious of Allah' — taqwa explicitly named; 'be with the sincere' — sincerity explicit; 9:120 — people of Medina not to stay behind the Messenger; every deed recorded; 'does not waste the reward' invokes knowledge.

9:122.notes: Not all believers should march out; some stay to study religion and warn; fight nearby disbelievers; 'Allah is with the righteous' — taqwa. The Quran's effect on believers vs. hypocrites (9:124–127) — the-quran explicitly subject.

9:124.notes: When a surah revealed, believers' faith increases; hypocrites' corruption deepens → the-quran. v.125 'they die as unbelievers' → disbelief. v.126 they do not repent → repentance (negatively invoked, but repentance is explicit subject: 'they do not repent'). Hypocrisy of those who slip away.

9:128.notes: Direct description of the Messenger's care for believers; 'compassionate and merciful' toward believers invokes mercy; his role as messenger invokes prophethood-general.

9:129.notes: Direct address — 'Say:'; 'no god except He' — tawhid; 'in Him I have put my trust' — trust-in-god explicitly named; 'Lord of the Sublime Throne' — sovereignty.

11:1.notes: Opens with Alif-Lam-Ra disjoined letters. Section covers the Quran's perfection, tawhid command, call to repentance/forgiveness, God's provision and power, and warning of a grievous Day.

11:5.notes: God's knowledge of hidden hearts and His provision for all creatures on earth.

11:7.notes: Creation in six days; test of conduct; disbelievers' mockery of resurrection; those who are patient and do good deeds earn forgiveness. 'Patience' triggered explicitly in v11: 'those who are patient.'

11:12.notes: Direct address to the Prophet (v12: 'perhaps you wish to disregard…'); qul in v13; challenge to produce ten chapters; reference to Book of Moses as prior scripture; hell for those who deny.

11:18.notes: Contrast between those who fabricate lies about Allah (presented before Lord, cursed, doubled punishment, losers in Hereafter) and believers who do good deeds (inhabitants of Paradise). Angels/witnesses testify on Day of Judgment.

11:25.notes: Noah's mission to his people, their rejection, Noah's defense of the believers among them, divine decree, God's knowledge of souls.

11:35.notes: Single verse: accusation of fabrication answered with 'Say' command; qul present.

11:36.notes: God reveals to Noah no more will believe; command to build ark; mockery by his people; Noah's son drowning; mercy of God invoked ('Forgiving and Merciful' v41). Marriage-and-family: Noah's son and family on the ark.

11:44.notes: Flood ends; Noah calls to his Lord (v45: 'Rabbi…'—uttered supplication) about his son; God's response; Noah's refuge-seeking du'a in v47 ('Rabbi inni a'udhu bika…' plus asking forgiveness—dua-forgiveness and dua-distress both apply); blessings on Noah and communities. Taqwa: 'the future belongs to the pious' (v49).

11:50.notes: Hud's mission to 'Ad; their rejection; Hud's declaration of trust in God (v56: 'I have placed my trust in Allah'); 'Ad destroyed; mercy saves Hud and believers. Trust-in-god explicitly named.

11:61.notes: Salih's mission to Thamud; she-camel as sign/miracle; 'My Lord is Near and Responsive' (v61); Thamud destroyed; Salih and believers saved by mercy. Human creation: 'He initiated you from the earth' (v61). Power: 'Your Lord is the Strong, the Mighty' (v66).

11:69.notes: Angels visit Abraham with glad tidings of Isaac and Jacob; Abraham's wife laughs; angels sent to Lot's people; Abraham intercedes; irreversible punishment decreed. Marriage-and-family: Abraham's wife, Isaac, Jacob as family. 'Mercy and blessings of Allah' v73; 'Praiseworthy and Glorious' → sovereignty/praise, but praise label requires uttered formula—v73 is angels speaking it as statement not uttered hamd formula; tagging mercy for 'rahmat Allah wa barakatuhu'.

11:77.notes: Angels come to Lot; his people rush to commit sins; Lot offers his daughters; people refuse; angels reveal identity and give escape instructions; city destroyed with stones of baked clay. Corruption-on-earth: the people's habitual sins. Chastity-and-boundaries: the sexual transgression context.

11:84.notes: 13 labels — at ceiling. Shuayb's mission to Madyan; prohibition of short-measuring (trade-and-debt, justice-and-witness); 'do not spread corruption in the land' (corruption-on-earth explicitly named v85); Shuayb's trust in Allah (v88: 'In Him I trust'); repentance called for (v90); mercy named (v90: 'My Lord is Merciful'); prior nations Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot referenced by name (v89). Trim candidates if needed: justice-and-witness (subsumed by trade-and-debt context).

11:91.notes: People threaten Shuayb; Shuayb responds that God comprehends all; punishment falls on wrongdoers; Shuayb and believers saved by mercy; Madyan destroyed like Thamud.

11:96.notes: Moses sent with signs to Pharaoh; Pharaoh's people follow him; Pharaoh leads them into Fire on Day of Resurrection; curse follows them in this world and the next.

11:100.notes: Stories of destroyed towns; their gods availed nothing; God's grip when He seizes sinful towns; Day of Judgment described—humanity gathered, miserable in Fire, happy in Paradise. Justice: 'We did not wrong them' (v101).

11:109.notes: Direct address to Prophet (v112: 'be upright as you are commanded'); Moses's scripture and its dispute; God's full repayment of deeds; command to be steadfast with repentants; warning not to incline to wrongdoers or Fire will touch. Muhammad tagged for direct second-person command to him. Repentance: 'those who repented with you' (v112).

11:114.notes: Command to establish prayer at borders of day/night; good deeds expiate bad deeds; 'a reminder for those who remember' (remembrance); patience commanded (v115); corruption on earth named explicitly (v116); God's mercy and will (v118–119); divine decree: 'I will fill Hell with jinn and humans' (v119).

11:120.notes: God narrates messengers' stories to strengthen the Prophet's heart; truth and reminder for believers; 'say to those who do not believe' (qul in v121); direct address to Muhammad implied throughout (v120: 'to strengthen your heart').

11:123.notes: God owns the unseen of heavens and earth; command to worship Him and rely on Him; God never unaware. Trust-in-god: 'rely on Him' explicitly commanded.

12:1.notes: Section opens with Alif-Lam-Ra disjoined letters, then declares the Quran revealed in Arabic. Straightforward revelation-facet section.

12:3.notes: 12 labels at the ceiling. Joseph named (v.4), Jacob implicit ('family of Jacob'), Abraham and Isaac named (v.6). The dream of eleven planets, sun and moon → cosmic-bodies. 'Knowing and Wise' closing formula → knowledge + wisdom. 'Satan is man's sworn enemy' → iblis. The Quran as revelation framing (v.3) → the-quran. Father-son counsel → children-and-parents. God's selection and blessing of Joseph → divine-decree.

12:7.notes: Brothers plot against Joseph out of jealousy over Jacob's favoritism. Envy is the explicit driver ('dearer to our father than we'). Plotting explicitly named ('they plot and scheme'). Joseph, Jacob (as 'father'), and family dynamics all present.

12:11.notes: Brothers deceive Jacob to take Joseph out; Jacob expresses fear. The deception plot continues. Father-son/family dynamic central.

12:15.notes: Brothers cast Joseph into the well; God inspires Joseph that he will one day tell them of this deed (v.15) — a divine inspiration/miracle. The fabricated bloody shirt deception against Jacob. Jacob's response 'patience is beautiful, and Allah is my Help' invokes patience explicitly by name → but the rule-5 trigger is met since 'patience' (sabr) is named in the Arabic/translation. Adding patience. Also 'Allah is my Help' → trust-in-god is borderline but 'on Him I rely' is not yet said — dropping it. Adding patience.

12:19.notes: Joseph pulled from the well by a caravan, hidden as merchandise, sold cheaply. 'Allah was aware of what they did' → knowledge. The commercial transaction (buying/selling) → trade-and-debt.

12:21.notes: Joseph bought by the Egyptian; God establishes him in the land. 'Allah has control over His affairs' → divine-decree. 'To teach him the interpretation of events' → knowledge (God's gift of knowledge). The Egyptian's provision of good care for Joseph → provision (borderline, but God is the ultimate provider here). 'Most people do not know' → knowledge.

12:22.notes: Covers verses 22–29: Joseph given wisdom and knowledge (v.22) → knowledge + wisdom. Seduction attempt by the wife → chastity-and-boundaries. Joseph's refusal citing God → sincerity. Her plotting → plotting. The shirt-evidence scene and the witness judgment (v.26-27) → justice-and-witness. 'Sinners never succeed' and 'He was one of Our loyal servants' (v.24) → sincerity. 'Allah has given me a good home' → provision borderline but not the section's subject. 8 labels, within ceiling.

12:30.notes: City women gossip about the governor's wife (v.30); the banquet scene (v.31-32); Joseph's uttered du'a (v.33): 'My Lord, prison is more desirable to me... unless You turn their scheming away from me' → dua-protection (uttered supplication seeking refuge from scheming). God answers him (v.34) → nearness-and-response. 'He is the Hearer, the Knower' closing formula → knowledge (also nearness-and-response already covers the Hearer aspect). Chastity-and-boundaries: ongoing seduction episode. Plotting: the women's scheming.

12:35.notes: Joseph imprisoned despite signs of innocence (v.35). Two fellow prisoners share their dreams (v.36). Short section bridging the seduction episode to the prison dream-interpretation narrative. Chastity-and-boundaries: imprisonment stems from the seduction affair.

12:37.notes: Joseph interprets dreams via God's gift (v.37) → knowledge. He declares the faith of his forefathers Abraham, Isaac, Jacob (v.38) → all three named. 'It is not for us to associate anything with Allah' → tawhid + shirk (refutation of). 'Are diverse lords better, or Allah, the One, the Supreme?' (v.39) → tawhid. 'You do not worship besides Him except names' (v.40) → shirk. 'Judgment belongs to none but Allah' → sovereignty borderline; tawhid covers it. 'Deniers of the Hereafter' (v.37) → disbelief + day-of-judgment. Prophethood-general: Joseph speaks as a prophet-messenger. 10 labels, within ceiling.

12:43.notes: The king's dream of fat/lean cows (v.43); the court scholars fail to interpret it (v.44); the released prisoner remembers Joseph (v.45). Short narrative bridge. Divine-decree: the dream itself is part of God's unfolding plan for Joseph.

12:46.notes: Joseph interprets the king's dream (v.46-49): seven years of abundance, seven of hardship, then relief. The interpretation is a gift from God → knowledge. The agricultural plan (storing grain) → provision. The 'year of relief' when people press (juice/oil) → provision.

12:50.notes: Joseph insists on clearing his name before leaving prison (v.50); women testify he did no wrong (v.51); governor's wife confesses (v.51); Joseph's integrity established → justice-and-witness. 'Allah does not guide the scheming of the betrayers' (v.52) → knowledge. 'The soul commands evil except those on whom my Lord has mercy' (v.53) → mercy. 'My Lord is Forgiving and Merciful' closing → mercy. Chastity-and-boundaries: resolution of the seduction affair. Sincerity: Joseph's loyalty ('I did not betray him in secret').

12:54.notes: Joseph appointed by the king over the storehouses (v.54-56). 'We touch with Our mercy whomever We will' (v.56) → mercy. 'We never waste the reward of the righteous' → righteous-conduct borderline but 'righteous' is named. 'Reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and observed piety' (v.57) → taqwa explicitly named + paradise (Hereafter reward). Joseph's role as storekeeper → provision. Adding righteous-conduct since 'righteous' is named explicitly as the section's subject.

12:58.notes: Joseph's brothers arrive in Egypt; he recognizes them but they do not recognize him (v.58). He demands they bring their other brother (v.59-60). He secretly returns their goods (v.62). Family reunion dynamics → children-and-parents. The unfolding of God's plan → divine-decree.

12:63.notes: Brothers return to Jacob; he demands a pledge before sending Benjamin (v.66) → covenant. 'Allah is the Best Guardian, He is the Most Merciful' (v.64) → mercy borderline but 'Most Merciful of the merciful' is a divine attribute claim → adding mercy. 'I cannot avail you anything against Allah. The decision rests only with Allah. On Him I rely' (v.67) → trust-in-god explicitly named + sovereignty ('The decision rests only with Allah'). Jacob's knowledge from God (v.68) → knowledge. Family dynamics throughout → children-and-parents.

12:69.notes: Joseph reveals himself to his brother Benjamin (v.69); plants the cup in Benjamin's bag (v.70); the accusation of theft (v.70-75). The brothers swear they are not thieves (v.73) → justice-and-witness. The planting of the cup is Joseph's stratagem → plotting (but this is divine plotting/plan rather than sinful scheming; still, the label 'plotting' covers divine counter-plans per taxonomy). Family dynamics → children-and-parents.

12:76.notes: God's plan to keep Benjamin with Joseph via the cup (v.76). 'Thus We devised a plan for Joseph' → divine-decree + plotting (God's plan). 'We elevate by degrees whomever We will' → sovereignty. 'Above every person of knowledge there is one more learned' → knowledge.

12:77.notes: Brothers slander Joseph (v.77); Joseph's eldest refuses to return (v.80); brothers instructed to go back to Jacob (v.81-82). 'Your father received a pledge before Allah' (v.80) → covenant. 'He is the Best of Deciders' (v.80) → justice/sovereignty — adding sovereignty. Jacob's response 'Patience is a virtue' (v.83 in next section, but this section ends at v.82). The eldest's staying → family dynamics. 'Allah is Aware of what you allege' (v.77) → knowledge. Covers vv.77-82; patience not yet named here — it appears in 12:83. Removing patience, adding justice-and-witness (the brothers' testimony v.81).

12:83.notes: Jacob says 'Patience is a virtue' (v.83) → patience explicitly named. 'He is the Knowing, the Wise' (v.83) → knowledge + wisdom. Jacob's grief over Joseph (v.84). 'I only complain of my grief and sorrow to Allah' (v.86) — this is an uttered expression directed to God but is it a formal du'a? It is more of a statement than a supplication; not tagging dua-distress. 'Do not despair of Allah's comfort' (v.87) → trust-in-god (reliance on God). 'None despairs of Allah's comfort except the disbelieving people' (v.87) → disbelief explicitly named.

12:88.notes: Brothers return in distress asking for charity (v.88) → zakat-and-charity. Joseph reveals himself (v.89-90). 'He who practices piety and patience—Allah never fails to reward the righteous' (v.90) → taqwa + patience both explicitly named. Brothers confess wrongdoing (v.91) → repentance (implicit acknowledgment; 'We were definitely in the wrong'). Joseph forgives them (v.92): 'Allah will forgive you. He is the Most Merciful of the merciful' → mercy. Jacob's sight-restoration via the shirt (v.93) → miracles (a miraculous healing). Adding miracles.

12:94.notes: Jacob's promise to pray for forgiveness (v.98) is an intent to make du'a rather than a fully uttered supplication; dua-forgiveness tagged with caution. 'He is the Forgiver, the Most Merciful' closing → mercy confirmed.

12:99.notes: Family reunited in Egypt (v.99-100); Joseph's dream fulfilled (v.100) → divine-decree. 'My Lord is Most Kind towards whomever He wills. He is the All-knowing, the Most Wise' (v.100) → knowledge + wisdom. 'After the devil had sown conflict between me and my brothers' (v.100) → iblis. 'Initiator of the heavens and the earth' (v.101) → creation-of-heavens-earth. Joseph's uttered du'a (v.101): 'My Lord, You have given me some authority... Receive my soul in submission, and unite me with the righteous' → this is a full uttered supplication asking for a good death and union with the righteous → dua-distress is not quite right; it is more of a du'a of gratitude and for a good end. Using dua-gratitude for the thankful portion and noting the request for a good death. Sovereignty: 'You have given me some authority' → sovereignty. Replacing dua-distress with dua-gratitude.

12:102.notes: 11 labels. 'This is news from the past that We reveal to you' (v.102) — direct address to the Prophet → muhammad. 'You were not present with them' → direct 2nd person address to the Prophet. The Quran as revelation → the-quran. 'Most people are not believers' (v.103) → disbelief. 'It is only a reminder for all mankind' (v.104) → mankind. 'Signs in the heavens and the earth' (v.105) → natural-signs. 'Most of them associate others' (v.106) → shirk. 'The Hour will come upon them suddenly' (v.107) → day-of-judgment. 'Say, This is my way' (v.108) → qul-statements. 'Glory be to Allah' (v.108) → praise (subhan Allah uttered). Prophethood-general: the Prophet's da'wah mission described.

12:109.notes: Only men inspired from towns sent as prophets (v.109) → prophethood-general. 'Have they not roamed the earth and seen the consequences for those before them?' (v.109) → punishment-of-past-nations. 'The Home of the Hereafter is better for the righteous' → paradise + taqwa (piety named). 'Until the messengers despaired... Our help came to them' (v.110) → power (God's might saving the messengers). 'Our severity is not averted from the guilty people' → punishment-of-past-nations reinforced. Disbelievers: 'the guilty people' who are destroyed.

12:111.notes: Closing verse of the surah. 'In their stories is a lesson' → the narrative as Quranic teaching → the-quran. 'A confirmation of what came before it' → previous-scriptures. 'A detailed explanation of all things' → the-quran. 'Guidance, and mercy for people who believe' → guidance (explicitly named as the subject) + mercy + believers. Prophethood-general: the stories of the prophets affirmed as true revelation.

13:1.notes: 12 labels at the ceiling. Section opens with Alif-Lam-Mim-Ra (disjoined letters), asserts the Qur'an as truth (the-quran), describes most people not believing (disbelievers, mankind). Verses 2–4 describe Allah raising heavens, throne, sun and moon (creation-of-heavens-earth, cosmic-bodies, sovereignty, power, creation), rivers, fruits, night/day (natural-signs, provision), and 'everything by measure' running to an appointed term (divine-decree). Trim candidates if needed: provision (implicit in fruits/rivers), divine-decree (the 'specified period' reading).

13:5.notes: Verse 5: disbelievers mock resurrection ('when we become dust') → resurrection, disbelievers, hell. Verse 6: 'examples have passed away before them' → punishment-of-past-nations; 'your Lord is full of forgiveness' → mercy. Verse 7: 'you are only a warner' → prophethood-general; disbelievers demand a miracle → denial-of-revelation.

13:8.notes: Verses 8–9: Allah knows what every womb bears, everything is by measure, Knower of the unseen and visible, Grand, Supreme → knowledge, divine-decree, power. Verse 10: He knows the hidden and public speech → knowledge. Verse 11: guardian angels accompany each person (angels); 'Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves' → guidance (God as source/withholder of guidance); His will is irresistible → power, divine-decree. Angels are explicitly mentioned as the protecting succession.

13:12.notes: Verses 12–13: lightning, heavy clouds, thunder glorifying Allah, angels in awe, thunderbolts → natural-signs, angels, power; 'they argue about Allah' while He is 'Tremendous in might' → sovereignty, disbelievers. Verse 14: 'To Him belongs the call to truth'; those called besides Him cannot respond → tawhid, shirk. Verse 15: everything in heavens and earth prostrates to Allah willingly or unwillingly → sovereignty, tawhid.

13:16.notes: Verse 16: multiple 'Say:' (qul) commands → qul-statements; 'Allah is the Creator of all things, the One, the Irresistible' → tawhid, creation, sovereignty; associates ascribed to Allah who created nothing → shirk; blind/seeing, darkness/light analogies → guidance. Verse 17: rain and riverbeds parable of truth vs. falsehood → natural-signs. Verse 18: those who respond to their Lord get the best; those who don't face 'the worst reckoning' and Hell → reckoning, hell, disbelievers.

13:19.notes: 12 labels at the ceiling. Verse 19: contrast between the seeing (believers) and the blind (disbelievers). Verses 20–22: description of believers fulfilling Allah's covenant (covenant), joining what Allah commanded to be joined (practical-ethics), fearing the reckoning, practicing patience (patience — explicitly named: 'patiently seek'), establishing prayer (prayer), spending from provision (zakat-and-charity, provision). Verse 23–24: Everlasting Gardens, angels entering on them (paradise, angels). Verse 25: those who violate covenant and spread corruption on earth → corruption-on-earth, hell. Verse 26: Allah expands and restricts provision → provision. Trim candidates if needed: practical-ethics (subsumed by covenant + prayer + charity enumeration).

13:27.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Verse 27: disbelievers demand a miracle (denial-of-revelation); 'Say, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever repents' (qul-statements, guidance, divine-decree, repentance). Verse 28: believers' hearts find comfort in dhikr — 'remembrance of Allah' explicitly named → remembrance, believers. Verse 29: believers doing righteous deeds get happiness → believers. Verse 30: 'Thus We sent you' → prophethood-general; reciting revelation to them → the-quran; they deny the Benevolent One → disbelievers, mankind; 'Say, He is my Lord…in Him I trust, to Him is my repentance' → qul-statements, trust-in-god, repentance. Verse 31: even if the Quran moved mountains they would not believe; 'had Allah willed He would have guided all humanity' → divine-decree, guidance, mankind. Trim candidates: prophethood-general (derivable from context), the-quran (secondary to guidance theme).

13:32.notes: Verse 32: messengers before were ridiculed then seized → mockery, prophethood-general, punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 33: 'Is He who is watchful over the deeds of every soul?' → knowledge; they ascribe associates to Allah → shirk; 'the scheming of those who disbelieve is made to appear good to them' → plotting; 'whomever Allah misguides has no guide' → disbelievers. Verse 34: torment in this life and the hereafter is harsher → hell.

13:35.notes: 12 labels at the ceiling. Verse 35: description of paradise promised to the muttaqun (paradise, taqwa); disbelievers get the Fire (hell, disbelievers). Verse 36: People of the Book rejoice at the revelation; some factions reject parts (people-of-the-book, the-quran); 'Say, I am commanded to worship Allah and never associate anything with Him' → qul-statements, tawhid, shirk. Verse 37: revealed as an Arabic code → the-quran, language tagged implicitly. Verse 38: messengers sent before with wives and offspring; no messenger brings a sign except by Allah's permission; 'for every era is a scripture' → prophethood-general, divine-decree. Verse 39: Allah abolishes and affirms what He wills, with Him is the source of Scripture → divine-decree, the-quran. Verse 40: 'Ours is the reckoning' → reckoning. Verse 41–42: God's sovereign judgment; those who plotted before, entire plan belongs to Allah; disbelievers will know the Ultimate Home → divine-decree, plotting (straddling with 13:32 section).

13:43.notes: Disbelievers say 'you are not a messenger' → disbelievers, prophethood-general, denial-of-revelation implicitly. 'Say, Allah is sufficient witness' → qul-statements, knowledge. 'Whoever has knowledge of the Scripture' → people-of-the-book (per Ibn Kathir, this refers to those with knowledge of the Torah/Gospel who recognize the Prophet), previous-scriptures. denial-of-revelation is the implicit context but not explicitly named — keeping people-of-the-book and previous-scriptures as the cleaner tags.

14:1.notes: Alif-Lam-Ra opens the section → disjoined-letters. 'A Scripture that We revealed to you, that you may bring humanity from darkness to light' → the-quran, guidance, mankind. 'Path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy' → sovereignty. 'The Mighty, the Wise' closing → wisdom. 'Woe to the disbelievers' → disbelievers. 'We never sent any messenger except in the language of his people' → prophethood-general, language-and-revelation-terms.

14:5.notes: 'We sent Moses with Our signs' → moses, prophethood-general, miracles. 'Bring your people out of darkness into light' → guidance, children-of-israel. 'He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh' → pharaoh, children-of-israel, punishment-of-past-nations. 'Every patient and thankful person' / 'If you give thanks, I will grant you increase' → gratitude (shukr explicitly named as the subject of God's proclamation). Patience is mentioned in passing ('patient and thankful') but gratitude is made the explicit subject of the Lord's proclamation in v.7.

14:9.notes: Noah, 'Ad, Thamud named → noah, ad, thamud. 'Their messengers came to them with the clear proofs, but they rejected' → prophethood-general, denial-of-revelation, disbelievers, punishment-of-past-nations. 'Maker of the heavens and the earth' (v.10) → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'In Allah let the faithful put their trust' and 'we will persevere' (v.11–12) → trust-in-god and patience (both explicitly named as the subject of the messengers' exhortation).

14:13.notes: 'Those who disbelieved said to their messengers, we will expel you' → disbelievers, prophethood-general. 'We will destroy the wrongdoers / We will settle you in the land after them. That is for him who fears My Majesty' → taqwa (God-consciousness explicitly invoked as the criterion for inheriting the earth). 'Beyond him lies Hell' → hell. The destruction of the oppressors aligns with punishment-of-past-nations. 'Disbelieve' and 'disbelief' are the explicit state of the antagonists → disbelief.

14:19.notes: 'Allah created the heavens and the earth' → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'If He wills, He can do away with you, and bring a new creation' → power. Scene of the Day of Judgment, all standing before Allah → day-of-judgment. Satan's speech disowning those who followed him → iblis. 'They set up associates / I reject your associating with me' (v.22) → shirk. Wrongdoers will have a torment → hell. 'Those who believed … admitted into gardens' → believers, paradise. The accounting exchange between followers and leaders → reckoning.

14:24.notes: The parable of the good tree and bad tree is explicitly addressed to 'the people' (v.25 'Allah presents the parables to the people') → mankind. The good word / bad word parable is classically interpreted as faith vs. disbelief → believers, disbelievers. 'Allah gives firmness to those who believe with the firm word' → believers, guidance. 'Allah leads the wicked astray' → disbelievers. The 'good word' parable is closely linked to the Qur'an itself in tafsir, but on the surface text the-quran is borderline; marking medium confidence for that label. Omitting the-quran and keeping at medium for the parable-as-guidance reading.

14:28.notes: 'Those who exchanged the blessing of Allah with blasphemy' → disbelievers. 'They set up rivals to Allah' → shirk. 'Hell — they will roast in it' → hell. 'Say, Enjoy yourselves; your destination is the Fire' and 'Tell My servants who have believed' → qul-statements (two qul imperatives present). 'Perform the prayers and give from what We have given them' → prayer, zakat-and-charity. 'Before a Day comes' → day-of-judgment. Believers addressed as the recipients of the command → believers.

14:32.notes: 'Allah created the heavens and the earth' → creation-of-heavens-earth, creation. 'Sends down water from the sky, produces fruits for your sustenance' → provision, natural-signs. 'Ships sailing through the sea, rivers' → natural-signs. 'Sun and the moon … night and the day' → cosmic-bodies. 'He has given you something of all what you asked; if you count Allah's blessings you cannot enumerate them' → provision. 'The human being is unfair and ungrateful' — shukr/gratitude is explicitly invoked (its absence named as the human failing) → gratitude. Universal address implied for all humanity → mankind.

14:35.notes: 16 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Abraham's extended prayer → abraham. 'Ishmael and Isaac' named (v.39) → ishmael, isaac. 'Keep me and my sons from worshiping idols' → dua-protection, shirk. 'Settled … by Your Sacred House' → sacred-mosque-and-qiblah. 'Make the hearts incline toward them and provide them with fruits' → dua-family-offspring, provision. 'You know what we conceal and what we reveal' → knowledge. 'You are Forgiving and Merciful' (v.36) → mercy. 'Praise be to Allah … the Hearer of Prayers' (v.39) → praise, nearness-and-response. 'Make me one who performs the prayer' → prayer, dua-family-offspring (already tagged). 'Forgive me, and my parents, and the believers, on the Day the Reckoning' → dua-forgiveness, believers, reckoning. Trim candidates (lowest priority first): reckoning (implied by dua-forgiveness context), nearness-and-response (subsumed by the prayer theme), believers (only implicit via 'forgive the believers').

14:42.notes: 'Do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do' → knowledge. 'He only defers them until a Day' → day-of-judgment. 'Warn mankind of the Day' → mankind, prophethood-general (the warning-and-messenger function). 'The wicked will say, Our Lord, defer us' → disbelievers. 'You inhabited the homes of those who wronged themselves' → punishment-of-past-nations. 'They planned their plans … even if their plans can eliminate mountains' → plotting.

14:47.notes: 'Allah will not break His promise to His messengers' → prophethood-general. 'Allah is Strong, Able to Avenge' → sovereignty, justice. 'The earth is changed into another earth … before Allah, the One, the Irresistible' → day-of-judgment, tawhid. 'Sinners bound together in chains … garments of tar, Fire covering their faces' → hell, disbelievers. 'That Allah may repay each soul according to what it has earned. Allah is Quick in reckoning' → reckoning, justice.

14:52.notes: 'This is a proclamation for mankind' → mankind, the-quran. 'That they may be warned' → prophethood-general. 'Know that He is One God' → tawhid. 'People of understanding may remember' — remembrance is only mentioned in passing as a purpose clause, not as the section's explicit subject, so remembrance label is withheld per rule 5.

15:1.notes: Section opens with Alif-Lam-Ra disjoined letters → disjoined-letters. The Quran is named as subject ('these are the verses of the Book; a Quran that makes things clear') → the-quran. Disbelievers wish they had been Muslims → disbelievers. They mock the Prophet and demand angels → mockery, angels. God's response about not sending angels and the preservation of the Message → denial-of-revelation, prophethood-general. 'No nation can bring its time forward' → divine-decree. Past nations mocked and were destroyed → punishment-of-past-nations. 9 labels.

15:16.notes: Constellations in the sky → cosmic-bodies. Spreading the earth, mountains, plants → creation-of-heavens-earth, natural-signs. Livelihoods for creatures → provision. Devils driven away from heaven → iblis. 'With Us are its stores, sent down in precise measure' → divine-decree. 'We give life and cause death' → death-and-dying. 'We know those who go forward and those who lag behind' → knowledge. Closing 'He is the Wise, the Knowing' → wisdom, knowledge. 9 labels.

15:26.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Creation of human from clay → adam, human-creation. Creation of jinn from fire → jinn. Angels prostrate; Iblis refuses → angels, iblis. Iblis's refusal is explicit arrogance ('I am not about to prostrate') → arrogance. Iblis reprieved until Day of Judgment → day-of-judgment. Hell described with seven doors → hell. The righteous (muttaqin) in gardens → paradise, taqwa. Iblis excepts 'sincere servants' (mukhlasin) → sincerity (the word is explicit in the Arabic). Closing 'I am the Forgiver, the Merciful' → mercy. Every label independently triggered.

15:51.notes: The guests of Abraham arrive with good news → abraham, angels. They announce a knowledgeable son → mercy ('who despairs of his Lord's mercy but the lost?'). They are sent to Lot's sinful people → lot. 'We have determined that she will be of those who lag behind' → divine-decree. 5 labels.

15:61.notes: Envoys arrive at Lot's family → lot, angels. The people of the town come seeking indecency; Lot pleads with them → lot. The Blast destroys them → punishment-of-past-nations. 'Surely in that is a sign for the believers' → believers. 'We informed him of Our decree' → divine-decree. 5 labels.

15:78.notes: People of the Woods (Ashab al-Aykah = people of Madyan/Shuayb) → madyan. People of the Rock (al-Hijr = Thamud) → thamud. Both rejected messengers → prophethood-general, denial-of-revelation. Both were punished → punishment-of-past-nations. 5 labels.

15:85.notes: 11 labels. Direct second-person address to the Prophet throughout ('your Lord', 'We have given you', 'do not extend your eyes', 'lower your wing to the believers', 'your heart is strained') → muhammad. 'We did not create the heavens and the earth … except with truth' → creation-of-heavens-earth, creation. 'The Hour is coming' → day-of-judgment. 'Seven of the pairs and the Grand Quran' → the-quran. 'Those who made the Quran obsolete' → denial-of-revelation implicitly, but 'By your Lord we will question them all' → reckoning. 'Turn away from the polytheists' → polytheists. 'Lower your wing to the believers' → believers. 'We are enough for you against the mockers' → mockery. 'Your Lord is the All-Knowing Creator' → knowledge. 'And say, I am the clear warner' → qul-statements. 'Glorify the praise of your Lord' is a command, not an uttered praise, so praise label withheld per §5.6b.

15:99.notes: Single verse commanding worship of the Lord until certainty comes. No named figures, no du'a uttered, no eschatological description beyond the reference to certainty (death). The explicit instruction to worship → prayer (as the primary worship act commanded). Short section; single label is appropriate per rule 2 ('single-label sections are common in short surahs').

16:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with 'Subḥānahu' (Glory be to Him) → praise. Verse 2 sends angels with tawhid message → angels + tawhid + prophethood-general. Verses 3-4 creation of heavens/earth and human from drop → creation-of-heavens-earth + human-creation. Verses 5-8 livestock, horses, mules as provision and natural signs → natural-signs + provision. Verse 7 closing 'Clement and Merciful' → mercy. Verse 9 guidance from Allah → guidance. Shirk refuted throughout ('exalted above what they associate') → shirk. 11 labels — within ceiling.

16:10.notes: Verses 10-13: rain, vegetation, grains, olives, palms, grapes → natural-signs + provision. Verse 12: night, day, sun, moon, stars → cosmic-bodies. Verse 14: sea, fresh meat, ornaments, ships → natural-signs + provision. Verse 15: mountains, rivers, roads → natural-signs. Verse 17: 'Is He who creates like him who does not create?' → tawhid + creation.

16:18.notes: Verse 18: 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Verse 19: 'Allah knows what you hide and disclose' → knowledge. Verse 20: those invoked besides Allah create nothing → tawhid + shirk. Verse 22: 'Your God is one God' → tawhid; disbelievers whose hearts are in denial and arrogant → disbelievers + arrogance. Verse 23: 'He does not like the arrogant' confirms arrogance as explicit subject → arrogance. Provision angle from verse 18 ('favors of Allah') → provision.

16:24.notes: Verse 24: 'Legends of the ancients' = denial of revelation → denial-of-revelation. Verse 25: loads on Day of Resurrection → day-of-judgment + reckoning. Verse 26: those before them schemed → plotting + punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 27: Day of Resurrection disgrace → day-of-judgment; 'disbelievers' named explicitly → disbelievers. Verses 28-29: angels taking souls + 'Enter gates of Hell' → angels + hell + arrogance ('residence of the arrogant').

16:30.notes: Verse 30: 'those who maintained piety' (muttaqun) addressed explicitly → taqwa. Verses 30-31: Paradise described for the pious → paradise. Verse 32: angels taking the wholesome → angels. Verse 33: 'command of your Lord to arrive; those before them did likewise' → punishment-of-past-nations + day-of-judgment. Verse 34: 'what they used to ridicule engulfed them' → mockery. Believers implied throughout → believers; disbelievers contrasted implicitly → disbelievers.

16:35.notes: Verse 35: polytheists speak → polytheists + shirk. 'Are the messengers responsible for anything but clear communication?' → prophethood-general. Verse 36: sent a messenger to every community → prophethood-general. Verse 37: 'Allah does not guide those who misguide' → guidance. Verse 38: 'Allah will not resurrect anyone who dies' + rebuttal → resurrection. Verse 40: 'Be and it becomes' = divine creative decree → divine-decree. Verses 41-42: those who emigrated → migration; 'endure patiently and put their trust' → patience + trust-in-god (both named explicitly).

16:43.notes: Verse 43: 'We did not send before you except men whom We inspired' → prophethood-general. 'Ask the people of knowledge' suggests prior scriptures → previous-scriptures. Verse 44: 'We revealed to you the Reminder [Dhikr] that you may clarify to the people' — direct second-person address to the Prophet and references the Quran → muhammad + the-quran + mankind ('the people').

16:45.notes: Verses 45-47: those who scheme evils warned of punishment — 'plotting' triggered by 'scheme evils' context from v.26 straddle and explicit here → plotting. 'Your Lord is Gentle and Merciful' → mercy. Verses 48-50: shadows prostrating, everything in heavens/earth bowing to Allah including angels → natural-signs + angels. 'Everything bows down' → sovereignty. Power of Allah to seize plotters → power.

16:51.notes: Verse 51: 'Do not take two gods; He is only One God' → tawhid. Verse 52: 'To Him belongs everything in the heavens and the earth' → sovereignty. Verse 53: 'Whatever blessing you have is from Allah' → provision. Verses 54-55: when harm lifted, some associate others with their Lord → shirk + disbelief.

16:56.notes: Verse 56: allocating share of provision to false gods → shirk + polytheists. Verse 57: attributing daughters to Allah ('Subḥānahu') → shirk + tawhid. Verses 58-59: female infanticide — burying daughters in dust → children-and-parents (direct parent-child conduct issue). Verse 60: 'He is the Mighty, the Wise' → wisdom; disbelievers set bad example → disbelievers + disbelief. Verse 61: Allah postpones mankind until appointed time → day-of-judgment. Verse 62: 'for them is the Fire' → hell implied; knowledge attribute invoked via contrast → knowledge. 10 labels — within ceiling.

16:63.notes: Verse 63: Satan made deeds appear alluring → iblis; messengers sent to prior communities → prophethood-general + punishment-of-past-nations; 'painful punishment' → disbelievers. Verse 64: 'We revealed to you the Scripture … guidance and mercy for people who believe' → the-quran + mercy + guidance + believers.

16:65.notes: Verse 65: rain revives the earth after death → natural-signs. Verse 66: milk from cattle → natural-signs + provision. Verse 67: date-palms and grapevines → natural-signs + provision. Verses 68-69: the bee inspired by Allah, produces healing fluid → natural-signs + creation. 'Healing for the people' → mankind. All framed as signs of God the Creator.

16:70.notes: Verse 70: Allah created you then takes you away, some to senility — 'Allah is Omniscient and Omnipotent' → human-creation + death-and-dying + knowledge + power. Verse 71: differential provision → provision. Verse 72: Allah gave you mates and children and good things → marriage-and-family + provision. Verses 73-74: they serve what possesses no provision — 'Allah knows and you do not' → shirk + tawhid + knowledge.

16:75.notes: Verse 75: parable of bonded slave vs. free man; 'Al-ḥamdu lillāh' uttered → praise. Verse 76: dumb man vs. one who commands justice parable → tawhid (idols vs. God). Verse 77: 'Allah has power over everything' → power; 'unseen of heavens and earth' → knowledge; 'the Hour is only as twinkling of eye' → day-of-judgment. Verse 78: brought out of mothers' wombs, given hearing/sight/hearts → human-creation; 'that you may give thanks' (shukr explicit) → gratitude. Verse 79: birds flying held by none but Allah → natural-signs. Verses 80-81: hides, wool, shade, mountains, garments → provision + natural-signs. 9 labels.

16:84.notes: Verse 84: witness from every community on the Day → day-of-judgment + reckoning + prophethood-general. Verse 85: punishment not lightened for wrongdoers → hell. Verse 86: idolaters see their associates → polytheists + shirk. Verse 88: 'We will add punishment … on account of the mischief they used to make' → corruption-on-earth + hell + disbelievers.

16:89.notes: Single verse. 'Bring you as a witness against these' — direct address to the Prophet → muhammad + prophethood-general. Witness from every community → day-of-judgment. 'We have revealed to you the Book … guidance, mercy and good news for those who submit' → the-quran + mercy + guidance + believers.

16:90.notes: Verse 90: 'Allah commands justice, and goodness, and generosity … forbids immorality, injustice, and oppression' — justice named explicitly as divine command → justice + practical-ethics + righteous-conduct (righteousness explicitly instructed). Verse 91: 'Fulfill Allah's covenant … do not break your oaths' — explicit → covenant + oaths-and-vows; 'Allah knows what you do' → knowledge. Verse 92: oath-breaking parable, Day of Resurrection clarification → day-of-judgment.

16:93.notes: Verse 93: 'He leaves astray whom He wills, and He guides whom He wills' → guidance + divine-decree; 'you will surely be questioned' → reckoning. Verse 94: 'do not use oaths to deceive' → oaths-and-vows. Verse 95: 'do not exchange Allah's covenant for small price' → covenant. Verse 96: 'We will reward those who are patient' — sabr named explicitly → patience. Verse 97: 'Whoever works righteousness … while being a believer' → righteous-conduct + believers.

16:98.notes: 15 labels — over the 12-label ceiling. This is a long section (verses 98–113) covering multiple themes. Verse 98: seek refuge from Satan when reading Quran → iblis + the-quran. Verse 99: believers who trust in their Lord → believers + trust-in-god. Verse 100: Satan's authority over those who associate → iblis + shirk (implied). Verse 101: substitution of verses, 'You are an impostor' → denial-of-revelation + the-quran. Verse 102: 'Say, The Holy Spirit has brought it down' → qul-statements + language-and-revelation-terms. Verse 103: foreign tongue vs. clear Arabic → language-and-revelation-terms. Verse 104: those who don't believe in Allah's revelations → disbelievers + denial-of-revelation. Verse 106: renouncing faith after believing → disbelief + disbelievers. Verse 110: emigrated after being persecuted, then struggled → migration; 'Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Verse 111: Day of Judgment every soul pleading → reckoning + day-of-judgment. Verse 112-113: parable of ungrateful town, messenger denied, punishment → punishment-of-past-nations. Trim candidates: shirk (not explicitly named, only implied via v.100), previous-creations-destroyed (subsumed by punishment-of-past-nations), day-of-judgment (subsumed by reckoning in v.111 context).

16:114.notes: Verse 114: 'Eat of the lawful and good things … be thankful for Allah's blessings' — shukr (thankfulness) explicitly commanded → gratitude + food-and-dietary. Verse 115: forbidden foods listed (carrion, blood, swine, consecrated to other than Allah) → food-and-dietary; 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Verse 116: do not fabricate halal/haram → food-and-dietary. Verse 118: 'For those who are Jews, We have prohibited…' → people-of-the-book. Verse 119: those who repent and reform → repentance; 'Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. Verse 117: brief enjoyment then punishment → disbelief (for those fabricating against Allah).

16:120.notes: Verses 120-122: Abraham described — 'devoted to Allah, a monotheist, not of polytheists, thankful for His blessings, guided to straight path' → abraham + tawhid + gratitude (shukr named explicitly) + guidance; contrasted with polytheists → polytheists. Verse 123: 'We inspired you: Follow the religion of Abraham' — direct address to the Prophet → muhammad + abraham + tawhid. Verse 124: 'The Sabbath was decreed only for those who differed about it' — Jews referenced → people-of-the-book + ritual-calendar-and-sacred-time; 'Your Lord will judge on Day of Resurrection' → day-of-judgment.

16:125.notes: Verse 125: 'Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good advice' — direct address to the Prophet → muhammad; wisdom named explicitly → wisdom; 'Your Lord is aware of those who stray / are guided' → knowledge + guidance. Verse 126: retaliate proportionately, 'if you resort to patience — it is better' → patience (sabr named explicitly). Verse 127: 'Be patient … your patience is solely from Allah … do not be stressed by their schemes' → patience + trust-in-god; 'their schemes' → plotting.

16:128.notes: Single verse. 'Allah is with those who are righteous (ittaqaw = taqwa) and those who are virtuous (muhsinun)' — both taqwa and righteousness named explicitly → taqwa + righteous-conduct + believers (the muttaqun/muhsinun = believers generously tagged).

17:1.notes: Verse 1: Night Journey (Isra) — 'Glory to Him' is an uttered praise formula (subhan), triggering praise. Muhammad is the servant journeyed; Sacred Mosque and Farthest Mosque named. 'He is the Listener, the Beholder' = knowledge. Verse 2: Moses named, Scripture given to Children of Israel. Verse 3: Noah named, his descendants addressed. 12 labels at the ceiling.

17:4.notes: The passage foretells two corruptions of the Children of Israel and their punishments. 'We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers' triggers hell and disbelievers. 'Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you' triggers mercy. The decree about punishment is framed as inscribed judgment — divine-decree. Corruption explicitly named.

17:9.notes: Verse 9: Quran guides to what is upright — the-quran and guidance are explicitly the subject. Believers promised great reward — paradise. Disbelievers get painful punishment — hell. Verses 12–14: Night and day as two signs — cosmic-bodies. Day of Resurrection and the open book of deeds — day-of-judgment and reckoning.

17:15.notes: Verse 15: No punishment until a messenger is sent — prophethood-general and guidance as explicit subjects. Verse 16: Destruction of towns — punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 17: Generations destroyed after Noah (Noah mentioned only categorically, not named in translation). Verses 18–21: Hell for those who want only the fleeting life, paradise/reward for the Hereafter-seekers; God provides to both — provision. The contrast of worldly vs. Hereafter ranks closes with divine-decree logic.

17:22.notes: Verse 22: Do not set up another god — tawhid/shirk. Verses 23–25: Honor parents, say kind words, lower the wing of humility — children-and-parents, practical-ethics, humility. Verse 24 contains an uttered du'a: 'My Lord, have mercy on them' — this is dua-forgiveness (asking mercy/forgiveness for parents). Verse 25: 'He is Forgiving to the obedient' — mercy. Verse 26: Give the relative, poor, and wayfarer their rights; do not squander — zakat-and-charity, practical-ethics. Verse 27: Extravagant are brethren of devils — iblis, greed-and-miserliness. Verse 28: Say words of comfort. Verse 29–30: Balance in spending; God expands/restricts provision — provision, knowledge. 12 labels at ceiling.

17:31.notes: Verse 31: Do not kill children for fear of poverty — children-and-parents, provision (We provide for them). Verse 32: Do not come near adultery — chastity-and-boundaries. Verse 33: Do not kill the soul — anger-and-violence, justice-and-witness (authority of next of kin). Verse 34: Do not approach orphan's property; honor pledge — orphan-care, oaths-and-vows. Verse 35: Give full measure and just scales — justice-and-witness. Verse 36: Do not pursue what you have no knowledge of — practical-ethics. Verse 37: Do not walk proudly on earth — arrogance (pride/kibr explicitly referenced by 'walking proudly'). Verse 38: All these evils are disliked.

17:39.notes: Verse 39: 'Some of the wisdom your Lord has revealed' — wisdom is explicitly named. Do not set up another god — tawhid/shirk. Hell threatened. Verse 40: Do you think God has chosen daughters from among the angels? — angels named; the question rebukes shirk and false attribution to God.

17:41.notes: Verse 41: Quran explained in various ways — the-quran; they deny — denial-of-revelation/disbelief. Verse 42: 'Say' (qul) — qul-statements; if there were other gods they would seek the Lord of the Throne — tawhid/shirk, sovereignty. Verse 43: 'Subhanahu' — praise uttered. Verse 44: Seven heavens and earth praise Him — creation-of-heavens-earth; 'Forbearing and Forgiving' — mercy. Note: qul-statements applies but is subsumed here under the tawhid argument; including it would push to 10 — adding it.

17:45.notes: Verses 45–46: Reading Quran — the-quran; barrier placed between Prophet and disbelievers — disbelievers, denial-of-revelation. Verse 47: 'We know well' — knowledge. Verses 49–52: Disbelievers deny resurrection — resurrection. Verses 50–51: Multiple qul ('Say') commands — qul-statements. 'The One who originated you the first time' — creation, power. Verse 52: Day when He calls you — resurrection. prophethood-general implied by context of the Prophet being addressed and his role discussed.

17:53.notes: Verse 53: Tell servants to say what is best; Satan sows discord — iblis, practical-ethics. Verse 54: God knows best; mercy or punishment — knowledge, mercy. Verse 55: 'We gave David the Psalms' — david, previous-scriptures; prophethood-general (ranking of prophets). Verse 56: Qul — qul-statements; call on those you claim besides Him, they have no power — tawhid, shirk. Verse 57: They seek means to their Lord, fear His punishment — mercy (hoping for mercy), punishment. Verse 58: Every city will be destroyed before the Day of Resurrection — punishment-of-past-nations, day-of-judgment. 12 labels at ceiling.

17:59.notes: Verse 59: Thamud named and the she-camel miracle cited — thamud, miracles. Ancients denied signs — denial-of-revelation. Signs sent only to instill reverence. Verse 60: Direct address to Muhammad ('We said to you') — muhammad. 'Your Lord encompasses humanity' — mankind, power. The vision shown to him as a test for people — divine-decree.

17:61.notes: Verse 61: Angels commanded to bow to Adam — adam, angels. Iblis refuses — iblis. Verse 62: Iblis vows to bring Adam's descendants under his sway — plotting, arrogance (implied by his refusal based on superiority; 'You honored him more than me'). Verse 63: Hell is the reward for those who follow Iblis — hell. Verse 64: Iblis's methods of enticing humans — plotting. Verse 65: 'My devotees — you have no authority over them.' Human creation referenced: 'created from mud' — human-creation. Day of Resurrection referenced — day-of-judgment.

17:66.notes: Verse 66: God propels ships for you to seek His bounty — provision, mercy, natural-signs. Verse 67: When harm at sea, you call on Him alone; when saved, you turn away — tawhid (they revert to calling on Him alone in distress), disbelief (being ungrateful/thankless). Verse 68–69: Power to cause land to cave in or hurricane — power. Verse 70: 'We have honored the Children of Adam' — mankind; provided them with good things — provision. The human being contrasted with rest of creation.

17:71.notes: Verses 71–72: Day when every people called with their leader; records given — day-of-judgment, reckoning. Verses 73–77: Direct address to Muhammad about those who tried to lure him from revelation — muhammad. 'Had We not given you stability' — divine-decree. They almost expelled him from the land — migration (expulsion motif, though not hijrah per se). Verse 77: Tradition of messengers before him — prophethood-general. migration label is borderline here; the expulsion attempt relates to Islamic history rather than hijrah as a legal/moral concept. Confidence medium for migration tag.

17:78.notes: Verse 78: Establish prayer at decline of sun through night; Quran at dawn — prayer, ritual-calendar-and-sacred-time, the-quran. Verse 79: Night vigil prayer for the Prophet — prayer, muhammad. Verse 80: Uttered du'a: 'My Lord, lead me in through an entry of truth…' — dua-protection (seeking a supporting power and safe passage). Verse 81: Qul ('And say, the truth has come') — qul-statements.

17:82.notes: Verse 82: Quran is healing and mercy for believers — the-quran, believers, mercy. Increases wrongdoers in loss — disbelief. Verse 83: Human ingratitude when blessed — (no concrete concept label triggered beyond disbelief/ingratitude; gratitude would require explicit shukr). Verse 84: Qul ('Say, each does according to his disposition') — qul-statements. 'Your Lord knows best who is better guided' — knowledge, guidance.

17:85.notes: Verse 85: Question about the Spirit; Qul — qul-statements; 'The Spirit belongs to the domain of my Lord; you were given only little knowledge' — knowledge. Verse 86–87: If God willed He could take away the revelation — the-quran, mercy ('except through a mercy from your Lord'). Verse 88: Qul — qul-statements; mankind and jinn together could not produce the like of this Quran — challenge-to-produce, mankind, jinn. Verses 89–96: People deny and demand signs — denial-of-revelation. Verse 93: 'Glory be to my Lord. Am I anything but a human messenger?' — prophethood-general, praise (subhana Rabbi uttered). Verse 95: Qul — qul-statements.

17:97.notes: Verse 97: Whom God guides is guided; whom He leads astray — guidance. Gathered on Day of Resurrection blind, dumb, deaf — day-of-judgment, resurrection. Abode is Hell — hell. Verse 98: Because they denied revelations and rejected resurrection — disbelief. Verse 99: God who created heavens and earth is able to recreate — power, creation-of-heavens-earth. Verse 100: Qul — qul-statements; if you possessed God's mercy-treasuries you would withhold — greed-and-miserliness, provision.

17:101.notes: Verse 101: Moses given nine clear signs; Pharaoh accuses him of being bewitched — moses, pharaoh, children-of-israel, miracles, denial-of-revelation. Verse 102: Moses responds to Pharaoh — prophethood-general. Verse 103: Pharaoh tried to expel them; God drowned him and all with him — punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 104: Children of Israel told to inhabit the land; when the Hereafter's promise arrives — children-of-israel, divine-decree.

17:105.notes: Verse 105: Sent down in truth; Muhammad sent as bearer of good news and warner — the-quran, prophethood-general, muhammad. Verse 106: Quran revealed gradually for recitation over time — the-quran, language-and-revelation-terms. Verse 107: Qul — qul-statements; those given knowledge before it (people of earlier scriptures) fall prostrating — people-of-the-book. Verse 108: They say 'Glory to our Lord' — praise (subhana Rabbina uttered). Verse 109: They fall weeping; it adds to their humility — humility (explicitly named: 'khushuan').

17:110.notes: Verse 110: Qul — qul-statements. 'Call Him Allah or call Him the Most Merciful; whichever name you use, to Him belong the Best Names' — tawhid (oneness affirmed through His names), mercy (Ar-Rahman invoked). Instructions on the volume of prayer — prayer. 'To Him belong the Best Names' — knowledge (attribute of God knowing and encompassing all names).

17:111.notes: Verse 111: Qul — qul-statements. 'Praise be to Allah who has not begotten a son, nor has He a partner in sovereignty' — tawhid (no son, no partner), sovereignty (mulk), praise (al-hamdu lillah uttered explicitly). 'Glorify Him constantly' reinforces praise.

18:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with 'al-hamdu lillah' → praise. The section introduces the Quran's purpose (warn/glad-tidings) → the-quran + prophethood-general. Verse 4 warns those who say 'Allah has begotten a son' → shirk + tawhid. Verse 6 is direct address to the Prophet about his grief → muhammad. Believers promised excellent reward (paradise implied) and severe punishment warned (hell implied). 11 labels, within ceiling.

18:7.notes: Verses 7–8 describe the earth as an ornament for testing → natural-signs. Verse 9 introduces the People of the Cave as wondrous signs → companions-of-the-cave + miracles. Verse 10 contains an uttered supplication 'Rabbana atina min ladunka rahmatan wa hayyi' → dua-guidance (asking for mercy and guidance from Allah). Verse 11–12 describe God sealing their ears and awakening them → divine-decree. 'Mercy from Yourself' → mercy. 'Allah knows' → knowledge.

18:13.notes: Verses 13–14: youths believed in their Lord, Allah increased them in guidance → companions-of-the-cave, guidance, believers. Verse 14 contains their declaration of tawhid ('Our Lord is Lord of heavens and earth, we will call on no god besides Him') → tawhid. Verse 15: their people took other gods → shirk. Verse 16: call to withdraw and Allah will spread His mercy → mercy. No uttered du'a (verse 14 is a declaration, not a supplication), so no dua label.

18:17.notes: The sun veering from the cave → cosmic-bodies. The miraculous preservation in the cave with sun described as 'one of Allah's wonders' → miracles + natural-signs. 'He whom Allah guides is truly guided; he whom He misguides finds no directing friend' → guidance. Still within the cave narrative → companions-of-the-cave.

18:19.notes: The youths awaken and discuss how long they stayed — 'Your Lord knows best how long you stayed' → knowledge. They send one for food/provision → provision. The whole awakening is part of God's decree → divine-decree. Still core companions-of-the-cave narrative.

18:21.notes: Verse 21: Allah reveals them so people know 'the promise of Allah is true and the Hour is not in doubt' → day-of-judgment, divine-decree. Building a place of worship over them → mosques-and-sacred-places. Verse 22 contains 'Qul rabbi a'lamu' → qul-statements. 'Allah knows their number' → knowledge. 'He shares His sovereignty with no one' (v.26) → sovereignty.

18:27.notes: Verse 27: 'Recite what was revealed to you from the Book of your Lord' → the-quran. Verse 28: keep company with those who call on their Lord morning and evening → believers, remembrance. Verse 29 contains 'Qul al-haqqu min rabbikum' → qul-statements; also describes Hell for wrongdoers → hell; and disbelievers warned → disbelievers. Verse 30–31: believers doing righteous deeds → believers; Gardens of Eden → paradise. Sending of messengers implied → prophethood-general.

18:32.notes: The parable of two men: the wealthy man is arrogant and denies the Hour (verse 36) and doubts his Lord → disbelievers (in conduct). His believing friend rebukes him: 'Are you ungrateful to Him who created you from dust, then sperm-drop?' → human-creation. 'I never associate with my Lord anyone' → tawhid; the unbeliever implicitly commits shirk. The gardens and their destruction → natural-signs. Verse 44: 'Authority belongs to Allah the True' → sovereignty. The destruction by decree → divine-decree. The moral lesson and advice of the believing friend → practical-ethics. 8 labels.

18:45.notes: Verse 45: parable of water/plants → natural-signs; 'Allah has absolute power over everything' → power. Verses 47–49: Day when mountains move, earth emerges, all gathered → day-of-judgment + resurrection. The Book placed, deeds enumerated → reckoning. 'Your Lord does not wrong anyone' → justice. Sinners (criminals) fearful → disbelievers.

18:50.notes: Verse 50: command to angels to bow to Adam → adam + angels. Iblis refused, being of jinn → iblis + jinn. 'Will you take him and his offspring as lords instead of Me?' → shirk. 'Evil is the exchange for the wrongdoers' → disbelievers (the wrongdoers here). Verse 51: 'I did not call them to witness the creation of the heavens and the earth' → creation-of-heavens-earth. Verse 52–53: sinners see the Fire → hell.

18:54.notes: Verse 54: 'We have elaborated in this Quran for the people every kind of example' → the-quran + mankind. Verse 55: people prevented from accepting faith → disbelievers; mention of 'precedent of the ancients' → punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 56: messengers sent as warners → prophethood-general; disbelievers argue with falsehood and take verses as a joke → denial-of-revelation + mockery. Verse 58: 'Your Lord is the Forgiver, Possessor of Mercy' → mercy (closing attribute). Verse 59: destroyed towns → punishment-of-past-nations (already tagged). 8 labels.

18:60.notes: Moses named explicitly → moses. They seek a servant whom Allah taught 'knowledge from Our Own' (verse 65) → knowledge. 'Blessed with mercy from Us' → mercy. Moses asks to follow and be taught guidance → this is essentially a request for knowledge/guidance. Verse 66: Moses asks to follow to be taught guidance → dua-knowledge-wisdom (the request qualifies as an uttered request for knowledge/wisdom: 'May I follow you so that you may teach me some of the guidance you were taught?'). Verse 67–69: Al-Khidr warns about patience; Moses pledges patience → patience (the word 'patient/sabr' is named explicitly in verses 67–69). 5 labels.

18:71.notes: The three actions of Al-Khidr and their explanations → narrative centered on moses. Verse 79: holing the boat to protect poor workers from a tyrant king → justice (protecting the oppressed), divine-decree. Verse 80–81: killing the boy to protect his believing parents from his future oppression → divine-decree, mercy ('mercy from your Lord'). Verse 82: repairing the wall for two orphaned boys so their treasure is preserved → orphan-care, divine-decree, mercy. The entire section is about knowledge beyond apparent understanding → knowledge. 6 labels.

18:83.notes: Verse 83: 'They ask you about Zul-Qarnain. Say...' → dhul-qarnayn + qul-statements. Verse 84: 'We established him on earth and gave him all kinds of means' → power. Verses 86–88: Dhul-Qarnayn addresses people at sunset — punish wrongdoers (→ hell/punishment) and reward the righteous (→ paradise); his judgment → justice. Verse 91: 'We had full knowledge of what he had' → knowledge. 7 labels.

18:92.notes: Verse 94: 'Gog and Magog are spreading chaos in the land' → corruption-on-earth. Dhul-Qarnayn builds the barrier → dhul-qarnayn. 'What my Lord has empowered me with is better' → power. The barrier construction itself is a feat of power/knowledge-application. Verse 91 carried forward: God's encompassing knowledge → knowledge. 4 labels.

18:98.notes: Verse 98: 'This is a mercy from my Lord; when the promise of my Lord comes, He will turn it into rubble' → mercy + divine-decree. Verse 99: 'the Trumpet will be blown and We will gather them' → resurrection + day-of-judgment. Signs of Gog/Magog and cosmic dissolution → signs-of-the-hour. Verse 100: Hell presented to disbelievers → hell + disbelievers. Still part of Dhul-Qarnayn narrative (his speech closes at v.98) → dhul-qarnayn. 8 labels.

18:103.notes: Verse 103: 'Say, shall We inform you of the greatest losers...' → qul-statements. Verse 104: those whose efforts are misguided thinking they do well → disbelievers. Verse 105: 'they rejected the communications of their Lord... works are in vain... on Day of Resurrection We will consider them of no weight' → day-of-judgment + reckoning. Verse 106: Hell for their disbelief and mockery of messengers → hell + mockery. Verse 107: believers who do righteous deeds get Gardens of Paradise → paradise + believers. 8 labels.

18:109.notes: Single verse. 'Say, if the ocean were ink for the words of my Lord...' → qul-statements + the-quran. The inexhaustibility of God's words → knowledge (God's infinite knowledge manifested in His words). 3 labels — short section, appropriate.

18:110.notes: Verse 110: 'Say, I am only a human being like you, being inspired that your god is One God' → qul-statements + tawhid + prophethood-general (Muhammad declares his humanness and the revelation). 'Never associate anyone with the service of his Lord' → shirk (warning against it). 'Whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him work righteousness' → day-of-judgment (meeting the Lord = eschaton) + righteous-conduct (the explicit instruction to 'work righteousness' makes this a concrete trigger per rule 5). 6 labels.

20:1.notes: Opens with disjoined letters Tā-Hā. Section covers the Quran's purpose as reminder, God's creation of heavens and earth, His settling on the Throne, His omniscience of the secret and hidden, and closes with the assertion of tawhid and the Beautiful Names.

20:9.notes: Moses's call at the fire; God reveals Himself with 'I am Allah, there is no god but I'; commands prayer for God's remembrance; mentions the Hour coming; warns against those who deny it and follow desire.

20:17.notes: The staff and glowing hand miracles; God sends Moses to Pharaoh; Moses utters an extended du'a asking for ease, eloquence, and Aaron as helper so they may glorify and remember God much. 'That we may glorify You much' is uttered praise within the du'a. dua-knowledge-wisdom applies because the du'a includes untying the tongue/speech for comprehension.

20:36.notes: God grants Moses's request, recounts His past favors: Moses placed in the chest, cast into the river, returned to his mother, tested, years in Madyan — all framed as divine providence. Sent to Pharaoh with signs; commanded not to neglect God's remembrance. The narrative of Moses's infant life is recalled.

20:45.notes: Moses and Aaron's fear expressed as a du'a-like address ('Lord, we fear...'); God responds with reassurance 'I am with you, I hear and I see' — nearness-and-response. They are instructed to approach Pharaoh and call for release of Children of Israel. Peace promised to those who follow guidance.

20:49.notes: Pharaoh's question 'Who is your Lord?'; Moses answers with God as Creator who gives everything its existence and guides it; knowledge of prior generations is with God; earth made as habitat, rain, plants, livestock as provision and signs; closes with 'from it We created you, into it We return you, and from it bring you out again' — covers human creation and resurrection/death cycle.

20:56.notes: Pharaoh shown all signs, denies and refuses; accuses Moses of sorcery; plans a counter-sorcery contest; sets the Day of the Festival as the appointment. Denial of revelation, sorcery accusation, and plotting by Pharaoh are all present.

20:60.notes: Pharaoh assembles his plan; Moses warns the magicians against fabricating lies against Allah; the magicians' ropes and sticks appear to move by magic; God reassures Moses he is uppermost and commands him to throw his staff to swallow their work. Sorcery contest narrative.

20:70.notes: The magicians prostrate and declare belief in the Lord of Aaron and Moses; Pharaoh threatens mutilation and crucifixion; the magicians declare 'We have believed in our Lord so that He may forgive us our sins' — this is an uttered dua-forgiveness; they contrast God (Better and more Lasting) with Pharaoh; hell and paradise contrasted in verses 74-76 which are part of this narrative close.

20:74.notes: Explicit contrast: whoever comes to God guilty → Hell (neither dies nor lives); whoever comes as a believing doer of righteousness → highest ranks and Gardens of Perpetuity. Righteous conduct is named explicitly ('worked righteousness') as the criterion.

20:77.notes: God commands Moses to lead the Children of Israel across the sea by night; Pharaoh pursues with his troops and is overwhelmed by the sea; Pharaoh misled his people. Exodus miracle; drowning of Pharaoh as punishment of a past nation.

20:80.notes: Direct address 'O Children of Israel' — delivered from enemy, promised at the right side of the Mount, given manna and quails (provision); warned not to be excessive lest God's wrath descends; God declares His forgiveness for those who repent, believe, act righteously, and remain guided.

20:83.notes: Moses rushes ahead to God; the Samarian misleads the people; Moses returns angry; the golden calf worshipped as a god — explicit shirk; Aaron had warned them. Anger and disappointment of Moses; shirk of the calf-worship. The Samarian is named but has no taxonomy label; no suggestedNewLabel as he is a minor figure not warranting a standalone label.

20:92.notes: Moses confronts Aaron; Aaron explains his fear of causing division; Moses questions the Samarian; Samarian confesses and is punished (exile); Moses declares that only Allah is their god — explicit tawhid assertion 'there is no other god... He comprehends everything in knowledge.' Shirk is refuted and tawhid affirmed.

20:99.notes: God narrates past reports as a form of Quranic revelation; those who turn away carry a burden on the Day of Resurrection; the Trumpet is blown, sinners gathered 'blue'; they murmur about how long they lingered — resurrection and reckoning scene.

20:105.notes: Contains 'Say' (qul) command in v.105 about the mountains.
