Mountains crumbled on that Day; voices hushed before the Merciful; intercession only for those He permits; God knows what is before and behind; faces humbled before the Living, the Eternal; righteous believers fear neither injustice nor grievance; closes with the Quran revealed in Arabic with diversified warnings so they may be righteous (taqwa explicitly named as purpose).

20:114.notes: Opens with exaltation of God the True King and instruction not to rush the Quran; contains uttered du'a 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge' — dua-knowledge-wisdom. Then the Adam narrative: covenant with Adam, angels commanded to prostrate, Iblis refuses, Adam warned about Satan as enemy, Garden's blessings described, Satan whispers, Adam and wife eat from the tree, Adam disobeys and falls, then is pardoned and guided. Marriage-and-family applies because Adam and his wife are the subject (the couple in the Garden). Divine-decree because Adam's covenant, forgetting, and eventual repentance are framed as ordained.

20:123.notes: God commands Adam and his adversary to descend; promises guidance for followers, confined life and resurrection-blind for those who turn away; the scene of the blind man on Judgment Day asking why; God answers that signs were forgotten; past generations destroyed as warning. previous-creations-destroyed applies to v.128 ('how many generations before them We destroyed').

20:129.notes: Direct address to the Prophet — 'bear patiently what they say', 'celebrate the praises of your Lord' (uttered praise formula implied by 'sabbih bi-hamd'), times of prayer/glorification specified before sunrise and sunset; told not to extend glance toward worldly splendor; commanded to exhort his family to pray; 'the good ending is that for righteousness' (taqwa explicitly named). Muhammad addressed directly in second person throughout, so muhammad label applies. Patience is explicitly commanded ('fāṣbir').

20:133.notes: Disbelievers demand a miracle; response appeals to miracles already in former scriptures; counterfactual: if destroyed before the messenger came they would complain no messenger was sent. Previous-scriptures referenced ('the former scriptures'). Denial of revelation and demand for signs are the subject.

20:135.notes: Single verse with explicit 'Say' (qul) command; declares all are waiting and the rightly-guided on the straight path will be known. qul-statements applies; guidance is the explicit subject ('who is rightly-guided', 'people of the straight path').

21:1.notes: Verse 4 has 'My Lord knows what is said in heaven and earth; He is the Hearer, the Knower' — tagging knowledge. Verse 7 affirms prophethood-general (only men were sent). Verse 9 references destruction of past extravagant peoples. The accusations of sorcery/poetry/dreams in v3/5 trigger denial-of-revelation and mockery.

21:10.notes: Section opens with the Book sent down as a message (the-quran), then depicts God crushing guilty towns (punishment-of-past-nations, power).

21:16.notes: Verses 16-17 assert the sky and earth were not created for amusement — wisdom of creation. Verse 22 'subhana Allah' — praise uttered (though in a refutation context, the tasbih is explicit). Verse 19-20 describe angels praising night and day. Sovereignty: 'To Him belongs everyone in heavens and earth.' Tawhid: the argument that multiple gods would cause ruin (v22) is in the next section; this section focuses on creation purpose and angels' worship.

21:21.notes: Verse 22 'subhana Allah, Lord of the Throne' — praise uttered. Verse 24 contains 'qul' — tagging qul-statements. Angels discussed extensively (v26-28) including intercession limits. Verse 25 states all messengers were inspired with tawhid — prophethood-general. Verse 29 threatens hell for any who claims divinity beside Allah.

21:30.notes: Verse 30 — heavens and earth torn apart, water as origin of life (creation-of-heavens-earth, natural-signs, human-creation implied via 'every living thing from water'). Verse 33 — night, day, sun, moon in orbits (cosmic-bodies). Verse 34-35 — no immortality, every soul tastes death (death-and-dying). Verse 36 — disbelievers mock the Prophet (mockery). Tawhid implicit in the cosmological argument against polytheism.

21:37.notes: Verse 37 'human was created of haste' — human-creation (nature of human). Verses 38-40 describe the coming punishment/fire that disbelievers mock (hell, day-of-judgment, signs-of-the-hour).

21:41.notes: Verse 41 — messengers before were ridiculed (mockery, prophethood-general, punishment-of-past-nations). Verses 42 and 45 contain 'qul' — qul-statements. Verse 42 mentions 'the Merciful' — mercy. Verse 47 — scales of justice set up for Day of Resurrection, no soul wronged even a mustard-seed's weight (reckoning, justice, day-of-judgment).

21:48.notes: Verses 48-49 — the Criterion/Torah given to Moses and Aaron as illumination for the righteous (muttaqin) who fear their Lord. Verse 50 — 'this blessed message We revealed' refers to the Qur'an. Taqwa: 'those who fear their Lord in private' is the explicit subject of v49. Believers: the muttaqun are the implied audience.

21:51.notes: Long section covering Abraham confronting idol-worship (shirk, tawhid), his declaration that the Lord created the heavens and earth (creation-of-heavens-earth), his smashing of idols (miracles — God's protection of him), and the people's plot to burn him (plotting). God making fire cool and safe for Abraham is a miracle. 9 labels within ceiling.

21:71.notes: Abraham and Lot delivered to blessed land. Isaac and Jacob granted. v73 — inspired to do good works, establish prayer, give charity. Lot saved from the town of abominations (punishment-of-past-nations). v75 — admitted into God's mercy.

21:76.notes: Noah called and was answered (nearness-and-response). His people denied God's signs and were drowned (punishment-of-past-nations, disbelievers). Noah and family saved by God's mercy.

21:78.notes: David and Solomon's judgment — wisdom and knowledge given to both. Mountains and birds subjected to sing praises with David — praise uttered (tasbih). Wind subjected to Solomon. Devils (jinn) diving for Solomon — miracles. Natural-signs: mountains and birds as subjected creation. v81 'We are aware of everything' — knowledge.

21:83.notes: 17 labels — over the 12-label ceiling. Rich section covering multiple prophets. Job's uttered cry (dua-distress: 'Great harm has afflicted me, you are the Most Merciful' — uttered supplication). Zechariah's uttered cry for an heir (dua-family-offspring: 'My Lord, do not leave me alone'). Jonah's uttered tasbih in the darkness (fits dua-distress as cry in darkness). Ishmael, Idris, Dhul-Kifl described as steadfast (patience — explicitly named: 'each was one of the steadfast'). Mary and her son mentioned v91 — mary, jesus, human-creation (spirit breathed into her), angels implicit. John given to Zechariah. God's mercy and response throughout (mercy, nearness-and-response). Believers: 'Thus We save the faithful' (v88). Trim candidates if needed: angels (not explicitly named in this section, only implicit via 'spirit'), human-creation (borderline — 'breathed Our spirit' does invoke it).

21:92.notes: Verse 92 — 'this community is one, I am your Lord, worship Me' (tawhid, mankind addressed). Verses 93 — factions (disbelief context). v94 — righteous deeds recorded (reckoning). v95-96 — destroyed towns and Gog & Magog released (signs-of-the-hour, punishment-of-past-nations). v97-100 — Day of Judgment, disbelievers in horror, they and their idols fuel for hell (day-of-judgment, hell, shirk, disbelievers).

21:101.notes: v101-102 — the righteous kept away from hell, in paradise forever. v103 — angels receive them on the Day. v104 — heaven folded like a scroll, creation repeated as God's promise (creation-of-heavens-earth, power, divine-decree — 'a promise binding on Us, We will act').

21:105.notes: v105 — reference to the Psalms (Zabur) and the Reminder (previous-scriptures). v107 — 'We did not send you except as mercy to mankind' — direct address to Muhammad (muhammad), mercy. v108 contains 'qul' — qul-statements, tawhid ('your God is One God'). v109 contains 'qul' again. v110 — 'He knows what is said openly and what you conceal' (knowledge).

21:112.notes: Single verse. 'My Lord, judge with justice' — uttered supplication asking for justice (closest to dua-distress as a cry against oppressors; justice is explicitly named). 'Our Lord is the Gracious, Whose help is sought' — mercy (Ar-Rahman). Justice named explicitly.

22:1.notes: Opens with 'O people' (yā ayyuhā an-nās) → mankind. Taqwa explicitly commanded ('be conscious of your Lord'). The quaking of the Hour and its terror described → day-of-judgment, signs-of-the-hour. Devil leads followers to the Blaze → iblis, hell. Arguing about Allah without knowledge = disbelievers. Decree for the devil's followers → divine-decree.

22:5.notes: Opens with 'O people' → mankind. Stages of human creation from dust/drop/clot/lump → human-creation. Argument from creation for the reality of resurrection → resurrection. Rain reviving dead earth as analogical sign → natural-signs. 'He is Capable of everything' → power. Death and old age mentioned → death-and-dying.

22:7.notes: Hour is coming with certainty; Allah resurrects those in graves → resurrection, day-of-judgment. The arguer without knowledge leads others astray → disbelievers. Torment of burning on Day of Resurrection → hell. 'Allah is not unjust to the servants' → justice. Section addresses a type among 'the people' broadly → mankind.

22:11.notes: Describes a type among 'the people' → mankind. Invoking what can neither harm nor benefit = idolatry/shirk. Losing this world and the next → disbelief. Believers in good deeds admitted to gardens → paradise. 'Allah guides whomever He wills' → guidance. 'Thus We revealed it as clarifying signs' explicitly refers to the Qur'an as revelation → the-quran.

22:17.notes: Lists believers, Jews, Sabeans, Christians, Zoroastrians, Polytheists → believers, people-of-the-book, sabeans, polytheists. Allah judges between them on Day of Resurrection → day-of-judgment. 'Allah is witness to all things' → knowledge. Prostration of sun, moon, stars → cosmic-bodies. Mountains, trees, animals prostrating → natural-signs. Garments of fire and scalding water for disbelievers → hell. Believers in gardens with gold and silk → paradise. Tawhid is the implicit backdrop of the judgment between groups. 11 labels — at the ceiling; all independently justified.

22:25.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. Disbelievers blocking Sacred Mosque → disbelievers, sacred-mosque-and-qiblah. Sacred Mosque designated for all mankind → mankind. Abraham shown location of the House → abraham. Purifying for prayer rites (circling, standing, bowing, prostrating) → prayer. Call to pilgrimage → hajj-and-pilgrimage. Appointed days / ritual calendar → ritual-calendar-and-sacred-time. Feeding the poor and animal livestock → zakat-and-charity, food-and-dietary. 'Fulfill their vows' → oaths-and-vows. Ancient House / Sacred Mosque → mosques-and-sacred-places. 'Do not associate anything with Me' → shirk.

22:30.notes: Veneration of Allah's sanctities → hajj-and-pilgrimage. 'It is from the piety of the hearts' — taqwa explicitly named → taqwa. 'Stay away from the abomination of idols' → shirk. Livestock permitted except what is recited → food-and-dietary. 'Your God is One God, so to Him submit' → tawhid. 'Performing the prayer' explicitly mentioned → prayer. 'Spend from what We have provided' → zakat-and-charity. 'Those who endure what has befallen them' — patience (sabr) explicitly depicted → patience. 'Hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned' → remembrance. Ancient House and its circuits → mosques-and-sacred-places. 10 labels — within ceiling.

22:36.notes: Animal offerings as emblems of Allah at Hajj → hajj-and-pilgrimage. Eat from them and feed the contented and beggar → food-and-dietary, zakat-and-charity. 'Pronounce Allah's name upon them' → remembrance. 'That you may be thankful' — shukr explicitly named → gratitude.

22:37.notes: Flesh/blood of offerings does not reach Allah — only taqwa does; taqwa explicitly named → taqwa, hajj-and-pilgrimage. 'Glorify Allah for guiding you' general praise but not an uttered formula. Permission to fight given to those wronged → war-and-treaties. Those evicted from homes → migration. Monasteries, churches, synagogues, mosques protected → mosques-and-sacred-places. 'Observe the prayer' → prayer. 'Give regular charity' → zakat-and-charity. 'Allah is Strong and Mighty' → power. 'Allah defends those who believe' → believers.

22:42.notes: People of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, Abraham, Lot, Madyan, Moses all named → noah, ad, thamud, abraham, lot, madyan, moses. All denied their prophets → disbelievers, punishment-of-past-nations. Ruined towns with stilled wells and lofty mansions → previous-creations-destroyed. Pattern of prophet-denial → prophethood-general. 11 labels — within ceiling.

22:47.notes: Disbelievers ask to hasten punishment → disbelievers. 'Allah never breaks His promise'; a day with the Lord = thousand years → day-of-judgment, divine-decree. Reprieve then seizure of unjust towns → punishment-of-past-nations. 'To Me is the destination' implies ultimate justice → justice.

22:49.notes: 14 labels — over 12 ceiling. 'Say, O people, I am only a plain warner' → qul-statements, mankind, prophethood-general. Forgiveness and generous provision for believers → paradise, believers. Inmates of Hell for those striving against revelations → hell, disbelievers. Satan interfering in prophets' wishes; Allah nullifies it → iblis, the-quran. 'Allah is Omniscient and Wise' → knowledge, wisdom. Allah guides believers to straight path → guidance. 'Sovereignty on that Day belongs to Allah' → sovereignty, day-of-judgment. Trim candidates: wisdom (closing formula, lower priority), sovereignty (brief mention at close).

22:58.notes: Those who emigrate in Allah's cause then die → migration, believers. Allah provides fine provisions and admits them pleasingly → paradise, provision. 'Allah is Knowing and Clement' → knowledge. Fair retaliation and Allah's support → justice. 'Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving' → mercy. Night/day alternation as sign → cosmic-bodies. 'Allah is the Reality' and what they invoke besides Him is vanity → tawhid, shirk. 'Allah is the Sublime, the Grand / Strong and Powerful' → power. 11 labels — within ceiling.

22:63.notes: Rain sent down greening the earth → natural-signs, provision. 'Allah is Kind and Aware' → knowledge. 'To Him belongs everything in the heavens and earth' → sovereignty. Ships sailing, sky held up → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'Allah is Gracious towards the people, Most Merciful' → mercy, mankind. Life then death then revival → death-and-dying. 'The human being is unappreciative' (kafur) → disbelief.

22:67.notes: Every nation given acts of devotion → prophethood-general. 'Do not let them dispute with you' — direct address to the Prophet → muhammad. 'You are upon a straight guidance' → guidance. 'Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection' → day-of-judgment. 'Allah knows everything in the heavens and the earth … in a book' → knowledge, divine-decree.

22:71.notes: Worshipping things besides Allah without warrant → shirk, disbelievers. 'O people! A parable' → mankind. 'Say, Shall I inform you …' → qul-statements. Idols cannot create a fly — powerlessness argument for tawhid → tawhid. Allah's strength versus weakness of idols → power. Disbelievers react with disgust to clear verses → denial-of-revelation. 'The Fire! Allah has promised it to those who disbelieve' → hell.

22:75.notes: Allah chooses messengers from angels and people → angels, prophethood-general. 'Allah is Hearing and Seeing; He knows what is before and behind them' → knowledge. 'O you who believe! Kneel, prostrate, worship your Lord' → believers, prayer.

22:78.notes: Addressed to believers with 'strive for Allah' → believers, war-and-treaties. 'The faith of your father Abraham' → abraham. Abraham named Muslims before → prophethood-general. 'So that the Messenger may be a witness over you' — substantive reference to the Prophet's role → muhammad. 'Pray regularly and give regular charity' → prayer, zakat-and-charity. 'Cleave to Allah. He is your Protector' → trust-in-god. 'He has chosen you' and the naming covenant → covenant. Taqwa implicit in 'He has not burdened you in religion' and the overall call to submission, but the explicit trigger here is obedience/worship; holding back on taqwa as it is not explicitly named — confidence remains high. 9 labels — within ceiling.

23:1.notes: Section explicitly names taqwa-adjacent virtues as its subject (humility in prayer named directly: 'humble in their prayers'); righteous-conduct triggered by the explicit enumeration of good deeds as the section's structural subject. Chastity named explicitly ('safeguard their chastity'). Covenant triggered by 'faithful to their trusts and pledges'. Paradise named at close.

23:12.notes: 'Most Blessed is Allah, the Best of Creators' — tabāraka utterance triggers praise. Section addresses all humans universally about their own creation and death/resurrection, triggering mankind. Creation label for God as Creator.

23:17.notes: Seven pathways above = creation of heavens; rain, gardens, palms, vines, olive tree, livestock = natural signs and provision. 'We are Able to take it away' triggers power.

23:23.notes: Noah's da'wah and his people's rejection. 'My Lord, help me, for they have rejected me' (v.26) = uttered du'a in distress → dua-distress. 'Praise be to Allah who has saved us' (v.28) = uttered praise formula → praise. 'My Lord, land me with a blessed landing' (v.29) = uttered supplication for protection/blessing → dua-protection. Ark construction under divine inspiration = miracles. 'Worship Allah, you have no deity other than Him' = tawhid. Drowning of the wrongdoers = punishment-of-past-nations.

23:31.notes: Generic post-Noah generation narrative: messenger sent, people deny resurrection (v.35–37), call messenger a liar, are destroyed by the Blast. 'No nation can advance its time' (v.43) = divine-decree. Denial of resurrection explicitly stated by the people. Successive messengers pattern = prophethood-general.

23:45.notes: Moses and Aaron sent with signs to Pharaoh who turned arrogant (v.46, 'they turned arrogant' — explicit trigger for arrogance). Pharaoh's people destroyed (v.48). Torah given to Moses (v.49) = previous-scriptures. Mary's son and his mother made a sign (v.50) = mary, jesus, miracles.

23:51.notes: Address to messengers (v.51–52); warning about sectarian division; description of true believers (v.57–61) who avoid shirk (v.59, explicit). 'I am aware of what you do' = knowledge. 'We never burden any soul beyond its capacity…a record that tells the truth' = reckoning. Arrogance triggered explicitly at v.67: 'Arrogant towards it.' Taqwa triggered at v.52: 'fear Me' (command for taqwa as explicit subject). Denial of revelation triggered by v.66–67.

23:68.notes: Section challenges those who deny the Qur'an (v.68–70); 'He brought them the truth' = prophethood-general; 'The revenue from your Lord is better, and He is the Best of providers' = provision and mercy; 'You are inviting them to a straight path' = guidance (explicit: straight path named); 'they would still blindly persist in their defiance' = corruption-on-earth (fasad implied by persistent transgression after mercy — borderline; confidence remains high as the section explicitly describes persistent wrongdoing despite mercy and suffering). the-quran triggered by pondering 'the Word' and recited verses.

23:78.notes: 13 labels — over 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: human-creation (creation covers it here; v.78–79 are about producing faculties, not embryology stages), cosmic-bodies (night/day cycle mentioned at v.80 — borderline; keep for straddling). Full justification: hearing/eyesight/hearts produced by God = creation + human-creation; night/day alternation = cosmic-bodies; resurrection denial by people then qul-rhetorical questions = qul-statements (multiple 'Say:' imperatives v.84–89); sovereignty ('dominion of all things', 'Lord of seven heavens and Throne' = sovereignty); knowledge ('Knower of the hidden and manifest' = knowledge); power ('We are surely Able' = power); tawhid ('Allah has never begotten a son, nor is there any god besides Him'); shirk ('far above what they associate'); 'Glory be to Allah' = praise (subhān formula v.91); dua-protection (v.97–98 'My Lord, I seek refuge with You from the urgings of the devils' = uttered supplication). Trim candidates: human-creation (subsumed by creation for this section's argument).

23:99.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. Death scene at v.99–100; barzakh; Horn blown (resurrection); scales of deeds (reckoning); Hell described v.103–104; dialogue in Hell about rejected revelations (disbelievers); believers who were mocked quoted at v.109 ('Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us, and have mercy on us; You are the Best of the merciful') = uttered dua-forgiveness + mercy; mockery: 'you made them a target of ridicule…you used to laugh at them' (v.110) = explicit trigger; patience: 'I have rewarded them for their endurance' (v.111) = patience named explicitly as the reason for reward; day-of-judgment = overarching frame of judgment dialogue.

23:116.notes: v.116: 'Exalted is Allah, the Ruler, the Real. There is no god except He, the Lord of the Noble Throne' = tawhid + sovereignty. v.117: invoking another god = shirk; reckoning with his Lord; disbelievers will not succeed = disbelief.

23:118.notes: Single verse: 'Say, My Lord, forgive and have mercy, for You are the Best of the merciful.' = qul-statement containing uttered dua-forgiveness. 'Best of the merciful' = mercy attribute.

24:1.notes: Verse 1 declares this a revealed surah with clear verses (the-quran). Verses 2-3 legislate flogging for adultery and marriage restrictions (chastity-and-boundaries). Verse 4 legislates punishment for false accusation of chaste women (justice-and-witness). Verse 5 grants exception for repentance (repentance) and closes with Forgiving/Merciful (mercy). 'Believers' addressed implicitly throughout as the regulated community. 'If you believe in Allah and the Last Day' signals disbelief as a foil.

24:6.notes: Li'an procedure — spousal accusation of adultery without witnesses. Four oaths plus fifth invoking Allah's curse/wrath. Knowledge implied by God's awareness of truth. Chastity-and-boundaries co-applies as the regulation concerns unlawful intimacy.

24:10.notes: This long section (vv.10-21) covers the incident of the slander (ifk): God's grace and mercy mentioned repeatedly (mercy); 'Knowing and Wise' closing (knowledge, wisdom); the spreading of false accusation is slander-and-backbiting; verse 21 directly addresses 'O you who believe' (believers) and warns against following Satan's footsteps (iblis). Justice-and-witness applies because v.13 insists on four witnesses as the evidentiary standard.

24:22.notes: Single verse instructing the affluent not to withhold from relatives, the needy, and emigrants (zakat-and-charity; migration). Commands to pardon and overlook (practical-ethics). Closes with 'Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful' (mercy). 'Do you not love for Allah to pardon you?' invokes repentance logic.

24:23.notes: Verse 23 curses those who slander innocent believing women (slander-and-backbiting, believers). Verses 24-25 describe Day of Judgment testimony of limbs and full settlement of accounts (day-of-judgment, reckoning, justice). Verse 26 pairs good/bad people regarding marriage/moral compatibility (marriage-and-family) and promises forgiveness and provision (mercy).

24:27.notes: Verses 27-29 legislate seeking permission before entering homes (practical-ethics, chastity-and-boundaries). Verse 30 uses 'Tell (qul) the believing men' — qul-statement. Verse 31 'Tell (qul) the believing women' — second qul-statement; detailed dress/modesty code for women including which mahrams may see adornment (chastity-and-boundaries, marriage-and-family). Closes with call to repentance addressed to 'all you believers' (believers). Knowledge: 'Allah is aware of what you do' (v.28).

24:32.notes: Verse 32 commands facilitating marriage for singles and righteous servants/maids; God will enrich them (marriage-and-family, provision). 'Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing' (knowledge). Verse 33 instructs granting freedom to enslaved who seek it (manumission-and-captives), prohibits forcing girls into prostitution (chastity-and-boundaries), closes with 'Forgiving and Merciful' (mercy).

24:34.notes: Single verse: declares revealed clarifying verses (the-quran); 'examples of those who passed on before you' (punishment-of-past-nations); 'advice for the righteous/muttaqin' — taqwa is explicitly named as the audience.

24:35.notes: 13 labels — over the 12-label ceiling. Verse 35: 'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth' (guidance, creation-of-heavens-earth); 'Allah guides to His light whomever He wills' (guidance); 'Allah is cognizant of everything' (knowledge). Verse 36: 'houses Allah has permitted to be raised, His name celebrated therein' (mosques-and-sacred-places); 'glorified therein morning and evening' (praise, remembrance). Verse 37: men not distracted from dhikr (remembrance), prayer (prayer), zakat (zakat-and-charity); 'they fear a Day' (day-of-judgment). Verse 38: reward and provision (provision); 'dominion of the heavens and the earth' (sovereignty) — actually v.42 is next section; v.38 closes with provision. Trim candidates: sovereignty (not yet asserted in this section — appears in 24:42), praise (uttered via tasbih in v.36 — retain).

24:39.notes: Verse 39: works of disbelievers like a mirage (disbelievers, disbelief); God settles their account (reckoning); 'swift in reckoning'. Verse 40: darkness in deep ocean/clouds/fog as metaphor for those without God's light (guidance — its absence); 'He to whom Allah has not granted a light has no light'. The mirage/ocean/waves/clouds/fog are natural phenomena used as signs (natural-signs). The 'brilliant planet' simile in preceding section carries over; darkness contrasts with light. Cosmic-bodies is borderline — waves and ocean are natural-signs; confidence medium on cosmic-bodies.

24:41.notes: Verse 41: everything in heavens and earth glorifies God including birds in flight (praise — tasbih uttered by creation; natural-signs — birds); 'Allah knows well' (knowledge). Verse 42: 'dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah' (sovereignty). Verse 43: clouds, rain, hail, lightning driven by God (natural-signs); 'Allah creates whatever He wills' (power). Verse 44: alternation of night and day (cosmic-bodies). Verse 45: creation of all creatures from water (creation, power — 'Allah is Capable of everything'). Knowledge closing in v.41.

24:46.notes: Verse 46: enlightening revelations sent down (the-quran); guidance (guidance). Verses 47-50: group who profess belief but turn away — classic hypocrisy pattern (hypocrites); 'Is there sickness in their hearts?' Verses 51-52: true believers say 'we hear and obey' (believers); 'fears Allah and is conscious of Him' — taqwa named (taqwa). Verse 53: 'Say (qul), do not swear' (qul-statements); swearing oaths (oaths-and-vows). Verse 54: 'Say (qul), obey Allah and obey the Messenger' (qul-statements, muhammad — direct reference to Messenger's role/authority, prophethood-general). Knowledge: 'Allah is experienced with what you do' (v.53), knowledge.

24:55.notes: Verse 55: God's promise to establish believers as successors on earth, establish their religion, replace fear with security (divine-decree, islamic-history-and-community, believers); 'they worship Me, never associating anything with Me' — tawhid; disbelievers become sinners (disbelievers). Verse 56: 'Pray regularly, give regular charity, obey the Messenger' (prayer, zakat-and-charity); 'so that you may receive mercy' (mercy). Verse 57: disbelievers cannot escape; 'their place is the Fire' (hell, disbelievers).

24:58.notes: Verses 58-59: permission rules for servants and pre-pubescent children at three private times tied to prayer times — Dawn Prayer, noon, Evening Prayer (chastity-and-boundaries; prayer; ritual-calendar-and-sacred-time; children-and-parents; manumission-and-captives for the servants). Verse 60: post-menopausal women and relaxed dress rules (chastity-and-boundaries, marriage-and-family). Closing 'Allah is Knowledgeable and Wise' (knowledge, wisdom). Direct address 'O you who believe' (believers).

24:61.notes: Single verse exempting the blind, lame, sick, and others from blame when eating at relatives' homes. Lists father's, mother's, brothers', sisters', uncles', aunts' homes (children-and-parents, marriage-and-family). General social eating and greeting etiquette (practical-ethics). Mentions specific permitted foods/eating arrangements (food-and-dietary). Addressed to believers implicitly.

24:62.notes: Verses 62-63 address etiquette with the Prophet directly — believers do not leave his assembly without permission; direct second-person address to the Prophet ('give permission to any of them you wish, and ask Allah's forgiveness for them') — muhammad. Verse 63 warns against addressing the Messenger casually; God knows those who slip away (knowledge). Closing 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' (mercy). Practical social-conduct norms around the Prophet (practical-ethics).

24:64.notes: Single closing verse: 'to Allah belongs everything in the heavens and the earth' (sovereignty); 'He knows what you are about' (knowledge); 'on the Day they are returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did' (day-of-judgment, reckoning); 'Allah has full knowledge of all things' (knowledge).

25:1.notes: Tabāraka opens the surah → praise. The Criterion (Al-Furqan) sent as warning → the-quran + prophethood-general. Verse 2: sovereignty of heavens/earth, no son, no partner → tawhid + sovereignty. 'Created everything and determined its measure' → creation + power. Verse 3: false gods who create nothing and are themselves created → shirk + disbelievers. 'Warning to humanity' → mankind.

25:4.notes: 14 labels — over the 12 ceiling. This is a very long section (verses 4–19). Verse 6 has 'Qul' → qul-statements; 'He who knows the Secret in the heavens and the earth' → knowledge; 'Forgiving and Merciful' closing → mercy. Verses 11–14: Hell described with raging/roaring, people shackled → hell. Verse 15: 'qul' again, Garden of Eternity for the righteous → paradise + qul-statements. Verses 17–19: Day of gathering, interrogation of worshipped idols → day-of-judgment + shirk + reckoning. Trim candidates: punishment-of-past-nations (only indirectly implied via 'ruined people'), reckoning (partially subsumed by day-of-judgment).

25:20.notes: Verse 20: prior messengers ate food and walked in markets — prophethood-general. 'Will you be patient?' — patience explicitly named as subject of exhortation → patience. 'Your Lord is always Observing' → knowledge (borderline; 'Observing/Basir' maps to knowledge cluster). Verse 21: 'They have grown arrogant' (istakbara explicitly stated) → arrogance; mention of angels → angels. Verses 22–24: Day when angels sent down, no good news for sinners, paradise vs. scattered deeds → day-of-judgment + paradise + hell. Verse 25–26: Sky cleft, angels sent in streams, 'true sovereignty… of the Merciful' → sovereignty + mercy + angels. Verses 27–29: wrongdoer bites hands, 'Satan has always been a betrayer' → iblis. Knowledge label dropped in favor of tighter set; 'Observing' is closing formula quality → keeping knowledge. 12 labels exactly.

25:30.notes: Verse 30's 'Yā Rabbi' is speech reported as future (Day of Judgment); not tagging dua-distress per rule 6 (context is eschatological scene, not a present uttered supplication). Confidence remains high.

25:35.notes: Verse 35: Moses and Aaron explicitly named → moses + aaron. Verse 36: people who rejected Our signs destroyed → punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 37: people of Noah drowned → noah. Verse 38: Aad and Thamood named explicitly → ad + thamud. Verse 40: city drenched by terrible rain — tafsir identifies this as Lot's people → lot (medium confidence for lot specifically, but the reference is standard). Verses 41–42: mockery of the Prophet ('is this the one Allah sent as a messenger?') → mockery. Verse 43: worshipping desire as god → shirk (desire-worship). Verse 44: like cattle, further astray → disbelievers. 'Painful retribution / prepared for wrongdoers' → hell. prophethood-general for the pattern of sending messengers. Dropped shirk to keep within ceiling — mockery and disbelievers adequately cover 41–44 context. 11 labels.

25:45.notes: Verses 45–46: shadow extended, sun as pointer → cosmic-bodies + natural-signs. Verse 47: night as covering, sleep, day as revival → natural-signs (day/night cycle). Verse 48: winds and rain from sky → natural-signs. Verse 49: rain revives dead lands, provides drink for animals and humans → provision + creation (God as creator of animals and humans). Verse 50: 'most people persist in thanklessness' — the word 'thanklessness/kufran' is present but it describes disbelief/ingratitude of the many → disbelievers. Verse 51: 'We could have sent to every town a warner' → prophethood-general. Verse 52: direct address to the Prophet ('do not obey the disbelievers') → muhammad. power implied by God's sovereign control over shadow/sun/rain; confirmed by verse 54's 'Omnipotent' in next section rather than here, but 'had He willed, He could have made it still' is a power statement → power.

25:53.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Verse 53: two seas with barrier → natural-signs. Verse 54: human created from fluid, relationships through marriage → human-creation. 'Your Lord is Omnipotent' → power. Verse 55: worshipping what neither profits nor harms → shirk + disbelievers (tawhid by contrast). Verse 56: Muhammad sent as herald and warner → prophethood-general (dropped in favor of other labels). Verse 57: 'Qul' → qul-statements. Verse 58: 'put your trust in the Living' → trust-in-god; 'celebrate His praise' (sabbih bihamdihi — explicit praise command uttered) — this commands praise rather than utters it, so per §5.6b praise is not applied here. 'All-Informed Knower' → knowledge. Verse 59: created heavens and earth in six days, throne → creation-of-heavens-earth; 'the Most Merciful' → mercy. Verse 60: denial of prostrating to ar-Rahman → tawhid + shirk (redundant; keeping tawhid). Verse 61: 'Tabāraka' opens the verse → praise (uttered). Constellations, lamp (sun), moon → cosmic-bodies. Verse 62: night and day alternate → natural-signs (already tagged). Trim candidates: shirk (partially redundant with tawhid + disbelievers), prophethood-general (not explicitly in this section's verses).

25:63.notes: 14 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Verse 63: servants of the Merciful walk in humility, say 'Peace' to ignorant → humility (explicitly modeled). Verse 64: pass night in prostration and standing → prayer. Verse 65: uttered supplication 'Rabbanā isrif ʿannā ʿadhāb jahannam' → dua-protection + hell. Verse 67: neither wasteful nor stingy in spending → zakat-and-charity (spending in balance). Verse 68: do not call on other gods → shirk; do not kill unjustly → anger-and-violence; do not commit adultery → chastity-and-boundaries. Verse 69: doubled punishment on Day of Resurrection → day-of-judgment (borderline; hell already covers punishment dimension). Verse 70: repent and do good deeds → repentance; 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. 'Righteous deeds' explicitly named → righteous-conduct. Verse 71: repentance reiterated → repentance (already tagged). Verse 74: 'Rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wa dhurriyyātinā' → dua-family-offspring; 'make us a good example for the righteous' → believers (addressed group of pious). Verse 75: paradise reward for patience → paradise; 'for their patience' (sabaru) → patience. Trim candidates (lowest priority): zakat-and-charity (spending balance is ethical conduct rather than formal zakat), righteous-conduct (present but could be subsumed under repentance context), anger-and-violence (one-clause mention).

25:72.notes: Verse 72: do not bear false witness → justice-and-witness; pass by indecency with dignity → practical-ethics. Verse 73: when reminded of Lord's revelations, do not fall deaf and blind → the-quran (responsiveness to revelation). Verse 74: 'Rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wa dhurriyyātinā' (uttered supplication for spouses and children) → dua-family-offspring; spouses and children as content → marriage-and-family + children-and-parents. 'Make us a good example for the righteous' → believers (the muttaqun addressed). Verse 75: rewarded the Chamber for their patience (sabaru explicitly stated) → patience; paradise reward → paradise.

25:77.notes: Single verse. 'Qul' → qul-statements. 'What are you to my Lord without your prayers (duā'ukum)?' — this asserts the centrality of prayer/du'a as what gives humans worth before God → prayer (the verse names du'a as the subject). Addressed to those who have denied → disbelievers. Universal address ('What are you…') has mankind dimension, though not yā ayyuhā an-nās formula; the rhetorical universal address warrants mankind.

26:1.notes: Disjoined letters Tā-Sīn-Mīm open the surah. Direct address to the Prophet ('perhaps you will destroy yourself with grief') justifies muhammad. Verses 7-8 invoke earth's plant-pairs as natural signs.

26:10.notes: Moses's call from his Lord, his uttered fear ('My Lord, I fear they will reject me' and his request for Aaron) constitutes a dua in distress / dua for support. God's response 'We will be with you, listening' marks nearness-and-response.

26:18.notes: Pharaoh's dialogue with Moses about Moses's past — the incident of the killing, his upbringing in Pharaoh's household, his being made a messenger. Children of Israel referenced as enslaved people.

26:23.notes: Moses declares God as Lord of heavens, earth, east and west (tawhid, creation, sovereignty). Pharaoh dismisses him as crazy and threatens imprisonment. Moses shows the staff-serpent and white hand miracles. Pharaoh accuses him of sorcery.

26:41.notes: The magicians' contest, their prostration and conversion, their uttered hope 'We are eager for our Lord to forgive us our sins' constitutes a dua-forgiveness. They name 'Lord of Moses and Aaron' so aaron is tagged. The section features the conversion of the magicians as new believers.

26:52.notes: The Exodus narrative: revelation to Moses to travel by night, Pharaoh's pursuit, parting of the sea, drowning of Pharaoh's army. Closing formula 'Almighty, the Merciful' → power + mercy. 'He will guide me' (Moses) → guidance invoked.

26:69.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Abraham's narrative: confronting idolaters (shirk, tawhid), describing God as creator, guide, feeder, healer, giver of death and life (creation, provision, death-and-dying). Verses 82-89 contain Abraham's uttered du'a for wisdom (dua-knowledge-wisdom), forgiveness for his father (dua-forgiveness), inclusion with the righteous, paradise, and honor at resurrection (paradise, day-of-judgment). Prophethood affirmed. Trim candidates: dua-family-offspring (not strongly present; the du'a for his father is more forgiveness than family; remove this one). Keeping 12 after removing dua-family-offspring.

26:90.notes: Eschatological scene: Paradise brought near for the righteous, Hell displayed for the deviants. Idols fail to help (shirk refutation). Iblis's soldiers cast into Hell. Lament over having no intercessors. Closing formula 'Almighty, the Merciful' → power + mercy.

26:105.notes: Noah's da'wah to his people, their rejection, his uttered supplication 'My Lord, my people have denied me — so judge between me and them and deliver me and the believers' (dua-distress). The Ark, the drowning of the rest. Closing formula → power + mercy.

26:123.notes: Hud's da'wah to 'Ad: their vanity-building, merciless violence (corruption-on-earth), God's provision of livestock, children, gardens (provision). Their rejection and destruction. Closing formula → power + mercy.

26:141.notes: Salih's da'wah to Thamud: the she-camel sign (miracles), God's provision of gardens and springs (provision), warning against corruption/extravagance (corruption-on-earth), their slaughter of the camel and resulting punishment. Closing formula → power + mercy.

26:160.notes: Lot's da'wah: condemning same-sex conduct (chastity-and-boundaries), marriage referenced ('wives your Lord created for you' → marriage-and-family). Lot's uttered supplication 'My Lord, save me and my family from what they do' → dua-protection. Lot and family saved, others destroyed. Closing formula → power + mercy.

26:176.notes: Shuayb's da'wah to the People of the Woods (Aykah/Madyan): commands for honest weights and measures (trade-and-debt, justice-and-witness), prohibition of corruption on earth (corruption-on-earth). 'My Lord is Well Aware of what you do' → knowledge. Their denial and punishment by the day of gloom. Closing formula → power + mercy.

26:192.notes: The Qur'an declared as revelation from the Lord of Worlds brought by the Honest Spirit (Gabriel/angels). Revealed in clear Arabic (language-and-revelation-terms). Attested in earlier scriptures and by Children of Israel scholars (previous-scriptures, children-of-israel). Disbelievers will not believe until punishment arrives. Past towns destroyed only after warners sent — God is never unjust (justice, punishment-of-past-nations).

26:210.notes: Refutation that devils brought the Qur'an (the-quran, iblis, denial-of-revelation). Direct commands to the Prophet: 'do not pray to another god' (tawhid), 'warn your close relatives', 'lower your wing to believers', 'put your trust in the Almighty, the Merciful' — direct second-person address to Muhammad → muhammad. 'He is the Hearer, the Aware' → knowledge. 'Trust in the Almighty, the Merciful' → power + mercy. Verse 216 contains 'say' imperative → qul-statements.

26:225.notes: Brief continuation of the poets passage: poets ramble and say what they do not do — a critique of those who follow falsehood, linked to the denial of revelation context.

26:227.notes: Exception for believing poets who do good deeds and remember Allah frequently (righteous-conduct, remembrance, believers). Warning to wrongdoers of their coming overturning (day-of-judgment, disbelievers). 'Remember Allah frequently' is explicit trigger for remembrance.

27:1.notes: Opens with Ṭā-Sīn disjoined letters → disjoined-letters. Verse 6 closing formula 'All-Wise, All-Knowing' triggers knowledge and wisdom. Day-of-judgment and hell from v4–5 describing punishment of those who reject the Hereafter.

27:7.notes: Covers Moses at the fire through the nine signs sent to Pharaoh. 'Glorified be Allah, Lord of the Worlds' is praise formula but uttered in direct speech attributed to the divine call, not a standalone uttered praise by a human supplicant — tagging praise is borderline; omitted per §5.6b which requires it to be uttered in the section itself (here it is God's voice). Mercy and wisdom from closing 'I am Forgiving and Merciful' and 'Almighty, the Wise'. Pharaoh named as target of nine miracles → pharaoh.

27:13.notes: V14 explicitly uses 'wickedness and pride' (arrogance trigger) and 'mischief-makers' (corruption-on-earth trigger). 'See how the outcome was for the mischief-makers' frames this as a warning about past destruction.

27:15.notes: V15 'Praise Allah' uttered by David and Solomon → praise (uttered praise formula). V19 Solomon utters 'Rabbi awziʿnī an ashkura…' — an explicit uttered supplication asking to be thankful → dua-gratitude. 'O people' (v16) = mankind address. Jinn troops in v17. Knowledge given to David and Solomon in v15 → knowledge. The section is centered on the gratitude theme explicitly named in v40's parallel, and Solomon's du'a explicitly asks for gratitude.

27:20.notes: The hoopoe's report centers on the Queen of Sheba's people worshipping the sun instead of Allah (shirk); Satan diverted them (iblis). V25–26 assert Allah's knowledge of hidden and revealed things (knowledge) and his sovereignty as 'Lord of the Sublime Throne' (tawhid + sovereignty). The Queen of Sheba is not named in taxonomy; no label invented.

27:29.notes: The Queen reads Solomon's letter aloud which opens with 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' (mercy). Section is diplomatic narrative — the Queen and her counselors deliberating. No named divine attributes beyond the basmala's mercy formula. No du'a uttered. Corruption-on-earth is discussed by the Queen (v34) but as a political observation, not as the section's explicit subject labeling the concept.

27:36.notes: Solomon rejects the gift declaring what Allah gave him is better (provision). He threatens military force (power implied through Solomon's might). A jinn-imp offers to bring the throne (jinn). No divine-attribute closing formula; provision and power arise from the substance of vv36–37.

27:40.notes: V40 explicitly names gratitude vs ingratitude as a test ('whether I am grateful or ungrateful') → gratitude. V43 'she belonged to a disbelieving people' → disbelief; 'what she worshiped besides Allah' → shirk. V44 Queen utters 'Rabbi innī ẓalamtu nafsī wa-aslamtu…' — an uttered supplication acknowledging wrong and submitting → dua-forgiveness (asking forgiveness/acknowledging sin to Lord). Guidance theme in v41 ('whether she will be guided'). Confidence medium on dua-forgiveness: the Queen's statement is more a declaration of submission than a formal forgiveness request, but 'I have done wrong to myself' with address to 'My Lord' meets the uttered-supplication threshold.

27:45.notes: Salih sent to Thamud → salih, thamud. V46 'seek Allah's forgiveness so you may be shown mercy' names mercy. V48 'nine who made mischief in the land' explicitly triggers corruption-on-earth. V49–50 the gang plots against Salih and God counter-plots → plotting. V51 destruction of Thamud → punishment-of-past-nations. V53 'those who believed and were pious' saved → believers + taqwa (explicit 'pious' = muttaqun).

27:54.notes: Lot's people's sexual transgression explicitly named (chastity-and-boundaries). V57 'whom We destined to be among the laggards' → divine-decree. V58 rain-punishment → punishment-of-past-nations.

27:59.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: power (not explicitly named as attribute), mercy (present but secondary to nearness-and-response).

27:65.notes: Multiple 'Qul' commands (vv65, 69, 72) → qul-statements. V70 'do not grieve… do not be troubled by what they plot' is direct address to the Prophet → muhammad. V65 'no one knows the unseen except Allah' → knowledge. V66–68 disbelievers denying resurrection → disbelievers + resurrection. V73 'Your Lord is gracious towards humanity' — mercy-adjacent but the section's attribute claim is knowledge (v74–75). Day-of-judgment implied in the Hour-questioning (vv71–72). V69 'observe the fate of the guilty' → punishment-of-past-nations. V75 'everything is in a Clear Book' → divine-decree.

27:76.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. V76 Qur'an relates to Children of Israel → the-quran + children-of-israel. V77 guidance and mercy for believers → guidance + mercy + believers. V78 'Almighty, All-Knowing' closing → knowledge + wisdom. V79 'rely on Allah' → trust-in-god (explicit tawakkul command). V80–81 cannot make dead/blind hear → disbelievers (those who reject). V82 the earth-creature as sign → signs-of-the-hour. V83–85 gathering of deniers on the Day → day-of-judgment + denial-of-revelation. Trim candidates: wisdom (knowledge is stronger here), signs-of-the-hour (v82 is the creature of the earth, a classic hour-sign).

27:86.notes: V86 night/day signs → cosmic-bodies + natural-signs. V87 trumpet blown, everyone comes in humility → resurrection + day-of-judgment. V88 mountains moving like clouds, 'He has perfected everything, fully Informed' → knowledge (closing attribute). V89 virtue rewarded with safety from that Day → paradise (implicit) + reckoning. V90 evildoers tumbled into Fire → hell. V91 'Lord of this town who has sanctified it' → sacred-mosque-and-qiblah (reference to Mecca as the sanctified town). V92 'recite the Quran' → the-quran. V92 'say: I am one of the warners' → qul-statements. 11 labels within ceiling.

27:93.notes: Single verse. 'Qul al-ḥamdu lillāh' → qul-statements + praise (uttered praise formula). 'Your Lord is not heedless of what you do' → knowledge (divine attribute of full awareness).

28:1.notes: Opens with Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm disjoined letters. Introduces the Moses-Pharaoh narrative with Pharaoh's oppression ('He was truly a corrupter') and God's plan to reverse the order in favour of the oppressed.

28:7.notes: Covers the infant Moses cast into the river, picked up by Pharaoh's household, and returned to his mother. Divine decree and mercy are both explicit ('We will return him to you'; 'Allah's promise is true').

28:14.notes: Moses reaches maturity, receives wisdom and knowledge from God, accidentally kills a man, attributes it to Satan's doing, and utters 'Rabbi inni zalamtu nafsi faghfir li' — a clear uttered du'a for forgiveness. God forgives him and is named 'the Forgiver, the Merciful' → mercy.

28:18.notes: Moses fears retribution the morning after the killing; the same man cries out to him again; a warning arrives that authorities want him dead; he flees and utters 'Rabbi najjini min al-qawm al-zalimin' — an uttered supplication in distress.

28:22.notes: Moses journeys to Median, meets Shuayb's daughters at the well, draws water for them, utters 'Rabbi inni lima anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqir' (du'a in need/distress), is hosted, and contracts a marriage agreement with Shuayb. The marriage-contract verses 27-28 also touch oaths-and-vows ('Allah is witness over what we say').

28:29.notes: Moses's call at the burning bush: God reveals Himself, gives Moses the staff and white-hand miracles, appoints Aaron to help, and assures both will be protected. Moses utters 'Rabbi inni qataltu minhum nafsan akhaf an yaqtulun' — a du'a in distress. Power and divine-decree are explicit in the commissioning.

28:36.notes: Pharaoh's court dismisses Moses's signs as 'fabricated magic'; Pharaoh claims to be the only god and orders Hamaan to build a tower to reach 'the God of Moses'. Denial-of-revelation and arrogance are explicit; tawhid is the counter-claim Moses asserts ('My Lord is well aware of him who brings guidance').

28:39.notes: Pharaoh and his troops act arrogantly, are drowned, cursed in this world and despised on Resurrection Day. God then gives Moses the Scripture as 'guidance and mercy' for mankind. 11 labels — within ceiling.

28:44.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('You were not on the Western Side…') confirms this is addressed to Muhammad personally, not merely a Say-command. Also contains one 'Qul' (v.49). Moses is referenced extensively. The Quran is contrasted with what was given to Moses as prior scripture. 10 labels.

28:51.notes: Describes pious People of the Book who embrace the Quran, receive double reward 'because they persevered' (patience is named explicitly), counter evil with good, and give from what God has provided (zakat/charity). Practical-ethics triggered by 'they counter evil with good' as an explicit conduct instruction.

28:56.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('You cannot guide whom you love'); Quraysh cite the Safe Sanctuary (Haram) as reason to resist; God reminds them of the provision He established there and destroyed cities that were ungrateful. Sacred-mosque-and-qiblah fits the 'Safe Sanctuary' reference. Prophethood-general via the messengers-sent-before-destruction argument.

28:61.notes: Scenes of the Day of Judgment: questioning about false associates, partners disowning their worshippers, punishment visible. Verse 67 explicitly names repentance ('he who repents'). Verse 68 'Subhana Allah wa ta'ala' → praise uttered. Verse 70 'lahu al-hamd' → praise; also tawhid ('There is no god but He') and sovereignty ('His is the decision'). 11 labels — within ceiling.

28:71.notes: Two Qul-passages (vv.71-72) about perpetual night/day as rhetorical arguments for God's uniqueness. The night-day alternation is a cosmic-bodies and natural-signs argument. Mercy invoked explicitly ('out of His mercy He made the night and the day'). Provision in 'seek some of His bounty'. Day of Judgment and reckoning in vv.74-75 where witnesses are drawn from every community.

28:76.notes: The Qarun (Korah) narrative: extreme wealth, oppression of his people, his arrogant claim that wealth came from his own knowledge, his being swallowed by the earth. 'Corruption in the land' is explicitly named (v.77). Taqwa triggered by 'the outcome is for the cautious' implicit close-reference; actually that verse is in 28:83 — remove taqwa here. Patience is named in v.80 ('none attains it except the steadfast'). Provision in v.82 ('Allah spreads the bounty'). 10 labels.

28:83.notes: Opens with the Home of the Hereafter reserved for the humble; reckoning in v.84 (deeds rewarded accordingly); v.85 direct address to the Prophet about the Quran and contains 'Qul' → qul-statements + muhammad; mercy explicit ('except as mercy from your Lord'); guidance named in the Qul-statement; prophethood-general in the sending of the Scripture. 10 labels.

28:88.notes: A single-verse section: 'Do not invoke with Allah any other god. There is no god but He. All things perish except His presence. His is the judgment.' Tawhid and anti-shirk are the explicit subject; sovereignty in 'His is the judgment'; death-and-dying in 'all things perish'.

29:1.notes: Opens with Alif-Lam-Mim (disjoined letters). The section addresses all people (mankind) about the test of faith, references God's knowledge, warns against shirk when parents urge associating partners, and promises paradise for the righteous. Taqwa is triggered explicitly by the exhortation to true belief under trial.

29:10.notes: Section explicitly names the hypocrites (munafiqun) and describes their behavior under persecution, contrasted with true believers. Disbelievers urge believers to follow them. The Day of Resurrection and the carrying of loads (reckoning) close the section.

29:14.notes: Noah named; his 950-year mission recounted; the Flood described; the Ark made a sign. Prophethood-general applies as the sending of a messenger narrative. Punishment of past nations applies for the Flood. The Ark as a sign for all peoples triggers miracles.

29:16.notes: Abraham named calling his people to worship Allah and fear Him (taqwa explicit). He condemns idol worship (shirk) and asserts that idols cannot provide rizq — only Allah provides (provision). 'Thank Him' (washkuru lahu) is an explicit call to gratitude (shukr). The final verse notes past communities also denied (denial-of-revelation) and the messenger's duty is only clear transmission (prophethood-general).

29:19.notes: Opens with a rhetorical question about originating creation and reproducing it — God's power over creation and resurrection. 'Say: roam the earth…' triggers qul-statements. 'He punishes whom He wills and grants mercy to whom He wills' triggers mercy. Disbelievers who reject signs are warned of painful torment. Previous-creations-destroyed applies via the argument from origination/re-creation and the reference to observing how creation began.

29:24.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Abraham saved from fire (miracle). Lot believes and emigrates (migration). Isaac and Jacob granted. Prophethood placed in Abraham's descendants. Shirk condemned (idols taken as protectors). Day of Judgment scene where idol-worshippers curse each other, their destiny Hell. Lot's emigration 'to my Lord; He is the Noble, the Wise' triggers power and wisdom. Trim candidates: power (less central than wisdom and miracles), iblis (not named but referenced implicitly via shirk's social bonds — actually iblis not named here, remove).

29:28.notes: Lot named confronting his people over sexual immorality (chastity-and-boundaries) and corruption (corruption-on-earth). Lot utters 'My Lord, help me against the people of corruption' — an uttered supplication → dua-distress. Angels arrive at Abraham with good news then go to Lot to save him — both Abraham and angels named. The destruction of the town is the punishment of past nations. The Ark-like saving of Lot's family is a miraculous divine intervention.

29:36.notes: 14 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Shuayb and Madyan named. Ad and Thamud named (their dwellings referenced). Moses named going to Pharaoh (and Qarun and Haman). Iblis named embellishing deeds. Arrogance explicitly stated ('they acted arrogantly'). Corruption-on-earth explicitly named ('do not spread corruption'). Each punished by a different destruction (punishment of past nations). The spider parable (shirk — idols as fragile protectors). Allah knows what they invoke (knowledge). Allah is Almighty, Wise (wisdom). 'These examples We put forward to the people' (mankind). Creation of heavens and earth in truth at section close triggers creation-of-heavens-earth implicitly but that label is in next section. Trim candidates: mankind (only implicit at v.43), wisdom (closing formula, defensible but lower priority); note Qarun not in taxonomy — no label available, flagged.

29:45.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('recite what is revealed to you… perform the prayer') — muhammad tagged. The Quran and recitation of scripture are explicit subjects (the-quran). Prayer established and its function explained (prayer). 'The remembrance of Allah is greater' — explicit dhikr (remembrance). 'Do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner' — people-of-the-book and previous-scriptures (belief in what was revealed to them). 'Our God and your God is One' — tawhid. 'Allah knows what you do' — knowledge. Those who reject are disbelievers.

29:48.notes: Direct address to Prophet about his not reading or writing before the Quran — muhammad. The Quran as clear signs in hearts (the-quran). Denial of revelation addressed. Two 'Say:' commands (qul-statements). 'Miracles are only with Allah' (prophethood-general). 'In that is mercy and a reminder' (mercy). Allah as witness knowing heavens and earth (knowledge). Disbelievers as losers.

29:53.notes: Those who hasten punishment addressed. A specified appointed time (divine-decree). Hell will engulf disbelievers. The Day of punishment described with torment from above and below (day-of-judgment).

29:56.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. 'O My servants who have believed' — believers. 'My earth is vast, so worship Me alone' — implies migration (travel the earth). 'Every soul will taste death' — death-and-dying. Paradise with mansions and rivers for believers — paradise. 'Those who endure patiently' — patience explicitly named. 'In their Lord they trust' — trust-in-god explicitly named. Animals and people provided for by Allah — provision. 'He is the Hearer, the Knowledgeable' — knowledge. 'Who created the heavens and earth and regulated sun and moon' — creation-of-heavens-earth and cosmic-bodies. 'Who sends water down reviving the earth' — natural-signs. 'Say: Praise be to Allah' — qul-statements and praise (al-hamdu lillah uttered). Trim candidates: migration (only implicit in 'earth is vast'), cosmic-bodies (brief mention in rhetorical question).

29:64.notes: Worldly life contrasted with the Hereafter (day-of-judgment). People pray sincerely at sea then commit shirk on land (shirk). The Secure Sanctuary established by Allah referenced (sacred-mosque-and-qiblah — the Haram). Fabricating lies against Allah and denying truth (denial-of-revelation). Hell as dwelling for disbelievers.

29:69.notes: Short closing verse: those who strive for Allah will be guided in His ways (guidance explicitly stated). 'Allah is with the doers of good' — righteous-conduct explicitly named (muhsineen). Believers addressed implicitly.

30:1.notes: Opens with Alif-Lam-Mim → disjoined-letters. Verse 4 'believers will rejoice' → believers. 'He is the Almighty, the Merciful' closing → mercy and power. 'The matter is up to Allah' → divine-decree. 'He did not create the heavens and the earth except with reason' → creation-of-heavens-earth. The Romans defeated/victory prophecy is a historically specific episode → islamic-history-and-community. Most people are heedless of the Hereafter and are disbelievers at verse 8 → disbelievers.

30:9.notes: Verse 9 'those before them' who were destroyed → punishment-of-past-nations and previous-creations-destroyed. 'Messengers came to them with clear signs' → prophethood-general. 'Allah would never wrong them' → justice. 'They rejected Allah's revelations and ridiculed them' → disbelievers (as the described collective). Verse 11 'Allah originates creation then repeats it' → creation and resurrection.

30:12.notes: Verse 12-14: the Hour, guilty in despair, separation → day-of-judgment. 'No intercessors from their idols' → intercession (negated) and shirk. Verse 15: believers in meadows (paradise) → paradise and believers. Verse 16: disbelievers hauled into torment → hell and disbelievers.

30:17.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: mercy (derived from v21 'love and compassion' which is more natural-signs/marriage-and-family than divine attribute mercy per se — borderline). Verse 17: 'Glorify Allah' → praise. Verse 18: 'His is the praise' → praise reinforced. Verse 19: brings living from dead, revives land → natural-signs, resurrection. Verse 20: created from dust → human-creation. Verse 21: mates, love and compassion → marriage-and-family, and 'love and compassion' is a divine attribute of mercy → mercy. Verse 22: creation of heavens and earth → creation-of-heavens-earth; diversity of languages and colors → creation. Verse 23: sleep, pursuit of bounty → natural-signs. Verse 24: lightning, rain, reviving earth → natural-signs. Verse 25: heaven and earth stand at His disposal → creation-of-heavens-earth, power; resurrection at His call → resurrection. Verse 26: all submissive to Him → sovereignty. Verse 27: 'He is the Almighty, the Wise' → wisdom; repeats creation → creation. Sovereignty present but subsumed by power/creation context — trim sovereignty as lowest-priority trim candidate.

30:28.notes: Verse 28: parable against idolatry → shirk. Verse 29: 'who can guide whom Allah leaves astray' → guidance. Verse 30: 'natural instinct Allah has instilled in mankind' → mankind and tawhid (monotheism as the innate religion). Verse 31: 'be conscious of Him' → taqwa (explicitly named); 'perform the prayer' → prayer; 'do not be of the idolaters' → polytheists. Verse 32: those who divided their religion into sects. Verse 33-35: people call on Allah in distress then attribute partners → shirk reinforced.

30:36.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: praise (v40 'Glorified is He' is brief; primary thrust is creation/shirk refutation). Verse 36: mercy given, people rejoice/despair → mercy. Verse 37: provision expanded or restricted → provision. Verse 38: give relative/destitute/wayfarer their rights → zakat-and-charity. Verse 39: usury vs zakat explicitly → interest and zakat-and-charity. Verse 40: Allah created, provides, causes death, revives → creation; 'Glorified is He' → praise; refutation of idols → shirk-adjacent → polytheists. Verse 41: 'Corruption has appeared on land and sea' → corruption-on-earth; mankind named as cause. Verse 42: 'Qul' command → qul-statements; 'most of them were idolaters' → polytheists. Verse 43: 'a Day that cannot be averted' → day-of-judgment. Verse 44: disbelievers vs righteous → disbelievers. Verse 45: reward believers → believers (implicit); 'does not love the ungrateful' → disbelievers/disbelief.

30:46.notes: Verse 46: winds, ships, bounty → natural-signs, provision, mercy. Verse 47: messengers sent before, clear proofs, revenge on sinners, helping believers → prophethood-general, punishment-of-past-nations, believers. Verse 48: winds, clouds, rain → natural-signs. Verse 50: 'observe effects of Allah's mercy, revives earth' → mercy, natural-signs; 'He is Capable of everything' → power. Verse 51: disbelievers persist despite rain → disbelievers. Verse 52-53: cannot make dead hear, cannot guide blind → guidance (negated for disbelievers). Verse 54: created from weakness then strength → human-creation; 'He is the Omniscient, the Omnipotent' → knowledge and power.

30:55.notes: Verse 55: sinners swear they stayed but an hour → day-of-judgment, disbelievers. Verse 56: 'those endowed with knowledge and faith' cite Allah's Book → resurrection, knowledge. Verse 57: excuses will not benefit → reckoning. 'Day of Resurrection' explicitly named → resurrection.

30:58.notes: Verse 58: 'We have cited in this Quran every sort of parable' → the-quran; disbelievers call them fakers even when a miracle is brought → denial-of-revelation, miracles, disbelievers. Verse 59: 'Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know' → disbelief reinforced.

30:60.notes: Verse 60: 'Be patient' — patience is explicitly commanded → patience. 'The promise of Allah is true' → divine-decree. 'Those who lack certainty' trying to belittle → disbelievers. Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('do not let them belittle you') but per instructions this is a command not a 'O Prophet' direct address form — not tagging muhammad. Patience is explicitly the subject of the instruction triggering the concept label.

31:1.notes: 16 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: arrogance (the 'turning away in pride' is the act but the word kibr is not used explicitly — borderline rule 5 call; could trim); mockery (explicitly named 'to make a mockery of it' — keep); guidance (named explicitly as 'A guide' — keep); mercy (named explicitly — keep). Lowest-priority trims: arrogance (borderline), then power (creation section is rich but power is implicit via creation). Section spans disjoined letters, Quran introduction, believers doing prayer/zakat, paradise promise, creation cosmology, and shirk-refutation all in one long section (vv 1–11).

31:12.notes: Verse 12 explicitly instructs 'Give thanks to Allah' making gratitude the named subject (rule 5 trigger met). Wisdom is given to Luqman explicitly. Verse 13 has Luqman advising his son against shirk, naming it 'a terrible wrong', triggering tawhid and shirk. Children-and-parents is invoked by the father-son advice context.

31:14.notes: Verse 14 explicitly commands gratitude to God and parents ('give thanks to Me and to your parents'). Verse 15 addresses the case of parents pressuring toward shirk — tag shirk. Children-and-parents is the central subject. 'Follow the path of him who turns to Me' invokes repentance/turning back to God — the word 'turns' (anaba) is an explicit trigger. Righteous-conduct: 'keep them company in this life, in kindness' is an explicit instruction in conduct.

31:16.notes: Verse 16: 'Allah will bring it to light. Allah is Kind and Expert' — knowledge explicitly invoked. Verse 17: 'observe the prayer' — prayer; 'be patient' — patience explicitly named (sabr trigger met). Verse 18: 'do not treat people with arrogance' — arrogance explicitly named as a warning; 'Allah does not love the arrogant showoffs' — confirms arrogance label. Humility: the prohibition of arrogance and the command to moderate one's stride constitute explicit instruction in humility. Practical-ethics: the social conduct instructions (modesty in gait, lowering the voice) fit this label. Righteous-conduct: the section is structured as an explicit instruction in conduct across several virtues.

31:20.notes: 16 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: the-quran (only implied by 'enlightening Scripture' reference — borderline; trim candidate); resurrection (v28 'your resurrection' is explicit — keep); reckoning ('We will inform them of what they did' — keep but lower priority); trust-in-god ('whoever submits himself wholly to Allah and is a doer of good' — explicitly named disposition, keep); iblis (v21 'Satan is calling them to the suffering of the Blaze' — named explicitly, keep); qul-statements (v25 'Say: Praise be to Allah' — keep); praise (v25 'al-hamdu lillah' uttered — keep). Lowest-priority trims: the-quran (only a passing reference to 'enlightening Scripture'), then power (implicit via creation/sovereignty). Mankind: v20 addresses 'you' universally about blessings; v33 is not in this section.

31:29.notes: Verse 29: sun and moon running to stated term — cosmic-bodies; merging of night and day — cosmic-bodies and natural-signs. 'Allah is Cognizant' — knowledge. Verse 30: 'Allah is the Reality, what they worship besides Him is falsehood' — tawhid and shirk. Verse 31: ships in sea, signs of Allah — natural-signs. Verse 32: 'they call upon Allah, devoting their religion to Him' — sincerity explicitly invoked (ikhlas trigger). Verse 33: 'O people! Be conscious of your Lord' — mankind (ya ayyuha an-nas) and taqwa (explicit 'be conscious of your Lord'). 'Dread a Day' — day-of-judgment. 'The promise of Allah is true' — divine-decree.

31:34.notes: Single verse. 'Knowledge of the Hour' — signs-of-the-hour explicitly. 'He sends down the rain' — natural-signs. 'He knows what the wombs contain' and 'Allah is All-Knowing, Well-Informed' — knowledge. 'No soul knows what it will reap tomorrow / in what land it will die' — divine-decree (the unknowability of fate). 'No soul knows in what land it will die' — death-and-dying.

32:1.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Disjoined letters (Alif-Lam-Mim) open the section. The Quran's divine origin is asserted and the fabrication accusation refuted. Creation in six days and the Throne. God's knowledge of unseen/visible plus power and mercy from closing formula v.6. Human creation from clay through stages in vv.7–9. Angel of death and return to Lord in v.11 triggers death-and-dying. Qul-statement in v.11.

32:12.notes: Guilty bowing their heads and begging to return — reckoning scene. Hell explicitly mentioned. 'I will fill Hell with jinn and humans' names jinn. Divine-decree label applies to the declarative 'the declaration from Me will come true.' Guidance triggered by v.13 'We could have given every soul its guidance.'

32:15.notes: Believers described prostrating and glorifying with praise (v.15 — 'glorify their Lord with praise') → praise label. Night prayer and spending from provision → prayer and zakat-and-charity. Paradise for believers, Fire for transgressors. Taqwa triggered by 'out of reverence and hope' (v.16 — fear/khawf as explicit disposition). 'Lesser torment prior to the greater torment' in v.21 references worldly punishment as warning, echoing punishment-of-past-nations pattern. Disbelievers addressed in v.20 'which you used to deny.'

32:23.notes: Moses given the Book → moses and previous-scriptures. Made guidance for Children of Israel → children-of-israel and guidance. Leaders appointed 'as long as they persevered' — patience explicitly named (sabaru) → patience. Day of Resurrection judgment between them → day-of-judgment. Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('do not be in doubt', 'Your Lord will judge') → muhammad. Prophethood-general for the pattern of sending messengers with scripture.

32:26.notes: Destroyed generations and their ruins → punishment-of-past-nations and previous-creations-destroyed. Water to dry land producing vegetation → natural-signs. Disbelievers asking about 'the day of victory' and being told faith will not avail them → disbelievers and day-of-judgment. Qul-statement in v.29.

32:30.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('turn away from them, and wait') → muhammad. 'Them' refers to the disbelievers → disbelievers. Short single-verse section with minimal thematic content beyond this command.

33:1.notes: Direct address 'O Prophet' triggers muhammad. Verse 4 introduces zihar (equating wives with mothers) and adoption rulings — marriage-and-family and children-and-parents both apply. 'Allah guides to the path' triggers guidance. Trust-in-god triggered by explicit 'put your trust in Allah'. Knowledge and wisdom from closing formula 'Knowledgeable and Wise'.

33:5.notes: Verse 5 legislates calling adopted sons by their fathers' names — children-and-parents. Verse 6 about the Prophet's wives being mothers to believers and blood-relatives' priority in inheritance — marriage-and-family. Mention of emigrants (muhajirin) warrants migration. Covenant hinted by 'inscribed in the Book'. Mercy from closing 'Forgiving and Merciful'. 'O Prophet' direct address in surrounding context; verse 6 substantively concerns his role and household.

33:7.notes: Five prophets named explicitly: Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus. Solemn covenant taken from all prophets. 'Prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment' — hell and disbelievers.

33:9.notes: This is the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwat al-Ahzab) passage — islamic-history-and-community and war-and-treaties. 'O you who believe' — believers. Hypocrites explicitly named (v.12). Wind sent against the armies — natural-signs. 'Allah is Observant' — knowledge. Verse 15 references a covenant/pledge made to Allah — covenant. Verses 16–17 contain 'Say' (qul) commands — qul-statements. Disbelief theme present (those with sickness). Trust-in-god not explicitly named; dropping it. Confidence remains high on the core labels.

33:18.notes: Verses 18–20 expose hypocrites' cowardice during Ahzab — hypocrites, islamic-history-and-community, war-and-treaties. 'Allah already knows' — knowledge. Verse 21 explicitly names 'Messenger of Allah' as excellent example and mentions 'remembers Allah frequently' — remembrance and prophethood-general. Believers as addressed/described group throughout.

33:22.notes: Verses 22–23 praise believers' steadfastness and their covenant with Allah — believers, covenant. Verse 24 mentions hypocrites' punishment — hypocrites, mercy (closing 'Forgiving and Merciful'). Verse 25 — disbelievers repelled, Allah 'Strong and Mighty' — power, disbelievers. Verse 26 — 'People of the Book who backed them' expelled, some killed, some taken captive — people-of-the-book, manumission-and-captives. Verse 27 — Allah gave you their land, 'power over all things' — power reinforced. War-and-treaties throughout. Islamic-history-and-community (Ahzab aftermath).

33:28.notes: Direct address 'O Prophet' and 'O wives of the Prophet' throughout — muhammad. Verses 28–29: choice offered to wives — marriage-and-family, divorce. Verses 30–32: special rules for Prophet's wives regarding conduct, punishment doubled — chastity-and-boundaries, taqwa explicitly named ('if you observe piety'). Verse 33: prayer and zakat commanded explicitly — prayer, zakat-and-charity. 'Do not display yourselves' — chastity-and-boundaries reinforced. Verse 34: 'remember what is recited…of Allah's revelations and wisdom' — the-quran. Closing 'Kind and Informed' — knowledge. Believers implicit in verse 31's contrast.

33:35.notes: This verse enumerates virtues with explicit naming of each: patience (al-sabireen), humility (al-khashi'een), charitable (al-mutasaddiqeen), fasting (al-sa'imeen), those who guard chastity (hafitheen furujahum), those who remember frequently (al-dhakereen). Each concept is explicitly named, satisfying rule 5. 'Allah has prepared for them a pardon and immense reward' — mercy and paradise. The verse addresses Muslim men and women broadly — mankind/believers. Dropping mankind as this is specifically Muslims, not universal address; believers is more precise.

33:36.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: angels (supporting role only in v.43), day-of-judgment (only implicit in v.44's 'Day they meet Him').

33:45.notes: Direct address 'O Prophet' — muhammad. Verses 45–46 describe his role as witness, bearer of good news, warner, caller to Allah, illuminating beacon — prophethood-general, guidance. Verse 47: 'give the believers the good news' — believers, paradise (great reward). Verse 48: 'do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites…rely on Allah' — disbelievers, hypocrites, trust-in-god.

33:49.notes: Verse 49: 'O you who believe' — believers; divorce before consummation — marriage-and-family, divorce. Verse 50: 'O Prophet' — muhammad; detailed rules on whom the Prophet may marry — marriage-and-family. 'Forgiving and Merciful' closing — mercy. Verse 51: Allah 'Omniscient and Clement' — knowledge. Verse 52: prohibition on additional wives — marriage-and-family. Migration implied in v.50 ('who emigrated with you') but not the section's subject.

33:53.notes: Verse 53: 'O you who believe' — believers; etiquette for entering Prophet's home, hijab screen rule — muhammad, chastity-and-boundaries, practical-ethics; prohibition on marrying his wives after him — marriage-and-family. Verse 54: 'Allah is Aware of all things' — knowledge. Verse 55: exceptions for mahram relatives — marriage-and-family, chastity-and-boundaries. Verse 56: 'Allah and His angels give blessings to the Prophet' — angels, muhammad. Verse 57: insulting Allah and Messenger cursed, 'demeaning punishment' — hell, slander-and-backbiting. Verse 58: harming believing men and women with false accusation — slander-and-backbiting, believers.

33:59.notes: Verse 59: 'O Prophet, tell your wives and daughters and women of the believers' — muhammad, believers; jilbab/garment ruling — chastity-and-boundaries; 'Forgiving and Merciful' — mercy. Verses 60–61: hypocrites and rumormongers threatened with expulsion and killing — hypocrites, war-and-treaties. Verse 62: 'Allah's precedent with those who passed away before' — divine-decree, punishment-of-past-nations.

33:63.notes: Verse 63: 'The people ask you about the Hour. Say…' — mankind, qul-statements, day-of-judgment; 'knowledge thereof rests with Allah' — knowledge. Verses 64–65: disbelievers cursed, prepared a Blaze dwelling forever — disbelievers, hell. Verses 66–67: faces flipped into Fire, lament over not obeying — hell, day-of-judgment, reckoning. Verse 68: uttered supplication in hell: 'Lord, give them double punishment' — this is speech of the damned addressed to Allah, functions as a du'a-like utterance but is not a pious supplication; not tagging dua-* as it is a cry of the condemned, not an accepted supplication pattern. Reckoning applies to the accountability scene.

33:69.notes: Verse 69: 'O you who believe, do not be like those who abused Moses' — believers, moses; 'Allah cleared him' — knowledge. Verse 70: 'O you who believe, be conscious of Allah (ittaqu Allah) and speak straightforwardly' — believers, taqwa (explicitly named as ittaqullah), practical-ethics. Verse 71: forgiveness, obeying Allah and Messenger. Verse 72: the Trust offered to heavens, earth, mountains — creation-of-heavens-earth; accepted by the human being — human-creation, mankind (al-insan). Knowledge implicit in Allah's awareness throughout.

33:73.notes: Single verse: Allah will punish hypocrites (men and women) and mushrikeen (idolaters, men and women) — hypocrites, polytheists; 'redeem the believers' — believers, repentance (tawba explicitly: 'yatuba Allah ala al-mu'mineen'). 'Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful' — mercy. Disbelief implied by hypocrites and polytheists context; tagging disbelief as their common underlying state.

34:1.notes: 13 labels — one over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: 'denial-of-revelation' is implicit (those who strive against revelations) rather than the section's primary subject; could be trimmed. 'Al-hamdulillah' opens the surah → praise tagged. Closing attributes Al-Hakeem Al-Khabeer → wisdom/knowledge; Ar-Raheem Al-Ghafoor → mercy.
