Verse 3 contains qul-statement ('Say, Yes indeed…') but the section overall is not dominated by qul-pattern; however qul is present → qul-statements added, pushing to 13. Trim candidate 2: qul-statements (only one occurrence, subordinate to the main tawhid/knowledge argument).

34:6.notes: Verse 6 — 'those who received knowledge' most plausibly refers to learned people of the Book who recognise the truth of the revelation (per Ibn Kathir). Verse 9 invokes God's power over heaven and earth as a warning. 'Guidance' tagged because verse 6 explicitly says the revelation 'guides to the path'. Resurrection tagged because verse 7 is about disbelievers mocking the idea of being recreated after being torn to shreds. 'creation-of-heavens-earth' tagged because verse 9 gestures to the sky and earth as signs.

34:10.notes: David: mountains and birds echo with him, iron softened — miracles. Solomon: wind subjugated, spring of tar, jinn working for him — miracles. Verse 13: 'O House of David, work with appreciation (shukran)' — gratitude explicitly named. Verse 14: Solomon's death and the earthworm — death-and-dying. Verse 14 also demonstrates that jinn do not know the unseen → knowledge (God's exclusive knowledge of the unseen asserted by contrast). 'natural-signs' for the birds and mountains responding. 'power' for God subjugating wind and iron.

34:15.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. People of Saba (Sheba) narrative: gardens, provision, 'eat and give thanks' (gratitude explicitly named). Flood of the dam as divine punishment for ingratitude/disbelief → punishment-of-past-nations, corruption-on-earth. Mercy: 'a forgiving Lord' (verse 15). Iblis named (verse 20). Believers mentioned as those who did not follow Iblis (verse 20). Disbelievers: those who turned away and were penalised for kufr (verse 17). Knowledge: verse 21 'Your Lord is Guardian over all things' — divine attribute of guardianship maps most closely to knowledge/sovereignty; tagged knowledge for the 'distinguish who believes' clause. natural-signs for the two gardens. previous-creations-destroyed for the destruction of Saba's prosperity. Verse 19 contains 'Rabbanā…' supplication → dua-distress could apply but the du'a is cited as an act of ingratitude/arrogance ('lengthen distances of our journeys'), not a sincere supplication — excluded on that basis (medium-confidence call). Sovereignty could replace knowledge for verse 21 but knowledge is more explicit in the 'distinguish/test' framing.

34:22.notes: 13 labels — one over ceiling. Trim candidate: 'wisdom' (derived from Al-Hakeem in verse 27, but sovereignty and power are stronger in that verse; wisdom is defensible but lowest priority). Multiple qul occurrences (verses 22, 24, 25, 26, 27, 30) → qul-statements strongly warranted. Verse 28: universal address to all people, 'a herald and warner' → mankind + prophethood-general. Intercession addressed explicitly in verse 23. Shirk: verses 22 and 27 directly address associating partners. Tawhid: 'But He is Allah, the Powerful, the Wise' (verse 27). Provision: verse 24 'Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?'. Day-of-judgment: verse 30 'You are promised a Day…'.

34:31.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Verse 31: disbelievers reject the Quran and what came before it → the-quran + previous-scriptures + denial-of-revelation. Arrogance: 'those who were arrogant' explicitly named in verses 31–33. Plotting: verse 33 'it was your scheming by night and day' — makr explicitly described. Hell: verse 33 'yokes around necks', punishment of fire verse 42 (straddles into next section but verse 33 has punishment). Day-of-judgment: wrongdoers captive before their Lord (verse 31). Reckoning: mutual accusations and recompense theme. Prophethood-general: verse 34 'We sent no warner to any town…'. Provision: verses 36/39 contain qul about God extending/withholding provision — qul-statements tagged. Provision for verses 36–39.

34:40.notes: 12 labels — at ceiling. Verse 41: angels say 'Subhanaka' (glorified be You) → praise uttered. Verse 41: they worshipped jinn → jinn + shirk. Day-of-judgment: gathering scene (verse 40). Hell: 'taste the agony of the Fire' (verse 42). Denial-of-revelation: verses 43 — 'fabricated lie', 'plain magic' accusations against the Quran. the-quran: verses 43–44 directly about the Quran being recited and denied. punishment-of-past-nations: verse 45 — those before them denied messengers. prophethood-general: verse 44 'We did not send them any warner before you' + verse 45 'they rejected My messengers'. tawhid: angels affirm they are not worshipped — God alone is Master (verse 41).

34:46.notes: Multiple qul occurrences (verses 46–50) → qul-statements. Verse 46: 'he is just a warner' → prophethood-general. Verse 47: 'He is Witness over all things' → knowledge. Verse 48: 'Knower of the Unseen' → knowledge. Verse 50: 'if I am guided it is by what my Lord inspires me' → guidance. Verse 50: 'He is Hearing and Near' → nearness-and-response. Denial-of-revelation implied by context (rebutting accusation of madness against the Prophet, verse 46). Day-of-judgment: 'before the advent of a severe punishment' (verse 46).

34:51.notes: Short two-verse section. Disbelievers terrified, unable to escape, seized — eschatological scene. Verse 52: 'We have believed in it' too late → reckoning/judgment. Denial-of-revelation: their late claim of belief implies prior rejection.

34:53.notes: Single verse. 'They have rejected it in the past' → disbelief + denial-of-revelation. 'Made allegations from a far-off place' → continued denial.

34:54.notes: Single verse. 'A barrier placed between them and what they desire' — eschatological sealing of fate. 'As was done formerly with their counterparts' → punishment-of-past-nations (pattern of prior destruction invoked as parallel). 'They were in disturbing doubt' → disbelief.

35:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with 'al-hamdu lillah' → praise. Angels described as messengers with wings → angels. Verse 3 is 'O people!' → mankind. 'Is there a creator other than Allah' → tawhid. 'Provides for you' → provision. 'He is the Exalted in Power, Full of Wisdom' → power + wisdom. 'Whatever mercy Allah unfolds' → mercy. Creation of heavens and earth named explicitly → creation-of-heavens-earth.

35:4.notes: Verse 4 addresses the Prophet directly ('if they reject you') → muhammad. 'O people' in v5 → mankind. Satan named as enemy → iblis. 'Inmates of the Inferno' → hell. 'Allah leads astray / guides' → guidance. 'Allah knows exactly what they do' → knowledge. Previous messengers rejected → prophethood-general + denial-of-revelation. Disbelievers contrasted with believers → disbelievers.

35:9.notes: Wind, clouds, rain reviving dead land → natural-signs. 'Likewise is the Resurrection' → resurrection. 'All honor belongs to Allah' → sovereignty. 'He elevates righteous conduct' → power. Human creation from dust and drop → human-creation. 'No female conceives except with His knowledge … in a Record' → knowledge + divine-decree. 'Those who plot evil … their planning will fail' → plotting.

35:12.notes: Two seas, fish, jewels, ships → natural-signs + provision. Night/day cycle, sun and moon regulated → cosmic-bodies. 'His is the sovereignty' → sovereignty. 'Those you call upon besides Him do not possess a speck' → tawhid + shirk. 'On the Day of Resurrection they will reject your partnership' → day-of-judgment. 'None informs you like an Expert' → knowledge.

35:15.notes: Opens 'O people!' → mankind. 'You are the poor, in need of Allah; Allah is the Rich' → tawhid. 'He can do away with you and produce a new creation' → power + creation. 'No burdened soul can carry the burden of another' → justice. 'Perform the prayer' explicitly named → prayer. 'We sent you … a bearer of good news and a warner; every community had a warner' → prophethood-general. 'Their messengers came with clear proofs, the Psalms, and the Enlightening Scripture' → previous-scriptures. Previous peoples rejected and seized → punishment-of-past-nations + denial-of-revelation. 11 labels — within ceiling.

35:27.notes: Rain, fruits, mountains, animals in varied colors → natural-signs. 'The learned fear Allah' (explicit subject of God-consciousness) → taqwa. 'Allah is Almighty, Oft-Forgiving' → mercy. 'Those who recite the Book of Allah' → the-quran. 'Perform the prayer' and 'spend of what We have provided' → prayer + zakat-and-charity. These are the believers described → believers. 'He will increase them from His bounty; He is Forgiving and Appreciative' → mercy (already tagged).

35:31.notes: Verse 31: revealed Book confirming what preceded it → the-quran + previous-scriptures. 'Allah is Well-Informed … All-Seeing' → knowledge. Verse 33: Gardens of Eden described → paradise. Verse 34: 'Praise Allah … Our Lord is Most Forgiving, Most Appreciative' → praise + mercy. The utterance in v34 ('praise Allah who lifted sorrow… Our Lord is Forgiving') is praise rather than a du'a; however 'al-hamdu lillah' is uttered — tagging praise. Verse 36: Fire of Hell, disbelievers → hell + disbelievers. Verse 37: screaming in Hell 'Our Lord, let us out' is an uttered supplication in desperation → dua-forgiveness. Believers distinguished as chosen servants → believers. 10 labels.

35:38.notes: Verse 38: 'Knower of the future … knows what hearts contain' → knowledge. Verse 39: made humans successors on earth → creation. Disbelief adds to their perdition → disbelievers + disbelief. Verse 40 opens with 'Say' (qul) → qul-statements. 'Partners you worship instead of Allah … what have they created?' → shirk + tawhid.

35:41.notes: Verse 41: Allah holds heavens and earth lest they fall → power + creation-of-heavens-earth. 'Most Clement, Most Forgiving' → mercy. Verse 42: They swore if a warner came they would be guided, but when he came their aversion increased → prophethood-general + denial-of-revelation. Verse 43: 'Priding themselves … arrogance' explicitly named → arrogance. 'Scheming evil' → plotting. 'Precedent of the ancients' → punishment-of-past-nations. Verse 44: 'Observe the fate of those who preceded them' → punishment-of-past-nations (already). 'He is Omniscient and Omnipotent' → knowledge (already) + power (already). 9 labels.

35:45.notes: Addressed universally to people ('the people', 'its surface', 'their time') → mankind. God deferring punishment rather than seizing immediately → mercy. The principle of earned consequences → justice. 'Until a stated time' → divine-decree. 'Allah is Observant of His creatures' → knowledge.

36:1.notes: 12 labels at ceiling. Disjoined letters Yā-Sīn open the section. 'The Wise Quran' → the-quran + wisdom. Direct address to the Prophet ('You are one of the messengers') → muhammad + prophethood-general. 'The Almighty, the Merciful' → mercy. Shackles/barriers image for disbelievers → disbelievers + disbelief + denial-of-revelation. 'We write down what they forwarded' + 'Clear Record' → knowledge + divine-decree. 'We revive the dead' → resurrection. Trim candidates if needed: divine-decree (subsumed by knowledge/resurrection context), wisdom (closing attribute of the Quran rather than standalone theme).

36:13.notes: Parable of the town and its messengers. Three messengers sent and denied → prophethood-general + denial-of-revelation. Townspeople mock and threaten → mockery + disbelievers + disbelief. The man from the far end of the city argues against false gods → shirk + tawhid. The intercession argument ('their intercession will not avail me') → shirk. Destruction by one Cry → punishment-of-past-nations.

36:26.notes: The believing man enters Paradise and wishes his people knew of God's forgiveness → paradise + mercy. The town is destroyed by a single Cry → punishment-of-past-nations. The narrative context of messengers continues → prophethood-general.

36:30.notes: 11 labels. 'Alas for the servants; no messenger came but they ridiculed him' → mockery + prophethood-general + disbelievers. 'How many generations We destroyed' → punishment-of-past-nations. 'All will be arraigned before Us' → reckoning. Dead land revived, grains, gardens, springs → natural-signs + provision. 'Glory be to Him who created all pairs' → praise + creation. Night/day cycle → cosmic-bodies. Sun runs to its destination, 'the Almighty, the All-Knowing' → knowledge + cosmic-bodies (sun and moon explicitly named).

36:41.notes: The laden Ark carrying offspring → natural-signs; tafsir identifies this as Noah's Ark → noah (medium confidence since the Arabic does not name Noah explicitly, but Ibn Kathir identifies it as such). God could drown them but spares them by mercy → mercy. Fruits and provision theme from prior section straddles into the reference to traveling → provision. 'Spend of what Allah has provided' refused by disbelievers → zakat-and-charity + disbelievers + disbelief.

36:48.notes: Mockers ask 'When will this promise be?' → denial-of-revelation + disbelievers + disbelief. The single blast seizing them while they feud → day-of-judgment + signs-of-the-hour. Short section (3 verses).

36:51.notes: 11 labels. Trumpet blown, rising from tombs → resurrection + day-of-judgment. 'No soul will be wronged' → justice. Paradise inhabitants in shade with fruits and peace → paradise + mercy ('Most Merciful Lord'). 'Step aside, you criminals' / Hellfire → hell + disbelief. 'Did I not covenant with you, O Children of Adam, that you shall not serve the devil?' → covenant + mankind + iblis.

36:65.notes: Mouths sealed, hands and feet testify → day-of-judgment + reckoning. God's power to blind or cripple → power. Old age reversing development → human-creation. 'We did not teach him poetry; it is a reminder and a Clear Quran' → the-quran + denial-of-revelation + prophethood-general. 'Warn whoever is alive; prove the Word against the faithless' → disbelievers + disbelief.

36:71.notes: Livestock created for humanity — riding, eating, drinking → natural-signs + provision + creation. False gods taken besides Allah → shirk + disbelievers. 'We know what they conceal and reveal' → knowledge. 'Let their words not sadden you' — direct address to the Prophet → muhammad.

36:77.notes: Human created from a seed yet argues against God → human-creation + disbelievers. 'Who will revive the bones?' → resurrection. 'Say: He who initiated them will revive them' → qul-statements. Green trees producing fire → natural-signs. 'Is not He who created the heavens and earth able to create the like?' → creation-of-heavens-earth + power + creation. 'He is the Supreme All-Knowing Creator' → knowledge. 'Be and it comes to be' → power + creation.

36:83.notes: 'Glory be to Him' (Subḥāna) → praise. 'In whose hand is the dominion of everything' → sovereignty + power. 'To Him you will be returned' → resurrection.

37:1.notes: Oath by the aligners/drivers/reciters — classical tafsir identifies these as angels. Verses 4–5 assert tawhid and divine sovereignty. Verses 6–10 describe the adorned lower heaven (cosmic-bodies, creation-of-heavens-earth) and the expulsion of defiant devils (iblis/jinn).

37:11.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Section opens with a challenge about human creation (clay), moves through mockers denying resurrection (resurrection, day-of-judgment, reckoning, hell), their arrogance at tawhid (arrogance, shirk), accusing the Prophet of being a mad poet (denial-of-revelation, mockery), and closes with confirmation of prophethood. Verse 18 contains 'Say' (qul-statements).

37:40.notes: Description of the sincere servants' reward in paradise — fruits, honor, Gardens of Bliss, pure drink, and companions. 'Sincere servants' triggers sincerity.

37:50.notes: Verses 50–61: dialogue between a paradise-dweller and his former friend now in hell (paradise, hell, reckoning); verse 57 'grace of my Lord' invokes mercy. Verses 62–68: Tree of Zaqqum in hell. Verses 69–73: the ancients who went astray despite messengers sent to them (punishment-of-past-nations, prophethood-general). Verse 74: exception for sincere servants closes the unit.

37:75.notes: Noah's call answered by God (nearness-and-response); his family saved; descendants made survivors; the others drowned (punishment-of-past-nations). Verse 81 explicitly names him among believing servants (believers).

37:83.notes: Abraham confronts his father and people over idol worship (shirk, tawhid). He smashes their idols (miracles — miraculous deed / sign). Verse 96 asserts Allah created them and what they make (creation). They plot to throw him in the furnace but God defeats them (plotting). Verse 83 links Abraham to Noah's lineage, so noah is tagged for the explicit reference.

37:99.notes: Verse 100 'My Lord, give me one of the righteous' is an uttered du'a for offspring (dua-family-offspring). The son (widely identified as Ishmael) submits patiently and says he will be 'one of the steadfast' — patience is explicitly named in the translation. God guides Abraham (guidance), redeems the sacrifice (divine-decree), blesses him (prophethood-general). Both Abraham and Ishmael are named/referenced.

37:112.notes: Isaac given as prophet to Abraham; Moses and Aaron blessed and delivered with their people (children-of-israel) from disaster; the Clarifying Scripture (previous-scriptures) and guidance upon the straight path explicitly mentioned.

37:123.notes: Elijah calls his people away from Baal-worship (shirk, tawhid). They reject him and will be brought forward for punishment (disbelievers, punishment-of-past-nations). Pattern of prophethood and divine reward for the sincere.

37:133.notes: Lot narrative (saved, family rescued, others destroyed — punishment-of-past-nations). Jonah narrative: fled on boat, swallowed by fish, saved because he was among those who praised (praise — tasbih explicitly invoked as the reason for rescue), thrown into wilderness, gourd tree grown for him (natural-signs). Sent to a hundred thousand who believed. Nearness-and-response implicit in God's rescue of both.

37:149.notes: Refutation of the claim that Allah has daughters/has begotten (shirk, tawhid, denial-of-revelation). Angels described as female is challenged. Jinn explicitly named in a supposed kinship with God (verse 158). Verse 159 'Subhana Allah' is an uttered praise formula (praise). Verses 164–166: angels declare their assigned ranks and glorification (praise again; angels).

37:167.notes: Disbelievers who claimed they would believe if given scripture but then rejected it (denial-of-revelation). God's word goes out to His messengers — they will be victorious (prophethood-general). Verse 174 'So disregard them' is direct address to the Prophet (muhammad). Verse 180 'Subhana Rabbika' is uttered glorification (praise); 'Lord of Glory' invokes sovereignty.

37:182.notes: Single verse: 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabbi l-'alamin' — uttered praise formula (praise); 'Lord of the Worlds' asserts sovereignty.

38:1.notes: Opens with the disjoined letter Ṣād — tag disjoined-letters. Disbelievers call the Prophet a 'lying magician' — denial-of-revelation and mockery. Their rejection of one God (tawhid/shirk). Past generations destroyed as warning — punishment-of-past-nations. Arrogance is explicitly named ('steeped in arrogance').

38:8.notes: Lists Noah, 'Aad, Pharaoh, Thamud, Lot's people, and dwellers of the Woods (Madyan/Shuayb's people) as past deniers. 'Treasuries of the mercy of your Lord—the Majestic, the Giver' → mercy and sovereignty. v16 contains 'Rabbanā' address but it is a taunt from disbelievers, not a sincere du'a — not tagging dua-*. Reckoning mentioned explicitly ('Day of Account'). madyan label omitted as the text says 'dwellers of the Woods' without naming Madyan explicitly; however that is the standard association — tagging medium note.

38:17.notes: Opens with command to 'be patient' — patience explicitly named. David as servant, mountains and birds glorifying with him — natural-signs. 'We gave him wisdom and decisive speech' — wisdom. The two disputants scene introduces a justice/judgment narrative.

38:24.notes: David seeks forgiveness and repents — repentance explicitly depicted. 'So We forgave him' — mercy and nearness-and-response. 'Judge between the people with justice' — justice-and-witness. 'Day of Account' — reckoning. 'Do not follow desire lest it diverts you from Allah's path' — guidance invoked explicitly.

38:27.notes: 'We did not create the heaven and the earth in vain' — creation-of-heavens-earth and creation. 'Woe to those who disbelieve because of the Fire' — hell and disbelievers. 'Those who believe and do righteous deeds' vs 'those who make trouble' vs 'the pious' (al-muttaqin) — taqwa explicitly named. 'A blessed Book' — the-quran. God's justice in not equating the righteous with the corrupt — justice.

38:30.notes: David and Solomon named. Solomon's testing and repentance — repentance. 'My Lord, forgive me' — uttered supplication → dua-forgiveness. Wind and demons subjected to Solomon — miracles. 'This is Our gift' — provision. 'Nearness to Us' — nearness-and-response. The demons are jinn (shayateen = jinn category in Qur'anic context).

38:41.notes: Job calls out to his Lord about Satan's affliction — uttered supplication in distress → dua-distress. Iblis named as the afflicting agent. 'We found him patient' — patience explicitly stated. 'We restored his family for him' — mercy and marriage-and-family. 'Do not break your oath' — oaths-and-vows explicitly addressed.

38:45.notes: Six prophets named: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul-Kifl. 'We distinguished them with the remembrance of the Home' — remembrance explicitly named as their distinguishing quality. prophethood-general for the category of chosen messengers.

38:49.notes: 'The devout (muttaqin) will have a good place of return' — taqwa and paradise. Gardens of Eden described with fruit, beverage, companions — paradise and provision. 'Day of Account' — reckoning. Implicit address to believers ('you are promised') — believers.

38:55.notes: Detailed description of Hell's punishments — hell. The transgressors debate inside Hell, blaming leaders — disbelievers. v63: 'Did we take them for mockery?' — mockery explicitly named within the Hell scene. 'Feuding of the people of the Fire' context. The utterance in v61 'Rabbanā' is by Hell's inhabitants cursing their misleaders — it is a speech of blame and curse, not a sincere supplication; not tagging dua-*.

38:65.notes: Two 'Say:' imperatives (v65, v67) — qul-statements. 'No god except Allah—the One, the Conqueror' — tawhid. 'Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Mighty, the Forgiver' — sovereignty and mercy. 'I have no knowledge of the Highest Assembly' — reference to the angels disputing (v69) — angels. 'It is a message of great importance' referring to the Qur'an — the-quran. Prophet described as 'a warner' — prophethood-general. Disbelievers 'turning away' — disbelievers.

38:71.notes: 12 labels — at the ceiling. Trim candidates if needed: resurrection (subsumed under day-of-judgment context), sincerity (only implicit in 'loyal servants' phrasing).

38:86.notes: 'Say:' imperative — qul-statements. 'I ask of you no wage' — prophethood-general (prophet's sincerity about his role). 'It is but a reminder to mankind' — the-quran and mankind explicitly named.

38:88.notes: Single verse: 'You will know its message after a while.' Refers back to the Qur'an's message — the-quran. Addressed implicitly to those turning away (disbelievers). Very sparse content; only 2 labels are defensible. Confidence medium due to minimal content requiring inference about addressees.

39:1.notes: v4 'Subhanahu' triggers praise. v5 closing 'Almighty, the Forgiver' → power + mercy. v3 refutes intercession-based shirk. v5 heavens/earth creation + sun/moon → creation-of-heavens-earth + cosmic-bodies. 11 labels within ceiling.

39:6.notes: v6 creation from one soul, womb stages → human-creation; livestock provision → provision; 'His is the kingdom' → sovereignty; tawhid assertion. v7 'if you are thankful He approves' → gratitude explicitly named; disbelief mentioned; reckoning at return → reckoning; 'He is aware of what hearts contain' → knowledge.

39:8.notes: v8 human calls on Lord in adversity (prayer described, not uttered du'a), then forgets and sets up rivals (shirk); 'Say, enjoy your disbelief' → qul-statements; hell mentioned. v9 devout worshipper fearing hereafter, hoping mercy → mercy; 'Say, are those who know equal?' → qul-statements. Taqwa triggered by v9's explicit fear/mindfulness of the hereafter framing.

39:10.notes: v10 'Say, O My devotees who have believed, keep your duty' → believers + qul-statements + taqwa; 'steadfast will be paid without reckoning' → patience explicitly named. v11-14 multiple qul commands, sincerity in religion explicitly stated. v15 Day of Resurrection losers → day-of-judgment. v16 layers of Fire → hell. 'Allah's earth is vast' in v10 is often read as referring to migration (hijrah) per tafsir; tagged migration with medium sub-confidence but overall high.

39:17.notes: v17 avoiding idol worship (shirk refuted) → shirk; 'theirs is the good news' + mansions/streams → paradise. v18 those Allah has guided → guidance. v19 those deserving punishment/Fire → hell. v20 those who fear Lord (taqwa) → paradise + taqwa.

39:21.notes: v21 rain/plants cycle as natural sign → natural-signs; 'reminder for those with understanding' → remembrance explicitly. v22 heart opened to Islam vs. hardened hearts → guidance; hardened hearts from 'mention of Allah' → disbelief. v23 'Allah has sent down the best of narrations: a Scripture' → the-quran; 'Allah's guidance, He guides with it' → guidance; 'remembrance of Allah' explicitly → remembrance.

39:24.notes: v24 terrible misery of Day of Resurrection → day-of-judgment; evildoers tasting what they earned → hell. v25 those before them denied and punishment came → punishment-of-past-nations + denial-of-revelation. v26 disgrace in present life + worse punishment in hereafter → punishment-of-past-nations.

39:27.notes: v27 'We have cited in this Quran for mankind every ideal' → the-quran + mankind. v28 'An Arabic Quran' → language-and-revelation-terms; 'so they may become righteous' → taqwa explicitly. v29 parable of man with quarrelling partners vs. one master → tawhid (shirk vs. monotheism parable); 'Praise be to Allah' (al-hamdu lillah) → praise.

39:30.notes: v30 direct address 'You will die' → muhammad (second-person direct address to the Prophet); death of all → death-and-dying. v31 quarrelling on Day of Resurrection → day-of-judgment. v32 liars about Allah, Hell for ungrateful → hell + disbelievers. v33 the righteous (muttaqun explicitly) → taqwa. v34-35 reward/paradise for virtuous; Allah acquits worst deeds → paradise + mercy.

39:36.notes: v36 direct address 'Is Allah not enough for His servant' / 'they frighten you' → muhammad; guidance vs. misguidance → guidance. v37 'Is Allah not Powerful' → power. v38 polytheists acknowledging Allah as Creator of heavens/earth → creation-of-heavens-earth; refutation of false gods' power → shirk + tawhid; 'Say' multiple times → qul-statements; 'On Him the reliant rely' → trust-in-god explicitly. v39-40 'Say: O my people, work' → qul-statements.

39:41.notes: v41 'We sent down upon you the Book for mankind' → the-quran + mankind. v42 Allah takes souls at death and during sleep, retains/releases → death-and-dying + divine-decree; 'signs for people who reflect' → natural-signs (the sleep/death phenomenon as sign). v43 'Say, even though they have no power' → qul-statements; false intercessors. v44 'Say, All intercession is up to Allah' → qul-statements + sovereignty implicitly.

39:45.notes: v46 'Say, Allahumma...' is technically a qul-commanded du'a (uttered by the Prophet on command). Per rule 6, this is borderline — it is uttered but framed as a 'Say:' command. Keeping qul-statements without a separate dua label; confidence remains high.

39:49.notes: v49 human in adversity calls on God but attributes blessing to own knowledge → disbelievers + arrogance-adjacent (but 'arrogance' keyword not explicit, not tagged). v50 those before them said the same, what they earned didn't avail → punishment-of-past-nations. v51 evils caught them → disbelief/punishment. v52 'Allah extends provision to whom He wills' → provision; 'signs for people who believe' → knowledge (God's knowledge of provision).

39:53.notes: v53 'Say, O My servants who transgressed, do not despair of Allah's mercy, Allah forgives all sins, He is the Forgiver, the Clement' → mercy + repentance explicitly + qul-statements. v54 'turn to your Lord and submit before retribution' → repentance + day-of-judgment. v55 follow best of what was revealed → guidance. v56 soul lamenting neglect of duty, having been of the scoffers → denial-of-revelation + disbelievers. v57 'Had Allah guided me' → guidance. v59 'My Verses came to you, you called them lies, turned arrogant' → denial-of-revelation + arrogance explicitly named. Believers addressed as addressees → believers.

39:60.notes: v60 faces blackened on Day of Resurrection → day-of-judgment; Hell for the arrogant → hell + arrogance explicitly named. v61 Allah saves those who maintained righteousness → taqwa. v62 'Allah is the Creator of all things, in Charge of all things' → creation + sovereignty. v63 'reins of heavens and earth belong to Him' → sovereignty; those who blaspheme against Allah's revelations → denial-of-revelation + disbelievers.

39:64.notes: v64 'Say, is it other than Allah you instruct me to worship' → qul-statements + tawhid + shirk; direct address to Prophet → muhammad. v65 revelation to Prophet and those before him about shirk nullifying deeds → prophethood-general + shirk. v66 'worship Allah and be of the appreciative' → tawhid. v67 'Subhanahu' → praise; earth in God's grip on Day of Resurrection, heavens folded → day-of-judgment + sovereignty (implicit). v68 Trumpet sounded, all stunned then rise → resurrection. v69 earth shines with Lord's light, prophets and witnesses brought in, judgment → day-of-judgment + reckoning + prophethood-general + angels (witnesses/angels implied) + justice. v70 every soul fully compensated, He knows → reckoning + knowledge. 12 labels at ceiling.

39:71.notes: v71 disbelievers driven to Hell in throngs, gates opened, keepers ask about messengers reciting revelations → disbelievers + hell + prophethood-general + day-of-judgment + denial-of-revelation. v72 'enter gates of Hell eternally, wretched destination of the arrogant' → hell + arrogance explicitly.

39:73.notes: v73 those who feared their Lord led to Paradise in throngs, gates opened, keepers say 'Peace be upon you, you have been good, enter to abide eternally' → taqwa + paradise + believers + day-of-judgment. v74 'Praise be to Allah who fulfilled His promise' (al-hamdu lillah uttered) → praise.

39:75.notes: Angels around the Throne glorifying Lord with praise → angels + praise (subhan/tasbih uttered). Judgment passed equitably → justice + day-of-judgment. 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds' uttered → praise. Throne → sovereignty.

40:1.notes: Opens with Ḥā-Mīm disjoined letters. Multiple divine attributes named: Almighty (power), Omniscient (knowledge), Forgiver of sins (mercy), Accepter of repentance (mercy), Severe in punishment (justice), Bountiful in bounty (provision — but mercy cluster fits better). 'No god but He' = tawhid. People of Noah named. Disbelievers argued against revelations. Closing sentence assigns them to Fire.

40:7.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: tawhid and shirk (verse 12 mentions associating partners; the section's core is the angels' du'a and the disbelievers' fate in hell). Angels around the Throne utter supplications (Rabbanā) asking forgiveness and protection for believers → dua-forgiveness and dua-protection both apply. 'You have encompassed everything in mercy and knowledge' → mercy and knowledge. 'The Almighty, the Most Wise' closing → wisdom. Paradise promised for believers' families → paradise. Disbelievers rebuked at Hell → hell. Verse 12: shirk and tawhid invoked explicitly. Repentance explicitly mentioned as a condition.

40:13.notes: God sends sustenance from sky → provision and natural-signs. 'Exalted in rank, Owner of the Throne' → sovereignty. 'He conveys the Spirit … to warn of the Day of Encounter' → prophethood-general and day-of-judgment. 'Call upon Allah with sincere devotion' → sincerity (explicit instruction). 'None pays heed except the repentant' → repentance (explicitly named). Knowledge implicit in 'nothing about them will be concealed' → knowledge. Disbelievers as subject. 'To whom does the sovereignty belong today? To Allah the One, the Irresistible' → tawhid could apply but sovereignty already covers it.

40:18.notes: 'Warn them' is a direct command addressed to the Prophet → muhammad. Day of Imminence described → day-of-judgment. 'No intercessor to be obeyed' → intercession (denial of). 'He knows the deceptions of the eyes and what the hearts conceal' → knowledge. 'Allah judges with justice' → justice. 'Those whom they invoke besides Him cannot judge' + 'Allah who is the Hearing, the Seeing' → tawhid and knowledge. Disbelievers as implicit subject.

40:21.notes: 'Have they not travelled through the earth … consequences for those before them' → previous-creations-destroyed. Past nations destroyed for rejecting messengers → punishment-of-past-nations. 'Their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved' → prophethood-general and denial-of-revelation. 'He is Strong, Severe in retribution' → power.

40:23.notes: Moses sent with signs and authority → moses, miracles, prophethood-general. Pharaoh, Hamaan, and Quaroon named — Pharaoh is the tagged person label; Hamaan and Quaroon are not in the taxonomy as separate labels. Moses says 'I have sought the protection of my Lord … from every tyrant who does not believe in the Day of Account' — this is an uttered supplication → dua-protection. Pharaoh plots to kill Moses → plotting, anger-and-violence. 'Kill the sons of those who believed' → anger-and-violence. They call Moses 'a lying sorcerer' → sorcery (accusation), denial-of-revelation implicit. Children of Israel referenced implicitly via 'sons of those who believed with him' — tagging children-of-israel generously per rule 3.

40:28.notes: The believing man from Pharaoh's family who conceals his faith defends Moses. 'My Lord is Allah' → tawhid. 'Allah does not guide the extravagant imposter' → guidance. 'Yours is the dominion today' → sovereignty. Pharaoh speaking. The believing man is not a named figure in the taxonomy — he is part of the believers group.

40:30.notes: The believing man warns his people invoking fate of Noah's people, 'Aad, and Thamood' — all three named → noah, ad, thamud and punishment-of-past-nations. 'Day of Calling Out' described → day-of-judgment. 'Whomever Allah misguides has no guide' → guidance. Disbelievers as addressed group.

40:34.notes: Joseph named explicitly → joseph. Pharaoh referenced via Hamaan and the tower narrative → pharaoh. 'Joseph had come to you with clear revelations, but you continued to doubt' → denial-of-revelation. 'Allah seals the heart of every proud bully' — 'mutakabbir' (arrogant) explicitly named → arrogance. 'Those who argue against Allah's revelations without any proof' → denial-of-revelation. Pharaoh builds tower to challenge God of Moses → disbelief, arrogance. Prophethood as category invoked.

40:38.notes: The believing man calls his people to the path of rectitude → guidance. 'Life of this world is fleeting, the Hereafter is the Home of Permanence' → day-of-judgment. 'Those who believe … will enter Paradise' → paradise. 'The transgressors are inmates of the Fire' → hell. 'You call me to reject Allah and to associate with Him' → tawhid and shirk explicitly named. 'The Mighty Forgiver' → mercy. 'I commit my case to Allah' → trust-in-god (explicit tawakkul act — 'I delegate/commit my affair to Allah' is the classic tawakkul formula).

40:45.notes: Intercession implicitly denied (keepers dismiss the plea). Tagging intercession.

40:51.notes: Praise is commanded rather than uttered by the text itself; confidence on that single label is medium but overall section is high. 12 labels exactly at ceiling.

40:57.notes: 'Creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of humanity' → creation-of-heavens-earth, human-creation. 'Most people do not know' → mankind (universal address about humanity). 'The Hour is coming' → day-of-judgment. 'Those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell' — 'yastakbirun' (proud/arrogant) explicitly named → arrogance, hell. 'Pray to Me and I will respond to you' → prayer (command to call upon God; nearness-and-response also fits — adding it). The call 'Pray to Me' → nearness-and-response.

40:61.notes: 'Allah made the night … and the day' → cosmic-bodies, natural-signs. 'Creator of all things. There is no god except Him' → tawhid, creation. 'He made the earth a habitat … sky a structure … designed you well … provided you with good things' → creation-of-heavens-earth, human-creation, provision. 'Most people do not give thanks' → mankind (universal reference). 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds' — al-hamdu lillah uttered → praise. 'So pray to Him, devoting your religion to Him' → sincerity (ikhlas explicitly invoked: 'mukhlisina lahu al-din'). 'tabāraka Allāhu' → praise (already tagged). 10 labels within ceiling.

40:66.notes: Opens with 'Say' (Qul) → qul-statements. 'I was prohibited from worshiping those you invoke besides Allah' → shirk, tawhid. 'He created you from dust, then from a seed, then from an embryo … and some of you die sooner … so that you may reach a predetermined age' → human-creation, death-and-dying, divine-decree. 'He who gives life and death; and when He decides on a thing, He just says to it, Be, and it comes to be' → power, divine-decree.

40:69.notes: 'Those who dispute regarding Allah's revelations' → denial-of-revelation. 'Those who call the Book a lie' → the-quran, disbelief. Dragged in chains, boiling water, Fire → hell. 'Where are those you used to deify instead of Allah?' → shirk. 'What a terrible dwelling for the arrogant' — 'mutakabbirun' explicitly named → arrogance.

40:77.notes: Direct address to the Prophet: 'So be patient' and 'whether We show you … or take you to Us' → muhammad. 'The promise of Allah is true' → divine-decree. 'So be patient' — explicit patience command → patience. 'We sent messengers before you … No messenger can bring a miracle except by leave of Allah' → prophethood-general, miracles. 'To Us they will be returned' / 'fair judgment will be passed' → day-of-judgment.

40:79.notes: 'Allah created the domestic animals for you — some to ride, some to eat … other benefits … transported on ships' → natural-signs (animals as signs of Creator), provision (sustenance and benefit), creation. 'He shows you His signs. So which of Allah's signs will you deny?' → natural-signs. Universal address about humanity's use of creation → mankind (the signs are shown to people generally).

40:82.notes: 'Have they not journeyed through the land … outcome for those before them' → previous-creations-destroyed, punishment-of-past-nations. 'When their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in the knowledge they had … the very things they used to ridicule besieged them' → prophethood-general, denial-of-revelation, mockery. 'They witnessed Our might, they said, We believe in Allah alone, and we reject what we used to associate with Him' → tawhid, shirk (explicitly named in the Arabic).

40:85.notes: 'Their faith could not help them once they witnessed Our might' → disbelief (faith rejected when too late). 'This has been Allah's way of dealing with His servants' — sunnatu-llah → divine-decree. 'The disbelievers lost' → disbelievers. Continuation of the punishment-of-past-nations theme from 40:82.

41:1.notes: Disjoined letters Hā-Mīm open the section. The Qur'an is described as a revelation from the Most Gracious/Merciful (mercy). Verse 6 contains a Qul statement asserting tawhid and warning polytheists (mushrikeen). Verse 7 names zakat and disbelief in the Hereafter. Verse 8 alludes to paradise (uninterrupted reward). Denial-of-revelation is evidenced by v4-5 (turning away, hearts screened).

41:9.notes: Begins with Qul. The section covers creation of the earth in two days, provision/sustenance planned within it, creation of seven heavens, decorating the lower heaven with stars (cosmic-bodies). Closing formula 'the Almighty, the All-Knowing' → power and knowledge. Shirk is addressed ('you attribute equals to Him').

41:13.notes: Opens with a Qul instruction to warn. Ad and Thamud are explicitly named. Their messengers (prophethood-general) came to them. Ad's arrogance is explicitly stated ('Who is more powerful than us?' — kibr named via 'istakbaru'). Thamud preferred blindness over guidance (guidance label triggered by explicit contrast). Both peoples received punishment (punishment-of-past-nations, hell referenced as worse than worldly punishment). Angels mentioned in v14 ('would have sent down angels'). Disbelief explicit.

41:19.notes: Describes the Day when enemies of Allah are herded into the Fire. Their own hearing, sight, and skins testify against them — a reckoning scene. God's knowledge is invoked ('Allah was unaware of much of what you do' — correcting their false assumption, thus asserting knowledge). Hell is the explicit destination.

41:25.notes: Companions (shayateen/jinn associates) assigned to mislead disbelievers — jinn and iblis-adjacent. V25 names 'communities of jinn and humans' (mankind). V26 references the Qur'an being talked over (denial-of-revelation, the-quran). V28 describes the Fire as eternal home (hell). V30-32 describe angels descending on the believers with glad tidings of paradise, and the closing formula 'All-Forgiving, Merciful' → mercy. Angels explicitly present.

41:33.notes: V33 commends calling to Allah and acting righteously (righteous-conduct, practical-ethics — both named/explicit). V34 instructs repelling evil with good (practical-ethics). V35 explicitly names those who 'persevere' (sabaru — patience named). V36 instructs seeking refuge from the Devil (iblis) and closes with 'the Hearer, the Knower' → knowledge.

41:37.notes: Night, day, sun, moon listed as signs → cosmic-bodies; rain reviving the earth → natural-signs. 'Do not bow to sun or moon but to Allah who created them' → tawhid and shirk (prohibition of worship of celestial bodies). 'He is Able to do all things' → power. Angels in the presence of the Lord praising (subhanahu implied) → praise and angels. 'He who revived it will revive the dead' → resurrection.

41:40.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: language-and-revelation-terms (subsumed by the-quran in context), wisdom (closing 'Wise and Praiseworthy' could be trimmed if needed). The section defends the Qur'an, describes it as guidance and healing (guidance), references Moses and the Torah (moses, previous-scriptures), contains a Qul statement (v44), mentions hell (v40) and Day of Resurrection (v40), God seeing all (knowledge), closing formula 'Wise and Praiseworthy' (wisdom + praise implicit but 'Hamid' is a divine attribute pointing to sovereignty/wisdom cluster). Mercy via 'Possessor of Forgiveness' in v43.

41:46.notes: V46 asserts God is not unjust (justice). V47 asserts God's knowledge of the Hour, knowledge of every fruit and conception (knowledge), and the Day when He calls 'where are My associates?' (day-of-judgment, shirk exposed). V47 also references the Hour (signs-of-the-hour). Fruits emerging from sheaths → natural-signs (earthly phenomena framed as signs of God's knowledge).

41:49.notes: V49-51 describe the human being (al-insan → mankind) who despairs in adversity and becomes arrogant in ease. Mercy mentioned explicitly (v50). Disbelievers warned of punishment (hell, day-of-judgment). V52 contains a Qul statement. V53 promises God will show signs on horizons and in their souls (natural-signs). Closing 'your Lord is witness over everything' → knowledge.

41:54.notes: Single verse closing section. Doubt about the encounter with their Lord (day-of-judgment). 'He comprehends everything' → knowledge (divine attribute of all-encompassing awareness).

42:1.notes: Opens with two sets of disjoined letters (Ha-Meem and Ayn-Seen-Qaf). Verse 3 mentions revelation to Muhammad and prior prophets (prophethood-general). Angels glorify and seek forgiveness (angels, mercy). 'Allah the Almighty, the Wise' → power, wisdom. 'The Sublime, the Magnificent' → sovereignty, power. 'The Forgiver, the Merciful' → mercy. 'Allah is in charge of them' → sovereignty. Revelation framed as wahyi → the-quran. Knowledge implicit in 'Allah is in charge' but not explicitly named; dropped in favor of tighter labeling.

42:7.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: tawhid (implicit through 'There is nothing like Him' but not the section's subject), creation-of-heavens-earth (mentioned as context for 'Originator of the heavens and earth' but not the section's main focus). Verse 7 addresses Muhammad directly about the Arabic Qur'an → muhammad, the-quran, language-and-revelation-terms. Day of Assembly → day-of-judgment. Garden/Furnace → paradise, hell. 'Admits into His mercy' → mercy. 'He gives life to the dead, He has power over all things' → power. 'To Him belongs absolute control' → sovereignty. 'Spreads the bounties' → provision. 'He is aware of all things' → knowledge. 'Originator of the heavens and earth' → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'There is nothing like Him' → tawhid.

42:13.notes: Four prophets named explicitly → noah, abraham, moses, jesus. 'He prescribed for you the same religion' → prophethood-general. Reference to prior revealed books and those who inherited the Book → previous-scriptures, people-of-the-book. 'As for the idolaters' → polytheists. 'He guides to Himself whoever repents' → guidance. 'A predetermined decision from your Lord' → divine-decree. 'Those who were made to inherit the Book … are in grave doubt' → disbelief (denial/doubt of truth after knowledge).

42:19.notes: Verse 19: 'Allah is kind … He provides' → provision, mercy; 'the Powerful, the Honorable' → power. Verse 20: harvest of Hereafter vs. this world → paradise (implied reward) and hell (no share). Verse 21: partners who legislate without God's permission → shirk. Verse 22: believers in Meadows of Gardens → paradise, believers; unjust face punishment → hell, disbelievers.

42:23.notes: Verse 23: 'Say, I ask of you no wage' → qul-statements; good news for believers → believers; 'Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative' → mercy. Verse 24: 'they say He forged a lie' → denial-of-revelation; 'He knows what is in the hearts' → knowledge. Verse 25: 'He accepts the repentance … remits sins' → repentance, mercy (already tagged). Verse 27: provision in precise measure → provision; 'Expert and Observant' → knowledge. Verse 28: rain after despair, mercy → natural-signs, mercy.

42:29.notes: Verse 29: 'signs … creation of heavens and earth … creatures' → creation-of-heavens-earth, natural-signs; 'He is Able to gather them' → power. Verse 30: misfortune from own deeds, yet He pardons → mercy. Verses 32-33: ships as signs → natural-signs; 'signs for every disciplined, grateful person' explicitly names patience (disciplined/ṣabbār) and gratitude (shakūr) → patience, gratitude. Verse 34: He could wreck them → power.

42:36.notes: Verse 36: what you have is temporary; better with God for those who believe and rely → believers, trust-in-god. Verse 37: avoiding major sins and forgiving anger → practical-ethics. Verse 38: prayer explicitly named → prayer; 'give of what We provided' → zakat-and-charity; consultation (shura) → practical-ethics. Verse 40-42: retribution equal to harm, pardon preferred; blame on those who wrong people and commit aggression → justice-and-witness, corruption-on-earth. Verse 43: 'whoever endures patiently and forgives' — patience named explicitly → patience. Hell implied for the unjust in v42 → hell.

42:44.notes: Verse 44: 'Whoever Allah leaves astray' → guidance (negated), divine-decree; transgressors asking to go back when seeing torment → day-of-judgment, hell, disbelievers. Verse 45: exposed to it in disgrace; believers declare the losers lost themselves on the Day of Resurrection → believers, day-of-judgment, hell. Verse 46: no allies against Allah, whoever Allah leaves astray has no way out → divine-decree.

42:47.notes: Verse 47: 'Respond to your Lord' — universal address to humanity → mankind; Day that cannot be turned back → day-of-judgment. Verse 48: 'We did not send you as a guardian' → prophethood-general; man tastes mercy then turns ungrateful → mercy; 'man turns blasphemous' (kafur) → disbelief (borderline — not tagged separately as section focus is on human character vis-à-vis mercy). Verses 49-50: God grants daughters, sons, or sterility as He wills → sovereignty, power, knowledge, divine-decree; granting of children also touches children-and-parents. Confidence medium because children-and-parents is a borderline application here — the passage is about God's sovereignty over birth, not parental duties per se.

42:51.notes: Verse 51: modes of divine communication — inspiration, veil, or messenger — defines how Allah speaks to humans → prophethood-general, language-and-revelation-terms; 'He is All-High, All-Wise' → power, wisdom. Verse 52: 'We inspired you … We made it a light' addressed directly to Muhammad → muhammad, the-quran; 'We guide whomever We will' and 'you surely guide to a straight path' → guidance.

42:53.notes: Single verse closing the surah: 'The path of Allah' → guidance; 'to whom belongs everything in the heavens and earth' → sovereignty; 'to Allah all matters revert' → tawhid (asserting God's absolute oneness and ultimate authority over all).

43:1.notes: Section opens with Ḥā-Mīm disjoined letters. The Quran is described as Arabic, clear, and 'sublime and wise' in the Source Book — triggering the-quran, language-and-revelation-terms, wisdom (Ḥakīm), and knowledge (implicitly via 'Knower' attribute of the Source Book context; 'wise' is the explicit trigger).

43:5.notes: References sending of many prophets to past peoples who ridiculed them, and their subsequent destruction. Mockery of prophets is explicit ('ridiculed him'). Denial of revelation implicit in their response to prophets.

43:9.notes: Polytheists themselves acknowledge God created the heavens and earth — 'Mighty, the Knower'. The section covers earth as habitat, rain reviving dead land, pairs, ships and animals. Verse 13 contains an uttered praise formula 'Glory be to Him Who placed these at our service' — tagging praise. 'Thus you will be brought out' references resurrection but only in passing simile, not the section's subject. Mankind addressed implicitly as the recipients of these favors.

43:15.notes: Section rebukes attributing a part/offspring to God and calling angels females. Shirk is the explicit subject. Tawhid is the counter-assertion implicit in the refutation. Angels are explicitly named as the objects of false attribution.

43:20.notes: The 'had God willed' argument is addressed and refuted — touching divine-decree (they misuse the concept of God's will). Following ancestors blindly, rejection of messengers across history, and divine retribution on deniers are all explicit. 'We reject what you are sent with' is clear denial of revelation.

43:26.notes: Abraham explicitly named declaring disavowal of idols and affirming the one Creator who will guide him. Tawhid and anti-shirk are the explicit subject. 'He will guide me' invokes guidance as a divine attribute.

43:29.notes: God's provision/enjoyment given to disbelievers and their forefathers ('I gave these and their forefathers some enjoyment'). The Quran is the subject of denial ('This is sorcery'). 'Is it they who allocate the mercy of your Lord?' — mercy named explicitly. God's distribution of livelihood references provision. 'A manifest messenger came to them' — prophethood-general.

43:33.notes: God explains He withheld silver houses from disbelievers lest all humanity unite in disbelief — 'humanity would become a single community' triggers mankind. 'The Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous (muttaqin)' — taqwa named explicitly. Provision is implicit in the silver/furnishings scenario. Greed-and-miserliness is borderline — the section contrasts worldly ornaments with the hereafter, but does not name greed as a trait; dropping this label. Confidence medium due to the borderline nature of some labels.

43:36.notes: Whoever shuns 'remembrance of the Most Gracious' — remembrance (dhikr) is explicitly named as what is being abandoned. A devil/Satan is assigned as companion — iblis label applies. The companion drags them to punishment on the Day — day-of-judgment and hell (partners in suffering/torment) are explicit eschatological references.

43:40.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('Can you make the deaf hear…', 'So adhere to what is revealed to you', 'You are upon a straight path', 'It is a message for you and for your people') — this is direct address to Muhammad, so tagging muhammad. The-quran is the subject of 'adhere to what is revealed to you' and 'it is a message for you.' Guidance and prophethood-general are explicit. Disbelief and denial-of-revelation appear in the context of those who cannot be guided.

43:46.notes: Moses sent to Pharaoh with signs — both named. Signs/miracles shown and mocked ('they started laughing'). Plagues afflicted on Pharaoh's people. Pharaoh's people broke their promise after relief — punishment-of-past-nations foreshadowed. Mockery explicit ('laughing at them').

43:51.notes: Pharaoh's arrogant proclamation ('do I not own the Kingdom of Egypt') is explicit arrogance (istakbara/kibr implied by his self-elevation). Moses referenced implicitly as 'this miserable wretch.' Angels mentioned ('came with him in procession'). Pharaoh and his people drowned — punishment-of-past-nations. Pharaoh's people described as 'wicked' (fasiqin).

43:57.notes: 'Son of Mary' cited as example by opponents — jesus tagged. 'We made him an example for the Children of Israel' — children-of-israel tagged. 'He is a portent of the Hour' — signs-of-the-hour tagged. 'Let not Satan divert you' — iblis tagged. 'Had We willed, We would have made of you angels' — angels tagged. The debate about Jesus versus their gods addresses shirk and tawhid implicitly. Disbelievers are the quarrelsome opponents.

43:63.notes: Jesus explicitly named ('When Jesus came with the clarifications'). Jesus declares 'I have come to you with wisdom' — wisdom named. 'Fear Allah' — taqwa explicitly named. 'Allah is my Lord and your Lord' — tawhid assertion. 'Woe to the wrongdoers from the suffering of a painful Day' — day-of-judgment. The factions who differed are disbelievers.

43:67.notes: Direct address 'O My servants' to believers on the Day of Judgment — believers tagged. Day-of-judgment is explicit ('On that Day'). Paradise described ('Enter the Garden… trays of gold… you will stay forever') — paradise tagged. 'Except for the righteous (muttaqin)' — taqwa named explicitly.

43:74.notes: Sinners in Hell forever — hell explicit. 'We did them no injustice' — justice (God's justice) explicitly asserted. Reckoning implied in the accounting of their deeds. Day-of-judgment framing throughout.

43:79.notes: 'Have they contrived some scheme? We too are contriving' — plotting (makr) explicitly invoked. 'Our messengers are by them, writing down' — knowledge (God's complete knowledge). 'Say, If the Most Gracious had a son…' — qul-statement present; refutes shirk and asserts tawhid. 'Glorified be the Lord of the heavens and the earth' (Subḥāna) — praise uttered. 'Until they encounter their Day' — day-of-judgment.

43:84.notes: 'He is Allah in heaven and Allah on earth' — tawhid. 'He is the Wise, the Knower' — wisdom and knowledge. 'Blessed is He (Tabāraka) Who has sovereignty over the heavens and the earth' — praise (tabāraka formula uttered) and sovereignty. 'He alone has knowledge of the Hour' — signs-of-the-hour (knowledge of when the Hour comes) and knowledge reinforced.

43:86.notes: 'Those they invoke besides Him are incapable of intercession' — intercession explicitly the subject; shirk implied by invoking others. Tawhid asserted by contrast. 'Who created them? — Allah' — creation invoked. Verse 88 contains the Prophet's lament 'My Lord, these are a people who do not believe' — this is an uttered address (Rabbi…) by the Prophet, functioning as a quasi-dua. However, it is not a formal supplication with a request; it is a statement/complaint. Tagging muhammad for his direct speech reported here. Confidence high but noting the borderline dua question in notes.

43:89.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('Pardon them, and say, Peace') — muhammad tagged for direct address. 'Say: Peace' is a qul-statement (imperative to declare something). Pardoning and responding with peace is a practical-ethics instruction. Short single-verse section.

44:1.notes: Opens with Hā-Mīm → disjoined-letters. The Blessed Night (Laylat al-Qadr) → ritual-calendar-and-sacred-time. 'He is the Hearer, the Knower' → knowledge. 'There is no god but He. He gives life and causes death' → tawhid and death-and-dying. 'Lord of the heavens and the earth' → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'They play around in doubt' → disbelievers. Revelation of the Qur'an on the Blessed Night → the-quran.

44:10.notes: 'The sky produces a visible smoke enveloping mankind' → mankind, signs-of-the-hour. 'Our Lord, lift the torment from us, we are believers' is an uttered supplication in distress → dua-distress. 'An enlightening messenger has already come to them' but 'they turned away… educated, but crazy!' → denial-of-revelation, prophethood-general. 'The Day when We launch the Great Assault' → day-of-judgment. 'We will avenge' → punishment-of-past-nations context. Verse 12 contains the uttered du'a 'Rabbanā ikshif…'.

44:17.notes: 'People of Pharaoh' and 'a noble messenger came to them' → pharaoh, moses (the noble messenger is Moses per context). 'Do not exalt yourselves above Allah' → arrogance. 'I have taken refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me' is an uttered refuge-seeking → dua-protection. 'Allah's servants' likely refers to children of Israel → children-of-israel. The testing of Pharaoh's people as warning → punishment-of-past-nations.

44:22.notes: 'He appealed to his Lord: These are a sinful people' is a prayer but functions more as narrative appeal than a formal uttered du'a supplication in the dua-* sense — however it is a direct address to God, so borderline dua-distress. Opting not to tag dua-distress as it reads as a narrative report rather than a uttered formula. 'Set out with My servants by night… cross the sea… they are an army to be drowned' → exodus narrative, miracles. 'We delivered the Children of Israel' → children-of-israel. 'We chose them knowingly' → knowledge. 'We gave them many signs' → miracles. Pharaoh described as 'transgressing tyrant' → pharaoh, punishment-of-past-nations. Exodus departure → migration.

44:34.notes: 'There is nothing but our first death, and we will not be resurrected' → denial of resurrection → disbelievers, resurrection. 'Bring back our ancestors' → mockery of resurrection claim. 'People of Tubba and those before them — We annihilated them' → punishment-of-past-nations. 'We did not create the heavens and the earth… to play… only for a specific purpose' → creation-of-heavens-earth, day-of-judgment (implicit purposeful creation pointing to accountability).

44:40.notes: 18 verses — largest section. 'Day of Sorting Out' → day-of-judgment. 'No friend will avail a friend' → intercession (negated). 'He is the Mighty, the Merciful' → mercy. Tree of Zaqqum, boiling bellies, dragged into Hell → hell. 'The righteous… in gardens and springs… silk and brocade… lovely companions… every kind of fruit' → paradise, taqwa (al-muttaqin explicitly named). 'They will not taste death beyond the first death' → death-and-dying. 'This is what you used to doubt' → disbelievers. 10 labels — within ceiling.

44:58.notes: 'We made it easy in your language so that they may remember' → the-quran, language-and-revelation-terms. Ease of recollection implies guidance as explicit purpose of revelation here.

44:59.notes: Single verse: 'So wait and watch. They too are waiting and watching.' — a warning addressed to the Prophet and disbelievers about the coming Day. Minimal content; 2 labels appropriate for this short closing verse.

45:1.notes: Opens with Ḥā-Mīm → disjoined-letters. Verse 2 asserts revelation from 'the Exalted in Might, the Wise' → power + wisdom. Verses 3–5 enumerate natural signs including human creation, animals, night/day alternation (cosmic-bodies), rain/provision, wind — all framed as ayat for believers.

45:6.notes: Verse 8: persists arrogantly (mustakbiran) → arrogance explicitly named. Verse 9: takes revelations in mockery → mockery. Verse 10: Hell awaits them → hell. Verse 11: 'This is guidance' → guidance. Disbelievers rejecting revealed verses → denial-of-revelation + disbelief.

45:12.notes: Sea tamed by Allah's command for ships and seeking bounty → provision + natural-signs. 'That you may give thanks' (tashkurun) explicitly names gratitude → gratitude triggered by concrete naming. Everything in heavens and earth subjected → creation-of-heavens-earth. Address is to humanity in general → mankind.

45:14.notes: Verse 14 opens with 'Qul' (Tell/Say) → qul-statements. Instruction to believers to forgive disbelievers → practical-ethics for the conduct commanded. 'He will fully recompense people' → justice + reckoning. Believers and disbelievers both present as addressed groups.

45:16.notes: Verse 16: children-of-israel given Book, wisdom, prophecy → children-of-israel + previous-scriptures + prophethood-general + provision. Verse 17: judged on Day of Resurrection → day-of-judgment. Verse 18: 'We set you (Muhammad) upon a pathway' — direct second-person address to the Prophet → muhammad. Verse 20: 'illumination for mankind, guidance and mercy' → mankind + guidance + mercy.

45:21.notes: Verse 21: contrast between evil-doers and believers → disbelievers + believers. Verse 22: 'Allah created the heavens and the earth with justice, so that every soul will be repaid' → creation-of-heavens-earth + justice. Verse 23: taking desire as god → shirk (associating desire as deity); Allah sealing heart/hearing → divine-decree. Disbelief implicit throughout → disbelief.

45:24.notes: Verses 24–25: materialist denial of afterlife and resurrection → disbelief + denial-of-revelation. Verse 26: 'Qul' → qul-statements. 'Allah gives you life then makes you die then gathers you for the Day of Resurrection' → death-and-dying + resurrection + day-of-judgment. 'Most people do not know' → mankind (universal reference).

45:27.notes: Verse 27: 'To Allah belongs the kingship of the heavens and the earth' → sovereignty. Day of Judgment / the Hour → day-of-judgment. Verse 28: every community called to its Book, repaid → reckoning. Verse 30: believers admitted into mercy → paradise (clear triumph). Verse 31: disbelievers turned arrogant → arrogance + disbelief + hell implied. Verse 29: 'This Book of Ours' → the-quran. 10 labels within ceiling.

45:33.notes: Verse 33: evils become evident; 'the very thing they ridiculed will haunt them' → mockery. Verse 34: 'Your abode is the Fire' → hell. Verse 35: 'you took Allah's revelations for a joke' → denial-of-revelation + mockery reinforced. Day of judgment context throughout → day-of-judgment.

45:36.notes: Single verse: 'Praise belongs to Allah; Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, Lord of humanity' — al-hamdu lillah uttered → praise. 'Lord of the heavens and earth and humanity' → sovereignty (dominion over all).

45:37.notes: Single verse: 'To Him belongs all supremacy in the heavens and the earth' → sovereignty. 'He is the Majestic (al-Aziz), the Wise (al-Hakim)' → power + wisdom (closing formula, rule 4).

46:1.notes: Opens with Ḥā-Mīm → disjoined-letters. Verse 2 asserts the Qur'an's divine origin (wisdom/power closing). Verse 3 references creation of heavens and earth. Verse 4 is a qul challenging polytheists. Verse 5 references the Day of Resurrection. 11 labels, within ceiling.

46:7.notes: Verse 7: disbelievers call revelation 'magic' → denial-of-revelation, sorcery. Verse 8: qul, 'He is the Forgiver, the Merciful' → mercy, knowledge. Verse 9: qul, prophethood-general. Verse 10: qul, Children of Israel witness → children-of-israel; 'you turned arrogant' → arrogance explicitly named in translation.

46:11.notes: Verse 11: disbelievers mock believers. Verse 12: Book of Moses as prior scripture → moses, previous-scriptures; Arabic Qur'an → language-and-revelation-terms; 'guides' → guidance (explicitly named). Verse 13: righteous who say 'Our Lord is Allah'. Verse 14: Paradise → paradise.

46:15.notes: Verse 15: enjoining kindness to parents → children-and-parents; stages of bearing/weaning → human-creation; the uttered supplication 'Lord, enable me to appreciate the blessings… and improve my children for me. I have sincerely repented' → dua-gratitude (thanking for blessings on self and parents), dua-family-offspring (asking for righteous children), repentance (explicitly stated: 'I have sincerely repented'). Verse 16: Paradise reward → paradise; overlooking misdeeds → mercy.

46:17.notes: Verse 17: son dishonors parents, denies resurrection → children-and-parents, resurrection, disbelief. Verse 18: sentence upon communities of jinn and humans → jinn. Verse 19: degrees of reward/punishment by deeds → reckoning. Verse 20: disbelievers paraded before Fire, 'your unjust arrogance on earth' explicitly named → arrogance, hell, day-of-judgment.

46:21.notes: Verse 21: 'brother of Aad' = Hud → hud, ad; warns of 'tremendous Day' → day-of-judgment; 'worship none but Allah' → tawhid. Verse 22: people reject and challenge him → disbelievers, shirk. Verse 23: 'knowledge is only with Allah' → knowledge; prophethood mission → prophethood-general. Verses 24-25: wind of destruction → natural-signs, punishment-of-past-nations.

46:26.notes: Verse 26: empowered them yet their senses availed nothing because they denied Allah's signs → ad, disbelief, denial-of-revelation; 'what they used to ridicule' → mockery. Verse 27: destroyed townships around them → punishment-of-past-nations, previous-creations-destroyed. Verse 28: idols failed them → shirk.

46:29.notes: Verses 29-30: jinn listen to the Qur'an → jinn, the-quran; 'sent down after Moses' → moses, previous-scriptures; 'guides to the truth' → guidance. Verse 31: call to believe, forgiveness of sins, salvation from punishment → prophethood-general. Verse 32: those who do not respond are in error → disbelief.

46:33.notes: Verse 33: creation of heavens and earth as proof of God's power to resurrect → creation-of-heavens-earth, resurrection, power. Verse 34: disbelievers presented to Fire on the Day → disbelievers, hell, day-of-judgment.

46:35.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('So be patient… do not be hasty regarding them') → muhammad; patience is the explicit subject and command ('be patient as the messengers with resolve were patient') → patience; 'messengers with resolve' → prophethood-general; 'the Day when they witness what they are promised' → day-of-judgment; 'sinful people' destroyed refers to the disbelievers → disbelievers.

47:1.notes: Muhammad is named explicitly in verse 2 ('what was sent down to Muhammad') — this is a naming, not a direct address, but it is substantive enough to tag. 'guidance' is triggered by explicit mention of 'the truth from their Lord' contrasted with 'falsehoods', and 'He remits their sins' invokes mercy but is framed as consequence rather than attribute invocation — mercy tagged below at closing formulas. 'denial-of-revelation' is triggered by the disbelievers following falsehood vs. the believers following what was revealed.

47:4.notes: 'patience' is triggered by explicit naming of the steadfast/tested believers in verse 4 context, but primarily by 'He thus tests some of you by means of others' — borderline. However 'patience' as a concept label needs explicit naming per rule 5. The word 'steadfast' does not appear here, so dropping patience. 'manumission-and-captives' is triggered by 'release them by grace, or by ransom'. 'power' by 'had Allah willed He could have defeated them Himself'. 'divine-decree' by the testing framework.

47:8.notes: Verse 10 invokes the rhetorical 'have they not traveled the earth' pattern pointing to destroyed past civilizations — tag 'punishment-of-past-nations' and 'previous-creations-destroyed'. Verse 12 contrasts paradise for believers and fire for disbelievers. Verse 13 references the eviction of the Prophet from his town (Mecca), which is a historical allusion to the Prophet — but as this is not direct address to Muhammad, it does not warrant the 'muhammad' tag per instructions. 'denial-of-revelation' from verse 9: they hated what Allah revealed.

47:14.notes: 'taqwa' is explicitly triggered in verse 15: 'the Garden promised to the muttaqun (the righteous/God-conscious)'. 'guidance' triggered by contrast between one on evidence from his Lord vs. one who follows desires. Paradise described in detail (rivers of water, milk, wine, honey, fruits) — tag 'paradise'. Hell described (boiling water, fire) — tag 'hell'. 'disbelievers' and 'believers' as contrasted groups.

47:16.notes: Verse 16 describes those who listen to the Prophet but don't understand — characteristic hypocrisy pattern. Verse 17 explicitly mentions guidance and taqwa ('He increases them in guidance, and has granted them their righteousness/taqwa'). Verse 18 mentions the Hour and its tokens — 'signs-of-the-hour'. Verse 19 contains the explicit tawhid formula 'there is no god but Allah' — tag 'tawhid'. Verse 19 also has a command to seek forgiveness for the Prophet and believers — this is a command directed at the Prophet (second-person address 'ask forgiveness for your sin') which is direct address to Muhammad — tag 'muhammad'. 'knowledge' from 'Allah knows your movements and resting-place'.

47:20.notes: Verse 20 references a decisive surah being sent down — 'the-quran' as subject. Verse 22 explicitly names 'make mischief on earth' — 'corruption-on-earth' triggered. Verse 22 also mentions severing family ties — 'children-and-parents' (kinship ties). Verse 24 'will they not ponder the Quran' — reinforces 'the-quran'. Verse 25 names Satan explicitly — tag 'iblis'. Verse 26 'Allah knows their secret thoughts' — 'knowledge'. 'guidance' from verse 25 ('after guidance became clear to them'). Hypocrites are the dominant subject (those with sickness in hearts, those who reverted). War/fighting mentioned in verse 20 — 'war-and-treaties'.

47:27.notes: Short section. Angels taking souls at death — 'angels' and 'death-and-dying'. The disbelievers' deeds nullified because they pursued what displeases Allah — 'disbelief' and 'disbelievers'.

47:29.notes: Verse 31 explicitly names 'those who are steadfast (al-sabireen)' — 'patience' triggered by explicit naming. Verse 30 'Allah knows your actions' — 'knowledge'. Verse 32 mentions opposing the Messenger — 'prophethood-general'. Verse 33 direct address 'O you who believe' — 'believers'. Verse 34 'Allah will not forgive them' — negation of mercy, but the attribute mercy is invoked; tag 'mercy'. War and striving (jihad) referenced in verse 31 — 'war-and-treaties'. Hypocrites as primary subject of verses 29-30.

47:35.notes: Verse 35 addresses believers regarding war — don't waver, don't call for peace from weakness — 'war-and-treaties'. Verse 36 explicitly mentions 'if you have faith and lead a righteous life (taqwa)' — 'taqwa' triggered explicitly. Verse 37 mentions becoming tightfisted — 'greed-and-miserliness' triggered by explicit reference to becoming tightfisted/miserly when asked to spend. 'believers' from the implied address.

47:38.notes: The whole section is about spending in Allah's cause — 'zakat-and-charity'. 'greed-and-miserliness' explicitly triggered: 'among you are those who withhold'. 'provision' from 'Allah is the Rich (al-Ghani) while you are the needy' — God as sustainer and provider. 'disbelief' from 'if you turn away' (tawalla) implying apostasy/turning away from faith. Short single-verse section — 5 labels appropriate.

48:1.notes: 14 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: praise (the morning/evening glorification in v9 is commanded rather than uttered, so this should be dropped per §5.6b), guidance (present but secondary to the main conquest/forgiveness theme). Core labels are: muhammad, believers, hypocrites, polytheists, mercy, knowledge, wisdom, power, paradise, hell, prophethood-general, islamic-history-and-community.

48:10.notes: V10 — pledging allegiance to the Prophet is pledging to Allah; covenant language explicit. V11 — hypocrites (the Desert-Arabs who remained behind) speaking with their tongues what is not in their hearts. V13 — disbelievers threatened with the Blazing Fire. V14 — Allah's sovereignty over heavens and earth; He forgives and punishes as He wills — mercy closing formula.

48:15.notes: Those who lagged behind (hypocrites in conduct) want to follow for the spoils. 'Qul' present. They accuse the believers of jealousy (envy label from their accusation; borderline — the envy label is triggered by the explicit use of the word 'jealous'). Divine decree: 'Allah has said so before' — His word cannot be changed.

48:16.notes: Direct 'Qul' command. Section addresses Desert-Arabs who lagged behind, calling them to future battle. Obedience rewarded with paradise; disobedience punished with a painful punishment (hell implied). Exemptions for the disabled establish a practical-ethics / war-conduct rule.

48:18.notes: The Bay'at al-Ridwan (pledge under the tree) — a historically specific community event. Allah's pleasure with the believers, His knowledge of their hearts, the sending of serenity. Promise of imminent conquest and abundant gains. Power closing formula: 'Allah is Capable of everything.'

48:22.notes: V22-23: Allah's unchanging sunna that disbelievers would have fled. V24: restraining of hands in the valley of Mecca — specific to Hudaybiyyah. V25: the Sacred Mosque explicitly named; believers and disbelievers intermingled; Allah's mercy for whom He wills. V26: 'words of taqwa' — explicit naming of taqwa as the word imposed on the believers, meeting rule-5 trigger. Knowledge closing formula.

48:27.notes: V27: Allah fulfills the Prophet's vision — entering the Sacred Mosque safely, heads shaven; pilgrimage rites referenced. Knowledge: 'He knew what you did not know.' V28: the Messenger sent with guidance and the religion of truth — prophethood-general and guidance. Divine decree implicit in the fulfillment of the vision.

48:29.notes: Muhammad named explicitly ('Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah'). The companions described: stern against disbelievers, merciful among themselves — mercy label. Their bowing and prostrating: prayer. Their description in the Torah and Gospel — previous-scriptures. The plant metaphor for the growing community. Promise of forgiveness and great reward to those who believe and do righteous deeds — righteous-conduct explicitly named ('believe and do good deeds'). Prophethood-general: 'Messenger of Allah.'

49:1.notes: Direct address to believers (yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū) multiple times. The Prophet is addressed in verse 4 ('those who call you from behind the chambers') — direct second-person address to Muhammad. Closing formula 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy; 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' → knowledge. Taqwa is explicitly named ('fear Allah'/'hearts tested for piety'). Humility is the explicit subject of instruction (lower your voices, do not precede Allah and His Messenger).

49:6.notes: Direct address to believers. Muhammad referenced ('among you is the Messenger of Allah'). Closing formula 'Allah is Knowing and Wise' → knowledge and wisdom. Guidance is explicitly named ('guided you to the faith' — also in v7's 'rightly guided'). Disbelief named explicitly ('made disbelief hateful to you'). Practical ethics is the explicit subject — verify news, do not act in ignorance.

49:9.notes: Direct address to believers. Rules for reconciliation between fighting Muslim factions — war-and-treaties (internal conflict and reconciliation). 'Reconcile between them with justice, and be equitable; Allah loves the equitable' → justice and justice-and-witness. Taqwa is explicitly named ('remain conscious of Allah'). Closing phrase 'so that you may receive mercy' → mercy.

49:11.notes: Verses 11–12 open with direct address to believers; verse 13 opens with 'O people!' (yā ayyuhā an-nās) → mankind. Mockery is the explicit subject ('No people shall ridicule other people'). Slander and backbiting are explicitly named ('nor shall you slander one another', 'nor backbite one another'). Repentance is explicitly named ('whoever does not repent'). Taqwa explicitly named twice ('remain mindful of Allah'). 'We created you from a male and a female' → human-creation. Closing 'Allah is All-Knowing, Well-Experienced' → knowledge.

49:14.notes: Multiple 'Say:' (qul) imperatives in verses 14, 16, 17 → qul-statements. Also addressed to Muhammad directly ('They regarded it a favor to you') → muhammad. Believers and disbelievers addressed as groups. Mercy in closing formula 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful'. Knowledge: 'Allah knows everything in the heavens and the earth' and closing. Guidance explicitly named: 'guiding you to the faith'. Sincerity explicitly named: 'these are the sincere', 'if you are sincere'. The Desert-Arabs' nominal profession without true faith is a hypocrisy-adjacent theme (outward submission without inner faith) → hypocrisy tagged; confidence remains high as the distinction between iman and islam is the explicit subject.

49:18.notes: Single verse. 'Allah knows the secrets of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is seeing of everything you do.' Pure divine-attribute statement — knowledge is the sole substantive content. No people named, no du'a, no narrative.

50:1.notes: 16 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: prophethood-general (implicit rather than explicit subject), provision (present but minor), natural-signs and creation-of-heavens-earth overlap significantly. The named peoples (Noah, Thamud, Ad, Pharaoh, Lot) and punishment-of-past-nations are all independently justified by explicit naming. 'Dwellers of the Woods' likely refers to Madyan/Shuayb's people per tafsir but 'shuayb' and 'madyan' not named explicitly so withheld.

50:15.notes: The two recording angels seated left and right are mentioned; 'angels' is tagged. 'We are nearer to him than his jugular vein' triggers nearness-and-response. 'With Us is a comprehensive book' (carried forward context) plus 'a watcher by him ready' triggers divine-decree and knowledge. Death's daze at v.19 triggers death-and-dying.

50:20.notes: The trumpet blown and every soul coming forward = resurrection and day-of-judgment. Driver and witness = angels. Hell addressed directly and commanded to receive disbelievers. Paradise brought near to the muttaqin — 'taqwa' is named explicitly ('mutaqeen'/'pious'). 'Who fabricated another god with Allah' = shirk explicitly named. Justice asserted: 'I am not unjust to the servants.' Reckoning present in the accounting of deeds and the escort's testimony.

50:36.notes: Verses 36–37 cite destroyed past generations as warning — punishment-of-past-nations and previous-creations-destroyed. Verse 38 states creation of heavens and earth in six days.
