Verses 39–40 directly address the Prophet to 'endure' and 'proclaim the praises of your Lord' at specific prayer times — triggers muhammad (direct second-person address to him), prayer (specific times of salah commanded), and praise (subbiḥ bi-ḥamdi rabbik — 'proclaim the praises'). Verses 41–44 describe the Day of Emergence/resurrection. Verse 43 asserts power over life and death.

50:45.notes: Short single-verse section. 'We are fully aware of what they say' = knowledge. Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('you are not a dictator over them') = muhammad. 'Remind by the Quran' = the-quran as explicit subject. 'So remind' is a command to the Prophet functioning analogously to a qul-statement pattern (directive speech from God to the Prophet); qul-statements tagged. No uttered du'a, no eschatology in this verse itself.

51:1.notes: Opening oath by spreading winds, laden clouds, and flowing ships (natural-signs) and the woven sky (cosmic-bodies). Verses 5–6 assert the Day of Judgment is true. Verses 13–14 describe the disbelievers presented to the Fire (hell). Verse 15 describes the pious in gardens and springs (paradise). Verse 17 references their night vigil in prayer; verse 18 their dawn supplication for pardon (prayer). Verse 19 their charity to the beggar and deprived (zakat-and-charity). Verse 15 explicitly names the muttaqin (taqwa). Verse 22 references provision from heaven (provision). Disbelievers addressed as mockers/imposters throughout. 11 labels — within ceiling.

51:24.notes: Verses 24–30 cover Abraham's angelic guests, the announcement of a knowledgeable son (isaac implied but not named — not tagging isaac), and the wife's reaction. Verse 30 closing formula: 'He is the Wise, the Knowing' → wisdom and knowledge. Verses 31–37 describe the angels' mission to Lot's guilty people, the stone-rain punishment, evacuation of believers, and a remaining sign. Lot is not named by name but his people and city are clearly the subject (the guilty sinners); tagging punishment-of-past-nations. Believers explicitly mentioned (v.35–36). Miracles: the angelic visitation and divinely marked rocks of punishment qualify.

51:38.notes: Verse 38: Moses sent to Pharaoh. Verse 39: Pharaoh calls him a sorcerer or madman (denial-of-revelation). Verse 40: Pharaoh and troops thrown into the sea. Verses 41–42: 'Ad destroyed by devastating wind. Verses 43–45: Thamud struck by lightning. Verse 46: People of Noah named. All four constitute punishment-of-past-nations. Prophethood-general: Moses is sent as a messenger, pattern of sending messengers implied. Verses 47–48: construction of the universe and spreading of the earth → creation-of-heavens-earth. 'We constructed the universe with power' → power. Verse 49: creation of all things in pairs → natural-signs (earthly sign for reflection). 11 labels — within ceiling.

51:50.notes: Verse 50: 'Flee towards Allah, I am a clear warner' — first-person prophetic address functioning as a qul-type declaration (qul-statements). Verse 51: explicit command not to set up another god with Allah → tawhid and shirk. Verse 52: prior peoples called messengers sorcerers or madmen → denial-of-revelation and prophethood-general (pattern of messengers rejected). Verse 53: describes disbelievers as rebellious → disbelievers. Verse 55: 'the reminder benefits the believers' → remembrance (dhikr named explicitly) and believers. Note: verse 50–51 contain first-person prophetic speech ('I am a clear warner') rather than a strict 'Say:' imperative, but the passage functions as a declarative qul-pattern address — tagging qul-statements at medium confidence for this element.

51:56.notes: Verse 56: 'I did not create the jinn and the humans except to worship Me' → jinn and mankind (both named), and creation (God as Creator). Verse 57: God needs no provision from them. Verse 58: 'Allah is the Provider, the One with Power, the Strong' → provision and power (divine attributes named explicitly). Verse 59: those who do wrong will have their turn like their counterparts → punishment-of-past-nations (reference to prior punished peoples as precedent) and disbelievers.

51:60.notes: Single verse. 'Woe to those who disbelieve because of that Day of theirs which they are promised' → disbelievers and day-of-judgment. Short section; 2 labels appropriate.

52:1.notes: The oath-sequence invokes cosmic and earthly phenomena (the Mount, the sea, the elevated roof/heaven, the frequented House) as precursors to the punishment declaration. 'Is this magic?' (v.15) echoes denial-of-revelation. The 'inscribed Book in a published scroll' is best read as referencing the heavenly record or the Qur'an itself.

52:17.notes: v.17 explicitly names the muttaqun → taqwa trigger met. v.21 on offspring joined to believing parents → children-and-parents. v.27 'spared us the agony' → mercy. v.28 'we used to pray to Him' — this is a reported/quoted past supplication; the du'a is quoted speech from the people of paradise ('we used to pray to Him'), which counts as an uttered supplication in the text → dua-distress (they prayed while fearful for their families). 'He is the Good, the Compassionate' → mercy (closing divine attribute).

52:29.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('By the grace of your Lord, you are neither a soothsayer...') → muhammad. v.31 contains explicit qul → qul-statements. Accusations of poet/madman/fabricator → denial-of-revelation. v.34 challenge to produce a like discourse → challenge-to-produce. v.35–36 rhetorical questions about creation → human-creation and creation-of-heavens-earth. v.43 'Allah transcends what they associate' → shirk and tawhid (subhana llah formula). v.41 'do they know the future' → knowledge (God's exclusive knowledge). 11 labels, within ceiling.

52:44.notes: v.44–46 describe the disbelievers' stubborn rejection and their coming Day → disbelievers, day-of-judgment. v.48 directly addresses the Prophet ('you are before Our Eyes') → muhammad. v.48 'patiently await' — the word patience/sabr is explicitly invoked as a command → patience trigger met. v.48 'proclaim the praises of your Lord' — subbiḥ bi-ḥamdi rabbika — explicit glorification/praise uttered → praise.

52:49.notes: Night glorification and glorification at the receding of stars → prayer (times of salah/dhikr). 'The receding of the stars' → cosmic-bodies. 'Glorify Him' is a command to utter praise → praise (the act of tasbiḥ is in the section).

53:1.notes: Section covers the Prophet's vision of Gabriel at the highest horizon, the revelation event, the Isra/Mi'raj ascent imagery, the Lotus Tree of the Extremity, and the Garden of Repose. 'Extremely Powerful' → power. Gabriel described → angels. Revelation described → the-quran + prophethood-general. 'Great Signs of his Lord' → miracles. Star oath → cosmic-bodies. Direct address implied toward Muhammad throughout ('your friend', 'His servant') → muhammad.

53:19.notes: Section refutes al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat as mere names with no divine authority → shirk + tawhid. Angels named female → polytheists + angels + disbelief. Intercession of angels avails nothing without God's permission → intercession. 'To Allah belong the Last and the First' → sovereignty. 'He knows best' (twice) → knowledge. 'Guidance has come to them from their Lord' → guidance. Vast section (19–32) covering idol refutation, day-of-judgment sovereignty, and intercession limits.

53:33.notes: 14 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: cosmic-bodies (Sirius mentioned only briefly as 'Lord of Sirius', marginal), previous-scriptures (Scrolls of Moses referenced as a pointer, not developed). Core anchors: moses + abraham (named explicitly), ad + thamud + noah (destroyed peoples), reckoning (deeds witnessed and rewarded), divine-decree (no soul bears another's burden, each gets only what they strive for), human-creation (sperm drop), provision (enriches and impoverishes), death-and-dying (He gives death and life), power (He destroyed, He topples).

53:56.notes: Warning linked to prior warners → prophethood-general. 'The inevitable is imminent' → day-of-judgment. Laughing, not weeping, lost in frivolity → mockery + disbelievers. 'This discourse' referring to the Qur'an → the-quran.

53:62.notes: Single verse commanding prostration and worship of Allah alone → tawhid. The command to bow and worship constitutes an act of praise/glorification uttered in the text → praise. This is a sajdah verse.

54:1.notes: Single verse. The splitting of the moon is a miracle and a sign of the approaching Hour. Cosmic-bodies applies as the moon is the subject.

54:2.notes: Disbelievers call the miracle 'continuous magic' (sorcery label for the accusation per 7:116 pattern). Verses 6–8 describe the Day of Resurrection and the disbelievers' horror — day-of-judgment and resurrection apply. 'Profound wisdom' invokes divine wisdom. Warnings and news of prophets = prophethood-general. Mockery/turning away = mockery.

54:9.notes: Noah's people deny him — denial-of-revelation. Noah utters a distress supplication ('I am overwhelmed, so help me') — dua-distress. The Flood with water from heaven and springs = natural-signs. 'A purpose already destined' = divine-decree. God's power in the Flood = power. The ark left as a sign. The Quran made easy refrain (v17) = the-quran. Punishment-of-past-nations for the Flood destruction.

54:18.notes: Hud is not named explicitly, but 'Aad' is named and the passage is about the people of Hud — tagged ad. Hud is not named by name in this section so omitted per rule 5 (no explicit naming). The screaming wind destroying people = natural-signs (wind as punishment). Power in the destruction. The Quran-easy refrain (v22) = the-quran. Punishment-of-past-nations. Denial-of-revelation (they denied the truth).

54:23.notes: Thamud named explicitly. The she-camel as a test is the miracle of Salih — miracles. Salih is the implied prophet (the single human being they refused to follow); though not named by name, the she-camel sign uniquely identifies this as Salih's narrative — tagged salih at medium confidence. The Scream = divine punishment. Prophethood-general for the theme of rejecting a messenger. The Quran refrain (v32) = the-quran.

54:33.notes: Lot named explicitly. Lot's people rejected warnings — denial-of-revelation. Shower of stones = punishment-of-past-nations. Family of Lot rescued — 'Thus We reward the thankful' explicitly names gratitude (shukr trigger). They lusted for his guest = chastity-and-boundaries (explicit depiction of the boundary violation). The Quran refrain (v40) = the-quran. Power in the seizure.

54:41.notes: People of Pharaoh explicitly named. Moses is implied (the warnings came to them as in the Exodus narrative) but not named here — however 'people of Pharaoh' and 'Our signs, all of them' directly echoes the Moses-Pharaoh narrative; Moses not explicitly named so omitted. Pharaoh tagged. Power in 'Almighty Omnipotent.' Denial-of-revelation for rejecting all signs. Punishment-of-past-nations.

54:43.notes: Direct address challenging contemporary disbelievers — disbelievers. Reference to 'the scriptures' (al-zubur) = previous-scriptures. The Hour as their appointed time = day-of-judgment. Saqar / dragged into Fire = hell. 'Everything We created is precisely measured' = divine-decree. God's command instant = power. 'We have destroyed your likes' = punishment-of-past-nations.

54:52.notes: Everything recorded in the Books = reckoning and divine-decree. Knowledge (God's complete record of all deeds, small and large). The righteous (al-muttaqun) in gardens and rivers = paradise; taqwa explicitly named ('al-muttaqin' = those with taqwa, concrete trigger met).

54:55.notes: Single verse. Assembly of virtue in the presence of an Omnipotent King = paradise. 'Omnipotent King' invokes sovereignty and power as divine attributes.

55:1.notes: Surah opens with the divine name Ar-Rahman (mercy), then lists three acts: teaching the Quran, creating man, teaching him expression. 'Man' here is universal humanity. No disjoined letters in this surah.

55:5.notes: Sun, moon, stars = cosmic-bodies; trees prostrating = natural-signs; sky raised and balance set = creation-of-heavens-earth and sovereignty; explicit command to maintain just weights = justice and practical-ethics trigger met.

55:10.notes: Earth spread for creatures (al-anam = mankind broadly), fruits, palms, grains = provision and natural-signs; earth set up as part of cosmic order = creation-of-heavens-earth.

55:14.notes: Two creation accounts side by side: man from clay, jinn from fire. Both are explicit creation statements — human-creation and creation both apply; jinn named directly.

55:17.notes: Lord of the two Easts/Wests = sovereignty over cosmic directions; two seas merging with a barrier = natural-signs and creation-of-heavens-earth; pearls and coral emerging = provision (natural bounty from the seas).

55:24.notes: Ships on the sea as His possession = sovereignty and natural-signs (sea framed as sign/bounty); 'everyone upon it is perishing' = death-and-dying; 'remains the Face of your Lord Full of Majesty' asserts sovereignty and eternal nature. Provision tag: ships as means of livelihood/transport from the sea.

55:29.notes: Everything in heavens and earth asks Him (nearness-and-response); 'every day He is managing' = sovereignty and power; direct address to 'O society of jinn and humans' = jinn and mankind both tagged explicitly.

55:35.notes: Flares of fire bombarding jinn and humans = eschatological punishment (day-of-judgment, hell); sky splitting = signs-of-the-hour; 'no human or jinn asked about his sins on that Day' = day-of-judgment and reckoning dimension. Reckoning not independently tagged as it is subsumed by day-of-judgment here without explicit weighing-of-deeds imagery.

55:41.notes: Guilty recognized by marks, seized by forelocks and feet = reckoning/day-of-judgment scene; 'This is Hell that the guilty denied' = hell and disbelief implied; 'the guilty' (mujrimun) = disbelievers as collective subject.

55:46.notes: 'Him who feared the standing of his Lord' = taqwa trigger met explicitly (khafa maqam rabbihi); two gardens with springs and fruits = paradise; believers implicitly addressed as the God-fearing; fruits = provision within paradise context.

55:54.notes: Reclining on brocade furnishings, fruits near at hand, maidens — detailed paradise description. Believers are the implied recipients. Provision not separately tagged as this is paradise reward context, subsumed by paradise.

55:62.notes: Two additional (lesser) gardens described in detail — springs, fruits, date-palms, pomegranates, good companions 'untouched by human or jinn' = paradise; 'no human or jinn has touched them' names both groups; believers are the implied recipients.

55:76.notes: Brief continuation: reclining on green cushions and exquisite carpets — short paradise description closing the paradise sequence. Only one label independently warranted; within the 2-label floor but the section is genuinely minimal.

55:78.notes: Tabaraka ismu rabbika = uttered praise formula (praise label triggered per §5.6b); 'Full of Majesty and Splendor' = sovereignty divine attribute.

56:1.notes: Section covers the opening of the Day — earth shaken, mountains scattered — then the three-fold division of humanity, with detailed paradise description for the forerunners (al-muqarrabun). Signs-of-the-hour for the cosmic upheaval (vv.1–6); paradise for vv.12–26.

56:27.notes: Describes the reward of the Companions of the Right — gardens, shade, water, fruit, and specially created companions. Human-creation triggered by 'We have created them of special creation' (v.35). Provision for the food and drink of paradise.

56:41.notes: Describes the punishment of the Left — searing wind, boiling water, Zaqqum tree. Their crime: luxury, persisting in great sin, and denial of resurrection (vv.47–48). Qul-statement at v.49 ('Say: the first and the last will be gathered...'). Day-of-judgment and reckoning for 'the Day of Retribution' (v.56).

56:57.notes: Series of rhetorical questions about human creation (semen, v.58–59), crops (v.63–65), water (v.68–70), and fire (v.71–73) — all framed as God's creative power, not humanity's. Gratitude triggered explicitly: 'Will you not be thankful?' (v.70). Divine-decree for 'We have decreed death among you' (v.60). Death-and-dying for v.60. Mankind as the universal addressee throughout the rhetorical challenge. Section closes with a command to glorify God (v.74) — not praise uttered, but commanded, so praise label withheld per §5.6b.

56:75.notes: Oath by the positions of the stars (cosmic-bodies, v.75). The Quran declared noble, preserved (the-quran, vv.77–80). Denial of the Quran addressed (denial-of-revelation, vv.81–82). Death-scene passage (vv.83–87) with God's nearness ('We are nearer to it than you,' v.85 — nearness-and-response). Three outcomes at death — paradise for the near ones and the Right (paradise), hell for the deniers (hell). Knowledge via 'Lord of the Worlds' and the protected Book framing.

56:95.notes: Two-verse closing. 'This is the certain truth' affirms the Quran's verity (the-quran). 'Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Magnificent' — 'glorify' (sabbih) is praise uttered/commanded toward God; per §5.6b praise is tagged when the formula is present. Sovereignty for 'the Magnificent' (al-'Azim) as a divine-attribute invocation.

57:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with 'Glorifying Allah' (sabbaha) — uttered praise → `praise`. Verses 2 and 5 assert sovereignty (mulk). Verse 3 asserts omniscience. Verse 4 describes creation of heavens and earth in six days plus the Throne. Verse 6 mentions day/night cycle (cosmic-bodies). Closing formula 'He knows what the hearts contain' reinforces `knowledge`. 'Over all things competent / power over all things' → `power`. 'Almighty, the Wise' → `wisdom`.

57:7.notes: Verse 7 addresses believers with a call to believe and spend — `believers`, `zakat-and-charity`. Verse 8 references 'the Messenger calls you' — `muhammad` (substantively about his role/call, not just a Say-command). Verse 9 says He sends down 'clear revelations upon His servant' to bring from darkness to light — `the-quran`, `guidance`. 'Allah is Gentle, Most Compassionate' → `mercy`. 'He knows what you do' → `knowledge`. Verse 10 references those who spent and fought before vs. after 'the conquest' — `islamic-history-and-community`, `prophethood-general` (messenger context throughout).

57:11.notes: Verse 11 invites a 'loan to Allah' (charitable spending) — `zakat-and-charity`. Verse 12 depicts believers on the Day of Judgment with light and garden — `believers`, `paradise`, `day-of-judgment`. Verse 13 describes the hypocrites on that Day separated from believers — `hypocrites`, `hypocrisy`. Verse 14 narrates their dialogue and exposes their self-deception — `hypocrisy`. Verse 15 declares no ransom will be accepted and the Fire is their refuge — `hell`, `disbelievers`, `disbelief`. 'Within it is mercy' (the wall) → `mercy`.

57:16.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: `sincerity` (verse 19 uses 'the sincere' as a descriptor but the section is not primarily about sincerity as a taught concept; borderline rule-5 trigger); `taqwa` (verse 16 uses 'khushoo' / heart-surrender to dhikr, not taqwa explicitly — however verse 21 urges racing to forgiveness which is taqwa-adjacent; still a borderline call). Verse 16 urges believers to let hearts submit to `remembrance` of Allah and not be like People of the Book whose hearts hardened — `believers`, `people-of-the-book`, `remembrance`. Verse 17 uses the revival of the earth as a sign — `natural-signs`. Verse 18 praises charitable men and women — `zakat-and-charity`. Verse 19 contrasts sincere believers (siddiqun) with disbelievers in hellfire — `disbelievers`, `disbelief`, `hell`. Verse 20 describes worldly life as vanity versus Hereafter agony or forgiveness — `mercy` (forgiveness from Allah). Verse 21 promises Paradise for believers — `paradise`. 'That is the grace of Allah' — `mercy`.

57:22.notes: Verse 22 establishes that all calamities are written before they occur — `divine-decree`. Verse 23 warns against pride (mukhtal fakhur — proud snob) — `arrogance`. Verse 24 condemns those who are stingy and urge others to stinginess — `greed-and-miserliness`. 'Allah is the Independent, the Praiseworthy' → no specific attribute label matches 'Independent' cleanly; 'Powerful/Strong' in verse 25 → `power`. Verse 25 mentions sending messengers with clear proofs and books and the Balance for justice — `prophethood-general`, `previous-scriptures`, `justice`. 'That humanity may uphold justice' → `mankind` (universal humanity referenced). 'Allah is Strong and Powerful' → `power`.

57:26.notes: Verse 26 names Noah and Abraham and establishes prophethood and scripture in their lineage — `noah`, `abraham`, `prophethood-general`, `previous-scriptures`. Verse 27 names Jesus son of Mary explicitly — `jesus`. 'We gave him the Gospel' → `previous-scriptures`. 'Instilled compassion and mercy in hearts of followers' → `mercy`. Verse 28 opens with 'O you who believe! Fear Allah' (ittaqu Allah) — `believers`, `taqwa` (explicit command to have taqwa). 'He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and will forgive you. Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → `mercy`. People who followed Jesus and deviated from monasticism → `people-of-the-book` (the Christians, followers of Jesus, addressed contextually).

57:29.notes: Short single-verse section. Explicitly addresses People of the Book — `people-of-the-book`. 'All grace is in Allah's hand; He gives it to whomever He wills' → `sovereignty`. 'Allah is Possessor of Great Grace' → `mercy` (fadl/grace is a mercy-cluster attribute).

58:1.notes: Section covers the zihar ruling (a pre-Islamic form of divorce-by-comparison), its expiation via freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding the needy, then closes with the resurrection and God's witnessing. 'Allah is Hearing and Seeing' → knowledge. 'Pardoning and Forgiving' → mercy. The resurrection/reckoning in v6 → day-of-judgment and reckoning. 10 labels, within ceiling.

58:7.notes: V7 asserts God's omniscient presence in all secret counsel → knowledge. V8 describes those prohibited from secret conspiracy who revert to it, conspiring in sin and defiance of the Messenger, greeting the Prophet with a distorted greeting — classic hypocrisy and plotting. Hell is explicitly mentioned ('Hell is enough for them'). Disbelievers implied by the damnation. Day of Judgment referenced in v7 close.

58:9.notes: Opens with 'O you who believe!' → believers. Instructs believers on proper secret counsel — virtue and piety (taqwa is explicitly named: 'converse in virtue and piety'). V10 names Satan as source of conspiracies → iblis. Closes with 'let the believers put their trust in Allah' → trust-in-god (tawakkul explicitly invoked). General conduct instruction → practical-ethics.

58:11.notes: Opens twice with 'O you who believe!' → believers. V11 addresses conduct in gatherings; God elevates the knowledgeable → knowledge (attribute). V12 instructs giving charity before private consultation with the Messenger → zakat-and-charity. The Messenger is the direct subject of address in v12 ('when you converse privately with the Messenger') → muhammad. Closing 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy.

58:13.notes: Addresses the easing of the charity-before-consultation ruling; 'Allah pardons you' → repentance (tawbah accepted). Commands: 'perform the prayer' → prayer; 'give alms' → zakat-and-charity. Closing 'Allah is Aware' → knowledge. Implicitly addresses believers throughout.

58:14.notes: 12 labels at the ceiling. 'Those who befriended a people with whom Allah has become angry' — per Ibn Kathir this refers to hypocrites allying with Jews (people-of-the-book). They swear false oaths → oaths-and-vows and hypocrisy. Satan has taken hold of them → iblis. They are 'inhabitants of the Fire' → hell. Day of resurrection referenced in v18 → day-of-judgment. 'Allah has written: I and My messengers will prevail' → divine-decree, prophethood-general. 'Allah is Strong and Mighty' → power. Their plotting/conspiring → plotting. Disbelievers evident from hell sentence. Trim candidates if needed: prophethood-general (passing reference), people-of-the-book (via tafsir inference).

58:22.notes: True believers do not befriend those who oppose Allah, even family → children-and-parents (parents, children, siblings named explicitly). God has inscribed faith in their hearts → divine-decree. They enter gardens of paradise → paradise. 'Allah is pleased with them and they with Him' → mercy (divine pleasure/approval). Day of judgment implied by 'the Last Day' reference. Disbelievers as the opposed group. 'These are the partisans of Allah' closes the surah's contrast.

59:1.notes: V1 opens with glorification (sabbaha) → praise. V2 explicitly names 'those who disbelieved among the People of the Book' driven from their homes → people-of-the-book, disbelievers. 'Hands of the believers' → believers. 'Allah came at them from where they never expected, threw terror' → power, sovereignty. 'Had He not decreed exile' → divine-decree. 'Punishment of the Fire' in hereafter → justice. The Banu Nadir expulsion is core early Islamic community history → islamic-history-and-community. Comparison implied to past nations destroyed → punishment-of-past-nations. 11 labels — within ceiling.

59:5.notes: V5: cutting/leaving trees 'by Allah's will' → divine-decree. V6: 'Allah gives authority to His messengers over whomever He will; Allah is Able to do all things' → power, prophethood-general. V7: distribution of fay' spoils to Messenger, relatives, orphans, poor, wayfarer → wealth-and-property-law, zakat-and-charity, orphan-care. 'Whatever the Messenger gives you, accept it' → muhammad (substantive instruction about the Prophet's authority). 'Fear Allah' explicit → taqwa.

59:8.notes: V8: the poor Muhajirin (emigrants) driven from homes → migration, islamic-history-and-community, believers. 'These are the sincere' → sincerity explicitly named. V9: the Ansar giving preference over themselves, 'whoever is protected from his natural greed' (shuḥḥ) — generosity/practical giving → practical-ethics; 'greed' mentioned but in the context of overcoming it, not warning against it per se. V10: uttered supplication 'Rabbana ighfir lana…' → dua-forgiveness. 'You are Clement and Merciful' closing → mercy. 8 labels — within ceiling.

59:11.notes: V11–12: the munafiqun making false promises to their disbelieving allies among the People of the Book → hypocrites, people-of-the-book, disbelievers, hypocrisy, plotting. V13: 'a people who do not understand' — disbelief. V15: 'like those before them, experienced consequences' → punishment-of-past-nations. V16: the Shaytan/Iblis analogy explicitly → iblis, disbelief. V17: 'both in the Fire forever' → hell. 9 labels — within ceiling.

59:18.notes: V18: 'O you who believe! Fear Allah' → believers, taqwa. 'Allah is Aware (Khabir) of what you do' → knowledge. 'Let every soul consider what it has forwarded for the morrow' → reckoning (explicit forward-looking account). V19: 'do not forget Allah' → remembrance explicitly invoked as the contrast. V20: 'inhabitants of Fire / inhabitants of Paradise' → hell, paradise. V21: 'this Quran…crumbling in awe of Allah…parables for the people so they may reflect' → the-quran, mankind ('the people' = universal address in the parable). 9 labels — within ceiling.

59:22.notes: V22: 'There is no god but He' → tawhid. 'Knower of secrets and declarations' → knowledge. 'Compassionate, the Merciful' → mercy. V23: 'the Sovereign' → sovereignty. 'Almighty, Omnipotent, Overwhelming' → power. 'Glory be to Allah, beyond what they associate' (Subhan Allah) → praise (uttered glorification); also implicitly rebukes shirk → shirk. 7 labels — within ceiling.

59:24.notes: V24: 'the Creator, the Maker, the Designer' → creation, tawhid (sole creator). 'His are the Most Beautiful Names' → tawhid. 'Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him' → praise (uttered/stated glorification). 'the Majestic' → sovereignty. 'the Wise' → wisdom. 5 labels — within ceiling.

60:1.notes: Direct address to believers (yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū). 'O Prophet' not present but the Messenger is referenced in third person as having been expelled; section is substantively about loyalty vs. enmity toward the hostile disbelievers in the context of migration and striving. Muhammad is referenced ('They have expelled the Messenger') but not directly addressed — borderline; included because his expulsion is the historical anchor. 'I know what you conceal and what you reveal' → knowledge attribute.

60:3.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: repentance (implied in 'to You we repent' but uttered as part of the du'a — keep as dua-forgiveness covers it; consider removing standalone repentance label) and shirk (explicit disavowal 'what you worship apart from Allah' warrants it — keep). Best trim: repentance (subsumed by the uttered du'a of turning back). Two uttered du'as present: 'Rabbanā alayka tawakkalnā wa-ilayka anabna' (trust/repentance — dua-protection/dua-guidance cluster) and 'Rabbanā lā tajʿalnā fitnatan … waghfir lanā' (dua-forgiveness + dua-protection). Day of Judgment explicitly named in v3. 'Forgiving, the Mighty and Wise' → wisdom attribute. Abraham named; his father referenced.

60:7.notes: 'Allah is Capable, Forgiving, Merciful' → power and mercy. 'Allah loves the equitable' → justice. Rules distinguishing non-hostile non-Muslims (treat kindly) from hostile ones (do not befriend) — practical legal-ethical guidance in the context of the early Muslim community.

60:10.notes: Direct address to believers. Rules about believing women emigrating, testing their faith, validity of their marriages to unbelievers, remarriage, and financial compensation — marriage, divorce, and migration law all present. 'Allah is Knowing and Wise' → knowledge and wisdom. 'Fear Allah' in v11 → taqwa (explicit naming of the concept). Muhammad not directly addressed but the section governs conduct relevant to the community he leads; borderline — keeping because the historical context is the Hudaybiyyah treaty and specifically addresses the community's legal obligations in his era. justice-and-witness for the testing/adjudication process.

60:12.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('O Prophet') → muhammad. Pledge of allegiance conditions: no shirk, no theft, no adultery, no killing children, no perjury as to parenthood, no disobedience. 'Not commit perjury as to parenthood' → slander-and-backbiting (false attribution of parentage is explicit false accusation). 'Killing their children' → children-and-parents. 'Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy. The bay'ah is a solemn covenant → covenant. Practical ethics: list of moral commitments.

60:13.notes: Direct address to believers. 'People with whom Allah has become angry' — per Ibn Kathir this refers to the Jews; tagged people-of-the-book accordingly (rule per §10 open policy: descriptive categories → judgement call). 'Despaired of the Hereafter' → day-of-judgment. Confidence medium because the people-of-the-book identification rests on tafsir rather than the surface text.

61:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with tasbih (glory/praise) of everything in the heavens and earth — tag 'praise'. Closing formula 'Almighty, the Wise' → 'power' and 'wisdom'. Verses 2–3 address believers directly about hypocrisy in speech vs. deed — 'practical-ethics' fits (the section names the concept explicitly: saying what you do not do). Verse 4 addresses fighting in ranks in God's cause — 'war-and-treaties'. 'Sincerity' is triggered because the explicit subject is acting in accordance with one's stated belief.

61:5.notes: Single verse. Moses named and addresses his people. Children of Israel named collectively. 'Allah does not guide the sinful/deviant people' — guidance explicitly invoked as withheld. Their swerving from the messenger = denial of revelation and disbelief.

61:6.notes: Jesus son of Mary named, addresses Children of Israel directly. Confirms the Torah → 'previous-scriptures'. Announces Ahmad (Muhammad) by name → 'muhammad'. Miracles shown → 'miracles'. People call it 'obvious sorcery' → 'sorcery' and 'denial-of-revelation'.

61:7.notes: Verse 7: fabricating falsehood against Allah while being invited to Islam → 'denial-of-revelation' and 'disbelief'. Verse 8: disbelievers trying to extinguish God's Light → 'disbelievers', 'disbelief'. Verse 9: the Messenger sent with guidance and true religion to prevail over all religions, and the polytheists (mushrikun named explicitly) dislike it → 'polytheists', 'prophethood-general', 'guidance'. God's guidance/light completing → 'guidance'.

61:10.notes: Direct address 'O you who believe!' → 'believers'. The 'trade' is believing, striving with possessions and selves — 'war-and-treaties' (striving/jihad in God's cause), 'zakat-and-charity' (spending possessions). Reward: forgiveness (God's mercy) → 'mercy'; gardens beneath which rivers flow, Gardens of Eden → 'paradise'. God's Messenger referenced → 'prophethood-general'. Verse 13 mentions imminent victory — part of the war-and-community context.

61:14.notes: Direct address 'O you who believe!' → 'believers'. Jesus son of Mary named, addressing the Hawariyyun (disciples) → 'jesus', 'disciples'. Children of Israel split into believers and disbelievers → 'children-of-israel'. The prophethood/messenger pattern invoked → 'prophethood-general'. God supporting the believers against their enemy.

64:1.notes: Verse 1 opens with tasbih (glorification) and 'to Him all praise is due' — tags praise. Sovereignty (mulk), power (qadir), creation of heavens/earth and of humans, and knowledge of the seen/unseen all explicitly named. Verse 2 names both believers and disbelievers as created groups.

64:5.notes: Section recounts past nations who rejected their messengers; they tasted ill consequences and painful torment awaits — punishment-of-past-nations and hell. The specific complaint 'Are human beings going to guide us?' is denial-of-revelation. Closing 'Allah is Independent and Praiseworthy' is a divine-attribute formula but Ghani/Hamid map to sovereignty/praise clusters — sovereignty added implicitly; however the dominant attribute here is independence/self-sufficiency which is closest to sovereignty.

64:7.notes: Contains explicit qul ('Say') command. The subject is disbelievers denying resurrection — resurrection label. They will be informed of their deeds — reckoning. 'That is easy for Allah' asserts power.

64:8.notes: Verse 8 calls to believe in Allah, His Messenger, and 'the Light which We sent down' — the-quran. Verse 9 describes the Day of Gathering with paradise for believers. Verse 10 describes hell for those who deny revelations — denial-of-revelation. Knowledge closing formula ('Allah is Aware'). Mercy not explicitly in closing formula here; forgiveness of misdeeds implied but no explicit mercy name — removed. Knowledge retained from 'Allah is Aware (Khabir)'.

64:11.notes: Verse 11: disasters only by Allah's leave — divine-decree; He guides the heart of the believer — guidance; 'Allah is Aware' — knowledge. Verse 12: obey Allah and the Messenger — prophethood-general. Verse 13: 'Allah, there is no god but He' — tawhid; 'let the believers put their trust' — trust-in-god, believers. Verse 14: 'O you who believe' — believers; warns about spouses and children as enemies — marriage-and-family, children-and-parents; closing 'Allah is Forgiver and Merciful' — mercy.

64:15.notes: Verse 15: wealth and children as a test — children-and-parents. Verse 16: 'be conscious of Allah' (ittaqu) — explicit taqwa trigger; 'give' (spend) — zakat-and-charity; 'protected from his stinginess' — greed-and-miserliness explicitly named (shuhh). Verse 17: lending to Allah (charitable giving) — zakat-and-charity; closing 'Appreciative and Forbearing' — mercy cluster (Ghafur implied; Shakur/Halim are not in the 12 attribute clusters precisely, but forgiveness is mentioned: 'will forgive you' — mercy). Believers addressed implicitly throughout.

64:18.notes: Single verse closing formula: 'Knower of the Unseen and the Seen' — knowledge; 'the Almighty' (Al-Aziz) — sovereignty/power; 'the Wise' (Al-Hakim) — wisdom. Short section with only divine-attribute content; 3 labels appropriate.

65:1.notes: Opens with 'O Prophet' — direct address to Muhammad, so `muhammad` applies. Divorce procedure and iddah rules are the main subject. 'Be pious before Allah' names taqwa explicitly. 'Allah may afterwards bring about a new situation' invokes divine-decree.

65:2.notes: Verses 2–3. Verse 2 covers end-of-iddah procedures and testimony requirements (justice-and-witness). Verse 3 'whoever fears Allah' names taqwa; 'whoever relies on Allah' names tawakkul (trust-in-god); 'provide for him from where he never expected' invokes provision; 'Allah has set a measure to all things' invokes divine-decree.

65:4.notes: Verses 4–5. Iddah rules for post-menopausal women, those who have not menstruated, and pregnant women — divorce law. Pregnant women's term until delivery touches children-and-parents context. Repeated 'whoever fears Allah' names taqwa explicitly. Verse 5 'this is the ordinance of Allah which He sent down to you' marks this as revealed law — the-quran label is appropriate as the revelation itself is referenced as the source of the ordinance.

65:6.notes: Verses 6–7. Housing and financial maintenance of divorced wives, expenditure on pregnant wives, nursing arrangements and payment — divorce and family law with clear wealth/property dimensions. 'Allah will bring ease after hardship' and 'spend according to what Allah has given him' invoke provision. Children-and-parents applies because nursing of the infant is explicitly addressed.

65:8.notes: Verses 8–9. Towns that defied the command of their Lord and His messengers — punishment-of-past-nations. Mentions 'messengers' generically — prophethood-general. Strict accounting — reckoning. Defiance of God's command implies disbelief and denial-of-revelation.

65:10.notes: Verses 10–11. 'O you who possess intellect and have faith' addresses believers directly. Hell (severe retribution prepared for the defiant) — hell. 'Beware of Allah' names taqwa. 'Allah has sent down to you a Reminder' and 'a messenger who recites to you Allah's verses' — the-quran and prophethood-general. 'Bring those who believe from darkness into light' — guidance. Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding forever — paradise. 'Allah has given him an excellent provision' — provision.

65:12.notes: Single verse. 'Created seven heavens and their like of earth' — creation-of-heavens-earth. 'Allah is Capable of everything' — power. 'Allah Encompasses everything in knowledge' — knowledge. Both power and knowledge are explicitly stated as the purpose of the cosmological description.

66:1.notes: Direct address 'O Prophet' triggers muhammad. Verse 1 addresses the Prophet's self-prohibition to please his wives (marriage-and-family). Verse 2 addresses dissolution of oaths (oaths-and-vows). Closing attributes: 'Forgiving and Merciful' → mercy; 'All-Knowing, the Most Wise' → knowledge and wisdom.

66:3.notes: Direct address to the Prophet throughout (muhammad). Verse 3 concerns a confidential disclosure among wives (marriage-and-family). Verse 4 mentions Gabriel and the angels as supporters (angels), calls the two wives to repentance (repentance), and references the righteous believers (believers). Verse 5 raises the possibility of divorce and replacement with better wives (divorce, marriage-and-family). 'All-Knowing, the All-Informed' → knowledge. Repentance is explicitly named as the subject in verse 4 — concrete trigger met.

66:6.notes: Verse 6 opens with 'O you who believe' (believers) and commands protection from Hell (hell) guarded by angels (angels). Verse 7 addresses 'O you who disbelieved' (disbelievers) on the Day of reckoning (day-of-judgment). Verse 8 opens again with 'O you who believe' (believers), exhorts sincere repentance (repentance), promises paradise (paradise), mentions the Prophet on that Day (muhammad), and contains an uttered du'a 'Rabbanā atimm lanā nūranā wa-ghfir lanā' asking for forgiveness → dua-forgiveness. Closing 'You are capable of all things' → power. 10 labels, within ceiling.

66:9.notes: Verse 9 addresses the Prophet directly (muhammad) and commands striving against disbelievers (disbelievers) and hypocrites (hypocrites), whose abode is Hell (hell). Verse 10 names Noah, Lot, and implicitly their wives as examples — triggering noah and lot; the wives' betrayal is a marriage-and-family theme; the disbelievers enter the Fire (hell again, already tagged). Verse 11 names Pharaoh (pharaoh) and his wife as an example for believers (believers); she utters a du'a 'Rabbi ibni lī 'indaka baytan fī al-janna wa-najjinī min Fir'awn' asking for protection and paradise (dua-distress fits — she is asking deliverance from a tyrannical oppressor; paradise is also requested). 11 labels, within ceiling.

66:12.notes: Mary daughter of Imran is named (mary, family-of-imran). 'Who guarded her womb' references chastity (chastity-and-boundaries). 'We breathed into her of Our Spirit' is the miraculous conception of Jesus, implying jesus even though not named, and is a miracle (miracles) and a mode of human-creation parallel to Adam's. 'Believed in the truth of her Lord's Words and His Books' references belief in scriptures (previous-scriptures). 'Was one of the devout (qanitin)' — sincerity/devotion is the explicit subject of the closing characterisation (sincerity). Jesus: per §5.1 the miraculous conception in this verse is the same event tagged jesus in 19:16 and 3:45; Ibn Kathir confirms this verse refers to the conception of Jesus.

68:1.notes: Nun (ن) opens the surah — disjoined-letters applies. Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('you are not insane', 'you will have a reward', 'you are of a great moral character') — muhammad applies. 'Your Lord knows best' → knowledge. The deniers, vile swearer, backbiter, spreader of slander, preventer of good explicitly named. Verse 15 ('Myths of the ancients') → denial-of-revelation. Verse 14 ('Just because he has money and children') → greed-and-miserliness. The overall section also concerns prophethood-general (the Prophet's character and reward). 10 labels — within ceiling.

68:17.notes: The parable of the garden owners is a cautionary narrative about hoarding from the poor (greed-and-miserliness triggered by v.24 explicit exclusion of the poor) and divine punishment of that greed. The owners' explicit repentance ('Glory to our Lord — We were indeed in the wrong', 'we were indeed domineering', 'We are turning to our Lord') → repentance with concrete trigger. 'The most reasonable said: if only you would glorify' alludes to taqwa as the missing disposition. Verse 33 ('the punishment of the Hereafter is greater') → hell. The destroyed garden as divine retribution → punishment-of-past-nations (parabolic exemplum). God's provision withheld as test → provision. Justice in God's ordering → justice.

68:34.notes: Verse 34 explicitly names Gardens of Delight for the muttaqin → paradise + taqwa. The contrast between Muslims and villains (mujrimin) → believers vs. disbelievers. 'Or do you have a scripture' → the-quran (challenge about scripture). 'Do they have partners?' → shirk + polytheists. 'Day of Resurrection' named → day-of-judgment. 'Shall We treat the Muslims like the villains? How do you judge?' → justice. The scene of the Day when the Shin is exposed and disbelievers cannot prostrate → day-of-judgment reinforced.

68:44.notes: Verse 48 explicitly names 'the Fellow of the Fish' (Sahib al-Hut) — canonical reference to Jonah → jonah. Direct address to the Prophet ('do not be like...', 'So wait patiently for the Decision of your Lord') → muhammad. Patience is explicitly commanded ('wait patiently') — concrete trigger for patience. 'My plan is firm' — God's counter-scheming → plotting. 'Were it not for his Lord's favor' → mercy. 'They do not know' / 'Or do they know the future' → knowledge. Denial of revelation implicit in v.44 ('those who reject this discourse') → denial-of-revelation. Prophethood-general: the Prophet's role and Jonah as a prophetic exemplum.

68:52.notes: Single verse: 'it is no less than a reminder to all the Worlds' — the Quran as subject → the-quran. 'All the Worlds' (lil-'alamin) is a universal address encompassing all humanity → mankind. Two labels appropriate for this single-verse section.

69:1.notes: Opening rhetorical triple — 'What is the Reality?' — introduces the Day of Judgment (Al-Haqqah) by name but gives no further content. Single label is appropriate for this very short rhetorical opener.

69:4.notes: Thamud and 'Ad named explicitly; Pharaoh named; the Flood/ship narrative invokes Noah implicitly ('We carried you in the cruising ship' — the ship of Noah is the referent per tafsir). The 'Overturned Cities' refers to the people of Lot but Lot himself is not named, so `lot` is not tagged. Destruction by wind, earthquake, flood — natural-signs as divine instruments of punishment. God's power in seizing them — `power`. Denial of messengers — `denial-of-revelation` and `disbelief`. `prophethood-general` because messengers (rusul) are mentioned generically.

69:13.notes: Long section covering: the Trumpet blast and cosmic collapse (resurrection/day-of-judgment); angels bearing the Throne (angels); full exposure before God — nothing hidden (knowledge); books given right and left hand (reckoning); lofty Garden with pleasant living (paradise); the sinner shackled and scorched in the Blaze, chained seventy cubits (hell); disbelief in Allah the Great and failure to feed the destitute as the cause of punishment (disbelief, greed-and-miserliness); 'Allah the Great' and His throne — sovereignty. 10 labels, within ceiling.

69:38.notes: God swears an oath defending the Qur'an as the speech of a noble messenger — `the-quran`, `prophethood-general`. Explicit refutation of claims that it is poetry or soothsaying — `denial-of-revelation`. The passage is substantively about the Prophet's integrity and the consequence had he fabricated anything — this is direct address about Muhammad's role and person, warranting `muhammad`. Disbelievers and deniers referenced — `disbelievers`. 'A message for the righteous (muttaqin)' — `taqwa` named explicitly. God's knowledge of rejectors — `knowledge`. God's power to seize the Prophet had he fabricated — `power`.

69:52.notes: Single verse commanding glorification (tasbih) of the Lord — `praise` for the explicit glorification formula. 'The Magnificent' (Al-Azim) invokes divine sovereignty/greatness — `sovereignty`.

70:1.notes: Patience (sabr) is explicitly commanded in v.5 with the word sabran jamilan — concrete trigger satisfied. Angels ascending mentioned in v.4. 'Lord of the Ways of Ascent' invokes sovereignty. The Day described as fifty thousand years invokes the Day of Judgment. Power implied by 'none can repel it.'

70:8.notes: Sky like molten brass and mountains like wool are cosmic dissolution signs of the Hour. The Raging Fire (laza) is a description of Hell. Hoarding/accumulation in v.18 triggers greed-and-miserliness. The criminal wishing to ransom himself with family invokes the desperation of the Day of Judgment.

70:19.notes: Human restlessness as a created trait triggers human-creation. Prayer explicitly named twice (vv.22–23, 34). Wealth with a rightful share for beggar and deprived triggers zakat-and-charity. Day of Judgment affirmed in v.26. Guarding chastity (v.29–31) triggers chastity-and-boundaries. Honoring trusts and pledges (v.32) triggers covenant. Standing by testimonies (v.33) triggers justice-and-witness. Paradise (gardens, v.35) explicitly named. Believers as the described group of virtuous traits. Fear of Lord's punishment (v.27–28) is a concrete taqwa trigger. 10 labels — within ceiling.

70:36.notes: Disbelievers stretching necks in mockery/scoffing posture (v.36–37) triggers mockery. 'Is every one of them aspiring to enter the Garden?' — paradise referenced rhetorically. 'We created them from what they know' — human-creation. 'Lord of the Easts and Wests, We are Able' — power. Meeting their promised Day (v.42) and emerging from tombs (v.43) — day-of-judgment and resurrection.

70:44.notes: Eyes cast down and overwhelmed by humiliation describes the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. Humility label applied here not as a virtue but as the state imposed — however the Arabic dhilla (humiliation/abasement) is the explicit subject of the verse, which is the forced lowering of the disbelievers. This is a borderline use of 'humility'; the more precise label would be abasement/humiliation of the disbelievers rather than voluntary humility, but no more precise label exists in the taxonomy. Confidence remains high as the other labels are unambiguous.

71:1.notes: Noah is sent with a warning; taqwa is explicitly named ('reverence Him'); mercy via the promise of forgiveness; divine-decree in the fixed, undeferable term.

71:5.notes: 13 labels — over the 12 ceiling. Trim candidates: denial-of-revelation (the section depicts rejection/flight rather than explicit accusation of falsehood), repentance (commanded rather than enacted — borderline; rule 5 trigger is that Noah explicitly says 'ask your Lord for forgiveness', making it the subject of an instruction). Arrogance has a concrete trigger: 'became more and more arrogant' (istakbara). Cosmic-bodies: sun and moon named. Human-creation: 'created you in stages' and 'germinated you from the earth'. Natural-signs: rain, rivers, gardens, the spread earth, diverse roads. Provision: wealth, children, gardens, rivers explicitly promised.

71:21.notes: Idols Wadd, Souwa, Yaghoos, Yaooq, Nassr named → shirk. 'Schemed outrageous schemes' → plotting. Drowning and fire → punishment-of-past-nations and hell. Noah addresses God ('My Lord') but this is a complaint-report, not an uttered supplication seeking something — no dua label triggered. Verse 24 ends with 'do not increase the wrongdoers except in confusion' which is an uttered supplication fragment; however it is embedded in Noah's narration to God and reads as a du'a-distress. Adding dua-distress is defensible but borderline — confidence remains high on main labels.

71:26.notes: Noah utters 'My Lord, do not leave of the unbelievers a single dweller on earth' — an uttered supplication calling for judgment on the disbelievers in distress → dua-distress. The rationale given (they will mislead servants and breed only wicked unbelievers) underscores disbelief as the subject.

71:28.notes: Classic uttered supplication: 'My Lord! Forgive me and my parents, and anyone who enters my home in faith, and all the believing men and believing women' → dua-forgiveness. Parents mentioned → children-and-parents. Believers explicitly named as beneficiaries → believers. Wrongdoers/unbelievers in closing → disbelievers.

72:1.notes: Jinn report hearing the Quran and affirm tawhid (no mate, no child). Verse 7 explicitly references denial of resurrection. 'guidance' triggered by explicit mention of the Quran guiding to rectitude (rule 5 concrete trigger met). shirk explicitly rejected ('we will never associate anyone with our Lord').

72:8.notes: Jinn describe probing the heaven and finding it guarded by stern angels and projectiles (shooting stars). Cosmic-bodies applies to the shuhub (projectiles/meteors). The guarded heaven and restriction of knowledge of the unseen gestures toward divine decree.

72:11.notes: Jinn describe their own diversity — righteous vs. compromisers. Hell explicitly mentioned as fate of the compromisers. 'guidance' triggered by explicit mention of 'when we heard the guidance'. Power invoked in 'we cannot defeat Allah on earth'.

72:16.notes: Conditional promise of abundant water for steadfastness — provision label applies. 'Whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord' — remembrance explicitly named as the trigger. Taqwa borderline; the section frames turning away from dhikr as the cause of punishment. Divine-decree applies to the conditional framing of God's testing. punishment-of-past-nations dropped in favor of eschatological punishment label; however the mounting torment is future-oriented rather than past-nations. Confidence medium on taqwa.

72:18.notes: Mosques declared for Allah alone — mosques-and-sacred-places applies. Explicit rejection of calling on others besides Allah — tawhid and shirk. Multiple qul commands (vv. 20, 21, 22). The Prophet's role as conveyor of messages — prophethood-general. Hell for those who defy Allah and His Messenger.

72:24.notes: Verse 24 references the promised punishment coming — day-of-judgment. Verse 26 'The Knower of the Invisible' — knowledge attribute explicitly named. Verse 27 describes guards dispatched with the messenger — angels. qul in v. 25. prophethood-general applies to God choosing a messenger and entrusting him with knowledge via guarded revelation. disbelievers implied by 'they were promised' and 'who is weaker'.

72:28.notes: God's encompassing knowledge and tallying of everything by number — knowledge and divine-decree. Messengers conveying their Lord's messages — prophethood-general. Short single-verse section; 3 labels appropriate.

74:1.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('O you Enrobed one', 'your Lord') warrants `muhammad`. Commands include magnifying the Lord (`prayer`), purifying clothes, abandoning abominations, showing no favor (`practical-ethics`), and being constant/patient (`patience` — the word 'be constant' maps to sabr and is the explicit instruction). The Trumpet and 'difficult day for the disbelievers' earns `day-of-judgment` and `disbelievers`.

74:11.notes: God gave the antagonist vast wealth and children (`provision`) yet he demanded more (`greed-and-miserliness`). He turned back and 'was proud' (`arrogance` — explicit 'istakbara'). He called the revelation 'magic' (`sorcery`, `denial-of-revelation`). He is threatened with Saqar, described in vivid detail (`hell`). `disbelievers` because the antagonist is the archetypal denier.

74:31.notes: Angels as wardens of the Fire (`angels`, `hell`). Four groups explicitly named: those who disbelieve (`disbelievers`), those given the Scripture (`people-of-the-book`), those who believe (`believers`), and those in whose hearts is sickness — the standard Qur'anic description of the hypocrites (`hypocrites`). 'Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills' (`guidance`). 'None knows the soldiers of your Lord except He' (`knowledge`). 'A reminder for the mortals' (`the-quran`).

74:32.notes: Oath by the moon, night, and morning (`cosmic-bodies`). 'A warning to the mortals' — universal address to humanity (`mankind`). The 'greatest' thing warned about contextually refers to Saqar/the Day (`day-of-judgment`). The warning function implies `prophethood-general` (the warner/reminder role).

74:38.notes: Every soul hostage to its deeds (`reckoning`). The righteous in Gardens (`paradise`). Guilty in Saqar (`hell`). Sinners confess: not praying (`prayer`), not feeding the destitute (`zakat-and-charity`), denying the Day of Judgment (`day-of-judgment`, `disbelievers`). Intercession will not avail them (`intercession`).

74:49.notes: Rebuke for turning away from the Reminder (`the-quran`, `denial-of-revelation`). The donkey-fleeing-lion simile characterises the `disbelievers`. They do not fear the Hereafter (`day-of-judgment`). 'Whoever wills shall remember it' — explicit mention of dhikr/remembrance (`remembrance`).

74:56.notes: Remembrance is conditional on Allah's will (`divine-decree`, `remembrance`). 'He is the Source of Righteousness (taqwa)' — taqwa explicitly named as a divine attribute (`taqwa`). 'Source of Forgiveness' → `mercy`. Allah's willing of guidance (`guidance`).

75:1.notes: God swears by the Day of Resurrection and the self-reproaching soul; man doubts reassembly of bones — God asserts power to reconstruct even fingertips. 'Man wants to deny what is ahead' triggers disbelief (kufr as denial of truth). Mankind is the implicit universal address throughout.

75:7.notes: Moon eclipsed, sun and moon joined — cosmic-bodies; these are also signs of the Hour. Man's accounting of what he put forward and left behind is reckoning. 'To your Lord on that Day is the settlement' — sovereignty. Man is evidence against himself.

75:16.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet about the manner of receiving revelation — do not hurry with your tongue; God guarantees collection, recitation, and explanation of the Qur'an. Both `the-quran` and `language-and-revelation-terms` apply; `muhammad` applies because this is direct second-person address to him ('your tongue', 'follow its recitation').

75:20.notes: 'You love the fleeting life and disregard the Hereafter' — direct address to mankind. Radiant faces looking toward their Lord = paradise; gloomy faces realizing calamity has befallen them = hell. Preferring the worldly over the Hereafter is a form of disbelief (denial/turning away from truth).

75:26.notes: Verses 26–30 depict the moment of death (soul reaching the breast-bones, the parting). Verses 31–35 describe the disbeliever: 'he neither believed nor prayed' (prayer explicitly named); 'he denied and turned away' (disbelief); 'full of pride' — arrogance (istakbara/tematā) is explicitly named in the walking with pride image, earning the `arrogance` tag. Woe-formulas close the section.

75:36.notes: The creation of man from a drop of semen, then a clot, then proportioned — classic human-creation sequence. God created male and female from him. The rhetorical purpose is to establish God's power as an argument for resurrection (anticipating 75:40).

75:40.notes: Single verse: 'Is He not Able to revive the dead?' — a direct assertion of God's power to resurrect. Short section, two labels are appropriate and fully justified.

76:1.notes: Verse 1 poses the rhetorical question of man's pre-existence; verse 2 describes creation from a mixed fluid (human-creation); verse 3 asserts God's guidance was sent and man's choice is gratitude or ingratitude. 'Guidance' is explicitly stated ('We guided him to the way'). 'Taqwa' is not named; the choice between thankfulness and unthankfulness is the section's subject. 'Disbelief' is triggered by 'kafoor' (unappreciative/ungrateful, a disbelief-flavored term). 'Mankind' fits the universal address about the human condition.

76:4.notes: Verse 4 mentions chains and fire for the faithless (hell + disbelievers). Verses 5–6 describe paradise drink for the righteous (paradise + believers). Verse 7 mentions fulfilling vows (oaths-and-vows) and fearing the Day (day-of-judgment). Verse 8 mentions feeding the poor, orphan, and captive (zakat-and-charity + orphan-care + manumission-and-captives). Verses 9–10 contain the uttered statement of sincerity ('We only feed you for the sake of Allah') — this models sincerity explicitly. Verse 12 rewards their patience with a garden (patience — explicitly named 'bima sabaru'). 11 labels — within ceiling.

76:13.notes: Verses 13–22 are a detailed description of Jannah — thrones, shade, fruit, silver vessels, crystal cups, ginger-flavored drink, the spring Salsabeel, pearl-like youths, silk garments, silver bracelets, and the pure drink offered by the Lord. 'Mercy' is not explicitly named but verse 21 says 'their Lord will offer them a pure drink' — this is God's direct provision, tagging 'provision' and 'mercy'. Verse 22's closing 'Your efforts are well appreciated' (mashkuran) does not name an attribute clearly enough to trigger an attribute label beyond what's already tagged. 'Sovereignty' is triggered by 'a vast kingdom' (mulkan kabiran) in verse 20.

76:23.notes: Verse 23 explicitly names the Qur'an as revealed ('We sent down the Quran upon you') — the-quran + language-and-revelation-terms. The 'you' is direct second-person address to the Prophet — muhammad. Verse 24 commands patience ('be patient') — patience is explicitly named (isbir). Verse 25 commands remembrance ('mention the Name of your Lord morning and evening') — remembrance. Verse 26 commands prostration and glorification at night — prayer. No 'qul' imperative; no dua uttered.

76:27.notes: Verse 27 describes those who love the fleeting life and neglect the Heavy Day — disbelievers + day-of-judgment. Verse 28 asserts God created them and strengthened their frames (human-creation + power) and can replace them whenever He wills (divine-decree + power).

76:29.notes: Verse 29 frames the surah as a reminder ('thadhkirah') and invites whoever wills to take a path to the Lord — guidance explicitly offered. Verse 30 asserts human will is subordinate to God's will ('you cannot will unless Allah wills') — divine-decree. Closing formula 'Allah is Knowing and Wise' — knowledge + wisdom (rule 4). 'The-quran' is tagged because verse 29 identifies the surah itself as a reminder (thadhkirah), referencing the revealed text.

76:31.notes: Verse 31 states God admits into His mercy whoever He wills (mercy + divine-decree) and has prepared painful punishment for wrongdoers (hell). Short single-verse section; 3 labels appropriate.

77:1.notes: The sworn entities (those unleashed, storming, scattering, separating, delivering) are interpreted by many commentators as angels or winds; Ibn Kathir favors angels carrying revelation. 'Delivering a message / excusing or warning' points to prophethood and revelation. The oath culminates in the promise that what is foretold will come — i.e. the Day of Judgment. Confidence medium because the identity of the sworn entities is debated.

77:8.notes: Stars obliterated, sky fractured, mountains blown away — classic signs of the Hour (cosmic-bodies and creation-of-heavens-earth both apply). Messengers alerted for the Day of Decision. 'Woe to the liars/rejecters' addresses disbelievers who denied revelation.

77:16.notes: 'Did We not destroy the ancients? Then succeeded them with the others?' is a direct reference to destroyed past peoples as warning. 'This is how We deal with the guilty' asserts divine justice. 'Woe on that Day to the rejecters' ties to the Day of Judgment and disbelief.

77:20.notes: Verses 20–23 address human creation from fluid lodged in a secure place for a known term — human-creation and creation labels both apply. 'We measured precisely; We are the best to measure' invokes power and wisdom. Verses 25–27 address the earth as homestead, mountains, and pure water — natural-signs and creation. Recurring 'Woe on that Day' refrain tags day-of-judgment and disbelievers throughout.

77:29.notes: Verses 29–40 describe Hell's punishment for the deniers in vivid detail (shadow of three masses, sparks like castles, Day of Separation, gathering of all). Verses 41–45 contrast with the righteous (muttaqin) in shades, fountains, and fruits — paradise and taqwa. 'Day of Separation' is the Day of Judgment; gathering for reckoning. Justice asserted via 'This is how We reward the doers of good.' Over 12 labels would be borderline; current count is 7, defensible.

77:46.notes: 'Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; you are indeed criminals' — contemptuous address to disbelievers in this world. 'When it is said to them, kneel, they do not kneel' — explicit refusal of prayer (salah), tagging prayer for the institution being refused, and disbelief for the rejection. Denial-of-revelation implicit in the overall pattern of this surah's refrain addressed to those who reject.

77:50.notes: Single rhetorical verse: 'In what message, beyond this, will they believe?' — directly addresses the Qur'an as the message being denied, tagging the-quran and denial-of-revelation. Addressed to disbelievers.

78:1.notes: The 'Great Event' (an-Naba' al-'azim) is understood by Ibn Kathir and classical tafsir as the Resurrection/Day of Judgment, about which the Quraysh/disbelievers were disputing. The rhetorical challenge ('they will find out') targets those in denial.

78:6.notes: A sustained rhetorical catalogue of God's creative acts: earth as cradle and mountains as pegs (natural-signs + creation-of-heavens-earth), creation in pairs (human-creation), sleep/night/day (cosmic-bodies + natural-signs), seven strong heavens (creation-of-heavens-earth), blazing lamp/sun (cosmic-bodies), rain, grains, vegetation, gardens (natural-signs + provision). Power is evidenced throughout the rhetorical 'Did We not…' framing.

78:17.notes: The Trumpet blast, gathering of humanity in droves, sky opening into gateways, mountains dissolving into mirage — all are classic resurrection/judgment-day imagery and cosmic signs of the Hour.

78:21.notes: Vivid description of Hell as destination for the oppressors/transgressors (al-taghin). Their punishment is framed explicitly as a 'fitting requital' (justice). Their crime: denying the reckoning and God's signs (denial-of-revelation). 'We have enumerated everything in writing' supports reckoning and justice labels.

78:31.notes: 'The righteous' (al-muttaqin) explicitly names the taqwa concept as the subject of this reward section. Gardens, spouses, drinks, and freedom from falsehood are classic paradise descriptions. The addressees are the muttaqin = believers.

78:37.notes: 'Lord of the heavens and the earth' asserts sovereignty; 'The Most Merciful' (twice) asserts mercy. Angels and the Spirit standing in rows on the Day is an eschatological scene. 'None will speak except whom the Most Merciful permits' is the classic intercession motif. 'Day of Reality' ties back to day-of-judgment.

78:40.notes: 'We have warned you' addresses mankind broadly; 'the faithless' (al-kafir) makes disbelievers the specific focus. The person observing what his hands produced is the reckoning theme. The single verse is compact but carries clear day-of-judgment + reckoning + disbelievers content.

79:1.notes: The swearing entities (those who snatch, remove, glide, race, regulate) are interpreted by the majority of classical scholars including Ibn Kathir as angels performing various functions — extracting souls, carrying out divine commands. 'Those who regulate events' (al-mudabbirat amra) is a strong pointer to divine-decree/angels managing affairs by God's command. Confidence medium because the identities are not explicitly named in the text itself.

79:6.notes: The quake and successor blast are eschatological signs of the Hour. The disbelievers' sceptical question about being 'restored to original condition' from hollow bones is explicit denial of resurrection. Their statement 'a losing proposition' reflects their disbelief in the afterlife.

79:15.notes: Moses is called by God in the sacred valley of Tuwa and sent to Pharaoh. The 'Greatest Miracle' is shown — miracles label applies. Pharaoh's declaration 'I am your Lord, the most high' is explicit arrogance (kibr/tughyan). His denial and defiance triggers divine seizure — punishment-of-past-nations. 'I will guide you to your Lord' invokes guidance. Disbelief label applies to Pharaoh's denial. Muhammad is addressed indirectly ('Has the story reached you?') but this is not direct second-person address warranting the muhammad label per instructions — it is a narrative aside.

79:27.notes: The section describes God constructing the heaven, raising its masses, dimming its night and bringing out its daylight (cosmic-bodies), spreading the earth, producing water and pasture (natural-signs/provision), and anchoring mountains. The closing 'a source of enjoyment for you and your animals' is directed at humanity (mankind — addressed universally). Power is evident in the creation argument.

79:34.notes: The Great Cataclysm triggers man's reckoning of his deeds. Hell is displayed. Those who were defiant and preferred this world go to Hell; those who feared the Standing of their Lord and restrained their desires go to Paradise. Taqwa is explicitly invoked — 'feared the Standing of his Lord' is a concrete trigger for taqwa.

79:42.notes: Direct second-person address to the Prophet ('You have no knowledge of it', 'You are just a warner') warrants the muhammad label. The question about the Hour and the response that its knowledge belongs to God invokes divine knowledge. 'You are just a warner' pertains to prophethood-general. No explicit qul imperative in the text, so qul-statements is removed on review — correcting: no 'Say:' formula appears here, so qul-statements should not be tagged.

79:46.notes: A single verse describing how on the Day of Judgment the disbelievers will feel they only lived an evening or its morning — a statement about the subjective experience of the Day. Signs-of-the-hour and day-of-judgment both apply.

80:1.notes: The section is a direct second-person rebuke of the Prophet (frowned and turned away) — qualifies as direct address to him, hence `muhammad`. The blind man seeking purification triggers `taqwa` (God-consciousness/purification explicitly named). The 'honorable pages' held by noble scribes refers to the Qur'an itself (`the-quran`) and its angelic carriers (`angels`). 'A Lesson... whoever wills shall remember it' invokes `remembrance` (dhikr explicitly). `guidance` applies as the Qur'an is described as the reminder/lesson that benefits those who seek it.

80:17.notes: 'Perish man!' addresses mankind generically. Creation from sperm drop → `human-creation`. Death and burial → `death-and-dying`. 'When He wills, He will resurrect him' → `resurrection`. 'He did not fulfill what He commanded him' → `disbelief` (thanklessness/denial framed as kufr, v.17 literally 'how thankless he is'). 'He eased the way for him' → `guidance` (God's facilitation of the path). `provision` is not strongly triggered here — the focus is on creation and moral failure, not sustenance.

80:24.notes: 'Let man consider his food' addresses mankind. Pouring water, cracking soil, growing grains/grapes/olives/dates/gardens/fruits → `natural-signs` and `provision`. God's direct agency in all these acts ('We pour', 'We crack', 'We grow') → `power` and `creation`.

80:33.notes: 'The Deafening Noise' is a name for the Day of Judgment → `day-of-judgment` and `signs-of-the-hour`. The fleeing from family members (brother, mother, father, consort, children) on that Day is a vivid eschatological image; the enumeration of family ties also makes `marriage-and-family` applicable as those bonds are explicitly named and dramatically dissolved. `resurrection` applies as this describes the state of people after being raised.

80:38.notes: Radiant, laughing, rejoicing faces → `paradise` (the blessed on that Day). Faces covered with misery and remorse → `hell` (the wretched on that Day). The contrast of fates on 'that Day' → `day-of-judgment` and `reckoning`.

80:42.notes: Single verse: 'These are the faithless, the vicious.' Direct identification of the disbelievers → `disbelievers` (people label) and `disbelief` (negative-attribute label). Minimal but fully justified; two labels is appropriate for this single-verse section.

82:1.notes: Verses 1–5 describe the cosmic upheaval at the end of time — sky splitting, planets scattered, oceans exploded, tombs overturned — all classic signs-of-the-hour imagery. Verse 5's 'each soul will know what it has advanced and deferred' is a reckoning trigger. cosmic-bodies covers the planets/sky; natural-signs covers the oceans.

82:6.notes: Direct address 'O man!' triggers mankind. Verses 7–8 describe God creating, forming, and proportioning the human — human-creation and creation both apply. 'Most Generous' is an attribute claim for provision/mercy family but is here framed under the power and knowledge of shaping; creation and power are the clearest attribute labels. The rhetorical question 'what deluded you?' addresses human arrogance/heedlessness — the word 'deluded' (gharraka) names the vice of being deceived into ingratitude, which is the section's explicit subject, warranting arrogance as the closest negative-attribute label.

82:9.notes: 'You reject the religion' is an explicit denial-of-revelation trigger. The angelic watchers/recorders (kiraman katibin) make angels and knowledge both applicable — God's knowledge is mediated here through angelic record-keepers. Reckoning is triggered by the recording of all deeds.

82:13.notes: Clear paradise/hell contrast. 'Day of Justice/Din' names day-of-judgment. 'The wicked' entering hell implies disbelievers as the addressed group. reckoning is implicit in the sorting of virtuous vs. wicked on that Day.

82:17.notes: A two-verse rhetorical doubling — 'what will convey to you what the Day of Justice is?' — with no additional thematic content beyond emphasising the gravity of the Day of Judgment. Minimal labeling appropriate for this short, structurally emphatic section.

82:19.notes: 'No soul will avail another soul anything' is the Qur'anic formula for the absence of intercession on that Day — intercession applies as its negation (consistent with taxonomy examples like 2:255). 'The decision on that Day is Allah's' asserts divine sovereignty explicitly.

83:1.notes: The address is universal ('mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds'); the fraud is mercantile — short-weighing explicitly invoked. Resurrection and the Day of Judgment are the warning anchor.

83:7.notes: 'Legends of the ancients' (v13) is the classic denial-of-revelation formula. The Sijjeen record, the screened-from-Lord fate, and the roasting in Hell are all eschatological content. Hearts corroded by deeds is a disbelief/denial theme.

83:18.notes: 'Those brought near' (al-muqarrabun) witnessing the Elliyyoon record and drinking from Tasneem echoes the angelic nearness motif; tagged angels for the muqarrabun class. Paradise described in rich detail.

83:29.notes: The winking, laughing, and calling believers 'lost' is the mockery motif explicitly depicted. The reversal on the Day — believers laughing at disbelievers from thrones — ties to Day of Judgment and Paradise.

83:36.notes: A single rhetorical closing verse — 'Have the unbelievers been repaid?' — sealing the recompense theme. Minimal but independent content; two labels clearly justified, three defensible.

10:1.notes: Opens with Alif-Lam-Ra disjoined letters. Verse 2 addresses mankind universally and the disbelievers accuse the prophet of sorcery.

10:3.notes: Creation of heavens and earth in six days, settling on throne, governance; intercession only by permission; return to Allah; reward with equity; boiling water for disbelievers.

10:5.notes: Sun and moon as signs (cosmic-bodies); alternation of night and day as signs (natural-signs); paradise rivers for believers; hellfire for heedless; verse 10 contains 'Glory be to You' and 'Praise be to Allah' — both uttered praise formulas.

10:11.notes: God's forbearance in not hastening punishment; human ingratitude when affliction is lifted; destruction of prior generations who rejected messengers; making current people successors.

10:15.notes: Two 'Say:' (qul) commands. Disbelievers demand a different Quran or alterations. Prophet affirms he only follows revelation and fears torment of a terrible Day.

10:17.notes: Multiple qul commands. Worship of idols as intercessors refuted; 'Glorified be He' uttered (praise); God's knowledge invoked against idolaters' claims; fabricating lies about Allah.

10:22.notes: Sea voyage parable; supplication uttered in distress on ship ('If You save us from this, we will be among the appreciative') — dua-distress triggered. After rescue they commit violations — addressed as 'O people' (mankind). Sincerity invoked explicitly ('professing sincere devotion').

10:24.notes: Parable of worldly life as rain, plants, then sudden destruction — natural-signs imagery used as a sign. Section ends with 'We clarify the revelations for people who reflect.' The divine command descending signals divine-decree.

10:25.notes: Allah invites to the Home of Peace (paradise) and guides whom He wills; those who do good get paradise; those who earned evil get hell and shame; judgment described with equity (justice).

10:28.notes: Scene of the Day of Gathering; polytheists and their false partners separated; partners disown worshippers; every soul experiences its deeds.

10:31.notes: Multiple qul commands. God questioned as provider, controller of senses, originator and repeater of creation, guide to truth. Polytheists implicitly follow conjecture. 'Allah is fully aware' — knowledge attribute. Rhetorical refutation of shirk through tawhid arguments.

10:37.notes: Quran could not be fabricated; it confirms prior scriptures; challenge to produce a single chapter; prior generations also denied — classic challenge-to-produce and denial-of-revelation section.

10:40.notes: Some believe, some don't; qul command to say 'I have my deeds'; God knows the mischief-makers; cannot make deaf hear or blind see; 'Allah does not wrong people' — justice; people wrong themselves.

10:45.notes: Gathering on the Day; every community has a messenger; judgment with justice; qul commands about harm/benefit and appointed time; eternal torment mentioned. Divine decree in appointed times for each nation.

10:53.notes: Confirmation of the Day's truth; if wrongdoers had all earth's wealth they would offer it as ransom; judged equitably; Allah owns everything in heavens and earth (sovereignty); He gives life and causes death.

10:57.notes: 'O people' — mankind address. Quran described as healing, guidance and mercy. Qul commands: rejoice in Allah's grace and mercy; question about making lawful/unlawful what Allah provided (food-and-dietary trigger); fabricating lies about Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

10:61.notes: God witnesses all actions; nothing escapes His knowledge even an atom's weight. Allah's friends have no fear (believers/taqwa explicitly named: 'those who believe and are aware'). Power/sovereignty — all in heavens and earth belong to Allah. Night and day as signs. Invoking other than Allah follows only assumptions.

10:68.notes: Claim that Allah has taken a son refuted; 'Be He glorified' — uttered praise. He is Self-Sufficient; owns all in heavens and earth (sovereignty). Qul command. Fabricators will not succeed; severe punishment on Day of Return.

10:71.notes: Story of Noah recounted. Noah expresses tawakkul ('in Allah I have put my trust' — trust-in-god explicitly named). His people rejected him; he and those with him saved in the Ark; deniers drowned — punishment of past nations.

10:74.notes: Messengers sent after Noah; Moses and Aaron sent to Pharaoh; Pharaoh's court acts arrogantly (arrogance named: 'acted arrogantly'); sorcery contest; Moses refutes sorcery claim; Allah upholds truth; only a few of Moses's people believed. Punishment-of-past-nations pattern present.

10:84.notes: Moses commands trust in Allah (trust-in-god explicitly named: 'put your trust in Him'). Uttered supplication by the believers: 'Our Lord, do not make us victims…' and 'deliver us by Your mercy' — dua-protection and dua-distress both present. Revelation to Moses and Aaron to establish homes as places of prayer (prayer label). Moses's du'a against Pharaoh (Rabbana × 3) also uttered.

10:90.notes: Crossing of the sea; Pharaoh's last-moment declaration of tawhid rejected as too late; his body preserved as a sign; Children of Israel settled and provided good things (provision); they will be judged on Day of Resurrection over their differences.

10:94.notes: Direct address to the Prophet ('If you are in doubt') — muhammad label applies. Ask people of prior scripture (people-of-the-book). Jonah's people named explicitly. Divine will regarding belief (divine-decree). Qul commands. Messengers and believers saved — punishment-of-past-nations pattern.

10:104.notes: Two 'Say: O people' (qul + mankind address). Prophet declares he does not worship idols but Allah alone (tawhid vs shirk). Command not to be of polytheists. 'He is the Forgiver, the Merciful' — mercy. Guidance is for one's own soul.

10:109.notes: Direct address to Prophet: 'follow what is revealed to you, and be patient' — patience explicitly commanded. 'Allah is the Best of judges' — justice. Divine decree in 'until Allah issues His judgment.'

84:1.notes: The sky splitting and earth being leveled/emptied are classic eschatological signs preceding the Hour and the gathering.

84:6.notes: Opens with 'O man' (ya ayyuha al-insan) — tag mankind. The book in right vs. behind back is the reckoning scene. Entry into the Blaze = hell. 'His Lord was watching him' = knowledge attribute. The one who thought he would never return = disbelief.

84:16.notes: Oaths by twilight, night, and moon = cosmic-bodies and natural-signs. The question about not prostrating when the Quran is recited = the-quran + denial-of-revelation. Disbelievers addressed implicitly ('what is the matter with them').

84:22.notes: Those who disbelieve are in denial — disbelievers + disbelief. 'Allah knows what they hide' = knowledge attribute. 'Inform them of a painful punishment' uses the imperative fa-bashshirhum which is addressed to the Prophet — this is a say/command pattern but not strictly a qul. Removed qul-statements as the imperative here is fa-bashshir, not qul. Confidence medium on knowledge label — it is directly stated ('Allah knows what they hide').

84:25.notes: Short closing verse contrasting believers who do good deeds with the disbelievers of the previous section. 'Undiminished reward' = paradise implied. 'Do good deeds' is explicitly named as the trigger for righteous-conduct label.
